[Contains English characters] साचा:Wiktionary Humour or humor is the tendency of particular cognitive experiences to provoke laughter and provide amusement.
[Contains English characters] Many theories exist about what humour is and what social function it serves.
[Contains English characters] People of all ages and cultures respond to humour.
[Contains English characters] The majority of people are able to be amused, to laugh or smile at something funny and thus they are considered to have a sense of humour.
[Contains English characters] The term derives from the humoral medicine of the ancient Greeks, which stated that a mix of fluids known as humours controlled human health and emotion.
[Contains English characters] A sense of humour is the ability to experience humour, although the extent to which an individual will find something humorous depends on a host of variables, including geographical location, culture, maturity, level of education, intelligence and context.
[Contains English characters] For example, young children may favour slapstick, such as Punch and Judy puppet shows or cartoons such as Tom and Jerry.
[Contains English characters] Satire may rely more on understanding the target of the humour and thus tends to appeal to more mature audiences.
[Contains English characters] Nonsatirical humour can be specifically termed recreational drollery.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Cleanup-section Arthur Schopenhauer lamented the misuse of the term humour to mean any type of comedy.
[Contains English characters] However, both humour and comic are often used when theorizing about the subject.
[Contains English characters] The connotation of humour is more that of response, while comic refers more to stimulus.
[Contains English characters] Humour also originally had a connotation of a combined ridiculousness and wit in one individual, the paradigm case being Shakespeares Sir John Falstaff.
[Contains English characters] The French were slow to adopt the term humour and in French, humeur and humour are still two different words, the former still referring only to the archaic concept of humours.
[Contains English characters] Western humour theory begins with Plato, who attributed to Socrates in the Philebus the view that the essence of the ridiculous is an ignorance in the weak, who are thus unable to retaliate when ridiculed.
[Contains English characters] Later, in Greek philosophy, Aristotle, in the Poetics, suggested that an ugliness that does not disgust is fundamental to humour.
[Contains English characters] In ancient Sanskrit drama, Bharata Munis Natya Shastra defined humour as one of the eight nava rasas, or principle rasas, which can be inspired in the audience by bhavas, the imitations of emotions that the actors perform.
[Contains English characters] Each rasa was associated with a specific bhavas portrayed on stage.
[Contains English characters] In the case of humour, it was associated with mirth .
[Contains English characters] The terms comedy and satire became synonymous after Aristotles Poetics was translated into Arabic in the medieval Islamic world, where it was elaborated upon by Arabic writers and Islamic philosophers such as Abu Bischr, his pupil Al-Farabi, Avicenna, and Averroes.
[Contains English characters] Due to cultural differences, they disassociated comedy from Greek dramatic representation, and instead identified it with Arabic poetic themes and forms, such as hija .
[Contains English characters] They viewed comedy as simply the art of reprehension and made no reference to light and cheerful events or troublous beginnings and happy endings associated with classical Greek comedy.
[Contains English characters] After the Latin translations of the 12th century, the term comedy thus gained a new semantic meaning in Medieval literature.
[Contains English characters] The Incongruity Theory originated mostly with Kant, who claimed that the comic is an expectation that comes to nothing.
[Contains English characters] Henri Bergson attempted to perfect incongruity by reducing it to the living and mechanical.
[Contains English characters] An incongruity like Bergsons, in things juxtaposed simultaneously, is still in vogue.
[Contains English characters] This is often debated against theories of the shifts in perspectives in humour; hence, the debate in the series Humor Research between John Morreall and Robert Latta.
[Contains English characters] Morreall presented mostly simultaneous juxtapositions, with Latta countering that it requires a cognitive shift created by a discovery or solution to a puzzle or problem.
[Contains English characters] Latta is criticized for having reduced jokes essence to their own puzzling aspect.
[Contains English characters] Humour frequently contains an unexpected, often sudden, shift in perspective, which gets assimilated by the Incongruity Theory.
[Contains English characters] This view has been defended by Latta and by Brian Boyd .
[Contains English characters] Boyd views the shift as from seriousness to play.
[Contains English characters] Nearly anything can be the object of this perspective twist; it is, however, in the areas of human creativity that the shift results from structure mapping to create novel meanings.
[Contains English characters] Arthur Koestler argues that humour results when two different frames of reference are set up and a collision is engineered between them.
[Contains English characters] Tony Veal, who takes a more formalised computational approach than Koestler, has written on the role of metaphor and metonymy in humour, using inspiration from Koestler as well as from Dedre Gentners theory of structure-mapping, George Lakoff and Mark Johnsons theory of conceptual metaphor, and Mark Turner and Gilles Fauconniers theory of conceptual blending.
[Contains English characters] Some claim that humour cannot or should not be explained.
[Contains English characters] Author E. B. White once said, Humor can be dissected as a frog can, but the thing dies in the process and the innards are discouraging to any but the pure scientific mind.
[Contains English characters] As with any form of art, acceptance depends on social demographics and varies from person to person.
[Contains English characters] Throughout history, comedy has been used as a form of entertainment all over the world, whether in the courts of the Western kings or the villages of the Far East.
[Contains English characters] Both a social etiquette and a certain intelligence can be displayed through forms of wit and sarcasm.
[Contains English characters] Eighteenth-century German author Georg Lichtenberg said that the more you know humour, the more you become demanding in fineness.
[Contains English characters] Alastair Clarke explains: The theory is an evolutionary and cognitive explanation of how and why any individual finds anything funny.
[Contains English characters] Effectively, it explains that humour occurs when the brain recognizes a pattern that surprises it, and that recognition of this sort is rewarded with the experience of the humorous response, an element of which is broadcast as laughter.
[Contains English characters] The theory further identifies the importance of pattern recognition in human evolution: An ability to recognize patterns instantly and unconsciously has proved a fundamental weapon in the cognitive arsenal of human beings.
[Contains English characters] The humorous reward has encouraged the development of such faculties, leading to the unique perceptual and intellectual abilities of our species.

[Contains English characters] References When using inline citations, it is important to maintain text-source integrity.
[Contains English characters] The point of an inline citation is to allow readers and other editors to check that the material is sourced; that point is lost if the citation is not clearly placed.
[Contains English characters] The distance between material and its source is a matter of editorial judgment, but adding text without placing its source clearly can lead to allegations of original research, violations of the sourcing policy, and even plagiarism.
[Contains English characters] Editors should exercise caution when rearranging or inserting material to ensure that text-source relationships are maintained.
[Contains English characters] The following inline citation, for example, is not helpful, because the reader does not know whether each source supports the material; each source supports part of it; or just one source supports it with the others added as further reading: N Delia Smith is the UKs best-selling cookery writer.
[Contains English characters] Where you are using multiple sources for one sentence, consider bundling citations at the end of the sentence or paragraph with an explanation in the footnote regarding which source supports which point; see below for how to do that.
[Contains English characters] You can combine or bundle citations between one set of ref tags at the end of a sentence or paragraph, along with an explanation in the footnote for which source supports which part of the text.
[Contains English characters] Citation bundling can be done with long or short footnotes, with or without citation templates.
[Contains English characters] It has multiple benefits: A simple example of citation bundling: The sun is pretty big, but the moon is not so big.
[Contains English characters] Notes In-text attribution is the attribution inside a sentence of material to its source, in addition to an inline citation after the sentence.
[Contains English characters] In-text attribution should be used with direct speech ; indirect speech ; and close paraphrasing.
[Contains English characters] It can also be used when loosely summarizing a sources position in your own words.
[Contains English characters] It avoids inadvertent plagiarism, and helps the reader see where a position is coming from.
[Contains English characters] An inline citation should follow the attribution, usually at the end of the sentence or paragraph in question.
[Contains English characters] For example: Y John Rawls argues that, to reach fair decisions, parties must consider matters as if behind a veil of ignorance.
[Contains English characters] When using in-text attribution, make sure it doesnt lead to an inadvertent neutrality violation.
[Contains English characters] For example, the following implies parity between the sources, without making clear that the position of Dawkins is the majority view: N Richard Dawkins argues that human beings evolved through natural selection, but John Smith writes that we arrived here in pods from Mars.
[Contains English characters] Neutrality issues apart, there are other ways in-text attribution can mislead.
[Contains English characters] The sentence below suggests The New York Times has alone made this important discovery: N According to The New York Times, the sun will set in the west this evening.
[Contains English characters] Simple facts such as this can have inline citations to reliable sources as an aid to the reader, but normally the text itself is best left as a plain statement without in-text attribution: YBy mass, oxygen is the third most abundant element in the universe after hydrogen and helium.
[Contains English characters] If an article is unreferenced you can tag it with the template Unreferenced, so long as it is not nonsensical or a biography of a living person, in which case request admin assistance.
[Contains English characters] Dont cite a source unless youve seen it for yourself.
[Contains English characters] Where you want to cite John Smith, but youve only read Paul Jones who cites Smith, write it like this : If you first learned of John Smiths book because it was cited in Paul Jones encyclopedia, but you then actually obtained and read John Smiths book, it is not necessary to give credit to any sources, search engines, library catalogs, etc.
[Contains English characters] , that led you to Smiths book.
[Contains English characters] You may cite Smiths book directly and solely in that instance.
[Contains English characters] For a source available in hardcopy, microform, and/or online, omit, in most cases, which one you read.
[Contains English characters] While it is useful to cite author, title, edition, and similar information, it generally is not important to cite a database such as ProQuest, EbscoHost, or JStor or to link to such a database requiring a subscription or a third partys login.
[Contains English characters] The basic bibliographic information you provide should be enough to search for the source in any of these databases that have the source.
[Contains English characters] Dont add a URL that has a part of a password embedded in the URL.
[Contains English characters] However, you may provide the DOI, ISBN, or another uniform identifier, if available.
[Contains English characters] If the publisher offers a link to the source or its abstract that does not require a payment or a third partys login for access, you may provide the URL for that link.
[Contains English characters] And if the source exists only online, give the link even if access is restricted.
[Contains English characters] Because this is the English Wikipedia, English-language sources should be used in preference to non-English language sources of equal caliber and content, though the latter are allowed where appropriate.
[Contains English characters] When quoting a source in a different language, please provide both the original-language quotation and an English translation, in the text, in a footnote, or on the talk page as appropriate, so long as the quotation is not so lengthy that it would violate copyright.
[Contains English characters] A convenience link is a link to a copy of your source on a webpage provided by someone other than the original publisher or author.
[Contains English characters] For example, a copy of a newspaper article no longer available on the newspapers website may be hosted elsewhere.
[Contains English characters] When offering convenience links, it is important to be reasonably certain that the convenience copy is a true copy of the original, without any changes or inappropriate commentary, and that it does not infringe the original publishers copyright.
[Contains English characters] Accuracy can be assumed when the hosting website appears reliable.
[Contains English characters] Where several sites host a copy of the material, the site selected as the convenience link should be the one whose general content appears most in line with Wikipedia:Neutral point of view and Wikipedia:Verifiability.
[Contains English characters] Multimedia material should be referenced just like article text.
[Contains English characters] Citations for a media file should appear on its file page.
[Contains English characters] Image captions should be referenced as appropriate just like any other part of the article.
[Contains English characters] If an infobox or table contains text that needs citing, but the box or table cannot incorporate an inline citation, the citation should appear in a caption or other text that discusses the material.
[Contains English characters] A citation is not needed for descriptions such as alt text that are verifiable directly from the image itself.

[Contains English characters] Scrolling lists, or lists of citations appearing within a scroll box, should never be used because of issues with readability, accessibility, printing, and site mirroring.
[Contains English characters] Additionally, it cannot be guaranteed that such lists will display properly in all web browsers.
[Contains English characters] See this July 2007 discussion for more detail.
[Contains English characters] A general reference is a citation to a reliable source that supports content, but is not displayed as an inline citation.
[Contains English characters] General references are usually listed at the end of the article in a References section.
[Contains English characters] They may be found in underdeveloped articles, especially when all article content is supported by a single source.
[Contains English characters] The disadvantage of using general references is that text-source integrity is lost, unless the article is very short.
[Contains English characters] The sourcing policy, Verifiability, requires inline citations for all quotations, and for anything challenged or likely to be challenged.
[Contains English characters] A general reference looks like this in the edit box: The Sun is pretty big, but the Moon is not so big.
[Contains English characters] This is how it looks in the article: The Sun is pretty big, but the Moon is not so big.
[Contains English characters] References Embedded links to external websites should not be used as a form of inline citation, because they are highly susceptible to linkrot.
[Contains English characters] Wikipedia allowed this in its early years—for example by adding a link after a sentence, like this, which looks like this.
[Contains English characters] This is no longer recommended.
[Contains English characters] Raw links are not recommended in lieu of properly written out citations, even if placed between ref tags, like this .
[Contains English characters] Embedded links should never be used to place external links in the body of an article, like this: Apple, Inc.
[Contains English characters] announced their latest product. . . Further reading or External links are used as section headings for books, articles, and websites related to the topic that have not been used as sources.
[Contains English characters] There are a number of citation styles.
[Contains English characters] See here for some examples.
[Contains English characters] They all include the same information, but vary in punctuation and the order of the authors name, publication date, title, and page numbers.
[Contains English characters] All of the citations within each Wikipedia article should follow a consistent style.
[Contains English characters] The citation style chosen for one article does not have to match the citation style chosen for another article, but within each article, the style used should be consistent.
[Contains English characters] If the article you are editing is already using a particular citation style, you should follow that style.
[Contains English characters] Do not change the citation style used in an article merely for personal preference or cosmetic reasons.
[Contains English characters] If you think the existing citation system is inappropriate for the specific needs of the article, gain consensus for a change on the talk page before changing it.
[Contains English characters] As with issues of spelling differences, if there is disagreement about which style is best, defer to the style used by the first major contributor.
[Contains English characters] If you are the first major contributor to an article, you may choose whichever style you think best for the article.
[Contains English characters] Citations for books typically include: Citations for journal articles typically incतिरपी मुद्राक्षरेlude: Citations for newspaper articles typically include: Citations for World Wide Web pages typically include: When citing lengthy sources, you should identify which part of a source is being cited.
[Contains English characters] For example, in the case of a book, specify the page number.
[Contains English characters] Page numbers are not required for a reference to the book as a whole.
[Contains English characters] When you specify a page number, it is helpful to specify the version of the source because the layout, pagination, length, etc.
[Contains English characters] can change between editions.
[Contains English characters] A citation ideally includes a link or ID number to help editors locate the source.
[Contains English characters] If you have a URL link, you can add it to the title part of the citation, so that when you add the citation to Wikipedia the URL becomes hidden and the title becomes clickable.
[Contains English characters] To do this, enclose the URL and the title in square brackets—the URL first, then a space, then the title.
[Contains English characters] For example: Carr A, Ory D .
[Contains English characters] PLoS Medicine, 3:e496. For web-only sources with no publication date you should include a Retrieved date instead, in case the webpage changes in the future.
[Contains English characters] For example: Retrieved 2008-07-15. You can also add an ID number to the end of a citation.
[Contains English characters] The ID number might be an ISBN for a book, a DOI for an article, or any of several ID numbers that are specific to particular article databases, such as a PMID number for articles on PubMed.
[Contains English characters] It may be possible to format these so that they are automatically activated and become clickable when added to Wikipedia, for example by typing ISBN following by a space followed by the ID number.
[Contains English characters] If your source is not available online, it should be available in reputable libraries, archives, or collections.
[Contains English characters] If a citation without an external link is challenged as unavailable, any of the following is sufficient to show the material to be reasonably available : providing an ISBN or OCLC number; linking to an established Wikipedia article about the source ; or directly quoting the material on the talk page, briefly and in context.
[Contains English characters] Citation templates are used to format citations in a consistent way.
[Contains English characters] The use of citation templates is neither encouraged nor discouraged.
[Contains English characters] Templates may be used or removed at the discretion of individual editors, subject to agreement with other editors on the article.
[Contains English characters] Because templates can be contentious, editors should not change an article with a distinctive citation format to another without gaining consensus.
[Contains English characters] Where no agreement can be reached, defer to the style used by the first major contributor.
[Contains English characters] Citations may be accompanied by metadata, though it is not mandatory.
[Contains English characters] Most citation templates on Wikipedia use the COinS microformat.
[Contains English characters] Metadata such as this allow browser plugins and other automated software to make citation data accessible to the user, for instance by providing links to their librarys online copies of the cited works.
[Contains English characters] In articles that format citations manually, metadata may be added manually in a span, according to the COinS specification; or the templates Template:Citation metadata or Template:COinS can be used.
[Contains English characters] You can insert a link beside each citation in Wikipedia, allowing you to export the citation to a reference manager, such as EndNote.
[Contains English characters] Just copy this code: to the end of Special:MyPage/monobook. js. Then, save the page and bypass your browsers cache.
[Contains English characters] To help prevent dead links, persistent identifiers are available for some sources.
[Contains English characters] Some journal articles have a digital object identifier ; some online newspapers and blogs, and also Wikipedia, have permalinks that are stable.
[Contains English characters] When permanent links arent available, consider archiving the referenced document when writing the article; on-demand web archiving services such as WebCite are fairly easy to use .
[Contains English characters] Dead links should be repaired or replaced if possible.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Intro-tooshortसाचा:Redirect6 साचा:Wiktionarypar2 The term multilingual can refer to an individual speaker who uses two or more languages, a community of speakers in which two or more languages are used, or speakers of different languages.
[Contains English characters] Multilingual speakers outnumber monolingual speakers in the worlds population.
[Contains English characters] A multilingual person, in a broad definition, is one who can communicate in more than one language, be it actively or passively .
[Contains English characters] More specifically, the terms bilingual and trilingual are used to describe comparable situations in which two or three languages are involved.
[Contains English characters] A generic term for multilingual persons is polyglot.
[Contains English characters] Multilingual speakers have acquired and maintained at least one language during childhood, the so-called first language .
[Contains English characters] The first language is acquired without formal education, by mechanisms heavily disputed.
[Contains English characters] Children acquiring two languages in this way are called simultaneous bilinguals.
[Contains English characters] Even in the case of simultaneous bilinguals one language usually dominates over the other.
[Contains English characters] This kind of bilingualism is most likely to occur when a child is raised by bilingual parents in a predominantly monolingual environment.
[Contains English characters] It can also occur when the parents are monolingual but have raised their child or children in two different countries.
[Contains English characters] One group of academicsसाचा:Fact argues for the maximal definition which means speakers are as proficient in one language as they are in others and have as much knowledge of and control over one language as they have of the others.
[Contains English characters] Another group of academics argues for the minimal definition, based on use.
[Contains English characters] Tourists, who successfully communicate phrases and ideas while not fluent in a language, may be seen as bilingual according to this group.
[Contains English characters] However, problems may arise with these definitions as they do not specify how much knowledge of a language is required to be classified as bilingual.
[Contains English characters] As a result, since most speakers do not achieve the maximal ideal, language learners may come to be seen as deficient and by extension, language teaching may come to be seen as a failure.
[Contains English characters] One does not expect children to speak chemistry or to have become a professional athlete by the time they have left school, yet for graduating school children anything less than fluency in a second language could be seen as inadequateसाचा:Fact.
[Contains English characters] Since 1992, Cook has argued that most multilingual speakers fall somewhere between minimal and maximal definitions.
[Contains English characters] Cook calls these people multi-competent.
[Contains English characters] A broadly held, yet nearly as broadly criticisedसाचा:Fact, view is that of the United States linguist Noam Chomsky in what he calls the human language acquisition device — a mechanism which enables an individual to recreate correctly the rules and certain other characteristics of language used by speakers around the learner.
[Contains English characters] This device, according to Chomsky, wears out over time, and is not normally available by puberty, which he uses to explain the poor results some adolescents and adults have when learning aspects of a second language .
[Contains English characters] If language learning is a cognitive process, rather than a language acquisition device, as the school led by Stephen Krashen suggests, there would only be relative, not categorical, differences between the two types of language learning.
[Contains English characters] Despite the differences in theories, most studies agree that the earlier children learn a second language, the better off they are, cognitively speaking at least.
[Contains English characters] These studies could be used to make the learning of a second language mandatory in all schools as early as possible, in order to give children every means of increasing their cognitive abilities.
[Contains English characters] Many European schools offer secondary language classes for their students, if for no other reason than the proximity of other countries with different languages.
[Contains English characters] The United States, however, in spite of its proximity to francophone Quebec and hispanophone Mexico, is the only technologically advanced country that does not require the study of a foreign language in its schools.
[Contains English characters] Even if someone is highly proficient in two or more languages, his or her so-called communicative competence or ability may not be as balanced.
[Contains English characters] Linguists have distinguished various types of multilingual competence, which can roughly be put into two categories: The distinction between compound and coordinate bilingualism has come under scrutiny.
[Contains English characters] When studies are done of multilinguals, most are found to show behavior intermediate between compound and coordinate bilingualism.
[Contains English characters] Some authors have suggested that the distinction should only be made at the level of grammar rather than vocabulary, others use coordinate bilingual as a synonym for one who has learned two languages from birth, and others have proposed dropping the distinction altogether .
[Contains English characters] Many theorists are now beginning to view bilingualism as a spectrum or continuum of bilingualism that runs from the relatively monolingual language learner to highly proficient bilingual speakers who function at high levels in both languages .
[Contains English characters] Those bilinguals who are highly proficient in two or more languages, such as compound and coordinate bilinguals, are reported to have a higher cognitive proficiency, and are found to be better language learners at a later age, than monolinguals.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact The early discovery that concepts of the world can be labelled in more than one fashion puts those bilinguals in the lead.
[Contains English characters] There is, however, also a phenomenon known as distractive bilingualism or semilingualism.
[Contains English characters] When acquisition of the first language is interrupted and insufficient or unstructured language input follows from the second language, as sometimes happens with immigrant children, the speaker can end up with two languages both mastered below the monolingual standard.
[Contains English characters] The vast majority of immigrant children, however, acquire both languages normallyसाचा:Fact.
[Contains English characters] In Japan, it has been found that a large number of older immigrant children, whose parents have come from other Asian nations or South America to work in Japanese factories and whose first language is seen by society at large as less prestigious than Japanese, were able to communicate with other children in the school grounds but were unable to master the language necessary for learning in the school system.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact As a result, thousands of these children have dropped out of the school system, without mastering either their first or second language.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact While community activists have long called for government help, only in the past few years has the Japanese Ministry of Education slowly begun to study this issue.
[Contains English characters] Literacy plays an important role in the development of language in these immigrant children.
[Contains English characters] Those who were literate in their first language before arriving in Japan, and who have support to maintain that literacy, are at the very least able to maintain and master their first language.
[Contains English characters] The neuroscientist Katrin Amunts studied the brain of Emil Krebs and determined that the area of Krebs brain responsible for language — Brocas area — was organized differently from monolingual men.
[Contains English characters] Receptive bilinguals are those who have the ability to understand a language, but do not speak it.
[Contains English characters] Receptive bilingualism may occur when a child realizes that the community language is more prestigious than the language spoken within the household and chooses to speak to their parents in the community language only.
[Contains English characters] Families who adopt this mode of communication can be highly functional, although they may not be seen as bilingual.
[Contains English characters] Receptive bilinguals may rapidly achieve oral fluency when placed in situations where they are required to speak the heritage language.
[Contains English characters] Receptive bilingualism is not the same as mutual intelligibility, which is the case of a native Spanish speaker who is able to understand Portuguese, or vice versa, due to the high lexical and grammatical similarities between Spanish and Portuguese .
[Contains English characters] A person who speaks several languages is called a polyglot.
[Contains English characters] The following claimed to speak ten or more languages: There is no clear definition of what it means to speak a language.
[Contains English characters] A tourist who can handle a simple conversation with a waiter may be completely lost when it comes to discussing current affairs or even using multiple tenses.
[Contains English characters] A diplomat or businessman who can handle complicated negotiations in a foreign language may not be able to write a simple letter correctly.
[Contains English characters] A four-year-old French child would usually be said to speak French fluently, but it is possible that he cannot handle the grammar as well as even some mediocre foreign students of the language do and may have a very limited vocabulary despite possibly having perfect pronunciation.
[Contains English characters] In addition there is no clear definition of what one language means.
[Contains English characters] For instance the Scandinavian languages are so similar that many of the native speakers understand all of them without much troubleसाचा:Fact.
[Contains English characters] This means that a speaker of Danish, Norwegian or Swedish can easily get his count up to 3 languages.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, the differences between variants of Chinese, like Cantonese and Mandarin, are so big that intensive studies are needed for a speaker of one of them to learn and even to understand a different one correctly.
[Contains English characters] A person who has learned to speak five Chinese dialects perfectly is quite accomplishedसाचा:Weasel-inline, but his count would still be only one language, and some would argue that the differences between these dialects are greater than the differences between many European Romance languages.
[Contains English characters] As another example, a person who has learned five different languages such as French, Spanish, Catalan, Italian and Portuguese, all belonging to the closely related group of Romance languages, has accomplished something less difficult than a person who has learnt Hebrew, Standard Mandarin, Finnish, Navajo and Welsh, of which none is remotely related to another.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, what is considered a language can change, often for purely political purposes, such as when Serbo-Croatian was assembled from Serbian and Croatian and later split after Yugoslavia broke up, or when Ukrainian was dismissed as a Russian dialect by the Russian tsars to discourage national feelings.
[Contains English characters] साचा:FixBunchingसाचा:FixBunching साचा:FixBunchingसाचा:FixBunching साचा:FixBunchingसाचा:FixBunching साचा:FixBunchingसाचा:FixBunchingसाचा:FixBunching Widespread multilingualism is one form of language contact.
[Contains English characters] Multilingualism was more common in the past than is usually supposedसाचा:Weasel-inline: in early times, when most people were members of small language communities, it was necessary to know two or more languages for trade or any other dealings outside ones own town or village, and this holds good today in places of high linguistic diversity such as Sub-Saharan Africa and India.
[Contains English characters] Linguist Ekkehard Wolff estimates that 50% of the population of Africa is multilingual.
[Contains English characters] In multilingual societies, not all speakers need to be multilingual.
[Contains English characters] Some states can have multilingual policies and recognise several official languages, such as Canada .
[Contains English characters] In some states, particular languages may be associated with particular regions in the state or with particular ethnicities .
[Contains English characters] When all speakers are multilingual, linguists classify the community according to the functional distribution of the languages involved: Whenever two people meet, negotiations take place.
[Contains English characters] If they want to express solidarity and sympathy, they tend to seek common features in their behavior.
[Contains English characters] If speakers wish to express distance towards or even dislike of the person they are speaking to, the reverse is true, and differences are sought.
[Contains English characters] This mechanism also extends to language, as has been described by Howard Giles Accommodation Theory.
[Contains English characters] Some multilinguals use code-switching, a term that describes the process of swapping between languages.
[Contains English characters] In many cases, code-switching is motivated by the wish to express loyalty to more than one cultural groupसाचा:Fact, as holds for many immigrant communities in the New World.
[Contains English characters] Code-switching may also function as a strategy where proficiency is lacking.
[Contains English characters] Such strategies are common if the vocabulary of one of the languages is not very elaborated for certain fields, or if the speakers have not developed proficiency in certain lexical domains, as in the case of immigrant languages.
[Contains English characters] This code-switching appears in many forms.
[Contains English characters] If a speaker has a positive attitude towards both languages and towards code-switching, many switches can be found, even within the same sentence.
[Contains English characters] If, however, the speaker is reluctant to use code-switching, as in the case of a lack of proficiency, he might knowingly or unknowingly try to camouflage his attempt by converting elements of one language into elements of the other language.
[Contains English characters] This results in speakers using words like courrier noir in French, instead of the proper word for blackmail, chantage.
[Contains English characters] Bilingual interaction can even take place without the speakers switching.
[Contains English characters] In certain areas, it is not uncommon for speakers each to use a different language within the same conversation.
[Contains English characters] This phenomenon is found, amongst other places, in Scandinavia.
[Contains English characters] Speakers of Swedish and Norwegian can easily communicate with each other speaking their respective languages.
[Contains English characters] It is usually called non-convergent discourse, a term introduced by the Dutch linguist Reitze Jonkman.
[Contains English characters] This phenomenon is also found in Argentina, where Spanish and Italian are both widely spoken, even leading to cases where a child with a Spanish and an Italian parent grows up fully bilingual, with both parents speaking only their own language yet knowing the other.
[Contains English characters] Another example is the former state of Czechoslovakia, where two languages were in common use.
[Contains English characters] Most Czechs and Slovaks understand both languages, although they would use only one of them when speaking.
[Contains English characters] For example, in Czechoslovakia it was common to hear two people talking on television each speaking a different language without any difficulty understanding each other.
[Contains English characters] Another example would be a Slovak having read a book in Czech and afterwards being unsure whether he was reading it in Czech or Slovak.
[Contains English characters] This bilinguality still exists nowadays, although it has started to deteriorate after Czechoslovakia split up साचा:Fact.
[Contains English characters] Sociopolitical as well as socio-cultural identity arguments may influence native language literacy.
[Contains English characters] While these two camps may occupy much of the debate about which languages children will learn to read, a greater emphasis on the linguistic aspects of the argument is appropriate.
[Contains English characters] In spite of the political turmoil precipitated by this debate, researchers continue to espouse a linguistic basis for it.
[Contains English characters] This rationale is based upon the work of Jim Cummins .
[Contains English characters] In this model, learners receive literacy instruction in their native language until they acquire a threshold literacy proficiency.
[Contains English characters] Some researchers use age 3 as the age when a child has basic communicative competence in L1 .
[Contains English characters] Children may go through a process of sequential acquisition if they migrate at a young age to a country where a different language is spoken, or if the child exclusively speaks his or her heritage language at home until he/she is immersed in a school setting where instruction is offered in a different language.
[Contains English characters] The phases children go through during sequential acquisition are less linear than for simultaneous acquisition and can vary greatly among children.
[Contains English characters] Sequential acquisition is a more complex and lengthier process, although there is no indication that non language-delayed children end up less proficient than simultaneous bilinguals, so long as they receive adequate input in both languages.
[Contains English characters] In this model, the native language and the community language are simultaneously taught.
[Contains English characters] The advantage is literacy in two languages as the outcome.
[Contains English characters] However, the teacher must be well-versed in both languages and also in techniques for teaching a second language.
[Contains English characters] This model posits that equal time should be spent in separate instruction of the native language and of the community language.
[Contains English characters] The native language class, however, focuses on basic literacy while the community language class focuses on listening and speaking skills.
[Contains English characters] Being a bilingual does not necessarily mean that one can speak, for example, English and French.
[Contains English characters] Cummins research concluded that the development of competence in the native language serves as a foundation of proficiency that can be transposed to the second language — the common underlying proficiency hypothesis.
[Contains English characters] His work sought to overcome the perception propagated in the 1960s that learning two languages made for two competing aims.
[Contains English characters] The belief was that the two languages were mutually exclusive and that learning a second required unlearning elements and dynamics of the first in order to accommodate the second .
[Contains English characters] The evidence for this perspective relied on the fact that some errors in acquiring the second language were related to the rules of the first language .
[Contains English characters] How this hypothesis holds under different types of languages such as Romance versus non-Western languages has yet to undergo research.
[Contains English characters] Another new development that has influenced the linguistic argument for bilingual literacy is the length of time necessary to acquire the second language.
[Contains English characters] While previously children were believed to have the ability to learn a language within a year, today researchers believe that within and across academic settings, the time span is nearer to five years .
[Contains English characters] An interesting outcome of studies during the early 1990s however confirmed that students who do successfully complete bilingual instruction perform better academically .

[Contains English characters] साचा:Morefootnotes Interpersonal attraction is the attraction between people which leads to friendships and romantic relationships.
[Contains English characters] The study of interpersonal attraction is a major area of research in social psychology.
[Contains English characters] Interpersonal attraction is related to how much we like, love, dislike, or hate someone.
[Contains English characters] It can be viewed as a force acting between two people that tends to draw them together and resist their separation.
[Contains English characters] When measuring interpersonal attraction, one must refer to the qualities of the attracted as well as the qualities of the attractor to achieve predictive accuracy.
[Contains English characters] It is suggested that to determine attraction, personality and situation must be taken into account.
[Contains English characters] Repulsion is also a factor in the process of interpersonal attraction, ones conception of attraction to another can vary from extreme attraction to extreme repulsion.
[Contains English characters] Many factors leading to interpersonal attraction have been studied.
[Contains English characters] The most frequently studied are:physical attractiveness, propinquity, familiarity, similarity, complementarity, reciprocal liking, and reinforcement.
[Contains English characters] According to Rowland Millers Intimate Relationships text, the propinquity effect can be defined as: the more we see and interact with a person, the more likely he or she is to become our friend or intimate partner.
[Contains English characters] This effect is very similar to the mere exposure effect in that the more a person is exposed to a stimulus, the more the person likes it; however, there are a few exceptions to the mere exposure effect.
[Contains English characters] As mentioned above, the mere exposure effect, also known as the familiarity principle, states that the more we are exposed to something, the more we come to like it.
[Contains English characters] This applies equally to both objects and people .
[Contains English characters] The social allergy effect occurs when a persons annoying habits grow worse over time, instead of growing more fond of his or her idiosyncrasies.
[Contains English characters] The notion of “birds of a feather flock together” points out that similarity is a crucial determinant of interpersonal attraction.
[Contains English characters] According to Morry’s attraction-similarity model, there is a lay belief that people with actual similarity produce initial attraction.
[Contains English characters] Perceived similarity develops for someone to rate others as similar to themselves in on-going relationship.
[Contains English characters] Such perception is either self-serving or relationship-serving .
[Contains English characters] Newcomb pointed out that people tend to change perceived similarity to obtain balance in a relationship.
[Contains English characters] Additionally, perceived similarity was found to be greater than actual similarity in predicting interpersonal attraction.
[Contains English characters] Findings suggest that interpersonal similarity and attraction are multidimensional constructs, in which people are attracted to others who are similar to them in demographics, physical appearance, attitudes, interpersonal style, social and cultural background, personality, interests and activities preferences, and communication and social skills.
[Contains English characters] A study conducted by Theodore Newcomb on college dorm roommates suggested that individuals with shared backgrounds, academic achievements, attitudes, values, and political views became friends.
[Contains English characters] Social homogamy refers to “passive, indirect effects on spousal similarity” .
[Contains English characters] The result showed that age and education level are crucial in affecting the mate preference.
[Contains English characters] Because people with similar age study and interact more in the same form of the school, propinquity effect plays a significant impact in spousal similarity.
[Contains English characters] Convergence refers to an increasing similarity with time.
[Contains English characters] Although the previous research showed that there is a greater effect on attitude and value than on personality traits, however, it is found that initial assortment, rather than convergence, plays a crucial role in explaining spousal similarity.
[Contains English characters] Active assortment refers to direct effects on choosing someone similar as self in mating preferences.
[Contains English characters] The data showed that there is a greater effect on political and religious attitudes than on personality traits.
[Contains English characters] A follow-up issue on the reason of the finding was raised.
[Contains English characters] The concepts of idiosyncratic and consensual in mate preference.
[Contains English characters] The data showed that mate preference on political and religious tend to be idiosyncratic, for example, A Catholic prefers to choose the one who is a Catholic, rather than a Buddhist.
[Contains English characters] Such idiosyncratic preference produces high level of active assortment which plays a vital role in affecting spousal similarity.
[Contains English characters] In summary, active assortment is the most powerful in explaining spousal similarity, whereas convergence has little evidence on showing such effect.
[Contains English characters] Similarity has effects on starting a relationship by initial attraction to know each other.
[Contains English characters] It is showed that high attitude similarity resulted in a significant increase in initial attraction to the target person and high attitude dissimilarity resulted in a decrease of initial attraction .
[Contains English characters] Besides, similarity also promotes relationship commitment.
[Contains English characters] Study on heterosexual dating couples found that similarity in intrinsic values of the couple was linked to relationship commitment and stability .
[Contains English characters] The model of complementarity explains whether birds of a feather flock together or opposites attract.
[Contains English characters] Studies show that complementary interaction between two partners increases their attractiveness to each other .
[Contains English characters] Complementary partners preferred closer interpersonal relationship than non-complementary ones .
[Contains English characters] Couples who reported the highest level of loving and harmonious relationship were more dissimilar in dominance than couples who scored lower in relationship quality. . Mathes and Moore found that people were more attracted to peers approximating to their ideal self than to those who did not.
[Contains English characters] Specifically, low self-esteem individuals appeared more likely to desire a complementary relationship than high self-esteem people.
[Contains English characters] We are attracted to people who complement to us because this allows us to maintain our preferred style of behavior, and through interaction with someone who complements our own behavior, we are likely to have a sense of self-validation and security .
[Contains English characters] Principles of similarity and complementarity seem to be contradictory on the surface .
[Contains English characters] In fact, they agree on the dimension of warmth.
[Contains English characters] Both principles state that friendly people would prefer friendly partners.
[Contains English characters] The importance of similarity and complementarity may depend on the stage of the relationship.
[Contains English characters] Similarity seems to carry considerable weight in initial attraction, while complementarity assumes importance as the relationship develops over time .
[Contains English characters] Markey found that people would be more satisfied with their relationship if their partners differed from them, at least, in terms of dominance, as two dominant persons may experience conflicts while two submissive individuals may have frustration as neither member take the initiative.
[Contains English characters] Perception and actual behavior might not be congruent with each other.
[Contains English characters] There were cases that dominant people perceived their partners to be similarly dominant, yet in the eyes of independent observers, the actual behavior of their partner was submissive, in other words, complementary to them .
[Contains English characters] Why do people perceive their romantic partners to be similar to them despite evidence to the contrary?
[Contains English characters] The reason remains unclear, pending further research.
[Contains English characters] Peoples feelings toward a potential partner are dependent on their perception of rewards and costs, the kind of relationships they deserve, and their likelihood for having a healthier relationship with someone else.
[Contains English characters] Rewards are the part of a relationship that makes it worthwhile and enjoyable.
[Contains English characters] A cost is something that can cause irritation like a friend overstaying his welcome.
[Contains English characters] Comparison level is also taken into account during a relationship.
[Contains English characters] This suggests that people expect rewards or costs depending on the time invested in the relationship.
[Contains English characters] If the level of expected rewards are minimal and the level of costs is high, the relationship suffers and both parties may become dissatisfied and unhappy.
[Contains English characters] Lastly, the comparison of alternatives means that satisfaction is conditional on the chance that a person could replace the relationship with a more desirable one.
[Contains English characters] Warren Kubitschek and Maureen Hallinan, University of Notre Dame, social psychologists who suggested that attraction is the result of the propinquity and similarity effects and the status of each party involved.
[Contains English characters] Their study was about the tracking program that organizes students according to their level of ability to learn.
[Contains English characters] This is mostly implemented in middle and almost all of high school.
[Contains English characters] Their goal is to prove that students on the same track have a higher probability of becoming friends compared to those in different tracks.
[Contains English characters] Other organizational based groupings should also follow these factors.
[Contains English characters] The propinquity effect creates an ideal environment where students are in close physical proximity with each other and have the chance to build familiarity that leads to friendship.
[Contains English characters] Similarity in tracking students is important because they found that track students tend to become friends with others who have the same academic achievement and expectations as themselves.
[Contains English characters] They also found that students on the same level of status concerning grades will likely name them than those who are on lower level than their own.
[Contains English characters] They conclude that although the factors mentioned do have great influence on friendship, they are not exclusive for organized program like tracking.
[Contains English characters] The triangular theory of loveby Robert Sternberg is based on intimacy, passion, and commitment.
[Contains English characters] The strongest type of love, consummate love, consists of these three aspects.
[Contains English characters] The idea of this theory is that love can consist of one component alone or any combination of the three parts: intimacy, passion, and commitment.
[Contains English characters] There are many factors taken into account when a relationship turns into love.
[Contains English characters] One big factor is culture.
[Contains English characters] This is a common issue among two people who come from very different cultural backgrounds.
[Contains English characters] In a study done by Phillip Shavers and his colleagues, they interviewed participants from different parts of the world and found that love has similar and different meanings cross-culturally.
[Contains English characters] The Chinese participants had several different love concepts such as sorrow-love,tenderness-pity, and sorrow-pity.
[Contains English characters] This ties into another study done by Rothbaym and his partner Tsang in 1998 in which they researched popular love songs from American and Chinese artists.
[Contains English characters] The difference was that the Chinese love songs had significantly more references to suffering and to negative outcomes than the American love songs.
[Contains English characters] This may be due to beliefs that interpersonal relationships are predestined, and thus have no control over love lives.
[Contains English characters] The evolutionary theory of human interpersonal attraction states that opposite-sex attraction most often occurs when someone has physical features indicating that he or she is very fertile.
[Contains English characters] Considering that the primary purpose of conjugal/romantic relationships is reproduction, it would follow that people invest in partners who appear very fertile, increasing the chance of their genes being passed down to the next generation.
[Contains English characters] This theory has been criticized because it does not explain relationships between same-sex couples or couples who do not want children, although this may have something to do with the fact that whether one wants children or not one is still subject to the evolutionary forces which produce them.
[Contains English characters] Another evolutionary explanation suggests that fertility in a mate is of greater importance to men than to women.
[Contains English characters] According to this theory, a woman places significant emphasis on a mans ability to provide resources and protection.
[Contains English characters] The theory suggests that these resources and protection are important in ensuring the successful raising of the womans offspring.
[Contains English characters] The ability to provide resources and protection might also be sought because the underlying traits are likely to be passed on to male offspring.
[Contains English characters] Critics of this theory point out that most genes are autosomal and non-sex-linked Evolutionary theory also suggests that people whose physical features suggest they are healthy are seen as more attractive.
[Contains English characters] The theory suggests that a healthy mate is more likely to possess genetic traits related to health that would be passed on to offspring.
[Contains English characters] Peoples tendency to consider people with facial symmetry more attractive than those with less symmetrical faces is one example.
[Contains English characters] However, a test was conducted that found that perfectly symmetrical faces were less attractive than normal faces.
[Contains English characters] It has also been suggested that people are attracted to faces similar to their own.
[Contains English characters] Case studies have revealed that when a photograph of a woman was superimposed to include the features of a mans face, the man whose face was superimposed almost always rated that picture the most attractive.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact This theory is based upon the notion that we want to replicate our own features in the next generation, as we have survived thus far with such features and have instinctive survival wishes for our children.
[Contains English characters] Another explanation given for the results of that study was that the man whose face was superimposed may have consciously or subconsciously associated the photographically altered female face with the face of his mother or other family member.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact A 2009 study by Melissa Burkley and Jessica Parker of Oklahoma State University found that 59% of women stated they were interested in pursuing a relationship when presented with a hypothetical ideal single man.
[Contains English characters] However, when instead told that the man was already in a romantic relationship, 90% of the women stated they were interested in pursuing a romantic relationship.
[Contains English characters] Breaking up is the ending of a relationship whether its a friendship or romantic relationship.
[Contains English characters] There are several reasons that a relationship may come to an end.
[Contains English characters] One reason derives from the equity theory .
[Contains English characters] If a person in the relationship feels that the personal costs of being in the relationship outweigh the rewards there is a strong chance that he/she will end the relationship.
[Contains English characters] This also may go for the rewards outweighing costs in some cases.

[Contains English characters] A Sadya is traditionally a vegetarian meal served on a plantain or banana leaf; people eat sitting cross-legged on the floor.
[Contains English characters] Sadhya can have up to 24 dishes served in it.
[Contains English characters] The dishes are plain boiled rice, many curries, papadum, plain yogurt or buttermilk, banana or plantain chips, and two or more sweet dishes.
[Contains English characters] The curries are made of different vegetables and have different flavourings.
[Contains English characters] They can be made of yogurt, bitter gourd, mango, jaggery, etc.
[Contains English characters] The reason for including so many dishes in the Sadya is to ensure that the diners will like at least two or three dishes.
[Contains English characters] Coconut, being abundant in Kerala, is used in almost all dishes.
[Contains English characters] Coconut milk also finds various uses in cooking.
[Contains English characters] Coconut oil is used for frying.
[Contains English characters] There is a specific place for each item on the plantain leaf.
[Contains English characters] For example, the pickles are served on the top left corner and banana on the bottom left corner.
[Contains English characters] Thus, the waiters can easily identify the requirement of the diner by just looking at his leaf.

[Contains English characters] Onion and garlic are not typically used in the sadya.
[Contains English characters] The sadya is usually served as lunch.
