[Contains English characters] कारण= दीर्घकाळा अ-भाषांतरीत मजकूर साचा:HTTPIn computing, a cookie स्मृतीशेष is a small piece of text stored on a users computer by a web browser.
[Contains English characters] A cookie consists of one or more name-value pairs containing bits of information such as user preferences, shopping cart contents, the identifier for a server-based session, or other data used by websites.
[Contains English characters] It is sent as an HTTP header by a web server to a web browser and then sent back unchanged by the browser each time it accesses that server.
[Contains English characters] A cookie can be used for authenticating, session tracking, and remembering specific information about users, such as site preferences or the contents of their electronic shopping carts.
[Contains English characters] The term cookie is derived from magic cookie, a well-known concept in UNIX computing which inspired both the idea and the name of browser cookies.
[Contains English characters] Some alternatives to cookies exist; each has its own uses, advantages, and drawbacks.
[Contains English characters] Being simple pieces of text, cookies are not executable.
[Contains English characters] They are neither spyware or viruses, although cookies from certain sites are detected by many anti-spyware products because they can allow users to be tracked when they visit various sites.
[Contains English characters] Most modern browsers allow users to decide whether to accept cookies, and the time frame to keep them, but rejecting cookies makes some websites unusable.
[Contains English characters] For example, shopping carts or login systems implemented using cookies do not work if cookies are disabled.
[Contains English characters] The term cookie derives from magic cookie, which is a packet of data a program receives and sends out again unchanged.
[Contains English characters] Magic cookies were already used in computing when Lou Montulli had the idea of using them in Web communications in June 1994. At the time, he was an employee of Netscape Communications, which was developing an e-commerce application for a customer.
[Contains English characters] Cookies provided a solution to the problem of reliably implementing a virtual shopping cart.
[Contains English characters] Together with John Giannandrea, Montulli wrote the initial Netscape cookie specification the same year.
[Contains English characters] Version 0.9beta of Mosaic Netscape, released on October 13, 1994, supported cookies.
[Contains English characters] The first use of cookies was checking whether visitors to the Netscape website had already visited the site.
[Contains English characters] Montulli applied for a patent for the cookie technology in 1995, and साचा:Cite patent was granted in 1998. Support for cookies was integrated in Internet Explorer in version 2, released in October 1995. The introduction of cookies was not widely known to the public at the time.
[Contains English characters] In particular, cookies were accepted by default, and users were not notified of the presence of cookies.
[Contains English characters] Some people were aware of the existence of cookies as early as the first quarter of 1995, but the general public learned about them after the Financial Times published an article about them on February 12, 1996. In the same year, cookies received lot of media attention, especially because of potential privacy implications.
[Contains English characters] Cookies were discussed in two U. S. Federal Trade Commission hearings in 1996 and 1997. The development of the formal cookie specifications was already ongoing.
[Contains English characters] In particular, the first discussions about a formal specification started in April 1995 on the www-talk mailing list.
[Contains English characters] A special working group within the IETF was formed.
[Contains English characters] Two alternative proposals for introducing state in HTTP transactions had been proposed by Brian Behlendorf and David Kristol respectively, but the group, headed by Kristol himself, soon decided to use the Netscape specification as a starting point.
[Contains English characters] On February 1996, the working group identified third-party cookies as a considerable privacy threat.
[Contains English characters] The specification produced by the group was eventually published as RFC 2109 in February 1997. It specifies that third-party cookies were either not allowed at all, or at least not enabled by default.
[Contains English characters] At this time, advertising companies were already using third-party cookies.
[Contains English characters] The recommendation about third-party cookies of RFC 2109 was not followed by Netscape and Internet Explorer.
[Contains English characters] RFC 2109 was followed by RFC 2965 in October 2000. Cookies may be used to maintain data related to the user during navigation, possibly across multiple visits.
[Contains English characters] Cookies were introduced to provide a way to implement a shopping cart, a virtual device into which a user can store items they want to purchase as they navigate the site.
[Contains English characters] Shopping basket applications today usually store the list of a basket contents in a database on the server side, rather than storing basket items in the cookie itself.
[Contains English characters] A web server typically sends a cookie containing a unique session identifier.
[Contains English characters] The web browser will send back that session identifier with each subsequent request and shopping basket items are stored associated with a unique session identifier.
[Contains English characters] Allowing users to log in to a website is a frequent use of cookies.
[Contains English characters] Typically the web server will first send a cookie containing a unique session identifier.
[Contains English characters] Users then submit their credentials and the web application authenticates the session and allows the user access to services.
[Contains English characters] Cookies may be used to remember the information about the user who has visited a website in order to show relevant content in the future.
[Contains English characters] For example a web server may send a cookie containing the username last used to log in to a web site so that it may be filled in for future visits.
[Contains English characters] Many websites use cookies for personalization based on users preferences.
[Contains English characters] Users select their preferences by entering them in a web form and submitting the form to the server.
[Contains English characters] The server encodes the preferences in a cookie and sends the cookie back to the browser.
[Contains English characters] This way, every time the user accesses a page, the server is also sent the cookie where the preferences are stored, and can personalize the page according to the user preferences.
[Contains English characters] For example, the विकिपीडिया website allows authenticated users to choose the webpage skin they like best; the Google search engine allows users to decide how many search results per page they want to see.
[Contains English characters] Tracking cookies may be used to track internet users web browsing habits.
[Contains English characters] This can also be done in part by using the IP address of the computer requesting the page or the referer field of the HTTP header, but cookies allow for a greater precision.
[Contains English characters] This can be done for example as follows: By looking at the log file, it is then possible to find out which pages the user has visited and in what sequence.
[Contains English characters] For example, if the log contains some requests done using the cookie id=dfhsiw, it can be determined that these requests all come from the same user.
[Contains English characters] The URL and date/time stored with the cookie allows for finding out which pages the user has visited, and at what time.
[Contains English characters] Third-party cookies and Web bugs, explained below, also allow for tracking across multiple sites.
[Contains English characters] Tracking within a site is typically used to produce usage statistics, while tracking across sites is typically used by advertising companies to produce anonymous user profiles .
[Contains English characters] A tracking cookie may potentially infringe upon the users privacy but they can be easily removed.
[Contains English characters] Current versions of popular web browsers include options to delete persistent cookies when the application is closed.
[Contains English characters] Images or other objects contained in a Web page may reside in servers different from the one holding the page.
[Contains English characters] In order to show such a page, the browser downloads all these objects, possibly receiving cookies.
[Contains English characters] These cookies are called third-party cookies if the server sending them is located outside the domain of the Web page.
[Contains English characters] This condition is common with on-line advertising.
[Contains English characters] Indeed, web banners are typically stored in servers of the advertising company, which are not in the domain of the Web pages showing them.
[Contains English characters] If third-party cookies are not rejected by the browser, an advertising company can track a user across the sites where it has placed a banner.
[Contains English characters] In particular, whenever a user views a page containing a banner, the browser retrieves the banner from a server of the advertising company.
[Contains English characters] If this server has previously set a cookie, the browser sends it back, allowing the advertising company to link this access with the previous one.
[Contains English characters] By choosing a unique banner URL for every Web page where it is placed or by using the HTTP referer field, the advertising company can then find out which pages the user has viewed.
[Contains English characters] The same technique can be used with web bugs.
[Contains English characters] These, unlike the obvious banners, are images embedded in the Web page that are undetectable by the user .
[Contains English characters] Third-party cookies are used to create an anonymous profile of the user.
[Contains English characters] This allows the advertising company to select the banner to show to a user based on the users profile.
[Contains English characters] The advertising industry has denied any other use of these profiles.
[Contains English characters] Many modern browsers, such as Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer and Opera block third party cookies if requested by the user.
[Contains English characters] Internet Explorer version 6 allows a mild form of blocking, called leashing.
[Contains English characters] A leashed cookie is a third-party cookie that is sent by the browser only when accessing a third-party document via the same first-party.
[Contains English characters] For example, if third.
[Contains English characters] com sets a cookie when an image is requested, and this cookie is set for the first time when the user views a document from first.
[Contains English characters] com, the same cookie is not sent if the user downloads a document that contains the same image but the document is on another site other.
[Contains English characters] com, if the cookie is leashed.
[Contains English characters] A leashed cookie is different from a blocked cookie in that it is sent, in this example, if the image is contained in another document from the same site first. com. Cookies are arbitrary pieces of data chosen by the Web server and sent to the browser.
[Contains English characters] The browser returns them unchanged to the server, introducing a state into otherwise stateless HTTP transactions.
[Contains English characters] Without cookies, each retrieval of a Web page or component of a Web page is an isolated event, mostly unrelated to all other views of the pages of the same site.
[Contains English characters] Other than being set by a web server, cookies can also be set by a script in a language such as JavaScript, if supported and enabled by the Web browser.
[Contains English characters] Cookie specifications suggest that browsers should be able to save and send back a minimal number of cookies.
[Contains English characters] In particular, an internet browser is expected to be able to store at least 300 cookies of four kilobytes each, and at least 20 cookies per server or domain.
[Contains English characters] According to section 3.1 of RFC 2965, cookie names are case insensitive.
[Contains English characters] The cookie setter can specify a deletion date, in which case the cookie will be removed on that date.
[Contains English characters] If the cookie setter does not specify a date, the cookie is removed once the user quits his or her browser.
[Contains English characters] As a result, specifying a date is a way for making a cookie survive across sessions.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, cookies with an expiration date are called persistent.
[Contains English characters] As an example application, a shopping site can use persistent cookies to store the items users have placed in their basket.
[Contains English characters] This way, if users quit their browser without making a purchase and return later, they still find the same items in the basket so they do not have to look for these items again.
[Contains English characters] If these cookies were not given an expiration date, they would expire when the browser is closed, and the information about the basket content would be lost.
[Contains English characters] Cookies can also be limited in scope to a specific domain, subdomain or path on the web server which created them.
[Contains English characters] Transfer of Web pages follows the HyperText Transfer Protocol .
[Contains English characters] Regardless of cookies, browsers request a page from web servers by sending them a usually short text called HTTP request.
[Contains English characters] For example, to access the page http://www. example. org/index. html, browsers connect to the server www.
[Contains English characters] example. org sending it a request that looks like the following one: GET /index.
[Contains English characters] html HTTP/1.1Host: www. example. org The server replies by sending the requested page preceded by a similar packet of text, called HTTP response.
[Contains English characters] This packet may contain lines requesting the browser to store cookies: HTTP/1.1 200 OKContent-type: text/htmlSet-Cookie: name=value The server sends the line Set-Cookie only if the server wishes the browser to store a cookie.
[Contains English characters] Set-Cookie is a request for the browser to store the string name=value and send it back in all future requests to the server.
[Contains English characters] If the browser supports cookies and cookies are enabled, every subsequent page request to the same server will include the cookie.
[Contains English characters] For example, the browser requests the page http://www. example. org/spec. html by sending the server www.
[Contains English characters] example. org a request like the following: GET /spec.
[Contains English characters] html HTTP/1.1Host: www. example. orgCookie: name=valueAccept: */* This is a request for another page from the same server, and differs from the first one above because it contains the string that the server has previously sent to the browser.
[Contains English characters] This way, the server knows that this request is related to the previous one.
[Contains English characters] The server answers by sending the requested page, possibly adding other cookies as well.
[Contains English characters] The value of a cookie can be modified by the server by sending a new Set-Cookie: name=newvalue line in response of a page request.
[Contains English characters] The browser then replaces the old value with the new one.
[Contains English characters] The term cookie crumb is sometimes used to refer to the name-value pair.
[Contains English characters] This is not the same as breadcrumb web navigation, which is the technique of showing in each page the list of pages the user has previously visited; this technique may however be implemented using cookies.
[Contains English characters] The Set-Cookie line is typically not created by the base HTTP server but by a CGI program.
[Contains English characters] The basic HTTP server facility just sends the result of the program to the browser.
[Contains English characters] Cookies can also be set by JavaScript or similar scripts running within the browser.
[Contains English characters] In JavaScript, the object document.
[Contains English characters] cookie is used for this purpose.
[Contains English characters] For example, the instruction document.
[Contains English characters] cookie = temperature=20 creates a cookie of name temperature and value 20. Beside the name/value pair, a cookie may also contain an expiration date, a path, a domain name, and whether the cookie is intended only for encrypted connections.
[Contains English characters] RFC 2965 also specifies that cookies must have a mandatory version number, but this is usually omitted.
[Contains English characters] These pieces of data follow the name=newvalue pair and are separated by semicolons.
[Contains English characters] For example, a cookie can be created by the server by sending a line Set-Cookie: name=newvalue; expires=date; path=/; domain=. example. org. The domain and path tell the browser that the cookie has to be sent back to the server when requesting URLs of a given domain and path.
[Contains English characters] If not specified, they default to the domain and path of the object that was requested.
[Contains English characters] As a result, the domain and path strings may tell the browser to send the cookie when it normally would not.
[Contains English characters] For security reasons, the cookie is accepted only if the server is a member of the domain specified by the domain string.
[Contains English characters] Cookies are actually identified by the combination of their name, domain, and path, as opposed to only their name .
[Contains English characters] In other words, same name but different domains or paths identify different cookies with possibly different values.
[Contains English characters] As a result, cookie values are changed only if a new value is given for the same name, domain, and path.
[Contains English characters] The expiration date tells the browser when to delete the cookie.
[Contains English characters] If no expiration date is provided, the cookie is deleted at the end of the user session, that is, when the user quits the browser.
[Contains English characters] As a result, specifying an expiration date is a means for making cookies survive across browser sessions.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, cookies that have an expiration date are called persistent.
[Contains English characters] The expiration date is specified in the Wdy, DD-Mon-YYYY HH:MM:SS GMT format.
[Contains English characters] As an example, the following is a cookie sent by a Web server : Set-Cookie: RMID=732423sdfs73242; expires=Fri, 31-Dec-2010 23:59:59 GMT; path=/; domain=. example. net The name of this particular cookie is RMID, while its value is the string 732423sdfs73242. The server can use an arbitrary string as the value of a cookie.
[Contains English characters] The server may collapse the value of a number of variables in a single string, like for example a=12&b=abcd&c=32. The path and domain strings / and . example. net tell the browser to send the cookie when requesting an arbitrary page of the domain .
[Contains English characters] example. net, with an arbitrary path.
[Contains English characters] Cookies expire, and are therefore not sent by the browser to the server, under any of these conditions: The third condition allows a server or script to explicitly delete a cookie.
[Contains English characters] Note that the browser doesnt send to the server information about cookie lifetime, so there is no way for the server to check if the cookie expires soon.
[Contains English characters] Since their introduction on the Internet, misconceptions about cookies have circulated on the Internet and in the media.
[Contains English characters] In 1998, CIAC, a computer incident response team of the United States Department of Energy, found the security vulnerability essentially nonexistent and explained that information about where you come from and what web pages you visit already exists in a web servers log files.
[Contains English characters] In 2005, Jupiter Research published the results of a survey, according to which a consistent percentage of respondents believed some of the following false claims: Cookies cannot erase or read information from the users computer.
[Contains English characters] However, cookies allow for detecting the Web pages viewed by a user on a given site or set of sites.
[Contains English characters] This information can be collected in a profile of the user.
[Contains English characters] Some profiles are anonymous, meaning they contain no personal information, yet even such profiles can be controversial.
[Contains English characters] According to the same survey, a large percentage of Internet users do not know how to delete cookies.
[Contains English characters] One reason people do not trust the concept of cookies is because some sites have abused the personal identification aspect of cookies and have shared them.
[Contains English characters] A large percentage of targeted advertising comes from information gleaned from tracking cookies.
[Contains English characters] Most modern browsers support cookies and allow the user to disable them.
[Contains English characters] The following are common options: Most browsers also allow a full wipe of private data including cookies.
[Contains English characters] Add-on tools for managing cookie permissions also exist.
[Contains English characters] Cookies have some important implications on the privacy and anonymity of Web users.
[Contains English characters] While cookies are sent only to the server setting them or the server in the same Internet domain, a Web page may contain images or other components stored on servers in other domains.
[Contains English characters] Cookies that are set during retrieval of these components are called third-party cookies.
[Contains English characters] This includes cookies from unwanted pop-up ads.
[Contains English characters] Advertising companies use third-party cookies to track a user across multiple sites.
[Contains English characters] In particular, an advertising company can track a user across all pages where it has placed advertising images or web bugs.
[Contains English characters] Knowledge of the pages visited by a user allows the advertisement company to target advertisement to the users presumed preferences.
[Contains English characters] The possibility of building a profile of users is considered by some a potential privacy threat, especially when tracking is done across multiple domains using third-party cookies.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, some countries have legislation about cookies.
[Contains English characters] The United States government has set strict rules on setting cookies in 2000 after it was disclosed that the White House drug policy office used cookies to track computer users viewing its online anti-drug advertising.
[Contains English characters] In 2002, privacy activist Daniel Brandt found that the CIA had been leaving persistent cookies on computers which had visited its web site.
[Contains English characters] When notified it was violating policy, CIA stated that these cookies were not intentionally set and stopped setting them.
[Contains English characters] On December 25, 2005, Brandt discovered that the National Security Agency had been leaving two persistent cookies on visitors computers due to a software upgrade.
[Contains English characters] After being informed, the National Security Agency immediately disabled the cookies.
[Contains English characters] The 2002 European Union telecommunication privacy Directive contains rules about the use of cookies.
[Contains English characters] In particular, Article 5, Paragraph 3 of this directive mandates that storing data in a users computer can only be done if: 1 the user is provided information about how this data is used; and 2 the user is given the possibility of denying this storing operation.
[Contains English characters] However, this article also states that storing data that is necessary for technical reasons is exempted from this rule.
[Contains English characters] This directive was expected to have been applied since October 2003, but a December 2004 report says that this provision was not applied in practice, and that some member countries did not even implement the provision in national law.
[Contains English characters] The same report suggests a thorough analysis of the situation in the Member States.
[Contains English characters] The P3P specification includes the possibility for a server to state a privacy policy, which specifies which kind of information it collects and for which purpose.
[Contains English characters] These policies include the use of information gathered using cookies.
[Contains English characters] According to the P3P specification, a browser can accept or reject cookies by comparing the privacy policy with the stored user preferences or ask the user, presenting them the privacy policy as declared by the server.
[Contains English characters] Many web browsers including Apples Safari and Microsoft Internet Explorer versions 6 and 7 support P3P which allows the web browser to determine whether to allow 3rd party cookies to be stored.
[Contains English characters] The Opera web browser allows users to refuse third-party cookies and to create global and specific security profiles for Internet domains.
[Contains English characters] Firefox 2.x dropped this option from its menu system but it restored it with the release of version 3.x.
[Contains English characters] Third-party cookies can be blocked by most browsers to increase privacy and reduce tracking by advertising and tracking companies without negatively affecting the users Web experience.
[Contains English characters] Many advertising operators have an opt-out option to behavioural advertising, with a generic cookie in the browser stopping behavioural advertising.
[Contains English characters] Besides privacy concerns, cookies also have some technical drawbacks.
[Contains English characters] In particular, they do not always accurately identify users, they can be used for security attacks, and they are at odds with the Representational State Transfer software architectural style.
[Contains English characters] If more than one browser is used on a computer, each usually has a separate storage area for cookies.
[Contains English characters] Hence cookies do not identify a person, but a combination of a user account, a computer, and a Web browser.
[Contains English characters] Thus, anyone who uses multiple accounts, computers, or browsers has multiple sets of cookies.
[Contains English characters] Likewise, cookies do not differentiate between multiple users who share the same user account, computer, and browser.
[Contains English characters] During normal operation cookies are sent back and forth between a server and the computer of the browsing user.
[Contains English characters] Since cookies may contain sensitive information, their values should not be accessible to other computers.
[Contains English characters] Cookie theft is the act of intercepting cookies by an unauthorized party.
[Contains English characters] Cookies can be stolen via packet sniffing in an attack called session hijacking.
[Contains English characters] Traffic on a network can be intercepted and read by computers on the network other than its sender and its receiver .
[Contains English characters] This traffic includes cookies sent on ordinary unencrypted http sessions.
[Contains English characters] Where network traffic is not encrypted, malicious users can therefore read the communications of other users on the network, including their cookies, using programs called packet sniffers.
[Contains English characters] This issue can be overcome by securing the communication between the users computer and the server by employing Transport Layer Security to encrypt the connection.
[Contains English characters] A server can specify the secure flag while setting a cookie; the browser will then send it only over a secure channel, such as an SSL connection.
[Contains English characters] However a large number of websites, although using encrypted https communication for user authentication, subsequently send session cookies and other data over ordinary, unencrypted http connections for performance reasons.
[Contains English characters] Attackers can therefore easily intercept the cookies of other users and impersonate them on the relevant websites or use them in a cookiemonster attack.
[Contains English characters] A different way to steal cookies is cross-site scripting and making the browser itself send cookies to malicious servers that should not receive them.
[Contains English characters] Modern browsers allow execution of pieces of code retrieved from the server.
[Contains English characters] If cookies are accessible during execution, their value may be communicated in some form to servers that should not access them.
[Contains English characters] Encrypting cookies before sending them on the network does not help against this attack.
[Contains English characters] This type of cross-site scripting is typically exploited by attackers on sites that allow users to post HTML content.
[Contains English characters] By embedding a suitable piece of code in an HTML post, an attacker may receive cookies of other users.
[Contains English characters] Knowledge of these cookies can then be exploited by connecting to the same site using the stolen cookies, thus being recognised as the user whose cookies have been stolen.
[Contains English characters] Hope and Walther provide a coded example.
[Contains English characters] A way for preventing such attacks is by using the HttpOnly flag; this is an option, first introduced by Microsoft and implemented in PHP since version 5.2.0 that is intended to make a cookie inaccessible to client side script.
[Contains English characters] However, web developers should consider developing their websites so that they are immune to cross-site scripting.
[Contains English characters] The cookie specifications constrain cookies to be sent back only to the servers in the same domain as the server from which they originate.
[Contains English characters] However, the value of cookies can be sent to other servers using means different from the Cookie header.
[Contains English characters] In particular, scripting languages such as JavaScript and JScript are usually allowed access to cookie values and have some means to send arbitrary values to arbitrary servers on the Internet.
[Contains English characters] These facts are used in combination with sites allowing users to post HTML content that other users can see.
[Contains English characters] As an example, an attacker running the domain example.
[Contains English characters] com may post a comment containing the following link to a popular blog they do not otherwise control: When another user clicks on this link, the browser executes the piece of code within the onclick attribute, thus replacing the string document.
[Contains English characters] cookie with the list of cookies of the user that are active for the page.
[Contains English characters] As a result, this list of cookies is sent to the example.
[Contains English characters] com server, and the attacker is then able to collect the cookies of other users.
[Contains English characters] This type of attack is difficult to detect on the user side because the script is coming from the same domain that has set the cookie, and the operation of sending the value appears to be authorised by this domain.
[Contains English characters] It is usually considered the responsibility of the administrators running sites where users can post to disallow the posting of such malicious code.
[Contains English characters] Cookies are not directly visible to client-side programs such as JavaScript if they have been sent with the HttpOnly flag.
[Contains English characters] From the point of view of the server, the only difference with respect of the normal case is that the set-cookie header line is added a new field containing the string `HttpOnly: When the browser receives such a cookie, it is supposed to use it as usual in the following HTTP exchanges, but not to make it visible to client-side scripts.
[Contains English characters] The `HttpOnly` flag is not part of any standard, and is not implemented in all browsers.
[Contains English characters] Note that there is currently no prevention of reading or writing the session cookie via an XMLHTTPRequest.
[Contains English characters] While cookies are supposed to be stored and sent back to the server unchanged, an attacker may modify the value of cookies before sending them back to the server.
[Contains English characters] If, for example, a cookie contains the total value a user has to pay for the items in their shopping basket, changing this value exposes the server to the risk of making the attacker pay less than the supposed price.
[Contains English characters] The process of tampering with the value of cookies is called cookie poisoning, and is sometimes used after cookie theft to make an attack persistent.
[Contains English characters] Most websites, however, store only a session identifier — a randomly generated unique number used to identify the users session — in the cookie itself, while all the other information is stored on the server.
[Contains English characters] In this case, the problem of cookie poisoning is largely eliminated.
[Contains English characters] Each site is supposed to have its own cookies, so a site like example.
[Contains English characters] com should not be able to alter or set cookies for another site, like example. org. Cross-site cooking vulnerabilities in web browsers allow malicious sites to break this rule.
[Contains English characters] This is similar to cookie poisoning, but the attacker exploits non-malicious users with vulnerable browsers, instead of attacking the actual site directly.
[Contains English characters] The goal of such attacks may be to perform session fixation.
[Contains English characters] Users are advised to use the more recent versions of web browsers in which such issue is mitigated.
[Contains English characters] The use of cookies may generate an inconsistency between the state of the client and the state as stored in the cookie.
[Contains English characters] If the user acquires a cookie and then clicks the Back button of the browser, the state on the browser is generally not the same as before that acquisition.
[Contains English characters] As an example, if the shopping cart of an online shop is realized using cookies, the content of the cart may not change when the user goes back in the browsers history: if the user presses a button to add an item in the shopping cart and then clicks on the Back button, the item remains in the shopping cart.
[Contains English characters] This might not be the intention of the user, who possibly wanted to undo the addition of the item.
[Contains English characters] This can lead to unreliability, confusion, and bugs.
[Contains English characters] Web developers should therefore be aware of this issue and implement measures to handle such situations as this.
[Contains English characters] Persistent cookies have been criticized by privacy experts for not being set to expire soon enough, and thereby allowing websites to track users and build up a profile of them over time.
[Contains English characters] This aspect of cookies also compounds the issue of session hijacking, because a stolen persistent cookie can potentially be used to impersonate a user for a considerable period of time.
[Contains English characters] Some of the operations that can be realised using cookies can also be realised using other mechanisms.
[Contains English characters] An unreliable technique for tracking users is based on storing the IP addresses of the computers requesting the pages.
[Contains English characters] This technique has been available since the introduction of the World Wide Web, as downloading pages requires the server holding them to know the IP address of the computer running the browser or the proxy, if any is used.
[Contains English characters] The server can log this information whether or not cookies are used.
[Contains English characters] However, these addresses are typically less reliable in identifying a user than cookies because computers and proxies may be shared by several users, and the same computer may be assigned different IP addresses in different work sessions .
[Contains English characters] The reliability of this technique can be improved by using another feature of the HTTP protocol: when a browser requests a page because the user has followed a link, the request that is sent to the server contains the URL of the page where the link is located.
[Contains English characters] If the server stores these URLs, the path of pages viewed by the user can be tracked more precisely.
[Contains English characters] However, these traces are less reliable than the ones provided by cookies, as several users may access the same page from the same computer, NAT router, or proxy and then follow two different links.
[Contains English characters] Moreover, this technique allows only for tracking and cannot replace cookies in their other uses.
[Contains English characters] Tracking by IP address can be impossible with some systems that are used to retain Internet anonymity, such as Tor.
[Contains English characters] With such systems, not only could one browser carry multiple addresses throughout a session but also multiple users could appear to be coming from the same IP address, thus making IP address use for tracking wholly unreliable.
[Contains English characters] Some major ISPs, including AOL, route all web traffic through a small number of proxies which makes this scheme particularly unworkable.
[Contains English characters] However some things make IP addresses more usable.
[Contains English characters] With the much more widespread use of routers many broadband users retain the same IP for as long as the power stays on.
[Contains English characters] Also combined with the User-Agent HTTP header, a tracker can differentiate users behind a NAT.
[Contains English characters] When combined with session cookies and links to their tracker on huge number of pages a tracker can track extensively even in the absence of persistent cookies.
[Contains English characters] A more precise technique is based on embedding information into URLs.
[Contains English characters] The query string part of the URL is the one that is typically used for this purpose, but other parts can be used as well.
[Contains English characters] The Java Servlet and PHP session mechanisms both use this method if cookies are not enabled.
[Contains English characters] This method consists of the Web server appending query strings to the links of a Web page it holds when sending it to a browser.
[Contains English characters] When the user follows a link, the browser returns the attached query string to the server.
[Contains English characters] Query strings used in this way and cookies are very similar, both being arbitrary pieces of information chosen by the server and sent back by the browser.
[Contains English characters] However, there are some differences: since a query string is part of a URL, if that URL is later reused, the same attached piece of information is sent to the server.
[Contains English characters] For example, if the preferences of a user are encoded in the query string of a URL and the user sends this URL to another user by e-mail, those preferences will be used for that other user as well.
[Contains English characters] Moreover, even if the same user accesses the same page two times, there is no guarantee that the same query string is used in both views.
[Contains English characters] For example, if the same user arrives to the same page but coming from a page internal to the site the first time and from an external search engine the second time, the relative query strings are typically different while the cookies would be the same.
[Contains English characters] For more details, see query string.
[Contains English characters] Other drawbacks of query strings are related to security: storing data that identifies a session in a query string enables or simplifies session fixation attacks, referer logging attacks and other security exploits.
[Contains English characters] Transferring session identifiers as HTTP cookies is more secure.
[Contains English characters] A form of session tracking, used by ASP.
[Contains English characters] NET, is to use web forms with hidden fields.
[Contains English characters] This technique is very similar to using URL query strings to hold the information and has many of the same advantages and drawbacks; and if the form is handled with the HTTP GET method, the fields actually become part of the URL the browser will send upon form submission.
[Contains English characters] But most forms are handled with HTTP POST, which causes the form information, including the hidden fields, to be appended as extra input that is neither part of the URL, nor of a cookie.
[Contains English characters] This approach presents two advantages from the point of view of the tracker: first, having the tracking information placed in the HTML source and POST input rather than in the URL means it will not be noticed by the average user; second, the session information is not copied when the user copies the URL .
[Contains English characters] A drawback of this technique is that session information is in the HTML code; therefore, each web page must be generated dynamically each time someone requests it, placing an additional workload on the web server.
[Contains English characters] All current web browsers can store a fairly large amount of data via JavaScript using the DOM property window. name. This data can be used instead of session cookies and is also cross domain.
[Contains English characters] The technique can be coupled with JSON/JavaScript objects to store complex sets of session variables on the client side.
[Contains English characters] The downside is that every separate window or tab will initially have an empty window.
[Contains English characters] name; in times of tabbed browsing this means that individually opened tabs will not have a window name.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore window.
[Contains English characters] name can be used for tracking visitors across different web sites, making it of concern for Internet privacy.
[Contains English characters] In some respects this can be more secure than cookies due to not involving the server, so it is not vulnerable to network cookie sniffing attacks.
[Contains English characters] However if special measures are not taken to protect the data, it is vulnerable to other attacks because the data is available across different web sites opened in the same window or tab.
[Contains English characters] As for authentication, the HTTP protocol includes the basic access authentication and the digest access authentication protocols, which allow access to a Web page only when the user has provided the correct username and password.
[Contains English characters] If the server requires such credential for granting access to a Web page, the browser requests them to the user and, once obtained, the browser stores and uses them also for accessing subsequent pages without requiring the user to provide them again.
[Contains English characters] From the point of view of the user, the effect is the same as if cookies were used: username and password are requested only once, and from that point on the user is given access to the site.
[Contains English characters] In the basic access authentication protocol, a combination of username and password is sent to the server in every browser request.
[Contains English characters] This means that someone listening in on this traffic can simply read this information and store for later use.
[Contains English characters] This problem is overcome in the digest access authentication protocol, in which the password is encrypted using a random nonce created by the server.
[Contains English characters] If a browser includes the Adobe Flash Player plugin, the Local Shared Objects functionality can be used in a way very similar to cookies.
[Contains English characters] Local Shared Objects may be an attractive choice to web developers because a majority of Windows users have Flash Player installed, the default size limit is 100 kB, and the security controls are distinct from the user controls for cookies, so Local Stored Objects may be enabled when cookies are not.
[Contains English characters] In some cases, web sites have created Flash LSOs that behave differently than what a user specifies for their http cookies, which has raised concern that web sites need to specify a consistent privacy policy across different types of cookies.
[Contains English characters] The major drawback with this approach is the same as every platform/vendor-specific approach: it breaks the webs global accessibility and interoperability, tying up web development to a specific clients platform, excluding users who use standards-compliant web user agents and instead forcing them to use platform/vendor-specific web agents, which perpetuates vendor lock-in.
[Contains English characters] Some web browsers support a script-based persistence mechanism that allows the page to store information locally for later retrieval.
[Contains English characters] Internet Explorer, for example, supports persisting information in the browsers history, in favorites, in an XML store, or directly within a Web page saved to disk.
[Contains English characters] With HTML 5 there will be a DOM Storage method, currently supported by only some browsers.
[Contains English characters] For Internet Explorer 5+ there is a userData method available through DHTML Behaviours.
[Contains English characters] A different mechanism relies on browsers normally caching JavaScript programs used in web pages.
[Contains English characters] As an example, a page may contain a link such as .
[Contains English characters] The first time this page is loaded, the program example.
[Contains English characters] js is loaded as well.
[Contains English characters] At this point, the program remains cached and is not reloaded the second time the page is visited.
[Contains English characters] As a result, if this program contains a statement such as id=3243242, this identifier remains valid and can be exploited by other JavaScript code the next times the page is loaded, or another page linking the same program is loaded.
[Contains English characters] The major drawback of this method is that the global JavaScript variable must be static, meaning that it cannot be changed or deleted persistently like a cookie.

[Contains English characters] द्राविडी लोकं Dravidian people also Dravidians refers to the people who natively speak languages belonging to the Dravidian language family.
[Contains English characters] Populations of speakers are found mostly in southern India.
[Contains English characters] Other Dravidian people are found in parts of central India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran.
[Contains English characters] Dravidian people with the most speakers are Telugus, Tamils, Kannadigas, Malayalis.
[Contains English characters] Others with 1-5 million speakers each are Tuluvas, Gonds and Brahui.
[Contains English characters] The English word Dravidian was first employed by Robert Caldwell in his book of comparative Dravidian grammar based on the usage of the Sanskrit word drāvida in the work Tantravārttika by .
[Contains English characters] Caldwell coined the term Dravidian from the Sanskrit drāvida, which was used in an 8th-century text to refer to South India by Adi Shankara.
[Contains English characters] The publication of the Dravidian etymological dictionary by T.
[Contains English characters] Burrow and M. B. Emeneau was a landmark event in Dravidian linguistics.
[Contains English characters] As for the origin of the Sanskrit word , there have been various theories proposed.
[Contains English characters] Basically the theories are about the direction of derivation between and .
[Contains English characters] That is to say, while linguists such as Zvelebil assert that the direction is >, others state that the name Dravida also forms the root of the word Tamil .
[Contains English characters] साचा:Who The word Dravida may also have its origin from Sanskrit Drava - meaning water or sea.
[Contains English characters] The word Dravidian may have been used to identify people living in India close to the sea.
[Contains English characters] Since southern India is surrounded by sea on three sides, the word may been used predominantly to identify the inhabitants of these areas.
[Contains English characters] There is no definite philological and linguistic basis for asserting unilaterally that the name Dravida also forms the origin of the word Tamil .
[Contains English characters] Zvelebil cites the forms such as dramila and then goes on to say : The forms /damila almost certainly provide a connection of dr and . . . * > - / damila- and further, with the intrusive, hypercorrect -r-, into dr.
[Contains English characters] The -m-/-v- alternation is a common enough phenomenon in Dravidian phonology Zvelebil in his earlier treatise states: It is obvious that the Sanskrit dr, Pali damila, and Prakrit d are all etymologically connected with and further remarks The r in > dr is a hypercorrect insertion, cf.

[Contains English characters] Zvelebil has suggested that proto-Dravidian was part of a larger Elamo-Dravidian language family.
[Contains English characters] However, George Starostin has disputed the existence of an Elamo-Dravidian language family .
[Contains English characters] According to a view put forward by geneticist Luigi Luca Cavalli-Sforza in the book The History and Geography of Human Genes, the Dravidians were preceded in the subcontinent by an Austro-Asiatic people, and followed by Indo-European-speaking migrants sometime later.
[Contains English characters] The original inhabitants may be identified with the speakers of the Munda languages, which are unrelated to either Indo-Aryan or Dravidian languages.
[Contains English characters] However, the Munda languages, as a subgroup of the larger Austro-Asiatic language family, are presumed to have arrived in the Indian subcontinent from the east, possibly from the area that is now southwestern China, so any genetic similarity between the present-day speakers of the Munda languages and the original inhabitants of India is likely to be due to assimilation of the natives by Southeast Asian immigrants speaking a proto-Munda language.
[Contains English characters] Some linguists believe that Dravidian-speaking people were spread throughout the Indian subcontinent before a series of Indo-Aryan migrations.
[Contains English characters] In this view, the early Indus Valley civilization is often identified as having been Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] Cultural and linguistic similarities have been cited by researchers such as Finnish Indologist Asko Parpola as being strong evidence for a proto-Dravidian origin of the ancient Indus Valley civilization.
[Contains English characters] Some scholars like J.
[Contains English characters] Bloch and M.
[Contains English characters] Witzel believe that the Dravidians moved into an already Indo-Aryan speaking area after the oldest parts of the Rig Veda were already composed.
[Contains English characters] This theory might be supported if a higher antiquity of the Indo-Aryan languages could be established.
[Contains English characters] However, since this theory is mainly a linguistic hypothesis, the Dravidian influence on Aryan languages need not necessarily be equated to a movement of populations.
[Contains English characters] The Brahui population of Balochistan has been taken by some as the linguistic equivalent of a relict population, perhaps indicating that Dravidian languages were formerly much more widespread and were supplanted by the incoming Indo-Aryan languages.
[Contains English characters] Thomason & Kaufman state that there is strong evidence that Dravidian influenced Indic through shift, that is, native Dravidian speakers learning and adopting Indic languages.
[Contains English characters] Elst claims that the presence of the Brahui language, similarities between Elamite and Harappan script as well as similarities between Indo-Aryan and Dravidian indicate that these languages may have interacted prior to the spread of Indo-Aryans southwards and the resultant intermixing of languages.
[Contains English characters] Erdosy states that the most plausible explanation for the presence of Dravidian structural features in Old Indo-Aryan is that the majority of early Old Indo-Aryan speakers had a Dravidian mother tongue which they gradually abandoned.
[Contains English characters] Even though the innovative traits in Indic could be explained by multiple internal explanations, early Dravidian influence is the only explanation that can account for all of the innovations at once – it becomes a question of explanatory parsimony; moreover, early Dravidian influence accounts for the several of the innovative traits in Indic better than any internal explanation that has been proposed.
[Contains English characters] Zvelebil remarks that Several scholars have demonstrated that pre-Indo-Aryan and pre-Dravidian bilingualism in India provided conditions for the far-reaching influence of Dravidian on the Indo-Aryan tongues in the spheres of phonology, syntax and vocabulary.
[Contains English characters] The genetic views on race differ in their classification of Dravidians.
[Contains English characters] According to population geneticist L. L. Cavalli-Sforza of Stanford, based on work done in the 1980s, Indians are genetically Caucasian, but Lewontin rejects the label Caucasian.
[Contains English characters] Cavalli-Sforza found that Indians are about three times closer to West Europeans than to East Asians. Dr. Eduardas Valaitis, in 2006, found that India is genetically closest to East and Southeast Asians with about 15% more genetic similarity than to Europeans; he also found that India could be considered very distinct from other regions.
[Contains English characters] Genetic anthropologist Stanley Marion Garn considered in the 1960s that the entirety of the Indian Subcontinent to be a race genetically distinct from other populations.
[Contains English characters] Others, such as Lynn B.
[Contains English characters] Jorde and Stephen P.
[Contains English characters] Wooding, claim South Indians are genetic intermediaries between Europeans and East Asians.
[Contains English characters] A number of earlier anthropologists held the view that the Dravidian peoples together were a distinct race.
[Contains English characters] Comprehensive genetic studies have proven that this is not the case.
[Contains English characters] The genetic studies also indicated that the origin of both Dravidian and Indo-Aryan speakers is the Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] Recent studies of the distribution of alleles on the Y chromosome, microsatellite DNA, and mitochondrial DNA in India have cast overwhelmingly strong doubt for a biologically identifiable Dravidian race distinct from non-Dravidians in the Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] The only distinct ethnic groups present in South Asia, according to genetic analysis, are the Balochi, Brahui, Burusho, Hazara, Kalash, Pathan and Sindhi peoples, the vast majority of whom are found in todays Pakistan.
[Contains English characters] In a 2009 study of 132 individuals, 560,000 SNPs in 25 different Indian groups were analyzed, providing strong evidence in support of the notion that modern Indians are a hybrid population descending from two pre-historic, genetically divergent populations, one of which, referred to as the Ancestral North Indians, aged 40.000 years and the other, called the Ancestral South Indians, aged 60.000 years.
[Contains English characters] The intermingling of ANIs and ASIs happened in the same period as the ANIs first appeared, 40.000 years ago.
[Contains English characters] The study also holds, that the caste system grew out of tribal-like organizations of the Indian society.
[Contains English characters] In another study of 2009 conducted among 10 Asian countries, Dravidians were connected with the other Indian populations and peoples of Malaysia, Singapore and China.
[Contains English characters] The best-known Dravidian languages are Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam .
[Contains English characters] There are three subgroups within the Dravidian linguistic family: North Dravidian, Central Dravidian, and South Dravidian, matching for the most part the corresponding regions in the Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] Dravidian languages are spoken by more than 200 million people.
[Contains English characters] They appear to be unrelated to languages of other known families like Indo-European, specifically Indo-Aryan, which is the other common language family on the Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] Some linguistic scholars incorporate the Dravidian languages into a larger Elamo-Dravidian language family, which includes the ancient Elamite language of what is now south-western Iran.
[Contains English characters] Dravidian is one of the primary linguistic groups in the proposed Nostratic language system, linking almost all languages in North Africa, Europe and Western Asia into a common family with its origins in the Fertile Crescent sometime between the last Ice Age and the emergence of proto-Indo-European 4-6 thousand years BC.
[Contains English characters] Dravidian grammatical impact on the structure and syntax of Indo-Aryan languages is considered far greater than the Indo-Aryan grammatical impact on Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] Some linguists explain this anomaly by arguing that Middle Indo-Aryan and New Indo-Aryan were built on a Dravidian substratum.
[Contains English characters] The term Dravidian is taken from the Sanskrit term Dravida, historically referring to Tamil.
[Contains English characters] It was adopted following the publication of Robert Caldwells Comparative grammar of the Dravidian or South-Indian family of languages ; a publication that established the language grouping as one of the major language groups of the world.
[Contains English characters] Over seventy-three languages are presently listed as Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] Further, the languages are spread out and cover parts of India, south eastern Iran, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] Robert Caldwell was an Anglican missionary and used the term Dravidian to refer to the people of South India.
[Contains English characters] Although in modern times speakers of the various Dravidian languages have mainly occupied the southern portion of India, nothing definite is known about the ancient domain of the Dravidian parent speech.
[Contains English characters] It is, however, a well-established and well-supported hypothesis that Dravidian speakers must have been widespread throughout India, including the northwest region.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Relatedसाचा:Two other uses Cooperation, co-operation, or coöperation is the process of working or acting together, which can be accomplished by both intentional and non-intentional agents.
[Contains English characters] In its simplest form it involves things working in harmony, side by side, while in its more complicated forms, it can involve something as complex as the inner workings of a human being or even the social patterns of a nation.
[Contains English characters] It is the alternative to working separately in competition.
[Contains English characters] Cooperation can also be accomplished by computers, which can handle shared resources simultaneously, while sharing processor time.
[Contains English characters] Cooperation, more formally speak is how the components of a system work together to achieve the global properties.
[Contains English characters] In other words, individual components that appear to be “selfish” and independent work together to create a highly complex, greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts system.
[Contains English characters] Examples can be found all around us.
[Contains English characters] The components in a cell work together to keep it living.
[Contains English characters] Cells work together and communicate to produce multicellular organisms.
[Contains English characters] Organisms form food chains and ecosystems.
[Contains English characters] People form families, gangs, cities and nations.
[Contains English characters] Neurons create thought and consciousness.
[Contains English characters] Atoms cooperate in a simple way, by combining to make up molecules.
[Contains English characters] Understanding the mechanisms that create cooperating agents in a system is one of the most important and least well understood phenomena in nature, though there has not been a lack of effort.
[Contains English characters] However, cooperation may be coerced, voluntary, or even unintentional, and consequently individuals and groups might cooperate even though they have almost nothing in common qua interests or goals.
[Contains English characters] Examples of that can be found in market trade, military wars, families, workplaces, schools and prisons, and more generally any institution or organisation of which individuals are part .
[Contains English characters] Even if all members of a group would benefit if all cooperate, individual self-interest may not favor cooperation.
[Contains English characters] The prisoners dilemma codifies this problem and has been the subject of much research, both theoretical and experimental.
[Contains English characters] Results from experimental economics show that humans often act more cooperatively than strict self-interest would seem to dictate.
[Contains English characters] One reason for this may be that if the prisoners dilemma situation is repeated, it allows non-cooperation to be punished more, and cooperation to be rewarded more, than the single-shot version of the problem would suggest.
[Contains English characters] It has been suggested that this is one reason for the evolution of complex emotions in higher life forms, who, at least as infants, and usually thereafter, cannot survive without cooperating – although with maturation they gain much more choice about the kinds of cooperation they wish to have.

[Contains English characters] The characteristic odor and flavor of ginger root is caused by a mixture of zingerone, shogaols and gingerols, volatile oils that compose about one to three percent of the weight of fresh ginger.
[Contains English characters] In laboratory animals, the gingerols increase the motility of the gastrointestinal tract and have analgesic, sedative, antipyretic and antibacterial properties.
[Contains English characters] Ginger contains up to three percent of a fragrant essential oil whose main constituents are sesquiterpenoids, with -zingiberene as the main component.
[Contains English characters] Smaller amounts of other sesquiterpenoids and a small monoterpenoid fraction have also been identified.
[Contains English characters] The pungent taste of ginger is due to nonvolatile phenylpropanoid-derived compounds, particularly gingerols and shogaols, which form from gingerols when ginger is dried or cooked.
[Contains English characters] Zingerone is also produced from gingerols during this process; this compound is less pungent and has a spicy-sweet aroma.
[Contains English characters] Ginger is also a minor chemical irritant, and because of this was used as a horse suppository by pre-World War I mounted regiments for feaguing.
[Contains English characters] Ginger has a sialagogue action, stimulating the production of saliva, which makes swallowing easier.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Nutritionalvalue Young ginger rhizomes are juicy and fleshy with a very mild taste.
[Contains English characters] They are often pickled in vinegar or sherry as a snack or just cooked as an ingredient in many dishes.
[Contains English characters] They can also be stewed in boiling water to make ginger tea, to which honey is often added as a sweetener; sliced orange or lemon fruit may also be added.
[Contains English characters] Mature ginger roots are fibrous and nearly dry.
[Contains English characters] The juice from old ginger roots is often used as a spice in Indian recipes and Chinese cuisine to flavor dishes such as seafood or mutton and vegetarian recipes.
[Contains English characters] Powdered dry ginger root is typically used to spice gingerbread and other recipes.
[Contains English characters] Fresh ginger can be substituted for ground ginger at a ratio of 6 parts fresh for 1 part ground, although the flavors of fresh and dried ginger are not exactly interchangeable.
[Contains English characters] Ginger is also made into candy, is used as a flavoring for cookies, crackers and cake, and is the main flavor in ginger ale—a sweet, carbonated, non-alcoholic beverage, as well as the similar, but spicier ginger beer which is popular in the Caribbean.
[Contains English characters] Fresh ginger should be peeled before being eaten .
[Contains English characters] For storage, the ginger should be wrapped tightly in a towel and placed in a plastic bag, and can be kept for about three weeks in a refrigerator and up to three months in a freezer.

[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty was a Tamil dynasty of South India which ruled the northern Tamil Nadu region and whole of Andhra Pradesh with their capital at Kanchipuram.
[Contains English characters] The word Pallava in Sanskrit means branch.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty is an offshoot of the Chola rulers .
[Contains English characters] They expanded into the Guntur region of Andhra Pradesh.
[Contains English characters] This area is still referred to as Palnadu or Pallava Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas gained prominence after the eclipse of Satavahanas of Andhra and decline of Cholas in Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas patronized Tamil, Telugu and Sanskrit.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most illustrious Sanskrit poets like Bharavi and Dandin and the seashore rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram belongs to the Pallavan era.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas rose in power during the reign of Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I and dominated the Telugu and northern parts of the Tamil region for about six hundred years until the end of the 9th century.
[Contains English characters] Throughout their reign they were in constant conflict with both Chalukyas of Badami in the north and the Tamil kingdoms of Chola and Pandyas in the south and were finally defeated by the Chola kings in the 8th century CE.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas are most noted for their patronage of architecture, still seen today in Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas, who left behind magnificent sculptures and temples, established the foundations of medieval south Indian architecture.
[Contains English characters] Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchipuram during Pallava rule and extolled their benign rule.
[Contains English characters] Many sources describe Bodhidharma, the founder of the Zen school of Buddhism in China, as a prince of the Pallava dynasty, a contemporary of Skandavarman IV and Nandivarman I, and the son of Simhavarman II, though this is debatable.
[Contains English characters] The word Pallava means branch in Sanskrit, in contrast with Chola meaning new country, Pandiya meaning old country and Chera meaning hill country in Sangam Tamil lexicon.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas are considered to be later offshoot of Cholas, who made Kanchipuram their capital and ruled Northern Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh .
[Contains English characters] They have also conquered Southern Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] The origins of the Pallavas are shrouded in myths and legends.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas are described to belong to the line of sage Bharadwaja.
[Contains English characters] Aswattama the son of Drona once while being in a hermitage near the province of Funan in South-East Asia was visited upon by the celestial nymph called Menaka who sought his hand.
[Contains English characters] The child that they begot was called Pallava.
[Contains English characters] Several grants recollect this by seeing Pallavas valour to be equal to that of Aswattaman who that night of war relentlessly fought the demonic army of Ghatotgacha the son of Bheema.
[Contains English characters] This apart several Pallavas were praised to have mastered and practiced alongside arms, the agamic worship rituals .
[Contains English characters] This apart the Pallava insignia of mace Khatvanga of Lord Siva and conch Samudraghosham of lord Siva was also sported by Aswattama.
[Contains English characters] It is also true that several Pallava princes who took charges in Kanchi came from many distant islands also where extended the authority of the great kings, let alone from Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] The rule of the Pallavas apparently starts as early as 275 CE, but their greatest epoch corresponds to the 7th and 8th century.
[Contains English characters] The history of the early Pallavas has not yet been satisfactorily settled.
[Contains English characters] The earliest documentation on the Pallavas is the three copper-plate grants, belonging to Skandavarman I and written in Prakrit.
[Contains English characters] Skandavarman appears to have been the first great ruler of the early Pallavas, though there are references to other early Pallavas who were probably predecessors of Skandavarman.
[Contains English characters] Skandavarman extended his dominions from the Krishna in the north to the Pennar in the south and to the Bellary district in the West.
[Contains English characters] He performed the Aswamedha and other Vedic sacrifices and bore the शीर्षक of Supreme King of Kings devoted to dharma.
[Contains English characters] In the reign of Simhavarman IV, who ascended the throne in 436 BC, the fallen prestige of the Pallavas was restored.
[Contains English characters] He recovered the territories lost to the Vishnukundins in the north up to the mouth of the Krishna.
[Contains English characters] The early Pallava history from this period onwards is furnished by a dozen or so copper-plate grants in Sanskrit.
[Contains English characters] They are all dated in the regnal years of the kings.
[Contains English characters] With the accession of Nandivarman I, the decline of the early Pallava family was seen.
[Contains English characters] The Kadambas had their aggressions and attacked even the headquarters of the Pallavas with the Pallavas taking retaliatory measures by expelling and invading Kadamba territories in Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] In coastal Andhra the Vishnukundins established their ascendency.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava authority was confined to Tondaimandalam.
[Contains English characters] With the accession of Simhavishnu, father of Mahendravarman I, c.
[Contains English characters] 575 BC, the Pallava revival began in the south.
[Contains English characters] The incursion of the Kalabhras and the confusion in the Tamil country was broken by the Pandya Kadungon and the Pallava Simhavishnu.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava kingdom began to gain both in territory and influence over the South Indian peninsula and were a regional power by the end of the 6th century.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas exercised control over their southern neighbours of Cholas and Pandyas.
[Contains English characters] But their history is marked by the continuous conflict with the Badami Chalukyas.
[Contains English characters] Narasimhavarma I and Paramesvaravarma I were the kings who stand out with glorious achievements in both military and architectural spheres.
[Contains English characters] Nandivarma II built the Shore Temple.
[Contains English characters] During the thirteenth and the fourteenth centuries CE, a small principality of the Kadava dynasty came into brief prominence.
[Contains English characters] These rulers claimed descent from the Pallavas.
[Contains English characters] The notable rulers of this dynasty are Kopperunchinga I, and his son and successor Kopperunchinga II .
[Contains English characters] Together they extended the influence of their kingdom and played a major part in the ultimate demise of the Chola dynasty.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas were followers of Hinduism and made gifts of land to gods and brahmins.
[Contains English characters] In line with the prevalent customs, some of the rulers performed the Aswamedha and other Vedic sacrifices.
[Contains English characters] They were, however, tolerant of other faiths.
[Contains English characters] The Chinese monk Xuanzang who visited Kanchipuram during the reign of Narasimhavarman I reported that there were 100 Buddhist monasteries, and 80 temples in Kanchipuram.
[Contains English characters] Mahendravarman I was initially a patron of the जैन धर्म faith.
[Contains English characters] He later re-converted to Hinduism under the influence of the Saiva saint Appar with the revival of Hinduism during the Bhakti movement in South India.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas were instrumental in the transition from rock-cut architecture to stone temples.
[Contains English characters] The earliest examples of Pallava constructions are rock-cut temples dating from 610–690 CE and structural temples between 690–900 CE.
[Contains English characters] A number of rock-cut cave temples bear the inscription of the Pallava king, Mahendravarman I and his successors.
[Contains English characters] The greatest accomplishments of the Pallava architecture are the rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] There are excavated pillared halls and monolithic shrines known as rathas in Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] Early temples were mostly dedicated to Shiva.
[Contains English characters] The Kailasanatha temple in Kanchipuram and the Shore Temple built by Narasimhavarman II are fine examples of the Pallava style temples.
