[Contains English characters] The expression limitations and exceptions to copyright refers to situations in which the exclusive rights granted to authors, or their assignees under copyright law do not apply.
[Contains English characters] Some critics prefer to regard limitations and exceptions as user rights; that is, rather than cutting down or modifying some idealized form of copyright, user rights provide an essential balance to the rights of copyright owners.
[Contains English characters] There is no consensus amongst copyright experts on this point; see for example the National Research Councils Digital Agenda Report, note 1. The concept of user rights has also been recognized by courts, including the Canadian Supreme Court in CCH Canadian Ltd v.
[Contains English characters] Law Society of Upper Canada, which classed fair dealing as such a user right.
[Contains English characters] These kinds of disagreements in philosophy are quite common in the philosophy of copyright, where debates about jurisprudential reasoning tend to act as proxies for more substantial disagreements about good policy.
[Contains English characters] Two important examples of limitations and exceptions to copyright are the fair use doctrine found in the United States, and the fair dealing doctrine found in many other common law countries.
[Contains English characters] Other more fundamental boundaries of copyright are caused by thresholds of originality, a threshold below which objects cease to be copyrightable, the idea-expression dichotomy, the public domain and the effect of Crown copyright.
[Contains English characters] Even copyright maximalists might interpret these as defining copyright, rather than being limitations or exceptions to it.
[Contains English characters] In addition copyright can only protect the artists expression of his/her work and not the ideas, systems, or factual information conveyed in it.
[Contains English characters] Likewise, the US court systems have determined that stock characters are also uncopyrightable.
[Contains English characters] While fair use in the United States is popularly understood as the only limitation to an authors exclusive rights, it is only one of several important limitations.
[Contains English characters] Section 106 of the U. S. copyright law, which defines the exclusive rights in copyrighted works, is subject to sections 107 through 122, which limit the copyright holders exclusive rights.
[Contains English characters] In the USA, the United Kingdom, and several other countries, it is legal to produce alternate versions of a copyrighted work to provide improved access to a work for blind and visually impaired persons without permission from the copyright holder.
[Contains English characters] The scope of copyright limitations and exceptions became a subject of significant controversy within various nations in the late 1990s and early 2000s, largely due to the impact of digital technology, the changes in national copyright legislations for compliance with TRIPS, and the enactment of anti-circumvention rules in response to the WIPO Copyright Treaty.
[Contains English characters] Defenders of copyright exemptions fear that digital rights management technology, which they sometimes call digital restrictions management, will massively reduce the scope of important exceptions.
[Contains English characters] Their opponents believe that if existing exemptions are allowed to continue, they will necessarily allow huge amounts of private copying or large-scale copyright infringement — if consumers can make a copy of a CD for their car, they can give MP3 files to everyone.
[Contains English characters] The development of permissive DRM, such as that formerly employed by iTunes, has not ended these debates.
[Contains English characters] Limitations and exceptions are also the subject of significant regulation by international treaties.
[Contains English characters] These treaties have harmonized the exclusive rights which must be provided by copyright laws, and the Berne three-step test operates to constrain the kinds of copyright exceptions and limitations which individual nations can enact.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, international copyright treaties place almost no requirements on national governments to provide exemptions from exclusive rights; a notable exception to this is Article 10 of the Berne Convention, which guarantees a limited right to make quotations from copyrighted works.
[Contains English characters] The convention also allows exceptions for educational reasons under article 10 - although the extent of this exemption has been interpreted differently in different countries.

[Contains English characters] Like many of his friends, he began to play football in the streets of his neighborhood.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldos actual date of birth is September 18, 1976, however, his father did not register his birth certificate until September 22 1976 so some discrepancy has existed as to his actual birth date.
[Contains English characters] In April 1999, Ronaldo married Milene Domingues.
[Contains English characters] The marriage lasted four years and ended in divorce.
[Contains English characters] The couple had a son, Ronald .
[Contains English characters] In 2005, Ronaldo got engaged to Brazilian model and MTV VJ Daniela Cicarelli, who became pregnant but suffered a miscarriage; their relationship lasted 3 months after their engagement.
[Contains English characters] He ended his relationship with Brazilian supermodel Raica Oliveira in December 2006. Writer Andrew Downie asserted a correlation between Ronaldos personal life and performance on the pitch, noting that his most prolific periods of goalscoring have coincided with the times when he was happily married.
[Contains English characters] In 2005, Ronaldo became co-owner of A1 Team Brazil, alongside Brazilian motorsports legend Emerson Fittipaldi.
[Contains English characters] The team participates in the A1 Grand Prix series, with Nelson Piquet, Jr.
[Contains English characters] , Tony Kanaan and João Paulo Oliveira as drivers for the debut season.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldos football abilities were first recognised when he was 14. He was recommended to the Brazil youth team by World Cup winner Jairzinho, who also arranged for his own former club, Cruzeiro Esporte Clube, to sign him when he was old enough for a professional contract.
[Contains English characters] साचा:FactRonaldo scored 12 goals in 13 games in the Brazilian National Championship, and in the Minas Gerais State Championship he scored all three goals in Cruzeiros 3-1 victory against arch-rival Atlético Mineiro.
[Contains English characters] After being scouted by Piet de Visser, he was soon transferred for US$6 million to PSV Eindhoven, where he scored 42 goals in 46 league games and reached a total of 55 goals in 57 official appearances.
[Contains English characters] Later he attracted the attention of Spains FC Barcelona.
[Contains English characters] He played for Barça in the 1996-97 season, scoring 47 in 49 on the way to leading the Catalan side to UEFA Cup Winners Cup triumph .
[Contains English characters] Inter Milan swooped to sign him the following year, and Ronaldo duly helped them repeat his former sides cup-winning run, this time in the UEFA Cup.
[Contains English characters] As of 2006, Ronaldo is the last player to score more than 30 goals in 1 season in the Spanish La Liga.
[Contains English characters] On 21 November 1999, during a Serie A match against Lecce, Ronaldo felt his knee buckle and was forced to limp off the pitch.
[Contains English characters] Medical exams after the match confirmed that the striker had ruptured a tendon in his right knee and would require surgery.
[Contains English characters] During his first comeback on April 12, 2000, he played only seven minutes during the first leg of the coppa italia final against Lazio before injuring his knee for a second time.
[Contains English characters] After two operations and 20 months of rehabilitation, Ronaldo came back for the 2002 FIFA World Cup, helping Brazil win their fifth World Cup शीर्षक.
[Contains English characters] Later in 2002 he won the World Player of the Year award for the third time, and transferred from Inter to रेआल माद्रिद for approximately €39,000,000, after frequent disputes with Inter coach Héctor Cúper.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact His transfer to Madrid was the subject of a media frenzy not just laced with the usual hype because of his reputation, but more so because he was now the third successive Galactico signed in as many years by the Spanish giants as part of their policy of signing the worlds biggest superstar football players in order to maintain their levels of success whilst broadening their reaches of fame.
[Contains English characters] साचा:FactRonaldo was such a well-known signing that sales of his shirt on the day of his signing alone broke all records the world over.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact Proof of his fame came with the fact that even though Ronaldo was sidelined through injury until October 2002, fans continued to chant his name in the stands.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo scored twice in his debut for रेआल माद्रिद.
[Contains English characters] That same reception was observed on the night of the final game of the season against Athletic Bilbao, where Ronaldo scored again to seal his first season with 23 league goals and the La Liga Championship शीर्षक for 2003, which Ronaldo had previously failed to win whilst at FC Barcelona.
[Contains English characters] On 18 January 2007 it was reported that Ronaldo has agreed terms with A. C. Milan for a transfer of about $7.8 million.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo was forced to pay for the remaining period on his contract which tied him to रेआल माद्रिद, only because the latter did not accept to release him, while A. C. Milan were not ready to pay such a sum.
[Contains English characters] On Thursday, 25 January Ronaldo flew from Madrid to Milan to watch A. C. Milan in a cup tie against AS Roma.
[Contains English characters] Statements on the clubs website said that Ronaldo was in Milan for a medical, and that a meeting had been arranged for Monday with रेआल माद्रिद officials to discuss and finalize his transfer to Milan.
[Contains English characters] On January 26 Ronaldo successfully completed his medical tests at the Milanello training complex under the supervision of club doctors, and the transfer completed on 30 January and got the jersey number 99. He made his debut as a substitute for Milan on 11 February 2007, during the 2-1 victory over Livorno.
[Contains English characters] The next game at Siena on 17 February 2007, Ronaldo scored twice and assisted on a third goal in his first start for Milan as they won an exciting game 4-3. In his first season at Milan, Ronaldo scored 7 goals in 14 appearances.
[Contains English characters] After his move to A. C. Milan, Ronaldo joined the list of the few players to have played for both Inter Milan and A.
[Contains English characters] C. Milan in the Milan derby and is the only player to have scored for both sides in the derby game .
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo is also one of the few players to have started for रेआल माद्रिद and FC Barcelona, which also boasts a heated rivalry.
[Contains English characters] However, Ronaldo has never transferred directly between the teams in the derby.
[Contains English characters] Despite his tremendous success over the past decade, Ronaldo has yet to win the UEFA Champions League in his club career which now looks to be on its final stretch.
[Contains English characters] During the 2006-07 season, though Milan won the 2006-07 शीर्षक, Ronaldo was cup-tied with Madrid and ineligible to take part.
[Contains English characters] The closest that he has even been was in 2003 when he helped रेआल माद्रिद to the semi-finals, where they lost to Juventus F. C. . Ronaldo made his international debut for Brazil in 1994, in a friendly match in Recife against Argentina.
[Contains English characters] He went to the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the USA as a 17-year-old but did not play.
[Contains English characters] He came to be known then as Ronaldinho, since Ronaldo Rodrigues de Jesus, his older team-mate on the tournament, was too called Ronaldo .
[Contains English characters] Another Brazilian player, Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, who is widely known as Ronaldinho, would come to be called Ronaldinho Gaúcho when he joined the Brazilian main national team in 1999.Voted the FIFA World Player of the Year in 1996 and 1997, he scored four goals and made three assists during the 1998 FIFA World Cup.
[Contains English characters] The night before the final, he suffered a convulsive fit.
[Contains English characters] He was initially removed from the starting lineup 72 minutes before the match but he requested to play and was later reinstated by coach Mario Zagallo.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo did not perform well and he was injured in a collision with French goalkeeper Fabien Barthez.
[Contains English characters] Brazil lost the final to hosts France 3-0.Adrian Williams, professor of clinical neurology at Birmingham University, said that Ronaldo should not have played, saying that he would have been feeling the after effects of the seizure and that there is no way that he would have been able to perform to the best of his ability within 24 hours of his first fit -- if it was his first fit.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo won the Golden Shoe as the top scorer in the 2002 FIFA World Cup with eight goals.
[Contains English characters] He scored against every team he came up against except England in the quarter finals and scored two in the final against Germany, helping Brazil win their fifth World Cup शीर्षक.
[Contains English characters] He also equaled Pelés Brazilian record of 12 World Cup goals, adding to the four he scored in the 1998 tournament.
[Contains English characters] On June 2 2004, Ronaldo scored an unusual hat-trick for Brazil against arch-rivals Argentina in a CONMEBOL qualifier for the 2006 World Cup, scoring all three of Brazils goals from the penalty spot, winning all the penalties himself.
[Contains English characters] In the 2006 FIFA World Cup, although Brazil won their first two group games against Croatia and Australia, respectively, Ronaldo was repeatedly jeered for being overweight and slow .
[Contains English characters] Nonetheless, coach Carlos Alberto Parreira kept him in the starting lineup in face of calls to have Ronaldo replaced.
[Contains English characters] With his two goals against Japan in the 2006 FIFA World Cup, he became the 20th player ever to score in three different FIFA World Cups.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo scored in the 1998, 2002 and 2006 FIFA World Cups.
[Contains English characters] On June 27 2006, he broke the all-time World Cup Finals scoring record of 14, held by Gerd Müller after scoring his 15th World Cup goal against Ghana in the 2006 FIFA World Cup Round of 16. He also equaled a much less talked about mark: with his third goal of the 2006 World Cup, Ronaldo became only the second player ever to score at least three goals in each of three World Cups.
[Contains English characters] However, Brazil was eliminated by France 1-0 in the quarter-finals.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo is currently the third highest all-time scorer of the Brazil national football team, with 66 goals.
[Contains English characters] He trails second place Zico, 66, and first place pele, 77.Following the 2006 World Cup, Ronaldo had surgery on July 16, 2006, to remove calcifications from his left tibia.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo became a United Nations Development Programme Goodwill Ambassador in 2000. No one should be doomed to a life of poverty, whether by birth or as a consequence of war, Ronaldo said.
[Contains English characters] Ronaldo has also supported numerous Israeli and Palestinian childrens charities and conducted a tour of Israel and the West Bank.

[Contains English characters] This wiki facilitates the localisation and internationalisation of the MediaWiki interface.
[Contains English characters] You may have changed many messages here on Wikipedia to use your language for your language profile, but if you would log in to for example the English language Wiktionary, you would not be able to use the interface as well translated as here.
[Contains English characters] If you wish to contribute to better support of your language in MediaWiki, as well as for many MediaWiki extensions, please visit Betawiki, create an account and request translator priviledges.
[Contains English characters] You can see the current status of localisation of your language on meta and do not forget to get in touch with others that may already be working on your language on Betawiki.
[Contains English characters] If you have any further questions, please let me know on my talk page on the Dutch Wikipedia.
[Contains English characters] We will try and assist you as much as possible, for example by importing all messages from a local wiki for you to start with.
[Contains English characters] You can also find us on the Freenode IRC network in the channel #mediawiki-i18n where we would be happy to help you get started.
[Contains English characters] Thank you very much for your attention and I do hope to see some of you on Betawiki soon!

[Contains English characters] What did happen in Nanded 1708 ?
[Contains English characters] Two Pathan brothers Gul Khan and Attaullah Khan had taken up employment in Guru Ji’s camp, as long as Mata Sahib Kaur stayed in Nanded, she looked after the security arrangements.
[Contains English characters] There was always an armed guard outside the tent.
[Contains English characters] The Pathans knew about Mata Ji’s departure to Delhi and they bided their time.
[Contains English characters] On a cold November night Gul Khan struck with a dagger that pierced Guru ji’s back.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji subsequently disposed of Gul and Attaullah Khan with his sword.
[Contains English characters] The emperor Bahadur Shah was aware of the conspiracy and was awaiting news.
[Contains English characters] In order to show sympathy towards Guru Ji he despatched his British surgeon Dr Cole to attend to Guru Ji’s wound.
[Contains English characters] The surgeon was a very capable doctor and he cleaned and stitched up the wound and stayed at Guru Ji’s side for nearly three weeks.
[Contains English characters] No doctor will leave a patients side unless he is absolutely sure that the patient had made a full recovery especially as he had been sent by the emperor.
[Contains English characters] This is born out in Shi Ranbirs book Yugh Purush and Lala Daulat Rams Swam-e-Umri.
[Contains English characters] We can be sure that Guru Gobind Singh Ji made a full recovery from the attack.
[Contains English characters] The truth is that Guru Ji recovered from the wound but knew how events were going to unfold, he gathered his Sikhs in Nanded and told them in no uncertain terms that Gods will was such that his time on Earth was ending .
[Contains English characters] He spoke the following lines of gurbani : When the soul becomes one with Brahama we assume the universal role of air.
[Contains English characters] Why need we come back to this world ?
[Contains English characters] Birth and death occur according to Gods Will.
[Contains English characters] When we realise this mystery of God’s Will, we will rest in peace.
[Contains English characters] ’ Sensing their feelings Guru Ji consoled them with the following : Whoever works in obedience to Self moves away from God and into suffering.
[Contains English characters] ’ From these words it can be seen that Guru Ji accepted Gods Will.
[Contains English characters] How could he say such things and then deceive his Sikhs?
[Contains English characters] The Sikhs realised that Guru Ji was preparing to depart from this world in accordance with Gods Will.
[Contains English characters] They came to Guru Ji and asked “Sahib Ji, to whose care are you leaving us and who will guide the Khalsa in your absence?
[Contains English characters] ” as mentioned by Dr Ganda Singh in his book.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji spoke softly “ The Khalsa will be entrusted to Akal Purkh”.
[Contains English characters] The Sikhs again asked “Who will adorn the Gurgaddi and be available for darshan? ”. This indeed was a very relevant question which had far reaching significance for the future of the Khalsa and all those who have faith in Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh Ji also being well aware of the chaos that would follow his passing had Aadh Granth Sahib Ji brought and opened with due respect and asked all Sikhs to assemble before it.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji spoke “ Listen, my beloved Khalsa Ji, the Gurgaddi is always given to a follower.
[Contains English characters] You are all my followers.
[Contains English characters] Out of you five came who offered me their heads for sacrifice.
[Contains English characters] They died and were reborn.
[Contains English characters] After I administered the baptism of the double-edged sword to them I also sought the same baptism from them.
[Contains English characters] They assumed the role of Guru Khalsa and I became their follower.
[Contains English characters] They were the five Beloved Ones and whenever five full-fledged Singhs assemble they represent the Guru in person.
[Contains English characters] This should be taken as an article of faith with you.
[Contains English characters] The second point I want to stress in that bani is Guru and Guru resides in his word.
[Contains English characters] This bani has been uttered as divine revelation.
[Contains English characters] Ever since Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Aadh Granth he conducted himself according to its teachings by recognising its superior status.
[Contains English characters] So the spiritual Guruship will rest with Aadh Granth Sahib Ji, no other person after me will become Guru.
[Contains English characters] Guru now rests with Aadh Granth Sahib Ji.
[Contains English characters] ” This concept of the Guru was emphasised by poets like Ratten Singh Bhangu, in Panth Parkash writes : Thereafter Guru Ji asked five Sikhs - Bhai Dharam Singh, Bhai Santokh Singh, Bhai Sahib Singh, Bhai Gurbaksh Singh Anandpuria and Bhai Deep Singh – to stand, then after saying prayers Guru Gobind Singh Ji went around the Granth Sahib five times and offered five paise and a coconut as a token of having passed the Guruship to the holy scriptures.
[Contains English characters] So Aadh Granth Sahib became Guru Granth Sahib Ji the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji opened Guru Granth Sahib Ji at random and read a shabad which indicates the permanent abode of the enlightened Guru, where, by remembrance of Gods Name happiness is attained and all desires fulfilled – Abchall Nagar Gobind Guru Ka, naam japat sukh paya.
[Contains English characters] These events are described by Sant Atam Das Udasi as an eye witness account in his book ‘Gojh Katha’.
[Contains English characters] On the following day Guru Ji rose early took his daily bath and dressed in saffron clothing and appeared before the Sikhs who had assembled.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji had a sandlewood pyre setup at the place where now the Gurdwara Hazur Sahib now stands.
[Contains English characters] All stood with anxious looks on their faces, but Guru Ji was in buoyant spirits.
[Contains English characters] He knew the state of mind of the Sikhs, in order to console them he spoke thus ; It was on Pancham Sudi Katak day in November 1708 Guru Ji went to the stables and said farewell to each and every of his horses.
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji heard the whole of Sodar Path prayer and asked all the Sikhs to reassemble.
[Contains English characters] He then asked Bhai Mana Singh ragi to sing the shabad ; Guru Ji then recited The Japji Sahib morning prayer and the following couplet from Bachittar Natak loudly; Guru Ji in full battle dress and armaments then loudly greeted everyone with “Waheguru Ji ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji ki fateh” and then entered the tent prepared for him which contained the sandlewood pyre.
[Contains English characters] Accompanying him into the enclosure was Mahatma Atam Dass, Balu Hasna, Sant Ishar Singh Udasi among others, all were reciting “Satnam Waheguru” .
[Contains English characters] Guru Ji stepped forward and sat on the sandlewood in the meditational pose and breathed his last.
[Contains English characters] Those inside the enclosure realised that the inevitable had happened.
[Contains English characters] They bowed reverently and left the the canvas wall, they looked and saw flames rising towards the sky.
[Contains English characters] Some historians have said that Guru Ji set the wood ablaze with his yogic powers, a recent instance of a Nihang Singh of Ganj Dadwara who produced fire from his own body and burnt himself confirms the possibilities of such things, this could explain why only a small kirpan was found afterwards.
[Contains English characters] The view of historian and author Giani Ishar Singh Nara is that Guru Gobind Singh, like Guru Nanak Dev Ji, disappeared bodily from inside the enclosure.
[Contains English characters] Some have taken the view that this amounted to suicide, but those who have studied Guru Ji’s philosophy of life and his compositions will not agree with this.
[Contains English characters] Great souls sent by God are aware of future events and make preparations for them.
[Contains English characters] After communion with God, Guru Gobind Singh Ji came to know that on Katak Sudi panchmi he would depart this world so he prepared for it.
[Contains English characters] Just as a commanders orders are carried out by rank and file, so the unalterable divine Will of God is obligatory to all.
[Contains English characters] Sri Krishan Maharaj used his powers to save Drupadi in the court of Druyodhan but when his time came he did not obstruct the hunter from hitting him with his arrow while he lay under a tree in the jungle.
[Contains English characters] Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, while meditating at Baba Bakala had to employ his spiritual powers to help Makhan Shahs ship, but when it came to sacrificing his own life for the sake of Dharam he did nothing.
[Contains English characters] When Guru Arjan Dev Ji was cruelly tortured by the orders of emperor Jahangir his devotee Mian Mir Ji asked permission to approach the emperor on Guru Ji’s behalf but Guru Ji forebade it saying this was the un- alterable Will of Waheguru.
[Contains English characters] In the same way Guru Gobind Singh Ji bowed to the will of God.
[Contains English characters] Having seen how Guru Ji addressed his Sikhs on his final day, calling “Khalsa Guru, Guru Khalsa” and having total respect for them and considering that in full view of the whole congregation Guru ji passed on the Guruship to Aadh Guru Granth Sahib Ji, can anyone really believe that Guru Ji played this as a charade and would deceive his Sikhs ?

[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh ji The tenth and the last Guru or Prophet-teacher of the Sikh faith, was born Gobind Rai Sodhi on Poh 7, 1723 sk/22 December 1666 at Patna, in Bihar.
[Contains English characters] His father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, the Ninth Guru, was then travelling across Bengal and Assam.
[Contains English characters] Returning to Patna in 1670, he directed his family to return to the Punjab.
[Contains English characters] On the site of the house at Patna in which Gobind Rai was born and where he spent his early childhood now stands a sacred shrine, Takht Sri Harimandar Sahib, one of the five most honoured seats of religious authority for the Sikhs.
[Contains English characters] Gobind Rai was escorted to Anandpur on the foothills of the Sivaliks where he reached in March 1672 and where his early education included reading and writing of Punjabi, Braj, Sanskrit and Persian.
[Contains English characters] He was barely nine years of age when a sudden turn came in his life as well as in the life of tile community he was destined to lead.
[Contains English characters] Early in 1675, a group Kashmiri Brahmans, drivels to desperation by the religious fanaticism of the Mughals General, Iftikar Khan, visited Anandpur to seek Guru Tegh Bahadurs intercession.
[Contains English characters] As the Guru sat reflecting what to do, young Gobind Rai, arriving there in company with his playmates, asked Why he looked so preoccupied.
[Contains English characters] The father, as records Kuir Singh in his Gurbilas Patshahi 10, replied, Grave are the burdens the earth bears.
[Contains English characters] She will be redeemed only if a truly worthy person comes forward to lay down his head.
[Contains English characters] Distress will then be expunged and happiness ushered in.
[Contains English characters] None could be worthier than yourself to make such a sacrifice, remarked Gobind Rai in his innocent manner.
[Contains English characters] Guru Tegh Bahadur soon aftenwards proceeded to the imperial capital, Delhi, and courted death on 11 November 1675. Guru Gobind Singh was formally installed Guru on the Baisakhi day of 1733 Bk/29 March 1676. In the midst of his engagement with the concerns of the community, he gave attention to the mastery of physical skills and literary accomplishment.
[Contains English characters] He had grown into a comely youth spare, lithe of limb and energetic.
[Contains English characters] He had a natural genius for poetic composition and his early years were assiduously given to this pursuit.
[Contains English characters] The Var Sri Bhagauti Ji Ki, popularly called Chandi di Var.
[Contains English characters] written in 1684, was his first composition and his only major work in the Punjabi language.
[Contains English characters] The poem depicted the legendary contest between the gods and the demons as described in the Markandeya Purana .
[Contains English characters] The choice of a warlike theme for this and a number of his later compositions such as the two Chandi Charitras, mostly in Braj, was made to infuse martial spirit among his followers to prepare them to stand up against injustice and tyranny.
[Contains English characters] Much of Guru Gobind Singhs creative literary work was done at Paonta he had founded on the banks of the River Yamuna and to which site he had temporarily shifted in April 1685. Poetry as such was, however, not his aim.
[Contains English characters] For him it was a means of revealing the divine principle and concretizing a personal vision of the Supreme Being that had been vouchsafed to him.
[Contains English characters] His Japu and the composition known as Akal Ustati are in this tenor.
[Contains English characters] Through his poetry he preached love and equality and a strictly ethical and moral code of conduct.
[Contains English characters] He preached the worship of the One Supreme Being, deprecating idolatry and superstitious beliefs and observances.
[Contains English characters] The glorification of the sword itself which he eulogized as Bhaguati was to secure fulfilment of Godsjustice.
[Contains English characters] The sword was never meant as a symbol of aggression, and it was never to be used for self-aggrandizement.
[Contains English characters] It was the emblem of manliness and self-respect and was to be used only in self-defence, as a last resort.
[Contains English characters] For Guru Gobind Singh said in a Persian couplet in his Zafarnamah: When all other means have failed,It is but lawful to take to the sword.
[Contains English characters] During his stay at Paonta, Guru Gobind Singh availed himself of his spare time to practise different forms of manly exercises, such as riding, swimming and archery.
[Contains English characters] His increasing influence among the people and the martial exercises of his men excited the jealousy of the neighbouring Rajpat hill rulers who led by Raja Fateh Chand of Garhval collected a host to attack him.
[Contains English characters] But they were worsted in an action at Bhangam, about 10 km northeast of Paonta, on 18 Assu 1745 sk/18 September 1688. Soon there after Guru Gobind Singh left Paonta and returned to Anandpur which he fortified in view of the continuing hostility of the Rajput chiefs as well as of the repressive policy of the imperial government at Delhi.
[Contains English characters] The Guru and his Sikhs were involved in a battle with a Mughal commander, Alif Khan, at Nadaun on the left bank of the Beas, about 30 km southeast of Kangra, on 22 Chet 1747 Bk/20 March 1691. Describing the battle in stirring verse in Bachitra Natak, he said that Alif Khan fled in utter disarray without being able to give any attention to his camp.
[Contains English characters] Among several other skirmishes that occurred was the Husaim battle fought against Husain K an, an imperial general, which resulted in a decisive victory for the Sikhs.
[Contains English characters] Following the appointment in 1694 of the liberal Prince Muazzam as viceroy of northwestern region including Punjab, there was however a brief respite from pressure from the ruling authority.
[Contains English characters] In 1698, Guru Gobind Singh issued directions to Sikh sangats or communities in different parts not to acknowledge masands, the local ministers, against whom he had heard complaints.
[Contains English characters] Sikhs, he instructed, should come to Anandpur straight without any intermediaries and bring their offerings personally.
[Contains English characters] The Guru thus established direct relationship with his Sikhs and addressed them as his Khalsa, Persian term used for crown-lands as distinguished from feudal chiefs.
[Contains English characters] The institution of the Khalsa was given concrete form on 30 March 1699 when Sikhs had gathered at Anandpur in large numbers for the annual festival of Baisakhi.
[Contains English characters] Gurb Gobind Singh appeared before the assembly dramatically on that day with a naked sword in hand and, to quote Kuir Singh, Gurbilas Patshahz 10, spoke: Is there present a true Sikh who would offer his head to the Guru as a sacrifice?
[Contains English characters] The words numbed the audience who looked on in awed silence.
[Contains English characters] The Gurb repeated the call.
[Contains English characters] At the third call Daya Ram, a Sobti Khatri of Lahore, arose and humbly walked behind the Guru to a tent near by.
[Contains English characters] The Gurb returned with his sword dripping blood, and asked for another head.
[Contains English characters] At this Dharam Das, a Jat from Hastinapur, came forward and was taken inside the enclosure.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh made three more calls.
[Contains English characters] Muhkam Chand, a washerman from Dvarka, Himmat, a water-carrier from Jagannath puri, and Sahib Chand, a barber from Bidar responded one after another and advanced to offer their heads.
[Contains English characters] All the five were led back from the tent dressed alike in saffron-coloured raiment topped over with neatly tied turbans similarly dyed, with swords dangling by their sides.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh then introduced khande da pahul, i. e. initiation by sweetened water churned with a double-edged broad sword .
[Contains English characters] Those five Sikhs were the first to be initiated.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh called them Panj Piare, the five devoted spirits beloved of the Guru.
[Contains English characters] These five, three of them from the so-called low-castes, a Ksatriya and a Jatt, formed the nucleus of the self-abnegating, martial and casteless fellowship of the Khalsa.
[Contains English characters] All of them surnamed Singh, meaning lion, were required to wear in future the five symbols of the Khalsa, all beginning with the letter K the kes or long hair and beard, kangha, a comb in the kes to keep it tidy as against the recluses who kept it matted in token of their having renounced the world, Kara, a steel bracelet, kachch, short breeches, and kirpan, a sword.
[Contains English characters] They were enjoined to succour the helpless and fight the oppressor, to have faith in one God and to consider all human beings equal, irrespective of caste and creed.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh then himself received initiatory rites from five disciples, now invested with authority as Khalsa, and had his name changed from Gobind Rai to Gobind Singh.
[Contains English characters] Hail, as the poet subsequently sang, Gobind Singh who is himself Master as well as disciple.
[Contains English characters] Further injunctions were laid down for the Sikhs.
[Contains English characters] They must never cut or trim their hair and beards, nor smoke tobacco.
[Contains English characters] A Sikh must not have sexual relationship outside the marital bond, nor eat the flesh of an animal killed slowly in the Muslim way .
[Contains English characters] These developments alarmed the casteridden Rajput chiefs of the Sivalik hills.
[Contains English characters] They rallied under the leadership of the Raja of Bilaspur, in whose territory lay Anandpur, to forcibly evict Guru Gobind Singh from his hilly citadel.
[Contains English characters] Their repeated expeditions during 1700-04 however proved abortive .
[Contains English characters] They at last petitioned Emperor Aurangzeb for help.
[Contains English characters] In concert with contingents sent under imperial orders by the governor of Lahore and those of the faujdar of Sirhind, they marched upon Anandpur and laid a siege to the fort in Jeth 1762 sk/May 1705. Over the months, the Guru and his Sikhs firmly withstood their successive assaults despite dire scarcity of food resulting from the prolonged blockade.
[Contains English characters] While the besieged were reduced to desperate straits, the besiegers too were chagrined at the tenacity with which the Sikhs held out.
[Contains English characters] At this stagy the besiegers offered, on solemn oaths of Quran, safe exit to the Sikhs if they quit Anandpur.
[Contains English characters] At last, the town was evacuated during the night of Poh suds 1, 1762 sk/5-6 December 1705. But soon, as the Guru and his Sikhs came out, the hill monarchs and their Mughal allies set upon them in full fury.
[Contains English characters] In the ensuing confusion many Sikhs were killed and all of the Gurus baggage, including most of the precious manuscripts, was lost.
[Contains English characters] The Guru himself was able to make his way to Chamkaur, 40 km southwest of Anandpur, with barely 40 Sikhs and his two elder sons.
[Contains English characters] There the imperial army, following closely on his heels, caught up with him.
[Contains English characters] His two sons, Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh and all but five of the Sikhs fell in the action that took place on 7 December 1705. The five surviving Sikhs bade the Guru to save himself in order to reconsolidate the Khalsa.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh with three of his Sikhs escaped into the wilderness of the Malva, two of his Muslim devotees, Gani Khan and Nabi Khan, helping him at great personal risk.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singhs two younger sons, Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, and his mother, Mata Gujari, were after the evacuation of Anandpur betrayed by their old servant and escort, Gangu, to the faujdar of Sirhind, who had the young children executed on 13 December 1705. Their grandmother died the same day.
[Contains English characters] Befriended by another Muslim admirer, Ral Kalha of Raikot, Guru Gobind Singh reached Dina in the heart of the Malva.
[Contains English characters] There he enlisted a few hundred warriors of the Brar clan, and also composed his famous letter, Zafarnamah or the Epistle of Victory, in Persian verse, addressed to Emperor Aurangzeb.
[Contains English characters] The letter was a severe indictment of the Emperor and his commanders who had perjured their oath and treacherously attacked him once he was outside the safety of his fortification at Anandpur.
[Contains English characters] It emphatically reiterated the sovereignty of morality in the affairs of State as much as in the conduct of human beings and held the means as important as the end.
[Contains English characters] Two of the Sikhs, Daya Singh and Dharam Singh, were despatched with the Zafarnamah to Ahmadnagar in the South to deliver it to Aurangzeb, then in camp in that town.
[Contains English characters] From Dina, Guru Gobind Singh continued his westward march until, finding the host close upon his heels, he took position astride the water pool of Khidrana to make a last-ditch stand.
[Contains English characters] The fighting on 29 December 1705 was hard and desperate.
[Contains English characters] In spite of their overwhelming numbers, the Mughal troops failed to capture the Guru and had to retire in defeat.
[Contains English characters] The most valorous part in this battle was played by a group of 40 Sikhs who had deserted the Guru at Anandpur during the long siege, but who, chided by their womenfolk at home, had come back under the leadership of a brave and devoted woman, Mai Bhago, to redeem themselves.
[Contains English characters] They had fallen fighting desperately to check the enemys advance towards the Gurus position.
[Contains English characters] The Guru blessed the 40 dead as 40 mukte, i. e. the 40 Saved Ones.
[Contains English characters] The site is now marked by a sacred shrine and tank and the town which has grown around them is called Muktsar, the Pool of liberations.
[Contains English characters] After spending some time in the Lakkhi Jungle country, Guru Gobind Singh arrived at Talvandi Sabo, now called Damdama Sahib, on 20 January 1706. During his stay there of over nine months, a number of Sikhs rejoined him.
[Contains English characters] He prepared a fresh recension of Sikh Scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, with the celebrated scholar, Bhai Mani Singh, as his amanuensis.
[Contains English characters] From the number of scholars who had rallied round Guru Gobind Singh and from the literary activity initiated, the place came to be known as the Gurus Kashi or seat of learning like Varanasi.
[Contains English characters] The epistle Zafarnamah sent by Guru Gobind Singh from Dina seems to have touched the heart of Emperor Aurungzeb.
[Contains English characters] He forthwith invited him for a meeting.
[Contains English characters] According to Ahkam-i-Alamgiri, the Emperor had a letter written to the deputy governor of Lahore, Munim Khan, to conciliate the Guru and make the required arrangements for his journey to the Deccan.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh had, however, already left for the South on 30 October 1706. He was in the neighbourhood of Baghor, in Rajasthan, when the news arrived of the death of the Emperor at Ahmadnagar on 20 February 1707. The Guru there upon decided to return to the Punjab, via Shahjahanabad .
[Contains English characters] That was the time when the sons of the deceased Emperor were preparing to contest succession.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh despatched for the help of the eldest claimant, the liberal Prince Muazzam, a token contingent of Sikhs which took part in the battle of Jajau, decisively won by the Prince who ascended the throne with the title of Bahadur Shah.
[Contains English characters] The new Emperor invited Guru Gobind Singh for a meeting which took place at Agra on 23 July 1707. Emperor Bahadur Shah had at this time to move against the Kachhvaha Rajputs of Amber and then to the Deccan where his youngest brother, Kam Baksh, had raised the standard of revolt.
[Contains English characters] The Guru accompanied him and, as says Tarzkh-i-Bahadur Shahi, he addressed assemblies of people on the way preaching the word of Guru Nanak.
[Contains English characters] The two camps crossed the River Tapti between 11 and 14 June 1708 and the Ban-Ganga on 14 August, arriving at Nanded, on the Godavari, towards the end of August.
[Contains English characters] While Bahadur Shah proceeded further South, Guru Gobind Singh decided to stay awhile at Nanded.
[Contains English characters] Here he met a Bairagi recluse, Madho Das, whom he converted a Sikh administering to him the vows of the Khalsa, renaming him Gurbakhsh Singh .
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Siligh gave Banda Singh five arrows from his own quiver and an escort, including five of his chosen Sikhs, and directed him to go to the Punjab and carry on the campaign against the tyranny of the provincial overlords.
[Contains English characters] Nawab Wazir Khan of Sirhind had felt concerned at the Emperors conciliatory treatment of Guru Gobind Singh.
[Contains English characters] Their marching together to the South made him jealous, and he charged two of his trusted men with murdering the Guru before his increasing friendship with the Emperor resulted in any harm to him.
[Contains English characters] These two pathans Jamshed Khan and Wasil Beg are the names given in the Guru Kian Sakhian pursued the Guru secretly and overtook him at Nanded, where, according to Sri Gur Sobha by Senapati, a contemporary writer, one of them stabbed the Guru in the left side below the heart as he lay one evening in his chamber resting after the Rahrasi prayer.
[Contains English characters] Before he could deal another blow, Guru Gobind Singh struck him down with his sabre, while his fleeing companion fell under the swords of Sikhs who had rushed in on hearing the noise.
[Contains English characters] As the news reached Bahadur Shahs camp, he sent expert surgeons, including an Englishman, Cole by name, to attend on the Guru.
[Contains English characters] The wound was stitched and appeared to have healed quickly but, as the Guru one day applied strength to pull a stiff bow, it broke out again and bled profusely.
[Contains English characters] This weakened the Guru beyond cure and he passed away on Kattak sudi 5, 1765 Bk/7 October 1708. Before the end came, Guru Gobind Singh had asked for the Sacred Volume to be brought forth.
[Contains English characters] To quote Bhatt Vahi Talauda Parganah Jind: Guru Gobind Singh, the Tenth Master, son of Guru Teg Bahadur, grandson of Guru Hargobind, great-grandson of Guru Arjan, of the family of Guru Ram Das Surajbansi, Gosal clan, Sodhi Khatri, resident of Anandpur, parganah Kahlur, now at Nanded, in the Godavari country in the Deccan, asked Bhai Daya Singh, on Wednesday, 7 October 1708, to fetch Sri Granth Sahib.
[Contains English characters] In obedience to his orders, Daya Singh brought Sri Granth Sahib.
[Contains English characters] The Guru placed before it five pice and a coconut and bowed his head before it.
[Contains English characters] He said to the sangat, It is my commandment: Own Sri Granthji in my place.
[Contains English characters] He who so acknowledges it will obtain his reward.
[Contains English characters] The Guru will rescue him.
[Contains English characters] Know this as the truth.
[Contains English characters] Guru Gobind Singh thus passed on the succession with due ceremony to the Holy Book, the Guru Granth Sahib, ending the line of personal Gurus.
[Contains English characters] The Gurus spirit, he said, will henceforth be in the Granth and the Khalsa.
[Contains English characters] Where the Granth is with any five Sikhs representing the Khalsa, there will the Guru be.
[Contains English characters] The Word enshrined in the Holy Book was always revered by the Gurus as well as by their disciples as of Divine origin.
[Contains English characters] The Guru was the revealer of the Word.
[Contains English characters] One day the Word was to take the place of the Guru.
[Contains English characters] The inevitable came to pass when Guru Gobind Singh declared the Guru Granth Sahib as his successor.
[Contains English characters] It was only through the Word that the Guruship could be made everlasting.
[Contains English characters] The Word as contained in the Guru Granth Sahib was henceforth, and for all time to come to be the Guru for the Sikhs.

[Contains English characters] Although goalkeepers have this specific award for their position, they are still eligible for the Golden Ball as well, as when Oliver Kahn was awarded in २००२. [Contains English characters] Only teams that qualified for the second round are considered.
[Contains English characters] The winners of this award earn the FIFA Fair Play Trophy, a diploma, a fair play medal for each player and official, and $५०,००० worth of football equipment to be used for youth development.
[Contains English characters] The FIFA Award for the Most Entertaining Team is a fairly new accolade for the FIFA World Cup.
[Contains English characters] It is a subjectively awarded prize for the team which has done the most to entertain the public with a positive approach to the game.
[Contains English characters] The award is always organized through public participation in a poll.
[Contains English characters] Recent awards have been determined by an Internet vote which may not fairly and accurately represent fan demographics.

[Contains English characters] Success in a military campaign is considered a strategic victory, while the success in a military engagement is a tactical victory.
[Contains English characters] In terms of human emotion, victory is accompanied with strong feelings of elation, and in human behaviour is often accompanied with movements and poses paralleling threat display preceding the combat, associated with the excess endorphin built up preceding and during combat.
[Contains English characters] Victory dances and victory cries similarly parallel war dances and war cries performed before the outbreak of physical violence.
[Contains English characters] Examples of victory behaviour reported in Roman antiquity, where the term originates, are the victory songs of the Batavi mercenaries serving under Gaius Julius Civilis after the victory over Quintus Petillius Cerialis in the Batavian rebellion of 69, and also the abominable song to Wodan, sung by the Langobards at their victory celebration in 579. The sacrificial animal was a goat, around whose head the Langobard danced in a circle while singing their victory hymn .

[Contains English characters] A trophy is a token of victory taken from the defeated party, such as the enemys weapons, or body parts .
[Contains English characters] In mythology, victory is often deified, as in Greek Nike or Roman Victoria.
[Contains English characters] Archetypical victories of good over evil, or of light over dark etc.
[Contains English characters] are a recurring theme in mythology and fairy tales.

[Contains English characters] However, unlike Hollywood, Bollywood does not exist as a physical place.
[Contains English characters] Though some deplore the name, arguing that it makes the industry look like a poor cousin to Hollywood, it has its own entry in the ऑक्सफर्ड इंग्लिश डिक्शनरी.
[Contains English characters] The term Bollywood has origins in the 1970s, when India overtook America as the worlds largest film producer.
[Contains English characters] Credit for the term has been claimed by several different people, including the lyricist, filmmaker and scholar Amit Khanna, and the journalist Bevinda Collaco.
[Contains English characters] The naming scheme for Bollywood was inspired by Tollywood, the name that was used to refer to the cinema of West Bengal.
[Contains English characters] Dating back to 1932, Tollywood was the earliest Hollywood-inspired name, referring to the Bengali film industry based in Tollygunge, which rhymed with Hollywood and was the center of the cinema of India at the time.
[Contains English characters] The name Bollywood later arose as the Bombay-based film industry overtook the one in Tollygunge as the center of the Indian film industry.
[Contains English characters] The 1930s and 1940s were tumultuous times: India was buffeted by the Great Depression, World War II, the Indian independence movement, and the violence of the Partition.
[Contains English characters] Most Bollywood films were unabashedly escapist, but there were also a number of filmmakers who tackled tough social issues, or used the struggle for Indian independence as a backdrop for their plots.
[Contains English characters] In 1937, Ardeshir Irani, of Alam Ara fame, made the first colour film in Hindi, Kisan Kanya.
[Contains English characters] The next year, he made another colour film, Mother India.
[Contains English characters] However, colour did not become a popular feature until the late 1950s.
[Contains English characters] At this time, lavish romantic musicals and melodramas were the staple fare at the cinema.
[Contains English characters] Following Indias independence, the period from the late 1940s to the 1960s are regarded by film historians as the Golden Age of Hindi cinema.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most critically-acclaimed Hindi films of all time were produced during this period.
[Contains English characters] Examples include the Guru Dutt films Pyaasa and Kaagaz Ke Phool and the Raj Kapoor films Awaara and Shree 420 .
[Contains English characters] These films expressed social themes mainly dealing with working-class urban life in India; Awaara presented the city as both a nightmare and a dream, while Pyaasa critiqued the unreality of city life.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most famous epic films of Hindi cinema were also produced at the time, including Mehboob Khans Mother India, which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, and K.
[Contains English characters] Asifs Mughal-e-Azam . V. Shantarams Do Aankhen Barah Haath is believed to have inspired the Hollywood film The Dirty Dozen .
[Contains English characters] Madhumati, directed by Bimal Roy and written by Ritwik Ghatak, popularized the theme of reincarnation in Western popular culture.
[Contains English characters] Other acclaimed mainstream Hindi filmmakers at the time included Kamal Amrohi and Vijay Bhatt.
[Contains English characters] Successful actors at the time included Dev Anand, Dilip Kumar, Raj Kapoor and Guru Dutt, while successful actresses included Nargis, Meena Kumari, Nutan, Madhubala, Waheeda Rehman and Mala Sinha.
[Contains English characters] While commercial Hindi cinema was thriving, the 1950s also saw the emergence of a new Parallel Cinema movement.
[Contains English characters] Though the movement was mainly led by Bengali cinema, it also began gaining prominence in Hindi cinema.
[Contains English characters] Early examples of Hindi films in this movement include Chetan Anands Neecha Nagar and Bimal Roys Two Acres of Land .
[Contains English characters] Their critical acclaim, as well as the latters commercial success, paved the way for Indian neorealism and the Indian New Wave.

[Contains English characters] Bollywood films are mostly musicals, and are expected to contain catchy music in the form of song-and-dance numbers woven into the script.
[Contains English characters] A films success often depends on the quality of such musical numbers.
[Contains English characters] Indeed, a films music is often released before the movie itself and helps increase the audience.
[Contains English characters] Indian audiences expect full value for their money, with a good entertainer generally referred to as paisa vasool, .
[Contains English characters] Songs and dances, love triangles, comedy and dare-devil thrills are all mixed up in a three-hour-long extravaganza with an intermission.
[Contains English characters] Such movies are called masala films, after the Hindi word for a spice mixture.
[Contains English characters] Like masalas, these movies are a mixture of many things such as action, comedy, romance etc.
[Contains English characters] Most films have heroes who are able to fight off villains all by themselves.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood plots have tended to be melodramatic.
[Contains English characters] They frequently employ formulaic ingredients such as star-crossed lovers and angry parents, love triangles, family ties, sacrifice, corrupt politicians, kidnappers, conniving villains, courtesans with hearts of gold, long-lost relatives and siblings separated by fate, dramatic reversals of fortune, and convenient coincidences.
[Contains English characters] There have always been Indian films with more artistic aims and more sophisticated stories, both inside and outside the Bollywood tradition .
[Contains English characters] They often lost out at the box office to movies with more mass appeal.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood conventions are changing, however.
[Contains English characters] A large Indian diaspora in English speaking countries, and increased Western influence at home, have nudged Bollywood films closer to Hollywood models.

[Contains English characters] Despite this, Bollywood continues to play a major role in fashion in India.

[Contains English characters] Bollywood employs people from all parts of India.
[Contains English characters] It attracts thousands of aspiring actors and actresses, all hoping for a break in the industry.
[Contains English characters] Models and beauty contestants, television actors, theatre actors and even common people come to Mumbai with the hope and dream of becoming a star.
[Contains English characters] Just as in Hollywood, very few succeed.
[Contains English characters] Since many Bollywood films are shot abroad, many foreign extras are employed too.
[Contains English characters] Stardom in the entertainment industry is very fickle, and Bollywood is no exception.
[Contains English characters] The popularity of the stars can rise and fall rapidly.
[Contains English characters] Directors compete to hire the most popular stars of the day, who are believed to guarantee the success of a movie .
[Contains English characters] Hence many stars make the most of their fame, once they become popular, by making several movies simultaneously.
[Contains English characters] Only a very few non-Indian actors are able to make a mark in Bollywood, though many have tried from time to time.
[Contains English characters] There have been some exceptions, one recent example is the hit film Rang De Basanti, where the lead actress is Alice Patten, an Englishwoman.
[Contains English characters] Kisna, Lagaan, and The Rising: Ballad of Mangal Pandey also featured foreign actors.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood can be very clannish, and the relatives of film-industry insiders have an edge in getting coveted roles in films or being part of a films crew.
[Contains English characters] Industry connections are no guarantee of a long career: competition is fierce and if film industry scions do not succeed at the box office, their careers will falter.
[Contains English characters] Some of the biggest stars, such as Dharmendra, Amitabh Bachchan, and Shahrukh Khan have succeeded despite total lack of show business connections.

[Contains English characters] Process known as looping in the sound or ADR—with the foley and sound effects added later.
[Contains English characters] This creates several problems, since the sound in these films usually occurs a frame or two earlier or later than the mouth movements or gestures.
[Contains English characters] The actors have to act twice: once on-location, once in the studio—and the emotional level on set is often very difficult to recreate.
[Contains English characters] Commercial Indian films, not just the Hindi-language variety, are known for their lack of ambient sound, so there is a silence underlying everything instead of the background sound and noises usually employed in films to create aurally perceivable depth and environment.
[Contains English characters] The ubiquity of ADR in Bollywood cinema became prevalent in the early 1960s with the arrival of the Arriflex 3 camera, which required a blimp in order to shield the sound of the camera, for which it was notorious, from on-location filming.
[Contains English characters] Commercial Indian filmmakers, known for their speed, never bothered to blimp the camera, and its excessive noise required that everything had to be recreated in the studio.
[Contains English characters] Eventually, this became the standard for Indian films.
[Contains English characters] The trend was bucked in 2001, after a 30-year hiatus of synchronized sound, with the film Lagaan, in which producer-star Aamir Khan insisted that the sound be done on location.
[Contains English characters] This opened up a heated debate on the use and economic feasibility of on-location sound, and several Bollywood films have employed on-location sound since then.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood film music is called filmi music .
[Contains English characters] Songs from Bollywood movies are generally pre-recorded by professional playback singers, with the actors then lip synching the words to the song on-screen, often while dancing.
[Contains English characters] While most actors, especially today, are excellent dancers, few are also singers.
[Contains English characters] One notable exception was Kishore Kumar, who starred in several major films in the 1950s while also having a stellar career as a playback singer. K. L. Saigal, Suraiyya, and Noor Jehan were also known as both singers and actors.
[Contains English characters] Some actors in the last thirty years have sung one or more songs themselves; for a list, see Singing actors and actresses in Indian cinema.
[Contains English characters] Playback singers are prominently featured in the opening credits and have their own fans who will go to an otherwise lackluster movie just to hear their favourites.
[Contains English characters] Going by the quality as well as the quantity of the songs they rendered, most notable singers of Bollywood are Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle, Geeta Dutt, Shamshad Begum and Alka Yagnik among female playback singers; and K. L. Saigal, Talat Mahmood, Mukesh, Mohammed Rafi, Manna Dey, Hemant Kumar, Kishore Kumar, Kumar Sanu, S.
[Contains English characters] P. Balasubramanyam, Udit Narayan and Sonu Nigam among male playback singers.
[Contains English characters] Mohammed Rafi is often considered arguably the finest of the singers that have lent their voice to Bollywood songs, followed by Lata Mangeshkar, who, through the course of a career spanning over six decades, has recorded thousands of songs for Indian movies.
[Contains English characters] The composers of film music, known as music directors, are also well-known.
[Contains English characters] Their songs can make or break a film and usually do.
[Contains English characters] Remixing of film songs with modern beats and rhythms is a common occurrence today, and producers may even release remixed versions of some of their films songs along with the films regular soundtrack albums.
[Contains English characters] The dancing in Bollywood films, especially older ones, is primarily modelled on Indian dance: classical dance styles, dances of historic northern Indian courtesans, or folk dances.
[Contains English characters] In modern films, Indian dance elements often blend with Western dance styles, though it is not unusual to see Western pop and pure classical dance numbers side by side in the same film.
[Contains English characters] The hero or heroine will often perform with a troupe of supporting dancers.
[Contains English characters] Many song-and-dance routines in Indian films feature unrealistically instantaneous shifts of location or changes of costume between verses of a song.
[Contains English characters] If the hero and heroine dance and sing a pas de deux, it is often staged in beautiful natural surroundings or architecturally grand settings.
[Contains English characters] This staging is referred to as a picturisation.
[Contains English characters] Songs typically comment on the action taking place in the movie, in several ways.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, a song is worked into the plot, so that a character has a reason to sing; other times, a song is an externalisation of a characters thoughts, or presages an event that has not occurred yet in the plot of the movie.
[Contains English characters] In this case, the event is almost always two characters falling in love.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films have always used what are now called item numbers.
[Contains English characters] A physically attractive female character, often completely unrelated to the main cast and plot of the film, performs a catchy song and dance number in the film.
[Contains English characters] In older films, the item number may be performed by a courtesan dancing for a rich client or as part of a cabaret show.
[Contains English characters] The dancer Helen was famous for her cabaret numbers.
[Contains English characters] In modern films, item numbers may be inserted as discotheque sequences, dancing at celebrations, or as stage shows.
[Contains English characters] For the last few decades Bollywood producers have been releasing the films soundtrack, as tapes or CDs, before the main movie release, hoping that the music will pull audiences into the cinema later.
[Contains English characters] Often the soundtrack is more popular than the movie.
[Contains English characters] In the last few years some producers have also been releasing music videos, usually featuring a song from the film.
[Contains English characters] However, some promotional videos feature a song which is not included in the movie.
[Contains English characters] The film script or lines of dialogue and the song lyrics are often written by different people.
[Contains English characters] Dialogues are usually written in an unadorned Hindi or Hindustani that would be understood by the largest possible audience.
[Contains English characters] Some movies, however, have used regional dialects to evoke a village setting, or old-fashioned courtly उर्दू भाषा in Mughal era historical films.
[Contains English characters] Contemporary mainstream movies also make great use of English.
[Contains English characters] Some movie scripts are first written in Roman alphabet.
[Contains English characters] Characters may shift from one language to the other to express a certain atmosphere .
[Contains English characters] Cinematic language, whether in dialogues or lyrics, is often melodramatic and invokes God, family, mother, duty, and self-sacrifice liberally.
[Contains English characters] Music directors often prefer working with certain lyricists, to the point that the lyricist and composer are seen as a team.
[Contains English characters] This phenomenon is not unlike the pairings of American composers and songwriters that created old-time Broadway musicals .
[Contains English characters] Song lyrics are usually about love.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood song lyrics, especially in the old movies, frequently use Arabo-Persic Urdu vocabulary.
[Contains English characters] Another source for love lyrics is the long Hindu tradition of poetry about the mythological amours of Krishna, Radha, and the gopis.
[Contains English characters] Many lyrics compare the singer to a devotee and the object of his or her passion to Krishna or Radha.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films are multi-million dollar productions, with the most expensive productions costing up to 100 crores rupees .
[Contains English characters] Sets, costumes, special effects, and cinematography were less than world-class up until the mid-to-late 1990s, although with some notable exceptions.
[Contains English characters] As Western films and television gain wider distribution in India itself, there is an increasing pressure for Bollywood films to attain the same production levels, particularly in areas such as action and special effects.
[Contains English characters] Recent Bollywood films have employed international technicians to improve in these areas, such as Krrish which has action choreographed by Hong Kong based Tony Ching.
[Contains English characters] The increasing accessibility to professional action and special effects, coupled with rising film budgets, has seen an explosion in the action and sci-fi genres.

[Contains English characters] Indian banks and financial institutions were forbidden from lending money to movie studios.

[Contains English characters] Another problem facing Bollywood is widespread copyright infringement of its films.
[Contains English characters] Often, bootleg DVD copies of movies are available before the prints are officially released in cinemas.

[Contains English characters] The Filmfare Awards ceremony is one of the most prominent film events given for Hindi films in India.
[Contains English characters] The Indian screen magazine Filmfare started the first Filmfare Awards in 1954, and awards were given to the best films of 1953. The ceremony was referred to as the Clare Awards after the magazines editor.
[Contains English characters] Modelled after the poll-based merit format of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, individuals may submit their votes in separate categories.
[Contains English characters] A dual voting system was developed in 1956. Like the Oscars, the Filmfare awards are frequently accused of bias towards commercial success rather than artistic merit.
[Contains English characters] As the Filmfare, the National Film Awards were introduced in 1954. Since 1973, the Indian government has sponsored the National Film Awards, awarded by the government run Directorate of Film Festivals .
[Contains English characters] The DFF screens not only Bollywood films, but films from all the other regional movie industries and independent/art films.
[Contains English characters] These awards are handed out at an annual ceremony presided over by the President of India.
[Contains English characters] Under this system, in contrast to the National Film Awards, which are decided by a panel appointed by Indian Government, the Filmfare Awards are voted for by both the public and a committee of experts.

[Contains English characters] Many Pakistanis watch Bollywood films, as they understand Hindi .
[Contains English characters] Pakistan banned the legal import of Bollywood movies in 1965. However, a thriving trade in pirated DVDs and illegal cable broadcasts ensured the continued popularity of Bollywood releases in Pakistan.
[Contains English characters] Exceptions were made for a few films, such as the 2006 colorized re-release of the classic Mughal-e-Azam or the 2006 film Taj Mahal.
[Contains English characters] Early in 2008, the Pakistani government eased the ban and allowed the import of even more movies; 16 were screened in 2008. Continued easing followed in 2009 and 2010. The new policy is controversial in Pakistan.
[Contains English characters] It is opposed by ardent nationalists and representatives of Pakistans small film industry; it is embraced by cinema owners, who are booking large profits after years of poor receipts.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood movies are also popular in Afghanistan due to the countrys proximity with the Indian subcontinent and certain other cultural perspectives present in the movies.
[Contains English characters] A number of Bollywood movies were filmed inside Afghanistan while some dealt with the country, including Dharmatma, Kabul Express, Khuda Gawah and Escape From Taliban.
[Contains English characters] Hindi films have also been popular in numerous Arab countries, including Palestine, Jordan, Egypt and the Gulf countries.
[Contains English characters] Imported Indian films are usually subशीर्षकd in Arabic upon the films release.
[Contains English characters] Since the early 2000s, Bollywood has progressed in Israel.
[Contains English characters] Special channels dedicated to Indian films have been displayed on cable television.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films are also popular across Southeast Asia and Central Asia .
[Contains English characters] Some Hindi movies also became big successes in the Peoples Republic of China during the 1940s and 1950s.
[Contains English characters] The most popular Hindi films in China were Dr.
[Contains English characters] Kotnis Ki Amar Kahani, Awaara and Two Acres of Land .
[Contains English characters] Raj Kapoor was a famous movie star in China, and the song Awara Hoon was popular in the country.
[Contains English characters] Since then, Hindi films significantly declined in popularity in China, until the Academy Award nominated Lagaan became the first Indian film to have a nation-wide release there in decades.
[Contains English characters] The Chinese filmmaker He Ping was impressed by Lagaan, especially its soundtrack, and thus hired the films music composer A. R. Rahman to score the soundtrack for his film Warriors of Heaven and Earth .
[Contains English characters] Several older Hindi films also have a cult following in Japan, particularly the films directed by the late Guru Dutt.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films have been dubbed into Russian, and shown in prominent theatres such as Mosfilm and Lenfilm.

[Contains English characters] In other words, films from India do more business in the United States than films from any other non-English speaking country.

[Contains English characters] Bollywoods immersion in the traditional Hollywood domain was further tied with such films as The Guru and Marigold: An Adventure in India trying to popularise the Bollywood-theme for Hollywood.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood is not as successful in the Oceanic countries and Pacific Islands such as New Guinea.

[Contains English characters] Australia is one of the countries where there is a large South Asian Diaspora.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood is popular amongst non-Asians in the country as well.
[Contains English characters] Since 1997 the country has provided a backdrop for an increasing number of Bollywood films.
[Contains English characters] Indian filmmakers have been attracted to Australias diverse locations and landscapes, and initially used it as the setting for song-and-dance sequences, which demonstrated the contrast between the values.
[Contains English characters] However, nowadays, Australian locations are becoming more important to the plot of Bollywood films.
[Contains English characters] Hindi films shot in Australia usually incorporate aspects of Australian lifestyle.

[Contains English characters] This was followed by Heyy Babyy Chak De!
[Contains English characters] India and Singh Is Kinng which turned out to be box office successes.

[Contains English characters] Australian actress Tania Zaetta, who co-starred in Salaam Namaste, among other Bollywood films, expressed her keenness to expand her career in Bollywood.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood movies are not influential in South America, though Bollywood culture and dance is recognised.
[Contains English characters] In 2006, Dhoom 2 became the first Bollywood film to be shot in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
[Contains English characters] Constrained by rushed production schedules and small budgets, some Bollywood writers and musicians have been known to resort to plagiarism.
[Contains English characters] Ideas, plot lines, tunes or riffs have been copied from other Indian film industries or foreign films .
[Contains English characters] This has led to criticism towards the film industry.
[Contains English characters] In past times, this could be done with impunity.
[Contains English characters] Copyright enforcement was lax in India and few actors or directors ever saw an official contract.
[Contains English characters] The Hindi film industry was not widely known to non-Indian audiences, who would not even be aware that their material was being copied.
[Contains English characters] Audiences may also not have been aware of the plagiarism since many audiences in India were unfamiliar with foreign films and music.
[Contains English characters] While copyright enforcement in India is still somewhat lenient, Bollywood and other film industries are much more aware of each other now and Indian audiences are more familiar with foreign movies and music.
[Contains English characters] Organizations like the India EU Film Initiative seek to foster a community between film makers and industry professional between India and the EU.
[Contains English characters] One of the common justifications of plagiarism in Bollywood is that producers often play a safer option by remaking popular Hollywood films in an Indian context.
[Contains English characters] Screenwriters generally produce original scripts, but due to financial uncertainty and insecurity over the success of a film many were rejected.
[Contains English characters] Screenwriters themselves have been criticised for lack of creativity which happened due to tight schedules and restricted funds in the industry to employ better screenwriters.
[Contains English characters] Certain filmmakers see plagiarism in Bollywood as an integral part of globalisation where American and western cultures are firmly embedding themselves into Indian culture, which is manifested, amongst other mediums, in Bollywood films.
[Contains English characters] Vikram Bhatt, director of films such as Raaz, a remake of What Lies Beneath, and Kasoor, a remake of Jagged Edge, has spoken about the strong influence of American culture and desire to produce box office hits based along the same lines in Bollywood, Financially, I would be more secure knowing that a particular piece of work has already done well at the box office.
[Contains English characters] Copying is endemic everywhere in India.
[Contains English characters] Our TV shows are adaptations of American programmes.
[Contains English characters] We want their films, their cars, their planes, their diet cokes and also their attitude.
[Contains English characters] The American way of life is creeping into our culture.
[Contains English characters] Mahesh Bhatt has said ,If you hide the source, youre a genius.
[Contains English characters] Theres no such thing as originality in the creative sphere.
[Contains English characters] There have been very few cases of film copyright violations taken to court because of serious delays in the legal process, and due to the long time they take to decide a case.
[Contains English characters] There have been some notable cases of conflict though.
[Contains English characters] The makers of Partner and Zinda have been targeted by the owners and distributors of the original films, Hitch and Oldboy.
[Contains English characters] American Studio Twentieth Century Fox brought the Mumbai-based B. R. Films to court over its forthcoming Banda Yeh Bindaas Hai, allegedly an illegal remake of its 1992 film My Cousin Vinny.
[Contains English characters] B. R. Films eventually settled out of court by paying the studio at a cost of about $200,000, paving the way for the films release.
[Contains English characters] Some on the other hand do comply with copyright law, with Orion Pictures recently securing the rights to remake the Hollywood film Wedding Crashers.
