[Contains English characters] मलबार किंवा मलबार विभाग/किनारपट्टी is a region of southern India, lying between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea.
[Contains English characters] The name is thought to be derived from the Malayalam word Mala and Puram derived or westernised into bar.
[Contains English characters] This part of India was a part of the British East India company controlled Madras State,when it was designated as Malabar District .
[Contains English characters] It included the northern half of the state of केरळ and some coastal regions of present day Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] The area is predominantly Hindu but the majority of केरळs Muslim population known as Mappila also live in this area, as well as a sizable ancient Christian population.
[Contains English characters] The name is sometimes extended to the entire southwestern coast of the peninsula, called the Malabar Coast.
[Contains English characters] Malabar is also used by ecologists to refer to the tropical moist forests of southwestern India .
[Contains English characters] The Malabar region lies along the southwest coast of the Indian peninsula and forms the northern part of present-day केरळ state.
[Contains English characters] Malayalam is the chief language of the region, and the ancestors of todays population have inhabited the region for centuries.
[Contains English characters] The region formed part of the ancient kingdom of Chera until the early 12th century.
[Contains English characters] Following the breakup of the Chera Kingdom, the chieftains of the region proclaimed there independence.
[Contains English characters] Notable among these were the Kolathiris of North Malabar, Zamorins of Calicut and the Valluvokonathiris of Walluvanad.
[Contains English characters] The Zamorin of Calicut became the most powerful of the Kings in the region by the 13th century primarily due to flourishing international trade at Calicut and Beypore port.
[Contains English characters] The region came under British rule in the 18th century, during the Anglo-Mysore Wars.
[Contains English characters] During the British rules, the Malabar area was divided in to two categories as North and South.
[Contains English characters] North Malabar comprises : Present Kasaragod and Kannur Districts, Mananthavady Taluk of Wayanad District and Vadakara Taluk of Kozhikode District.
[Contains English characters] Left over area in South Malabar.
[Contains English characters] At the conclusion of the Anglo-Mysore wars, the region was organized into a district of Madras Presidency.
[Contains English characters] The British district included the present-day districts of Kannur, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Malappuram, much of Palakkad and a small portion of Thrissur.
[Contains English characters] The administrative headquarters was at Calicut .
[Contains English characters] With Indias independence, Madras presidency became Madras State, which was divided along linguistic lines on 1 November 1956, whereupon Malabar district was merged with the Kasaragod district immediately to the north and the state of Travancore-Cochin to the south to form the state of केरळ.
[Contains English characters] The Malabar Coast, in historical contexts, refers to Indias southwest coast, lying on the narrow coastal plain of Karnataka and केरळ states between the Western Ghats range and the Arabian Sea.
[Contains English characters] The coast runs from south of Goa to Cape Comorin on Indias southern tip.
[Contains English characters] The Malabar Coast is also sometimes used as an all encompassing term for the entire Indian coast from the western coast of Konkan to the tip of the subcontinent at Cape Comorin.
[Contains English characters] It is over 525 miles or 845 km long.
[Contains English characters] It spans from the South - Western coast of महाराष्ट्र and goes along the coastal region of Goa, through the entire western coast of Karnataka and केरळ and reaches till Kanyakumari.
[Contains English characters] It is flanked by the Arabian Sea on the west and the Western Ghats on the east.
[Contains English characters] The Southern part of this narrow coast is the South Western Ghats moist deciduous forests.
[Contains English characters] The Malabar Coast features a number of historic port cities.
[Contains English characters] Notable among these are the Muziris, Beypore and Thundi during ancient times and Kozhikode, Cochin, and Kannur in the medieval period and have served as centers of the Indian Ocean trade for centuries.
[Contains English characters] Because of their orientation to the sea and to maritime commerce, the coastal cities of Malabar are very cosmopolitan and have hosted some of the first groups of Christians, Jews, and Muslims in India.
[Contains English characters] Geographically, the Malabar Coast, especially on its westward-facing mountain slopes, comprises the wettest region of southern India as the Western Ghats intercept the moisture-laden monsoon rains.
[Contains English characters] The term Malabar rainforests refers to one or more distinct ecoregions recognized by biogeographers: The Monsooned Malabar coffee bean comes from this area.

[Contains English characters] From now on new localisations that become available in SVN will become available to your project within 24 hours.
[Contains English characters] Your localisations get into SVN from translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net typically within a day and at worst in two days.
[Contains English characters] This is a huge improvement from the old practice where the localisations became available with new software.
[Contains English characters] This could take weeks, even months.
[Contains English characters] The localisations done by our community at translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net are committed to SVN typically every day.
[Contains English characters] When the system messages in English are the same as the local messages, they will now be inserted in a file and are available for use in all our projects in a timely manner Local messages have an impact on the performance of our system.
[Contains English characters] It is best when messages are as much as possible part of the system messages.
[Contains English characters] In order to remove unnecessary duplication, all the messages that have a local localisation and are exactly the same as the system message will be removed.
[Contains English characters] What we ask you to do is to compare and proof read the messages in translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net and the local messages.
[Contains English characters] You can then either remove local messages when the translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net message is to be preferred or, you can update the message at translatewiki. net. Messages that are specific to your project will have to stay as they are.
[Contains English characters] You do want to check if the format and the variables of the message are still the same.
[Contains English characters] When you localise at translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net, your messages will be used in all Wikimedia projects and eventually in all MediaWiki based projects.
[Contains English characters] This is how we provide the standard support for your language.
[Contains English characters] When messages change, at translatewiki.
[Contains English characters] net you will be prompted to revisit your translations.
[Contains English characters] Localising is more efficient because we have innovated the process to make you more efficient; there is text explaining about messages and we have applied AJAX technology to reduce the number of clicks you have to make.
[Contains English characters] We expect that with the implementation of LocalisationUpdate the usability of MediaWiki for your language will improve.
[Contains English characters] We are now ready to look at other aspects of usability for your language as well.

Change the language to your language, select the “vector” skin and add the advanced tool bar in in the preferences and check out the new functionality.
[Contains English characters] And make some changes in your user page.

[Contains English characters] We would like you to report each issue individually at http://meta. wikimedia. org/wiki/Usability_issues. When there are problems with the support of MediaWiki for your language, we really want to know about this.
[Contains English characters] It is best to report each issue separately.
[Contains English characters] In this way there will be no large mass of issues to resolve but we can address each issue on its own.

[Contains English characters] In India, Engineers day is celebrated on September 15. This day is celebrated in the honor of मोक्षगुंडम विश्वेश्वरय्या, who was a notable Indian engineer, scholar, statesman and the Diwan of Mysore during 1912 to 1919. Internationally recognised for his genius in harnessing water resources, he was responsible for successful design and construction of several river dams, bridges and implementing irrigation and drinking water schemes all over India.
[Contains English characters] He served as the dewan of Mysore State and was considered to be the architect of the all-round development of Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] Among his most successful projects are the design and construction of the K. R. Sagar dam and its adjoining Brindavan Gardens, turn-around of the Bhadravati Iron and Steel Works, setting up of the Mysore Sandalwood Oil Factory and the founding of the Bank of Mysore.

[Contains English characters] Morality has three principal meanings.
[Contains English characters] In its first, descriptive usage, morality means a code of conduct or a set of beliefs distinguishing between right and wrong behaviors.
[Contains English characters] Descriptive morality does not explain why any behavior should be considered right or wrong, only that it may be classified so.
[Contains English characters] For the most part right and wrong acts are classified as such because they cause benefit or harm, respectively.
[Contains English characters] However, this is not by any means an all encompassing criterion.
[Contains English characters] It is possible that many moral beliefs are based on prejudice, ignorance or even hatred.
[Contains English characters] In its second, normative and universal sense, morality refers to an ideal code of belief and conduct which would be preferred by the sane moral person, under specified conditions.
[Contains English characters] In this definitive sense, claims are made such as Killing is immoral.
[Contains English characters] While descriptive morality would not necessarily disagree that killing is immoral, it would prefer to say, Many believe that killing is immoral.
[Contains English characters] A refined adherence to this latter position is known as moral skepticism, in which the unchanging existence of a rigid, universal, objective moral truth is rejected.
[Contains English characters] In its third usage, morality is synonymous with ethics.
[Contains English characters] Ethics is the systematic philosophical study of the moral domain.
[Contains English characters] Ethics seeks to address questions such as how a moral outcome can be achieved in a specific situation, how moral values should be determined, what morals people actually abide by, what the fundamental nature of ethics or morality is, including whether it has any objective justification, and how moral capacity or moral agency develops and what its nature is .
[Contains English characters] In applied ethics, for example, the prohibition against taking human life is controversial with respect to capital punishment, euthanasia, abortion and wars of invasion.
[Contains English characters] In normative ethics, a typical question might be whether a lie told for the sake of protecting someone from harm is justified.
[Contains English characters] In meta-ethics, a key issue is the meaning of the terms moral or immoral.
[Contains English characters] Moral realism would hold that there are true moral statements which report objective moral facts, whereas moral anti-realism would hold that morality is derived from any one of the norms prevalent in society ; the edicts of a god ; is merely an expression of the speakers sentiments ; an implied imperative ; or falsely presupposes that there are objective moral facts .
[Contains English characters] Some thinkers hold that there is no correct definition of right behavior, that morality can only be judged with respect to particular situations, within the standards of particular belief systems and socio-historical contexts.
[Contains English characters] This position, known as moral relativism, often cites empirical evidence from anthropology as evidence to support its claims.
[Contains English characters] The opposite view, that there are universal, eternal moral truths are known as moral absolutism.
[Contains English characters] Moral absolutists might concede that forces of social conformity significantly shape moral decisions, but deny that cultural norms and customs define morally right behavior.
[Contains English characters] Celia Green has made a distinction between tribal and territorial morality.
[Contains English characters] She characterizes the latter as predominantly negative and proscriptive: it defines a person’s territory, including his or her property and dependents, which is not to be damaged or interfered with.
[Contains English characters] Apart from these proscriptions, territorial morality is permissive, allowing the individual whatever behaviour does not interfere with the territory of another.
[Contains English characters] By contrast, tribal morality is prescriptive, imposing the norms of the collective on the individual.
[Contains English characters] These norms will be arbitrary, culturally dependent and ‘flexible’, whereas territorial morality aims at rules which are universal and absolute, such as Kant’s ‘categorical imperative’.
[Contains English characters] Green relates the development of territorial morality to the rise of the concept of private property, and the ascendancy of contract over status.
[Contains English characters] some observers hold that individuals apply distinct sets of moral rules to people depending on their membership of an ingroup or an outgroup .
[Contains English characters] Some biologists, anthropologists and evolutionary psychologists believe this ingroup-outgroup discrimination has evolved because it enhances group survival.
[Contains English characters] Gary R.
[Contains English characters] Johnson and V. S. Falger have argued that nationalism and patriotism are forms of this ingroup/outgroup boundary.
[Contains English characters] Jonathan Haidt has noted that experimental observation indicates an ingroup criterion provides one moral foundation substantially used by conservatives, but far less so by liberals.
[Contains English characters] Peterson and Seligman approach the anthropological view looking across cultures and across millennia.
[Contains English characters] They conclude that certain virtues have prevailed in all cultures they examined.
[Contains English characters] The major virtues they identified include wisdom / knowledge; courage; humanity; justice; temperance; and transcendence.
[Contains English characters] Each of these includes several divisions.
[Contains English characters] For instance humanity includes love, kindness, and social intelligence.
[Contains English characters] Fons Trompenaars, author of Did the Pedestrian Die?
[Contains English characters] , tested members of different cultures with various moral dilemmas.
[Contains English characters] One of these was whether the driver of a car would have his friend, a passenger riding in the car, lie in order to protect the driver from the consequences of driving too fast and hitting a pedestrian.
[Contains English characters] Trompenaars found that different cultures had quite different expectations .
[Contains English characters] The development of modern morality is a process closely tied to the Sociocultural evolution of humanity, however its roots are probably to be found in our very nature.
[Contains English characters] Some evolutionary biologists, particularly sociobiologists, believe that morality is a product of evolutionary forces acting at an individual level and also at the group level through group selection .
[Contains English characters] Some sociobiologists contend that the set of behaviors that constitute morality evolved largely because they provided possible survival and/or reproductive benefits .
[Contains English characters] Humans consequently evolved pro-social emotions, such as feelings of empathy or guilt, in response to these moral behaviors.
[Contains English characters] In this respect, morality is not absolute, but relative and constitutes any set of behaviors that encourage human cooperation based on their ideology.
[Contains English characters] Biologists contend that all social animals, from ants to elephants, have modified their behaviors, by restraining selfishness in order to make group living worthwhile.
[Contains English characters] Human morality, though sophisticated and complex relative to other animals, is essentially a natural phenomenon that evolved to restrict excessive individualism and foster human cooperation.
[Contains English characters] On this view, moral codes are ultimately founded on emotional instincts and intuitions that were selected for in the past because they aided survival and reproduction .
[Contains English characters] Examples: the maternal bond is selected for because it improves the survival of offspring; the Westermarck effect, where close proximity during early years reduces mutual sexual attraction, underpins taboos against incest because it decreases the likelihood of genetically risky behaviour such as inbreeding.
[Contains English characters] The phenomenon of reciprocity in nature is seen by evolutionary biologists as one way to begin to understand human morality.
[Contains English characters] Its function is typically to ensure a reliable supply of essential resources, especially for animals living in a habitat where food quantity or quality fluctuates unpredictably.
[Contains English characters] For example, some vampire bats fail to feed on prey on any given night while others consume a surplus.
[Contains English characters] Bats that have successfully fed then regurgitate part of their blood meal to save a conspecific from starvation.
[Contains English characters] Since these animals live in close-knit groups over many years, an individual can count on other group members to return the favor on nights when it goes hungry Marc Bekoff and Jessica Pierce have argued that morality is a suite of behavioral capacities likely shared by all mammals living in complex social groups .
[Contains English characters] They define morality as a suite of interrelated other-regarding behaviors that cultivate and regulate complex interactions within social groups.
[Contains English characters] This suite of behaviors includes empathy, reciprocity, altruism, cooperation, and a sense of fairness.
[Contains English characters] In related work, it has been convincingly demonstrated that chimpanzees show empathy for each other in a wide variety of contexts.
[Contains English characters] They also possess the ability to engage in deception, and a level of social politics prototypical of our own tendencies for gossip and reputation management.
[Contains English characters] Christopher Boehm has hypothesized that the incremental development of moral complexity throughout hominid evolution was due to the increasing need to avoid disputes and injuries in moving to open savanna and developing stone weapons.
[Contains English characters] Other theories are that increasing complexity was simply a correlate of increasing group size and brain size, and in particular the development of theory of mind abilities.
[Contains English characters] Richard Dawkins in The God Delusion suggested that our morality is a result of our biological evolutionary history and that the Moral Zeitgeist helps describe how morality evolves from biological and cultural origins and evolves with time within a culture.
[Contains English characters] Research on mirror neurons, since their discovery in 1996, suggests that they may have a role to play not only in action understanding, but also in emotion sharing empathy.
[Contains English characters] Cognitive neuro-scientist Jean Decety thinks that the ability to recognize and vicariously experience what another individual is undergoing was a key step forward in the evolution of social behavior, and ultimately, morality.
[Contains English characters] The inability to feel empathy is one of the defining characteristics of psychopathy, and this would appear to lend support to Decetys view.
[Contains English characters] The explicit making of moral right and wrong judgments links to activation in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex while as theintuitive reactions to situations containing implicit moral issues activates the temporoparietal junction area.
[Contains English characters] In modern moral psychology, morality is considered to change through personal development.
[Contains English characters] A number of psychologists have produced theories on the development of morals, usually going through stages of different morals.
[Contains English characters] Lawrence Kohlberg, Jean Piaget, and Elliot Turiel have cognitive-developmental approaches to moral development; to these theorists morality forms in a series of constructive stages or domains.
[Contains English characters] Social psychologists such as Martin Hoffman and Jonathan Haidt emphasize social and emotional development based on biology, such as empathy.
[Contains English characters] Moral identity theorists, such as William Damon and Mordechai Nisan, see moral commitment as arising from the development of a self-identity that is defined by moral purposes: this moral self-identity leads to a sense of responsibility to pursue such purposes.
[Contains English characters] Of historical interest in psychology are the theories of psychoanalysts such as Sigmund Freud, who believe that moral development is the product of aspects of the super-ego as guilt-shame avoidance.
[Contains English characters] If morality is the answer to the question how ought we to live at the individual level, politics can be seen as addressing the same question at the social level.
[Contains English characters] It is therefore unsurprising that evidence has been found of a relationship between attitudes in morality and politics.
[Contains English characters] Jonathan Haidt and Jesse Graham have studied the differences between liberals and conservatives, in this regard.
[Contains English characters] Haidt found that Americans who identified as liberals tended to value care and fairness higher than loyalty, respect and purity.
[Contains English characters] Self-identified conservative Americans valued care and fairness less and the remaining three values more.
[Contains English characters] Both groups gave care the highest over-all weighting, but conservatives valued fairness the lowest, whereas liberals valued purity the lowest.
[Contains English characters] Haidt also hypothesizes that the origin of this division in the United States can be traced to geohistorical factors, with conservatism strongest in closely knit, ethnically homogenous communities, in contrast to port-cities, where the cultural mix is greater, thus requiring more liberalism.
[Contains English characters] Group morality develops from shared concepts and beliefs and is often codified to regulate behavior within a culture or community.
[Contains English characters] Various defined actions come to be called moral or immoral.
[Contains English characters] Individuals who choose moral action are popularly held to possess moral fiber, whereas those who indulge in immoral behavior may be labeled as socially degenerate.
[Contains English characters] The continued existence of a group may depend on widespread conformity to codes of morality; an inability to adjust moral codes in response to new challenges is sometimes credited with the demise of a community .
[Contains English characters] Within nationalist movements, there has been some tendency to feel that a nation will not survive or prosper without acknowledging one common morality, regardless of in what it consists.
[Contains English characters] Political Morality is also relevant to the behaviour internationally of national governments, and to the support they receive from their host population.
[Contains English characters] Noam Chomsky states that Codified morality is generally distinguished from custom, another way for a community to define appropriate activity, by the formers derivation from natural or universal principles.
[Contains English characters] In certain religious communities, the Divine is said to provide these principles through revelation, sometimes in great detail.
[Contains English characters] Such codes may be called laws, as in the Law of Moses, or community morality may be defined through commentary on the texts of revelation, as in Islamic law.
[Contains English characters] Such codes are distinguished from legal or judicial right, including civil rights, which are based on the accumulated traditions, decrees and legislation of a political authority, though these latter often invoke the authority of the moral law.
[Contains English characters] Morality can also be seen as the collection of beliefs as to what constitutes a good life.
[Contains English characters] Since throughout most of human history, religions have provided both visions and regulations for an ideal life, morality is often confused with religious precepts.
[Contains English characters] In secular communities, lifestyle choices, which represent an individuals conception of the good life, are often discussed in terms of morality.
[Contains English characters] Individuals sometimes feel that making an appropriate lifestyle choice invokes a true morality, and that accepted codes of conduct within their chosen community are fundamentally moral, even when such codes deviate from more general social principles.
[Contains English characters] Moral codes are often complex definitions of moral and immoral that are based upon well-defined value systems.
[Contains English characters] Although some people might think that a moral code is simple, rarely is there anything simple about ones values, ethics, etc.
[Contains English characters] or, for that matter, the judgment of those of others.
[Contains English characters] The difficulty lies in the fact that morals are often part of a religion and more often than not about culture codes.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, moral codes give way to legal codes, which couple penalties or corrective actions with particular practices.
[Contains English characters] Note that while many legal codes are merely built on a foundation of religious and/or cultural moral codes, oftentimes they are one and the same.
[Contains English characters] Examples of moral codes include the Golden Rule; the Five Precepts and the Noble Eightfold Path of Buddhism ; the ancient Egyptian code of Maat ;the ten commandments of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam; the yamas and niyama of the Hindu scriptures; the ten Indian commandments; and the principle of the Dessek.
[Contains English characters] Another related concept is the moral core which is assumed to be innate in each individual, to those who accept that differences between individuals are more important than posited Creators or their rules.
[Contains English characters] This, in some religious systems and beliefs, is assumed to be the basis of all aesthetics and thus moral choice.
[Contains English characters] Moral codes as such are therefore seen as coercive—part of human politics.
[Contains English characters] In the scientific literature, the degree of religiosity is generally found to be associated with higher ethical attitudes.
[Contains English characters] Although a recent study by Gregory S.
[Contains English characters] Paul published in the Journal of Religion and Society argues for a positive correlation between the degree of public religiosity in a society and certain measures of dysfunction, an analysis published later in the same journal contends that a number of methodological problems undermine any findings or conclusions to be taken from the research.
[Contains English characters] In another response, Gary Jensen builds on and refines Pauls study.
[Contains English characters] His conclusion, after carrying out elaborate multivariate statistical studies, is that a complex relationship exists between religiosity and homicide with some dimensions of religiosity encouraging homicide and other dimensions discouraging it.
[Contains English characters] Meanwhile, other studies seem to show positive links in the relationship between religiosity and moral behavior—for example, surveys suggesting a positive connection between faith and altruism.
[Contains English characters] Modern research in criminology also acknowledges an inverse relationship between religion and crime, with many studies establishing this beneficial connection .
[Contains English characters] Indeed, a meta-analysis of 60 studies on religion and crime concluded, “religious behaviors and beliefs exert a moderate deterrent effect on individuals’ criminal behavior”.
[Contains English characters] Many religions provide moral guidelines for their followers.
[Contains English characters] They believe that God has instructed them with a way to live, and that following these rules will lead to oneness with God.

[Contains English characters] Also in the early 1900s, motion picture production companies from New York and New Jersey started moving to California because of the good weather and longer days.
[Contains English characters] Although electric lights existed at that time, none were powerful enough to adequately expose film; the best source of illumination for movie production was natural sunlight.
[Contains English characters] Besides the moderate, dry climate, they were also drawn to the state because of its open spaces and wide variety of natural scenery.
[Contains English characters] Another reason was the distance of Southern California from New Jersey, which made it more difficult for Thomas Edison to enforce his motion picture patents.
[Contains English characters] At the time, Edison owned almost all the patents relevant to motion picture production and, in the East, movie producers acting independently of Edisons Motion Picture Patents Company were often sued or enjoined by Edison and his agents.
[Contains English characters] Thus, movie makers working on the West Coast could work independently of Edisons control.
[Contains English characters] If he sent agents to California, word would usually reach Los Angeles before the agents did and the movie makers could escape to nearby Mexico.

[Contains English characters] Riot laws: Riot Act, Black Act Under English law, a riot is defined by the Public Order Act 1986 as twelve or more persons who together use or threaten unlawful violence for a common purpose and the conduct of them is such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety.
[Contains English characters] A single person can be liable for an offense of riot when they use violence provided that it can be shown there were at least twelve present using or threatening violence.
[Contains English characters] The violence can be against the person or against property.
[Contains English characters] This carries the possibility of a fine and a sentence of up to ten years imprisonment.
[Contains English characters] If there are fewer than twelve people present, the lesser offense of Violent Disorder is charged, for which there is a requirement for at least three persons to use or threaten unlawful violence together.
[Contains English characters] This is defined similarly to riot, but no common purpose is required.
[Contains English characters] In the past, The Riot Act had to be read by an official - with the wording exactly correct - before any policing action could take place.
[Contains English characters] If the group did not disperse after the act was read, lethal force could legally be used against the crowd.
[Contains English characters] In recent times nobody has been charged with a Section 1 offense in England and Wales.
[Contains English characters] This is because if a Section 1 offense takes place the local police service are regarded as having failed and are liable to pay compensation.
[Contains English characters] The best known example of this is the Poll tax demonstrations of 1990 where nobody was charged with Section 1. All were charged as though a collection of Section 2 acts had just happened to take place in one location.
[Contains English characters] In English Law Riot forms part of the Public Order Act 1986 under section 1. The Public Order Act 1986 s.
[Contains English characters] 1 states: 1 Where twelve or more persons who are present together use or threaten unlawful violence for a common purpose and the conduct of them is such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety, each of the persons using unlawful violence for the common purpose is guilty of riot.
[Contains English characters] 2 It is immaterial whether or not the twelve or more use or threaten unlawful violence simultaneously.
[Contains English characters] 3 The common purpose may be inferred from conduct.
[Contains English characters] 4 No person of reasonable firmness need actually be, or be likely to be, present at the scene.
[Contains English characters] 5 Riot may be committed in private as well as in public places.
[Contains English characters] Under United States federal law, a riot is defined as A public disturbance involving an act or acts of violence by one or more persons part of an assemblage of three or more persons, which act or acts shall constitute a clear and present danger of, or shall result in, damage or injury to the property of any other person or to the person of any other individual or a threat or threats of the commission of an act or acts of violence by one or more persons part of an assemblage of three or more persons having, individually or collectively, the ability of immediate execution of such threat or threats, where the performance of the threatened act or acts of violence would constitute a clear and present danger of, or would result in, damage or injury to the property of any other person or to the person of any other individual. साचा:Usc. [Contains English characters] तेवर साचा:Infobox Ethnic group Thevar people are a Kshatriya warrior group,collectively forms the Mukkulathor मुक्कलदोर .
[Contains English characters] Mukkulathors are a group of Tamil aristocratic warrior/martial people, native to the Southern districts of Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The Mukkulathors descended from the three royal lineage namely Cholas, Pandyans and Cheras.
[Contains English characters] The name Mukkulathor alludes to the three roughly designated groups, Kallar, Maravar and Agamudaiyar, which make up this large endogamous social group.
[Contains English characters] Kallar and Maravar were inhabitants of Palai region during the Sangam period .
[Contains English characters] The literature during sangam period divided the regions based upon the climate and topography.
[Contains English characters] Palai was mainly a desert like region with little to no rain.
[Contains English characters] Nowadays, Mukkulathors are found all over the southern and central districts of Tamil Nadu, North-east Sri Lanka and amongst Tamil expatriate communities in South-East Asia and America.
[Contains English characters] There is also a small community in Chattisgarh where they had migrated during British rule.
[Contains English characters] The Royal houses of Sivagangai, Ramnad and Pudukkottai belongs to the Mukkulathor community.
[Contains English characters] See main article Kallar Kallar कळ्ळर Meaning Brave Peoples Kallars are one of the three related castes which constitute the Mukkulathor confederacy.
[Contains English characters] They are described as A fearless community shows many signs of independence and non-submission to any form of subjugation.
[Contains English characters] Historians postulate the word Kallar Derived from Kalla means Black in Sanscrit and Tamil Historians postulate Dravidians were called by Aryans as Kalla . . Thirumal is also stated Mal to meant he is Black and also Krishna means Black.
[Contains English characters] In olden days Black Dravidians were stated as Kalla to state their Bravery.
[Contains English characters] Kallars are largely found in the Southern districts of Thanjavur, Madurai, Pudukkottai, Trichy, Ariyalur, Theni, Dindigul, Sivaganga,Virudhunagar, Tirunelveli, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Ramanathapuram districts of Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] They are also present in Karur, Kanchipuram, Perambalur and Villupuram districts.
[Contains English characters] One of their popular deities is Kallazhagar who is a warrior incarnation of Lord Thirumala or Venkadavan.
[Contains English characters] The Pandi Temples found in Madurai and Southern regions of Tamilnadu were originally the Tombs of the Early Tamil Pandya Kings and Rulers.
[Contains English characters] Pandiyar Kudavarai which is found in Aritapatti has been built for the Siddhars by the Early Pandya Kings.
[Contains English characters] The Kallars are quintessentially a feudal society, with feudal classes such as the Ambalakarar.
[Contains English characters] They are found mainly in the Madurai, Tirchuripalli, Ariyalur and Sivaganga districts.
[Contains English characters] In these districts, each village is headed by an Ambalam and the Ambalam took upon themselves the power to adjudicate disputes that arose among the inhabitants in the Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The term Nadu is an ancient political and administrative system found wherever Kallar populations migrated.
[Contains English characters] Thenpandi Singam by M.
[Contains English characters] Karunanidhi is a book about Ambalakarars and it was also made into a Television serial broadcasted over Sun TV Network and music composed by Ilaiyaraaja.
[Contains English characters] They used to hear complaints, hold inquiries and punish the offenders.
[Contains English characters] They wielded considerable powers to intervene in any kind of transaction or transfer of property among the people.
[Contains English characters] No land could be alienated from one man to another without the permission of the Ambalams.
[Contains English characters] The sur-name Ambalamis given to them, because of their Administration in their Villages.
[Contains English characters] So they are mostly called as Ambalam.
[Contains English characters] Another important Kallar subcaste is the Piramalai Kallar.
[Contains English characters] They are a highly traditional people and have preserved their ancient customs to the present day.
[Contains English characters] They are also believed to be the oldest inhabitants of the Tamil country with reports of their presence going back to Tamil literary works of the 4th century B. C. They are found mainly in the districts of Madurai, Dindigul and Theni.
[Contains English characters] Their popular deity is Amman, the Mother Goddess.
[Contains English characters] They have contributed enormously in the freedom struggle for India.
[Contains English characters] Perungaamanallur people near Usilampatti, fought against the british and many have died and they have a Thiyagigal Thoon built in memory of them.
[Contains English characters] Piramalai Kallars have also made big contribution in Nethajis INA force when Subash chandra bose made a call for the INA force from the submarine radio lots of people from the community went and joint to fight against the british for India.
[Contains English characters] They are kept alive of our ancient culture.
[Contains English characters] Some of the other feudal classes include Koothappar Kallars, Periyasuriyur Kallars, Gandarvakoatai Kallars and Esanattu Kallars found largely dominated in the Thanjavur, Pudukkottai, Sivagangai & Trichy Districts.
[Contains English characters] Significant Kallar population also found in Srilanka and Malaysia.
[Contains English characters] Samy Vellu, Ex-Works Minister and Leader of Malaysian Indian Congress, S.
[Contains English characters] Thondaman, Leader of Indian Tamils of Sri Lanka are notable persons outside Tamilnadu.
[Contains English characters] See also main article Maravar Maravar also Maravan are one of the oldest social groups to be mentioned by the Sangam Tamil literature.
[Contains English characters] Maravars are courageous breed and were involved in almost all the major battles and wars that ancient Tamilnadu witnessed.
[Contains English characters] Maravars are found predominantly in the Southern districts of Tamilnadu viz.
[Contains English characters] , Madurai, Theni, Sivagangai, Ramanathapuram, Dindigul, Virudhunagar, Thirunelveli, Thoothukudi and Kanyakumari districts of Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] They ruled the vast land mass of Tamilnadu along with the coastal rulers,Paravars.
[Contains English characters] Both these tribes seems to have common origin,tamil nagas.
[Contains English characters] The Southern martial arts of Kalarippayattu, Silambam, Varma Kalai have been practiced primarily by Villavars of erstwhile Travancore areas.
[Contains English characters] The Maravar have close relation with Kalabhars even though they Maravars are a non-aryan, non-Kalabhar group.
[Contains English characters] Another aristocratic caste called Paravars are akin to Maravars.
[Contains English characters] They were ancient rulers of Pandya kingdom of coastal land and inland from the First Sangam Tamil age.
[Contains English characters] Their leaders were given the शीर्षक Meenavan and Pandyan respectively.
[Contains English characters] Edgar Thurston a British museologist and ethnographer identified the use of the boomerang by Kallars and Maravars of South India.
[Contains English characters] Large number of Maravars served in the armies of many princely states of केरळ.
[Contains English characters] But during the 18th and 19th centuries, most of them were assimilated in to the Tamil Padam Nair subcaste of the Nair community.
[Contains English characters] The Maravar regiment of the Travancore army was known as Maravar Padai, which supplemented Nair Pattalam, the larger indigenous military unit.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Padam Nair is recognized as a part of the Malayala Kshatriya social grouping.
[Contains English characters] The Ramnad Zamindars are accorded the शीर्षक Sethupathi even to this day.
[Contains English characters] There are 2 major subdivisions among the Maravar community.
[Contains English characters] One is Appa Nattu Kondyankottai Maravar and another one is Chembiya Nattu Maravar.
[Contains English characters] The Kondyan Kottai Maravars are related to the Vellalars and are still maintaining Killai as their sub sects.
[Contains English characters] The Killai is inherited from mother.
[Contains English characters] So a boy or girl will not marry in their same Killai.
[Contains English characters] It is assumed that they are brother & sister.
[Contains English characters] Such a practice is no longer prevailing amongst other maravars.
[Contains English characters] The married womens of kondyankottai maravers wear Thali in the shape of Shiva lingam.
[Contains English characters] So it is called Linga Thali.
[Contains English characters] Most of the Tamil castes wear the same type of Linga Thali.
[Contains English characters] Agamudayar meaning Fearless people .
[Contains English characters] Agamudayars are famously known by their शीर्षक ServaiThey make expert soldiers, warriors and constituted the bulk of Pandya armies.
[Contains English characters] The legendary Maruthu Pandiyar brothers came from the Agamudayar community.
[Contains English characters] when 29 April 1789, the British forces attacked Kollangudi.
[Contains English characters] It was defeated by a large body of Marudhu.
[Contains English characters] It is said that the Marudhu brothers could kill a tiger without using any weapons.
[Contains English characters] The lands the community owns are actually rewarded for their loyal and valuable service rendered for the cause of the Kings and the nation.
[Contains English characters] Agamudaiyars are found all over in Southern Tamilnadu in Sivagangai, Virudhunagar, Ramanathapuram, Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanyakumari, Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Pudukkottai, Madurai, Trichy, Ariyalur and Tiruvannamalai districts & Also in Karnataka state Hiriyur Taluk, Aranakatte & Maskal matti people are living. . The word Agamudaiyan or Ahamudaiyan is derived from the root Aham which in Tamil means the guts or brave of ones mind.
[Contains English characters] Agam also means land in Tamil, signifying that Agamudaiyars are Landlords and Householder ; the suffix Udeiyar indicating ownership.
[Contains English characters] The word is also used in another form, Ahampadiyar, derived from another meaning of the same root, i. e. , inside.
[Contains English characters] And, in this derivation, it signifies a meaning of a particular profession, whose office it was to attend to the business in the Interiors of the Kings Palace or in the Pagoda.
[Contains English characters] The name, Mr. J. H. Nelson writes, is said by the Rev.
[Contains English characters] G. U. Pope, in his edition of the Abbe Dubois work to be derived from aham, a temple, and padi, a step, and to have been given to them in consequence of their serving about the steps of temples.
[Contains English characters] But, independently of the fact that Madura pagodas are not approached by flights of steps, this seems to be a very far-fetched and improbable derivation of the word.
[Contains English characters] Or, perhaps, the name comes from aham in the sense of earth, and pati, master or possessor.
[Contains English characters] Agamudaiyar were employed by Srilankan kings as body guards & to protect palaces,according to Ceylon history, they were referred to as Agampadi Soldiers& it also gives the break down of the term Agampadi,, The ordinary शीर्षक of the Agamudaiyans is Servaikkaran, .
[Contains English characters] In Pudukkottai, Trichy, Sivangagai, Virudhunagar, Ramanathapuram, Thanjavur, Thirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanyakumari districts Agamudaiyans are also called Terkittiyar . . The Agamudaiyans are divided into the following sub-sects: Aivali Nattan, Kottaipattu, Malainadu, Nattumangalam, Rajaboja, Rajakulam, Rajavasal, Kalian, Sani, Maravan, and Servaikkaran.

[Contains English characters] In Baraha, by default, the Language, Font, Text Size, Text Color, Alignment, Bold, Italic, Underline and other formatting attributes of the output text are determined by the default values, that are specified in the Default Settings dialog box.
[Contains English characters] The default values affect the entire output text.
[Contains English characters] It is possible to selectively format the output text by using the Tags inside the angle brackets, which is called a Switch.
[Contains English characters] A switch is nothing but a group of one or more tags.
[Contains English characters] If more than one tag is specified in a switch, they have to be separated by either | or / character.
[Contains English characters] Every formatting attribute has an associated tag.
[Contains English characters] Attribute values specified using the tags override the default values.
[Contains English characters] A tag affects the value of the corresponding attribute, for all the text that follows it, until it is overridden by the same tag with a different value, or turned OFF using the corresponding closing tag.
[Contains English characters] When a tag is turned OFF, the default value will be used for that attribute from that point onwards.
[Contains English characters] For example, size=32 tag specifies the text size of 32 points.
[Contains English characters] This size will be used for all the text that follows the switch.
[Contains English characters] Later, if we use size=12 tag, the size of the following text becomes 12 points.
[Contains English characters] When we turn OFF the size value using the closing tag -size, the default text size will be used from that point onwards.
[Contains English characters] Tags are also used for inserting lines, graphics, hyperlinks.
[Contains English characters] A tag is composed of one or more Parameters.
[Contains English characters] A parameter can be just a Name or Name=Value pair.
[Contains English characters] If more than one parameter has to be specified, a space or comma is used to separate them.
[Contains English characters] If the Value itself has a space or comma character, double quotes should be used to enclose the value.

[Contains English characters] Dub localization, also often simply referred to as localization, of which it is a form, is the practice of altering the dubbed translation of a foreign language film or television series to further adapt it for a local audience.
[Contains English characters] Dub localization is a hot button issue amongst aficionados of foreign film and television, particularly anime fans as dubs are still a popular form of translation of animated series.
[Contains English characters] While some localization is virtually inevitable in translation, the controversy surrounding how much localization is too much is often much-discussed in such communities, especially when the final dub product is significantly different from the original.
[Contains English characters] Some frown on any extensive localization, while others expect it and, to a degree, appreciate it.
[Contains English characters] Some dub localizations are considered so extreme as to have produced a different show or film entirely.
[Contains English characters] Many localized dubs are the object of much controversy.
[Contains English characters] One relatively famous example of a controversial dub localization is Sailor Moon, which underwent heavy editing and many changes including the deletion of whole episodes, alteration of the animation itself, extensive use of valley girl slang and other slanguage, and even name changes that included changing the city from Tokyo to the fictional American city of Crossroads .
[Contains English characters] The first 65 episodes - the original DiC-produced dub - were most notorious for this, as later dubbed episodes edited far fewer of the Japanese cultural contents out and edited virtually none of the animation ; however, the latter portions of the dub are still controversial due to multiple character name changes, inconsistencies in things like names of attacks or plot-important items, the changing of a crossdressing characters sex, the making of Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune into relatives in an attempt to disguise their originally lesbian relationship, and the referring of Japanese kana in the context of Its all in pictures!

[Contains English characters] Many of the anime dubs by 4Kids Entertainment, such as those for Tokyo Mew Mew and One Piece, are controversial amongst many anime fans largely because of localization issues, including extensive and sometime bizarre censorship in order to release it on American childrens TV.
[Contains English characters] Many anime dubs contain mild to strong language that is non-existent in the original family friendly Japanese versions.
[Contains English characters] The best examples include the controversial Yu Yu Hakusho and One Piece dubs.
[Contains English characters] Another highly controversial dub localization was Cardcaptors, the English dubbed adaptation of Cardcaptor Sakura, which not only Americanized the setting and names, but actually changed the personalities of the characters and the focus of the show, to the point where the hero was Syaoran Li instead of Sakura, and the series genre was effectively switched from shōjo magical girl, to shōnen action-fantasy; this alteration proved to be unpopular, with the American DVD and VHS releases of Cardcaptors being canceled after only 27 episodes and the uncut subशीर्षकd release actually outselling the dub in the end, despite being released separately with little fanfare and virtually no extra features.
[Contains English characters] Some dub localizations are actually quite popular in their own right, with even a handful of greatly-altered शीर्षकs proving equally if not more popular than the original.
[Contains English characters] Several examples include some of ADVs comedy dubs, especially the alternate, Americanized dub for Super Milk-chan and the English dub for Ghost Stories, which contrary to the nature of the original show, was adult in nature and primarily a work of parody, and thus proved popular with a very different audience from the original childrens series.
[Contains English characters] However, the best example of a localization - indeed, an extreme localization - which actually proved to be extremely popular and in-demand, is likely Samurai Pizza Cats, the English version of which is still praised for its humor and often pointed to as an example of an extreme localization that actually worked.

[Contains English characters] The Master of Business Administration is a masters degree in business administration, which attracts people from a wide range of academic disciplines.
[Contains English characters] The MBA designation originated in the United States, emerging from the late 19th century as the country industrialized and companies sought out scientific approaches to management.
[Contains English characters] The core courses in the MBA program are designed to introduce students to the various areas of business such as accounting, marketing, human resources, operations management, etc.
[Contains English characters] Students in the MBA program have the option to select an area of concentration and focus approximately one-third of their studies in this area.
[Contains English characters] Accreditation bodies exist specifically for MBA programs to ensure consistency and quality of graduate business education, and business schools in many countries offer MBA programs tailored to full-time, part-time, executive, and distance learning students, with specialized concentrations.
[Contains English characters] The Tuck School of Business, part of Dartmouth College, was the first graduate school of business in the United States.
[Contains English characters] Founded in 1900, it was the first institution conferring advanced degrees in the commercial sciences, specifically, a Master of Science in Commerce degree, the forebear of the modern MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] In 1908, the Graduate School of Business Administration at Harvard University was established; it offered the worlds first MBA program, with a faculty of 15 plus 33 regular students and 47 special students.
[Contains English characters] The University of Chicago Graduate School of Business first offered working professionals the Executive MBA program in 1940, and this type of program is offered by most business schools today.
[Contains English characters] In 1950, the first MBA degrees were awarded outside the United States by The University of Western Ontario in Canada, followed in 1951 with the degree awarded by the University of Pretoria in South Africa.
[Contains English characters] The Institute of Business Administration, Karachi in Pakistan was established in 1955 as the first Asian business school by the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania.
[Contains English characters] In 1957, INSEAD became the first European business school to offer an MBA program.
[Contains English characters] The MBA degree has been adopted by universities worldwide, and has been adopted and adapted by both developed and developing countries.
[Contains English characters] Business schools or MBA programs may be accredited by external bodies which provide students and employers with an independent view of their quality, and indicate that the schools educational curriculum meets specific quality standards.
[Contains English characters] The three major accrediting bodies in the United States are Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business, which accredits research universities, the Association of Collegiate Business Schools and Programs, which accredits universities and colleges, and the International Assembly for Collegiate Business Education, all of which also accredit schools outside the US.
[Contains English characters] The AACSB and the ACBSP are themselves accredited in the United States by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation .
[Contains English characters] MBA programs with specializations for students pursuing careers in healthcare management also eligible for accreditation by the Commission on the Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education .
[Contains English characters] In the United States, a college or university must be accredited as a whole before it is eligible to have its MBA program accredited.
[Contains English characters] Bodies that accredit institutions as a whole include the Council for Higher Education Accreditation : Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools, New England Association of Schools and Colleges, Higher Learning Commission of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools, Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities, Southern Association of Colleges and Schools, and Western Association of Schools and Colleges .
[Contains English characters] Accreditation agencies outside the United States include the Association of MBAs, a UK based organization that accredits MBA, DBA and MBM programs worldwide, government accreditation bodies such as the All India Council for Technical Education that accredits MBA and PGDM programs across India, the Council on Higher Education in South Africa, the European Quality Improvement System for mostly European and Asian schools, and the Foundation for International Business Administration Accreditation in Europe.
[Contains English characters] Two-year MBA programs normally take place over two academic years .
[Contains English characters] For example in the Northern Hemisphere beginning in late August/September of year one and continuing until May of year two, with a three to four month summer break in between years one and two.
[Contains English characters] Students enter with a reasonable amount of prior real-world work experience and take classes during weekdays like other university students.
[Contains English characters] Accelerated MBA programs are a variation of the two year programs.
[Contains English characters] They involve a higher course load with more intense class and examination schedules.
[Contains English characters] They usually have less down time during the program and between semesters.
[Contains English characters] For example, there is no three to four month summer break, and between semesters there might be seven to ten days off rather than three to five weeks vacation.
[Contains English characters] Part-time MBA programs normally hold classes on weekday evenings, after normal working hours, or on weekends.
[Contains English characters] Part-time programs normally last three years or more.
[Contains English characters] The students in these programs typically consist of working professionals, who take a light course load for a longer period of time until the graduation requirements are met.
[Contains English characters] Executive MBA programs developed to meet the educational needs of managers and executives, allowing students to earn an MBA or another business-related graduate degree in two years or less while working full time.
[Contains English characters] Participants come from every type and size of organization – profit, nonprofit, government — representing a variety of industries.
[Contains English characters] EMBA students typically have a higher level of work experience, often 10 years or more, compared to other MBA students.
[Contains English characters] In response to the increasing number of EMBA programs offered, The Executive MBA Council was formed in 1981 to advance executive education.
[Contains English characters] Distance learning MBA programs hold classes off-campus.
[Contains English characters] These programs can be offered in a number of different formats: correspondence courses by postal mail or email, non-interactive broadcast video, pre-recorded video, live teleconference or videoconference, offline or online computer courses.
[Contains English characters] Many respectable schools offer these programs; however, so do many diploma mills.
[Contains English characters] Dual MBA programs combine MBA degree with others to let students cut costs, save time on education and to tailor the business education courses to their needs.
[Contains English characters] Some business schools offer programs in which students can earn both a bachelors degree in business administration and an MBA in four or five years.
[Contains English characters] Most programs base admission on the Graduate Management Admission Test, significant work experience, academic transcripts, essays, references or letters of recommendation and personal interviews.
[Contains English characters] The Graduate Record Examination is also accepted by some schools in lieu of the GMAT.
[Contains English characters] Schools are also interested in extracurricular activities, community service activities and how the student can improve the diversity and contribute to the student body as a whole.
[Contains English characters] All of these qualifications are important for admission; however, some schools do not weigh GMAT scores as heavily as other criteria.
[Contains English characters] In order to achieve a diverse class, business schools also consider the target male-female ratio and local-international student ratios.
[Contains English characters] Most top MBA programs cover similar subjects within their core required courses.
[Contains English characters] For information about the typical content of an MBA programs core curriculum, see the overview at the Wikiversity MBA topic page.
[Contains English characters] MBA programs expose students to a variety of subjects, which students may choose to specialize in a particular area.
[Contains English characters] Students traditionally study a wide breadth of courses in the programs first year, then pursue a specialized curriculum in the second year.
[Contains English characters] Full-time students typically seek an internship during the interim.
[Contains English characters] Typical specializations include: accounting; economics; Entrepreneurship; finance; international business; operations management; organizational behavior; marketing; real estate; and strategy, among others.
[Contains English characters] In 1957, INSEAD became the first European university offering the MBA degree, followed in 1964 by IESE, UCD Smurfit Business School in 1964, Manchester Business School and London Business School in 1965, The University of Dublin, the Rotterdam School of Management in 1966, the Cranfield School of Management in 1967 and in 1969 by the HEC School of Management and the Institut dEtudes Politiques de Paris.
[Contains English characters] In 1991, IEDC-Bled School of Management became the first school in the ex-socialist block of the Central and Eastern to offer an MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] See List of business schools in Europe In Europe, the recent Bologna Accord established uniformity in three levels of higher education: Bachelor, Masters, and Doctorate .
[Contains English characters] Students can acquire professional experience after their initial bachelor degree at any European institution and later complete their masters in any other European institution via the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System.
[Contains English characters] A European masters degree in Management is therefore equivalent to the American MBA having additional scientific content; for example, a European MBA normally requires writing and defending a masters thesis.
[Contains English characters] Accreditation standards are not uniform in Europe.
[Contains English characters] Some countries have legal requirements for accreditation, in some there is a legal requirement only for universities of a certain type, and others have no accreditation law at all.
[Contains English characters] Even where there is no legal requirement, many business schools are accredited by independent bodies voluntarily to ensure quality standards.
[Contains English characters] The UK based Association of MBAs was established in 1967 and is an active advocate for MBA degrees.
[Contains English characters] The Associations accreditation service is internationally recognised for all MBA, DBA and Masters in Business and Management programs.
[Contains English characters] AMBA also offer the only professional membership association for MBA students and graduates.
[Contains English characters] UK MBA programs typically consist of a set number of taught courses plus a dissertation or project.
[Contains English characters] January 1998 saw the first meeting of the Association of the Czech MBA Schools .
[Contains English characters] The Association is housed within the Centre for Doctoral and Managerial Studies of UEP, Prague.
[Contains English characters] All of the founding members of the Association have their MBA programmes accredited by partner institutions in Great Britain or in United States of America.
[Contains English characters] जर्मनी was one of the last western countries to adopt the MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] In 1998, the Hochschulrahmengesetz, a German federal law regulating higher education including the types of degrees offered, was modified to permit German universities to offer masters degrees.
[Contains English characters] The traditional German degree in business administration was the Diplom but since 1999, bachelors and masters degrees have gradually displaced the traditional degrees .
[Contains English characters] Today most German business schools offer the MBA.
[Contains English characters] Most German states require that MBA degrees have to be accredited by one of the six agencies officially recognized by the German Akkreditierungsrat, the German counterpart to the US-American CHEA.
[Contains English characters] The busiest of these six agencies is the Foundation for International Business Administration Accreditation .
[Contains English characters] All universities themselves have to be institutionally accredited by the state .
[Contains English characters] In ऑस्ट्रिया, MBA programs of private universities have to be accredited by the ऑस्ट्रियाn Accreditation Council .
[Contains English characters] State-run universities have no accreditation requirements, however, some of them voluntarily undergo accreditation procedures by independent bodies.
[Contains English characters] There are also MBA programs of non-academic business schools, who are enशीर्षकd by the ऑस्ट्रियाn government to offer these programs until 2010 .
[Contains English characters] Some non-academic institutions cooperate with state-run universities to ensure legality of their degrees.
[Contains English characters] In France and in the Francophone countries such as Switzerland, Monaco, Belgium, and Canada, the MBA degree programs at the public accredited schools are similar to those offered in the Anglo-Saxon countries.
[Contains English characters] Most French Business Schools are accredited by the Conférence des Grandes Écoles, which is an association of higher educational establishments outside the mainstream framework of the pu Italian MBAs programs at public accredited schools are similar to those offered elsewhere in Europe.
[Contains English characters] Italian Business Schools are accredited by EQUIS and by ASFOR.
[Contains English characters] Recently MBA programs appeared in Ukraine where there are now about ten schools of business offering a variety of MBA programs.
[Contains English characters] Two of these are subsidiaries of European schools of business, while the remaining institutions are independent.
[Contains English characters] Today, MBA and Doctor of Business Administration designations can be found in many countries and even accessed through on-line, distance learning or e-learning.
[Contains English characters] Because of the varying standards of MBAs worldwide, many business schools are accredited by independent bodies.
[Contains English characters] In Australia, 42 Australian business schools offer the MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] Universities differentiate themselves by gaining international accreditation and focusing on national and international rankings.
[Contains English characters] Most MBAs are one to two years full time.
[Contains English characters] There is little use of GMAT, and instead each educational institution specifies its own requirements, which normally entails several years of management-level work experience as well as proven academic skills.
[Contains English characters] Ratings for Australian MBAs are carried out by the Graduate Management Association of Australia, which publishes an annual Australian MBA Star Ratings.
[Contains English characters] See List of business schools in Australia.
[Contains English characters] In 2004, South Africa’s Council on Higher Education completed an extensive re-accreditation of MBA degrees offered in the country.
[Contains English characters] The process was the first of its kind in the world to be undertaken by a statutory body and attracted widespread international media attention for its innovation and thoroughness.
[Contains English characters] See List of business schools in South Africa.
[Contains English characters] Business schools of the traditional universities run a variety of MBA programs.
[Contains English characters] In addition, foreign accredited institutions offer MBA degrees by distance learning in Ghana.
[Contains English characters] There are 1600 business schools in India offering two year MBA programs targeting predominantly fresh graduates without any work experience.
[Contains English characters] Among those schools, the Indian Institutes of Management are the oldest institutions for management education in India.
[Contains English characters] Admission to any of the IIM schools or other business schools requires passing the Common Admission Test, XAT, GMAT, JMET or MAT each of which qualifies candidates for entrance into any management institutions in India, apart from these entrance tests there are few business schools which conducts aptitude test individually which qualifies candidates for that particular business school.
[Contains English characters] The IIM and other autonomous business schools offer a post-graduate diploma in management which is recognized in India as similar to an MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] Government accreditation bodies such as AICTE established that autonomous business schools can offer only the PGDM, whereas a post-graduate degree can be awarded by a university-affiliated colleges, in two-year full-time program.
[Contains English characters] The curriculum of the PGDM and MBA degrees are equivalent, although the MBA degree is examination oriented and concentrates on theoretical aspects of management whereas the PGDM is industry-oriented and mainly focuses on building soft skills.
[Contains English characters] However, a PGDM holder cannot pursue Ph. D. since the PGDM is not recognized.
[Contains English characters] Non-government accredited, one-year fast-track programs have proliferated in India, especially for candidates with work experience.
[Contains English characters] Such programs are commonly known as Post Graduate Programme in Business Management.
[Contains English characters] See List of business schools in India.
[Contains English characters] International MBA programs are acquiring brand value in Asia.
[Contains English characters] For example, while a foreign MBA is still preferred in the Philippines, many students are now studying at one of many Global MBA English language programs being offered.
[Contains English characters] English-only MBA programs are also offered in Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, Pakistan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand.
[Contains English characters] For North American students who want a different experience, many Asian programs offer scholarships and discounted tuition, to encourage an international environment in the classroom.
[Contains English characters] Rankings have been done for Asia Pacific schools by the magazine Asia Inc.
[Contains English characters] which is a regional business magazine with distribution worldwide.
[Contains English characters] The importance of MBA education in China has risen, too.
[Contains English characters] See List of business schools in Asia.
[Contains English characters] साचा:SeealsoEach year, well-known business publications such as US News & World Report, Business Week, Financial Times, The Economist, and the Wall Street Journal publish rankings of selected MBA programs that, while controversial in their methodology, nevertheless can directly influence the prestige of schools that achieve high scores.
[Contains English characters] The MBA degree has become one of the most popular masters degrees.
[Contains English characters] As more universities started offering the degree, differences in the quality of schools, faculty, and course offerings became evident.
[Contains English characters] Naturally, establishing some criteria of quality is needed to differentiate among MBA programs, especially for prospective students trying to decide on where to apply.
[Contains English characters] As MBA programs proliferated, a variety of publications began providing information on them.
[Contains English characters] Some of these consisted of compilations of information gathered from the universities offering the degree, usually published in book form.
[Contains English characters] Eventually periodicals began publishing articles describing various MBA schools and ranking them according to some perceived quality criteria.
[Contains English characters] One of the most prominent of these is Business Week, which devotes a biennial issue to ranking MBA programs.
[Contains English characters] Different methods of varying validity were used to arrive at rankings of MBA programs.
[Contains English characters] The Gourman Report, for example, did not disclose criteria or ranking methods, and these reports were criticized for reporting statistically impossible data, such as no ties among schools, narrow gaps in scores with no variation in gap widths, and ranks of nonexistent departments.
[Contains English characters] In 1977 The Carter Report published rankings of MBA programs based on the number of academic articles published by faculty.
[Contains English characters] Periodicals based their rankings on interviews with company recruiters who hired MBA graduates, surveys of MBA schools deans, polls of students or faculty, and a variety of other means.
[Contains English characters] The defunct MBA Magazine asked deans to vote on the best programs.
[Contains English characters] The methods of obtaining ranks often changed from year to year.
[Contains English characters] Initially, rankings included only a small number of universities consisting of the largest and best known Ivy League and state schools.
[Contains English characters] There are also many privately compiled rankings, including the Global Top 100 Business Schools compiled by the QS network.
[Contains English characters] The ranking of MBA programs has been discussed in articles and on academic Web sites.
[Contains English characters] Critics of ranking methodologies maintain that any published rankings should be viewed with caution for the following reasons: One study found that objectively ranking MBA programs by a combination of graduates starting salaries and average student GMAT score can reasonably duplicate the top 20 list of the national publications.
[Contains English characters] The study concluded that a truly objective ranking would be individualized to the needs of each prospective student.
[Contains English characters] National publications have recognized the value of rankings against different criteria, and now offer lists ranked different ways: by salary, GMAT score of students, selectivity, and so forth.
[Contains English characters] While useful, these rankings still are not tailored to individual needs, and their value is diminished if they use an incomplete population of schools, fail to distinguish between the different MBA program types offered by each school, or rely on subjective interviews.
[Contains English characters] The Financial crisis of 2007–2010 has raised new challenges and questions regarding the MBA degree.
[Contains English characters] Graduates of MBA programs have a reported tendency to go into Finance shortly after receiving the degree.
[Contains English characters] As the field of Finance is tightly linked to the global economic downturn, anecdotal evidence suggests new graduates are stepping onto alternate paths.
[Contains English characters] Deans at top business schools have acknowledged media and public perception of the MBA has shown some shifts as a result of the financial crisis.
[Contains English characters] Articles about public perception related to the crisis range from schools acknowledgment of issues related to the training students receive to general overviews of the MBAs role in society.

[Contains English characters] Emigrant communities are found across the world, notably Malaysia, Canada, Singapore, and the UK.

[Contains English characters] It has the oldest extant literature amongst other Dravidian languages.
[Contains English characters] The art and architecture of the Tamil people encompass some of the notable contributions of India and South-East Asia to the art world.

[Contains English characters] Thus, Tamils have been referred to as the last surviving classical civilisation on Earth.

[Contains English characters] It is unknown as to whether the term Tamilar and its equivalents in Prakrit such as Damela, Dameda, Dhamila and Damila was a self designation or a term denoted by outsiders.
