[Contains English characters] Possible evidence indicating the earliest presence of Tamil people in modern day Tamil Nadu are the megalithic urn burials, dating from around 1500 BC and onwards, which have been discovered at various locations in Tamil Nadu, notably in Adichanallur in Tirunelveli District which conform to the descriptions of funerals in classical Tamil literature.
[Contains English characters] Various legends became prevalent after the tenth century CE regarding the antiquity of the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] According to Iraiyanar Agapporul, a tenth/eleventh-century annotation on the Sangam literature, the Tamil country extended southwards beyond the natural boundaries of the Indian peninsula comprising 49 ancient nadus .
[Contains English characters] The land was supposed to have been destroyed by a deluge.
[Contains English characters] The Sangam legends also added to the antiquity of the Tamil people by claiming tens of thousands of years of continuous literary activity during three Sangams.
[Contains English characters] From around the third century BC onwards, three royal dynasties—the Cholas, the Cheras and the Pandyas—rose to dominate the ancient Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] Each of these dynasties had its own realm within the Tamil-speaking region.
[Contains English characters] Classical literature and inscriptions also describe a number of Velirs, or minor chieftains, who collectively ruled over large parts of central Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Wars between the kings and the chieftains were frequent, as were conflicts with ancient श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] These wars appear to have been fought to assert hegemony and demand tribute, rather than to subjugate and annex those territories.
[Contains English characters] The kings and chieftains were patrons of the arts, and a significant volume of literature exists from this period.
[Contains English characters] The literature shows that many of the cultural practices that are considered peculiarly Tamil date back to the classical period.
[Contains English characters] Agriculture was important during this period, and there is evidence that irrigation networks were built as early as 2nd century AD.
[Contains English characters] Internal and external trade flourished, and evidence exists of significant contact with Ancient Rome.
[Contains English characters] Large quantities of Roman coins and signs of the presence of Roman traders have been discovered at Karur and Arikamedu.
[Contains English characters] There is also evidence that at least two embassies were sent to the Roman Emperor Augustus by Pandya kings.
[Contains English characters] Potsherds with Tamil writing have also been found in excavations on the Red Sea, suggesting the presence of Tamil merchants there.
[Contains English characters] An anonymous first century travelers account written in Greek, Periplus Maris Erytraei, describes the ports of the Pandya and Chera kingdoms in Damirica and their commercial activity in great detail.
[Contains English characters] Periplus also indicates that the chief exports of the ancient Tamils were pepper, malabathrum, pearls, ivory, silk, spikenard, diamonds, sapphires, and tortoiseshell.
[Contains English characters] The classical period ended around the fourth century AD with invasions by the Kalabhra, referred to as the kalappirar in Tamil literature and inscriptions.
[Contains English characters] These invaders are described as evil kings and barbarians coming from lands to the north of the Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] This period, commonly referred to as the Dark Age of the Tamil country, ended with the rise of the Pallava dynasty.
[Contains English characters] According to Clarence Maloney, during the classical period Tamils also settled the Maldive Islands.
[Contains English characters] Although the Pallava records can be traced from the second century AD, they did not rise to prominence as an imperial dynasty until the sixth century.
[Contains English characters] The dynasty does not appear to have been Tamil in origin, although they rapidly adopted the local culture and the Tamil language.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas sought to model themselves after great northern dynasties such as the Mauryas and Guptas.
[Contains English characters] They therefore transformed the institution of the kingship into an imperial one, and sought to bring vast amounts of territory under their direct rule.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas were followers of the Hinduism, though for a short while one of their kings embraced Jainism and later converted to Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] The Bhakti movement in Hinduism was founded by Tamil saints at this time, and rose along with the growing influence of Jainism and Buddhism.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas pioneered the building of large, ornate temples in stone which formed the basis of the Dravidian temple architecture.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty was overthrown in the 9th century by the resurgent Cholas.
[Contains English characters] The Cholas become dominant in the 10th century and established an empire covering most of southern India and Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] The empire had strong trading links with China and Southeast Asia.
[Contains English characters] The Cholas navy conquered the South Asian kingdom of Sri Vijaya in Sumatra and continued as far as Thailand and Burma.
[Contains English characters] Chola power declined in the 12th and 13th centuries, and the Pandya dynasty enjoyed a brief period of resurgence thereafter during the rule of Sundara Pandya.
[Contains English characters] However, repeated Muslim invasions from the 15th century onwards placed a huge strain on the empires resources, and the dynasty came to an end in the 16th century.
[Contains English characters] The western Tamil lands became increasingly politically distinct from the rest of the Tamil lands after the Chola and Pandya empires lost control over them in the 13th century.
[Contains English characters] They developed their own distinct language and literature, which increasingly grew apart from Tamil, evolving into the modern Malayalam language by the 15th century.
[Contains English characters] No major empires arose thereafter, and parts of Tamil Nadu were for a while ruled by a number of different local chiefs, such as the Nayaks of the modern महाराष्ट्र and Andhra Pradesh regions.
[Contains English characters] From the 17th century onwards, European powers began establishing settlements and trading outposts in the region.
[Contains English characters] A number of battles were fought between the British, French and Danish in the 18th century, and by the end of the 18th century most of Tamil Nadu was under British rule.
[Contains English characters] There is little scholarly consensus over the presence of the Tamil people in Sri Lanka, also known as Eelam in early Tamil literature, prior to the medieval Chola period .
[Contains English characters] One theory states that there was not an organized Tamil presence in Sri Lanka until the invasions from what is now South India in the 10th century AD; another theory contends that Tamil people were the original inhabitants of the island.
[Contains English characters] The indigenous Veddhas are physically related to Dravidian language-speaking tribal people in South India and early populations of Southeast Asia, although they no longer speak their native languages.
[Contains English characters] It is believed that cultural diffusion, rather than migration of people, spread the Sinhalese and Tamil languages from peninsular India into an existing Mesolithic population, centuries before the Christian era.
[Contains English characters] Settlements of people culturally similar to those of present-day Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu in modern India were excavated at megalithic burial sites at Pomparippu on the west coast and in Kathiraveli on the east coast of the island, villages established between the 5th century BC and 2nd century AD.

[Contains English characters] By the 8th century AD there were Tamil villages collectively known as Demel-kaballa, Demelat-valademin, and Demel-gam-bim .

[Contains English characters] Upon arrival of European powers from the 17th century CE, the Tamils separate nation was described in their areas of habitation in the northeast of the island.

[Contains English characters] The Hindu migration and assimilation continued until the 18th century AD.
[Contains English characters] British colonists consolidated the Tamil territory in southern India into the Madras Presidency, which was integrated into British India.
[Contains English characters] Similarly, the Tamil parts of Sri Lanka joined with the other regions of the island in 1802 to form the Ceylon colony.
[Contains English characters] They remained in political union with India and श्रीलंका after their independence, in 1947 and 1948 respectively.
[Contains English characters] When India became independent in 1947, Madras Presidency became the Madras State, comprising present-day Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh, northern केरळ, and the southwest coast of Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] The state was subsequently split along linguistic lines.
[Contains English characters] In 1953, the northern districts formed Andhra Pradesh.

[Contains English characters] There was some initial demand for an independent Tamil state following the adoption of the federal system.
[Contains English characters] However, the Indian constitution granted significant autonomy to the states, and protests by Tamils in 1963 led to the government adopting a new policy called the three language formula.
[Contains English characters] This has led to Tamils in India becoming increasingly satisfied with the federal arrangement, and there is very little support for secession or independence today.
[Contains English characters] In Sri Lanka, however, the unitary arrangement led to a growing belief among some Tamils of discrimination by the Sinhalese majority.
[Contains English characters] This resulted in a demand for federalism, which in the 1970s grew into a movement for an autonomous Tamil country.

[Contains English characters] Today Tamils make up 18% of Sri Lankas population .
[Contains English characters] Most Indian Tamils live in the state of Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Tamils are the majority in the union territory of Pondicherry, a former French colony.
[Contains English characters] Pondicherry is a subnational enclave situated within Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Tamils account for at least one-sixth of the population in Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
[Contains English characters] There are also Tamil communities in other parts of India.
[Contains English characters] Most of these have emerged fairly recently, dating to the colonial and post-colonial periods, but some—particularly the Hebbar and Mandyam Tamils of southern Karnataka, पुणे, महाराष्ट्र, Andhra Pradesh, Palakkad in केरळ, and Delhi — date back to at least the medieval period.
[Contains English characters] There are two groups of Tamils in Sri Lanka: the Sri Lankan Tamils and the Indian Tamils.
[Contains English characters] The Sri Lankan Tamils are descendants of the Tamils of the old Jaffna Kingdom and east coast chieftaincies called Vannimais.
[Contains English characters] The Indian Tamils are descendants of bonded laborers sent from Tamil Nadu to Sri Lanka in the 19th century to work on tea plantations.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, there is a significant Tamil-speaking Muslim population in Sri Lanka; however, unlike Tamil Muslims from India, they are not ethnic Tamils and are therefore listed as a separate ethnic group in official statistics.
[Contains English characters] Most Sri Lankan Tamils live in the Northern and Eastern provinces and in the capital कोलंबो, whereas most Indian Tamils live in the central highlands.
[Contains English characters] Historically both groups have seen themselves as separate communities, although there is a greater sense of unity since 1980s.
[Contains English characters] In 1949, the United National Party government, which included G. G. Ponnambalam, leader of the Tamil Congress, stripped the Indian Tamils of their citizenship.
[Contains English characters] This was opposed by S. J. V. Chelvanayakam, the leader of Tamil nationalist Federal Party, and most Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] Under the terms of an agreement reached between the Sri Lankan and Indian governments in the 1960s, about 40 percent of the Indian Tamils were granted Sri Lankan citizenship, and many of the remainder were repatriated to India.
[Contains English characters] By the 1990s, most Indian Tamils had received Sri Lankan citizenship.
[Contains English characters] Significant Tamil emigration began in the 18th century, when the British colonial government sent many poor Tamils as indentured labourers to far-off parts of the Empire, especially Malaya, South Africa, Fiji, Mauritius and the Caribbean.
[Contains English characters] At about the same time, many Tamil businessmen also immigrated to other parts of the British Empire, particularly to Burma and East Africa.
[Contains English characters] Many Tamils still live in these countries, and the Tamil communities in Singapore, Reunion Island, Malaysia and South Africa have retained much of their culture and language.
[Contains English characters] Many Malaysian children attend Tamil schools, and a significant portion of Tamil children in Mauritius and Reunion are brought up with Tamil as their first language.
[Contains English characters] In Singapore, Tamil students learn Tamil as their second language in school, with English as the first.
[Contains English characters] To preserve the Tamil language, the Singapore government has made it an official language despite Tamils comprising only about 5% of the population, and has also introduced compulsory instruction of the language for Tamils.
[Contains English characters] Other Tamil communities, such as those in South Africa and Fiji, no longer speak Tamil as a first language, but still retain a strong Tamil identity, and are able to understand the language, while most elders speak it as a first language.
[Contains English characters] A large emigration also began in the 1980s, as Sri Lankan Tamils sought to escape the ethnic conflict there.
[Contains English characters] These recent emigrants have most often fled to ऑस्ट्रेलिया, युरोप, North America and Southeast Asia.
[Contains English characters] Today, the largest concentration of Tamils outside southern Asia is in Toronto, Canada.
[Contains English characters] Many young Tamil professionals from India have also immigrated to Europe and the United States in recent times in search of better opportunities.
[Contains English characters] These new immigrant communities have established cultural associations to protect and promote Tamil culture and language in their adopted homes.
[Contains English characters] Tamils have strong feelings towards the Tamil language, which is often venerated in literature as Tamil̲an̲n̲ai, the Tamil mother.
[Contains English characters] It has historically been, and to large extent still is, central to the Tamil identity.
[Contains English characters] Like the other languages of South India, it is a Dravidian language, unrelated to the Indo-European languages of northern India.
[Contains English characters] The language has been far less influenced by Sanskrit than the other Dravidian languages, and preserves many features of Proto-Dravidian, though modern-day spoken Tamil in Tamil Nadu, freely uses loanwords from Sanskrit and English.
[Contains English characters] Tamil literature is of considerable antiquity, and is recognised as a classical language by the government of India.
[Contains English characters] Classical Tamil literature, which ranges from lyric poetry to works on poetics and ethical philosophy, is remarkably different from contemporary and later literature in other Indian languages, and represents the oldest body of secular literature in South Asia.
[Contains English characters] Notable works in classical Tamil literature include the Tirukkural, by Tiruvalluvar, the five great Tamil epics, and the works of Auvaiyar.
[Contains English characters] Modern Tamil literature is diverse.
[Contains English characters] It includes Indian Nationalism, in the works of Subramanya Bharathi; historical romanticism, by Kalki Krishnamurthy; radical and moderate social realism, by Pudhumaipithan and Jayakanthan; and feminism, by Malathi Maithri and Kutti Revathi.
[Contains English characters] Sujatha Rangarajan, an author whose works range from romance novels to science fiction, is one of the most popular modern writers in Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Sri Lankan Tamil literature has produced several works reflecting the civilian tragedy caused by decades of war.
[Contains English characters] There is also an emerging diaspora literature in Tamil.
[Contains English characters] There are a number of regional dialects in use by the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] These dialects vary among regions and communities.
[Contains English characters] Tamil dialects are mainly differentiated by the disparate phonological changes and sound shifts that have evolved from Old Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Although most Tamil dialects do not differ significantly in their vocabulary, there are a few exceptions.
[Contains English characters] The dialects spoken in Sri Lanka retain many words that are not in everyday use in India, and use many other words slightly differently.
[Contains English characters] The dialect of the Iyers of Palakkad has a large number of Malayalam loanwords, has been influenced by Malayalam syntax, and has a distinct Malayalam accent.
[Contains English characters] The Sankethi, Hebbar, and Mandyam dialects, the former spoken by groups of Tamil Iyers, and the latter two by Vaishnavites who migrated to Karnataka in the 11th century, retains many Vaishnavite religious and spiritual values.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil spoken in चेन्नई infuses English words, and is called Madras Bashai .
[Contains English characters] Most traditional Tamil art is religious in some form and usually centres on Hinduism, although the religious element is often only a means to represent universal—and, occasionally, humanist—themes.
[Contains English characters] The most important form of Tamil painting is Tanjore painting, which originated in Thanjavur in the ninth century.
[Contains English characters] The paintings base is made of cloth and coated with zinc oxide, over which the image is painted using dyes; it is then decorated with semi-precious stones, as well as silver or gold thread.
[Contains English characters] A style which is related in origin, but which exhibits significant differences in execution, is used for painting murals on temple walls; the most notable example are the murals on the Kutal Azhakar and Meenakshi temples of Madurai, the Brihadeeswarar temple of Tanjore.
[Contains English characters] Tamil art, in general, is known for its stylistic elegance, rich colours, and attention to small details.
[Contains English characters] Tamil sculpture ranges from elegant stone sculptures in temples, to bronze icons with exquisite details.
[Contains English characters] The medieval Chola bronzes are considered to be one of Indias greatest contributions to the world art.
[Contains English characters] Unlike most Western art, the material in Tamil sculpture does not influence the form taken by the sculpture; instead, the artist imposes his/her vision of the form on the material.
[Contains English characters] As a result, one often sees in stone sculptures flowing forms that are usually reserved for metal.
[Contains English characters] As with painting, these sculptures show a fine eye for detail; great care is taken in sculpting the minute details of jewellery, worn by the subjects of the sculpture.
[Contains English characters] The lines tend to be smooth and flowing, and many pieces skillfully capture movement.
[Contains English characters] The cave sculptures at Mamallapuram are a particularly fine example of the technique, as are the bronzes of the Chola period.
[Contains English characters] A particularly popular motif in the bronzes was the depiction of Shiva as Nataraja, in a dance posture with one leg upraised, and a fiery circular halo surrounding his body.
[Contains English characters] Tamil temples were often simply treated as sculptures on a grand scale.
[Contains English characters] The temples are most notable for their high spires, known as Gopura, consisting of a number of stepped levels, and the vimanam, which rises above the sanctum sanctorum.
[Contains English characters] During the Chola period, the vimanams had more prominence, as seen in the Brihadīsvara temple of Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] During the Nayak period, the spires became progressively more elaborate and ornate, as exemplified by the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, while the vimanam became much smaller.
[Contains English characters] From the 13th century onwards, the entrance gates to the temples, called gopurams in Tamil, also began to grow bigger, and more elaborate.
[Contains English characters] The temples at Chidambaram and Srirangam have particularly impressive gopurams, covered with sculptures and reliefs of various scenes and characters from Hindu mythology.
[Contains English characters] As with Indian art in general, Tamil art does not traditionally aspire to portraiture or realism.
[Contains English characters] Much more emphasis is placed on the representation of ideal prototypes, and on depicting the symbols with which the theme of the artistic work is associated.
[Contains English characters] This means that small details, such as the direction which a hand faces, the animals or trees portrayed, or the time of day depicted, are often of critical importance to understanding the meaning of a work of art.
[Contains English characters] The traditional Tamil performing arts have ancient roots.
[Contains English characters] The royal courts and temples have been centres for the performing arts since the classical period, and possibly earlier.
[Contains English characters] Descriptions of performances in classical Tamil literature and the Natya Shastra, a Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts, indicate a close relationship between the ancient and modern artforms.
[Contains English characters] The aim of a performance in Tamil tradition, is to bring out the rasa, the flavor, mood, or feeling, inherent in the text, and its quality is measured by the extent to which it induces the mood in the audience.
[Contains English characters] Tamil shares a classical musical tradition, called carnatic music, with the rest of South India.
[Contains English characters] It is primarily oriented towards vocal music, with instruments functioning either as accompaniments, or as imitations of the singers role.
[Contains English characters] Ancient Tamil works, such as the Cilappatikaram, describe a system of music that includes old Carnatic modes, and a seventh-century Pallava inscription at Kudimiyamalai contains one of the earliest surviving examples of Indian music in notation.
[Contains English characters] Modern Carnatic music is organized around the twin notions of melody types, and cyclical rhythm types .
[Contains English characters] Unlike the northern Hindustani music tradition, carnatic music is almost exclusively religious.
[Contains English characters] In sharp contrast with the restrained and intellectual nature of carnatic music, Tamil folk music tends to be much more exuberant.
[Contains English characters] Popular forms of Tamil folk music include the Villuppattu, a form of music performed with a bow, and the Naattupurapaattu, ballads that convey folklore and folk history.
[Contains English characters] The dominant classical dance amongst Tamils is Bharatanatyam.
[Contains English characters] Bharatanatyam is performative, rather than participative.
[Contains English characters] The dance is an exposition of the story contained in a song, and is usually performed by one performer on stage, with an orchestra of drums, a drone, and one or more singers backstage.
[Contains English characters] The story is told through a complicated combination of mudras, facial expressions, and body postures.
[Contains English characters] Dancers used to be exclusively female, but the dance now also has several well-known male practitioners.
[Contains English characters] The most notable of Tamil folk dances is karakattam.
[Contains English characters] In its religious form, the dance is performed in front of an image of the goddess Mariamma.
[Contains English characters] The dancer bears, on his or her head, a brass pot filled with uncooked rice, decorated with flowers and surrounded by a bamboo frame, and tumbles and leaps to the rhythm of a song without spilling a grain.
[Contains English characters] Karakāṭṭam is usually performed to a special type of song, known as temmanguppattu, a folk song in the mode of a lover speaking to his beloved, to the accompaniment of a nadaswaram and melam.
[Contains English characters] Other Tamil folk dances include mayilattam, where the dancers tie a string of peacock feathers around their waists; oyilattam, danced in a circle while waving small pieces of cloth of various colors; poykkal kuthiraiyaattam, in which the dancers use dummy horses; manaattam, in which the dancers imitate the graceful leaping of deer; paraiyattam, a dance to the sound of rhythmical drumbeats; and thippanthattam, a dance involving playing with burning torches.
[Contains English characters] The kuravanci is a type of dance-drama, performed by four to eight women.
[Contains English characters] The drama is opened by a woman playing the part of a female soothsayer of the kurava tribe, who tells the story of a lady pining for her lover.
[Contains English characters] The therukoothu, literally meaning street play, is a form of village theater or folk opera.
[Contains English characters] It is traditionally performed in village squares, with no sets and very simple props.
[Contains English characters] The performances involve songs and dances, and the stories can be either religious or secular.
[Contains English characters] The performances are not formal, and performers often interact with the audience, mocking them, or involving them in the dialogue.
[Contains English characters] Therukkūthu has, in recent times, been very successfully adapted to convey social messages, such as abstinence and anti-caste criticism, as well as information about legal rights, and has spread to other parts of India.
[Contains English characters] The village of Melattur, in Tamil Nadu, has a special type of performance, called the bhagavata-mela, in honour of the local deity, which is performed once a year, and lasts all night.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Nadu also has a well developed stage theater tradition, which has been heavily influenced by western theatre.
[Contains English characters] A number of theatrical companies exist, with repertoires including absurdist, realist, and humorous plays.
[Contains English characters] Both classical and folk performing arts survive in modern Tamil society.
[Contains English characters] Tamil people in Tamil Nadu are also passionate about films.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil film industry, commonly dubbed Kollywood, is the second-largest film industry in India.
[Contains English characters] Tamil cinema is appreciated both for its technical accomplishments, and for its artistic and entertainment value.
[Contains English characters] Several actors dominated the early years of the cinema including Sivaji Ganesan, Gemini Ganesan, and several others.
[Contains English characters] As in the past, a small number of actors continue to dominate in Kollywood movies.
[Contains English characters] Several Tamil actresses have made their mark very strong in Bollywood over the years and have often dominated the scene, such as Vyjayanthimala, Rekha Ganesan, the original golden girl Hema Malini,Meenakshi Sheshadri, Vidya Balan, and Sridevi.
[Contains English characters] The overwhelming majority of Tamil films contain song and dance sequences, and Tamil film music is a popular genre in its own right, often liberally fusing elements of carnatic, Tamil folk, North Indian styles, hip-hop, and heavy metal.
[Contains English characters] Famous music directors of the late 20th century included M. S. Viswanathan, Ilayaraaja, and A.
[Contains English characters] R. Rahman. About 88% of the population of Tamil Nadu are Hindus.
[Contains English characters] Muslims and Christians account for 6% and 5.5% respectively.
[Contains English characters] Most of the Christians are Roman Catholics.
[Contains English characters] The majority of Muslims in Tamil Nadu speak Tamil, with less than 40% reporting Urdu as their mother tongue.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Jains number only a few thousand now.
[Contains English characters] Atheist, rationalist, and humanist philosophies are also adhered by sizable minorities, as a result of Tamil cultural revivalism in the twentieth century, and its antipathy to what it saw as Brahminical Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] The most popular deity is Murugan, also known as Karthikeya, the son of Siva.
[Contains English characters] The worship of Amman, also called Mariamman, is thought to have been derived from an ancient mother goddess, is also very common.
[Contains English characters] Kan̲n̲agi, the heroine of the Cilappatikār̲am, is worshipped as Pattin̲i by many Tamils, particularly in श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] There are also many followers of Ayyavazhi in Tamil Nadu, mainly in the southern districts.
[Contains English characters] In addition, there are many temples and devotees of Vishnu, Siva, Ganapathi, and the other Hindu deities.
[Contains English characters] The most important Tamil festivals are Pongal, a harvest festival that occurs in mid-January, and Varudapirappu, the Tamil New Year, which occurs around mid-April.
[Contains English characters] Both are celebrated by almost all Tamils, regardless of religion.
[Contains English characters] The Hindu festival Deepavali is celebrated with fanfare; other local Hindu festivals include Thaipusam, Panguni Uttiram, and Adiperukku.
[Contains English characters] While Adiperukku is celebrated with more pomp in the Cauvery region than in others, the Ayyavazhi Festival, Ayya Vaikunda Avataram, is predominantly celebrated in the southern districts of Kanyakumari, Tirunelveli, and Thoothukudi.
[Contains English characters] In rural Tamil Nadu, many local deities, called aiyyan̲ārs, are thought to be the spirits of local heroes who protect the village from harm.
[Contains English characters] Their worship often centers around nadukkal, stones erected in memory of heroes who died in battle.
[Contains English characters] This form of worship is mentioned frequently in classical literature and appears to be the surviving remnants of an ancient Tamil tradition.
[Contains English characters] The Saivist sect of Hinduism is significantly represented amongst Tamils, more so among Sri Lankan Tamils, although most of the Saivist places of religious significance are in northern India.
[Contains English characters] The Alvars and Nayanars, who were predominantly Tamils, played a key role in the renaissance of Bhakti tradition in India.
[Contains English characters] In the 10th century, the philosopher Ramanuja, who propagated the theory of Visishtadvaitam, brought many changes to worshiping practices, creating new regulations on temple worship, and accepted lower-caste Hindus as his prime disciples.
[Contains English characters] Christianity is believed to have come to Tamil Nadu with the arrival of St.
[Contains English characters] Thomas the apostle, and the number of Tamil Christians grew during the colonial period.
[Contains English characters] Most Tamil Christians are Catholic and Protestant.
[Contains English characters] Islam started flourishing in Tamilnadu after the arrival of Sulthan Syed Ibrahim Shaheed, descendant of Prophet Muhammmad who came from Madinah, Saudi Arabia during 12th century.
[Contains English characters] His grave is found in Erwadi dargah in Ramanathapuram district.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Muslims are mostly either mainstream Sunni or Sufi.
[Contains English characters] Each geographical area where Tamils live has developed its own distinct variant of the common dishes plus a few dishes distinctly native to itself.
[Contains English characters] The Chettinad region, comprising of Karaikudi and adjoining areas, is known for both traditional vegetarian dishes, like appam, uthappam, paal paniyaram, and non-vegetarian dishes, made primarily using chicken.
[Contains English characters] Rice, the major staple food in most of Tamil, is usually steamed and served with about two to six accompanying items, which typically include sambar, dry curry, rasam, kootu, and thayir or moru .
[Contains English characters] Tiffin or Light meals usually include one or more of Pongal, Dosai, idli, Vadai along with sambar and Chutney is often served as either breakfast or as an evening snack.
[Contains English characters] Ghee Clarified butter called neyyi in Tamil, is used to flavor the rice when eaten with dhal or sambar, but not with curds or buttermilk.
[Contains English characters] Morkulambu, a dish which can be spiced with moru, is also popular with steamed rice.
[Contains English characters] Various martial arts including Kuttu Varisai, Varma Kalai, Silambam Nillaikalakki, Maankombukkalai and Kalarippayattu, are practised in Tamil Nadu and केरळ.
[Contains English characters] The weapons used include Silambam, Maankombukkalai, Yeratthai Mulangkol, Surul Pattai, Val Vitchi, and Yeretthai Val .
[Contains English characters] The ancient Tamil art of unarmed bullfighting, popular amongst warriors in the classical period, has also survived in parts of Tamil Nadu, notably Alanganallur near Madurai, where it is known as Jallikaṭṭu or mañcuviraṭṭu and is held once a year around the time of the Pongal festival.
[Contains English characters] The global spread of the Tamil diaspora has hindered the formation of formal pan-Tamil institutions.
[Contains English characters] The most important national institutions for Tamils have been the governments of the states where they live, particularly the government of Tamil Nadu and the government of Sri Lanka, which have collaborated in developing technical and scientific terminology in Tamil and promoting its use since the 1950s.
[Contains English characters] Politics in Tamil Nadu is dominated by the Self-respect movement, founded by E. V. Ramasami, popularly known as Periyar, to promote self-respect and rationalism, and to fight casteism and the oppression of the lowest castes.
[Contains English characters] Every major political party in Tamil Nadu bases its ideology on the Self-respect Movement, and the national political parties play a very small role in Tamil politics.
[Contains English characters] In श्रीलंका, Tamil politics was dominated by the federalist movements, led by the Federal Party, until the early 1980s.
[Contains English characters] In the 1980s, the political movement for self determination in an autonomous Tamil Eelam was largely succeeded by a violent military campaign conducted by several militant groups.
[Contains English characters] The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, which emerged as the most important force amongst these groups in the 1990s, controlled a third of Sri Lanka, and had attempted to establish its own government there.
[Contains English characters] In the 1960s, the government of Tamil Nadu held a World Tamil Conference, which has continued to meet periodically since then.
[Contains English characters] In 1999, a World Tamil Confederation was established to protect and foster Tamil culture and further a sense of togetherness amongst Tamils in different countries.
[Contains English characters] The Confederation has since adopted a Tamil flag and Tamil song to act as trans-national symbols for the Tamil people; the words on the flag quote the opening line of a poem by the classical poet Kanian Poongundranaar, and means Everyone is our kin; Everyplace is our home.

[Contains English characters] Objectivity is both a central and elusive concept in philosophy.
[Contains English characters] While there is no universally accepted articulation of objectivity, a proposition is generally considered to be objectively true when its truth conditions are mind-independent—that is, not the result of any judgments made by a conscious entity.
[Contains English characters] Objective truths are those which are discovered rather than created.
[Unnaturally long word detected: निर्णयप्रक्रीयेतून] त्यांची निर्मिती व्यक्तिंकडून भावनाप्रधान जाणीवेच्या निर्णयप्रक्रीयेतून होऊ शकत नाही; सहसा सत्य परिस्थिती मनाच्या निरपेक्ष आणि निष्पक्ष असते तेव्हा ती वस्तिनिष्ठ सत्य समजली जाते.
[Contains English characters] वस्तुनिष्ठ सत्ये आढळतात ते निर्माण करता येत नाहीत In philosophy, an objective fact means a truth that remains true everywhere, independently of human thought or feelings.
[Contains English characters] For instance, it is true always and everywhere that in base 10, 2 plus 2 equals 4.
[Contains English characters] A subjective fact is one that is only true under certain conditions, at certain times, in certain places, or for certain people.
[Contains English characters] Among the truth-conducive tools of thought used by objective thinkers are the scientific virtues.
[Contains English characters] When formulating a hypothesis to explain a particular fact, the explainer makes sure that his or her hypothesis is the simplest one on offer, that it is adequate to all known evidence, that it can predict as diverse an array of phenomena as possible, and that it is fruitfully risky, according to Popperians, but more generally, that it can be verified by new or as yet unperformed experiments or observations.
[Contains English characters] The scientific virtue known as simplicity or parsimony has also come to be known as Ockham’s Razor because of its frequent use by the fourteenth century philosopher William of Ockham, whose primary statement of the principle in his nominalist epistemology is that in accounting for the facts nothing should be assumed as necessary unless it is established through evidentiary experience or reasoning, or is required by the articles of faith.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Original researchObjectivism is a term that describes a branch of philosophy that originated in the early nineteenth century.
[Contains English characters] Gottlob Frege was the first to apply it, when he expounded an epistemological and metaphysical theory contrary to that of Immanuel Kant.
[Contains English characters] Kants rationalism attempted to reconcile the failures he perceived in realism, empiricism, and idealism and to establish a critical method of approach in the distinction between epistemology and metaphysics.
[Contains English characters] Objectivism, in this context, is an alternate name for philosophical realism, the view that there is a reality or ontological realm of objects and facts that exists independent of the mind.
[Contains English characters] Stronger versions of this claim might hold that there is only one correct description of this reality.
[Contains English characters] If it is true that reality is mind-independent, it is thus inclusive of objects that are unknown and not the subject of intentionality.
[Contains English characters] Objectivity in referring requires a definition of truth.
[Contains English characters] According to metaphysical objectivists, an object may truthfully be said to have this or that attribute, as in the statement This object exists, whereas the statement This object is true or false is meaningless.
[Contains English characters] Thus, only propositions have truth values.
[Contains English characters] Essentially, the terms objectivity and objectivism are not synonymous, with objectivism being an ontological theory that incorporates a commitment to the objectivity of objects.
[Contains English characters] Platos realism was a form of metaphysical objectivism, holding that the Ideas exist objectively and independently.
[Contains English characters] Berkeleys empiricist idealism, on the other hand, could be called a subjectivism: he held that things only exist to the extent that they are perceived.
[Contains English characters] Both theories claim methods of objectivity.
[Contains English characters] Platos definition of objectivity can be found in his epistemology, which takes as a model mathematics, and his metaphysics, where knowledge of the ontological status of objects and ideas is resistant to change.
[Contains English characters] Plato considered knowledge of geometry as a condition of philosophical knowledge, both being concerned with universal truths.
[Contains English characters] Platos opposition between objective knowledge and doxa would become the basis for later philosophies intent on resolving the problem of reality, knowledge and human existence.
[Contains English characters] Personal opinions belong to the changing sphere of the sensible, opposed to a fixed and eternal incorporeal realm which is mutually intelligible.
[Contains English characters] Where Plato distinguishes between what and how we know things and their ontological status as things, subjectivism such as Berkeleys and a mind dependence of knowledge and reality fails to make the distinction between what one knows and what is to be known, or in the least explains the distinction superficially.
[Contains English characters] In Platonic terms, a criticism of subjectivism is that it is difficult to distinguish between knowledge, doxa, and subjective knowledge, distinctions which Plato makes.
[Contains English characters] The importance of perception in evaluating and understanding objective reality is debated.
[Contains English characters] Realists argue that perception is key in directly observing objective reality, while instrumentalists hold that perception is not necessarily useful in directly observing objective reality, but is useful in interpreting and predicting reality.
[Contains English characters] The concepts that encompasses these ideas are important in the philosophy of science.
[Contains English characters] The term, ethical subjectivism, covers two distinct theories in ethics.
[Contains English characters] According to cognitive versions of ethical subjectivism, the truth of moral statements depends upon peoples values, attitudes, feelings, or beliefs.
[Contains English characters] Some forms of cognitivist ethical subjectivism can be counted as forms of realism, others are forms of anti-realism.
[Contains English characters] David Hume is a foundational figure for cognitive ethical subjectivism.
[Contains English characters] On a standard interpretation of his theory, a trait of character counts as a moral virtue when it evokes a sentiment of approbation in a sympathetic, informed, and rational human observer.
[Contains English characters] Similarly, Roderick Firths ideal observer theory held that right acts are those that an impartial, rational observer would approve of.
[Contains English characters] William James, another ethical subjectivist, held that an end is good just in case it is desired by that person .
[Contains English characters] According to non-cognitive versions of ethical subjectivism, such as emotivism, prescriptivism, and expressivism, ethical statements cannot be true or false, at all: rather, they are expressions of personal feelings or commands.
[Contains English characters] For example, on A. J. Ayers emotivism, the statement, Murder is wrong is equivalent in meaning to the emotive ejaculation, Murder, Boo!
[Contains English characters] According to the ethical objectivist, the truth or falsity of typical moral judgments does not depend upon the beliefs or feelings of any person or group of persons.
[Contains English characters] This view holds that moral propositions are analogous to propositions about chemistry, biology, or history: they describe a mind-independent reality.
[Contains English characters] When they describe it accurately, they are true --- no matter what anyone believes, hopes, wishes, or feels.
[Contains English characters] When they fail to describe this mind-independent moral reality, they are false --- no matter what anyone believes, hopes, wishes, or feels.
[Contains English characters] There are many versions of ethical objectivism, including various religious views of morality, Platonistic intuitionism, Kantianism, utilitarianism, and certain forms of ethical egoism and contractualism.
[Contains English characters] Note that Platonists define ethical objectivism in an even more narrow way, so that it requires the existence of intrinsic value.
[Contains English characters] Consequently, they reject the idea that contractualists or egoists could be ethical objectivists.

[Contains English characters] Thompson was born in New Orleans, Louisiana, USA.
[Contains English characters] He received a Bachelor of Science in 1965 and Masters degree in 1966, both in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, from the University of California, Berkeley, where his Masters thesis advisor was Elwyn Berlekamp.
[Contains English characters] In the 1960s, Thompson and Dennis Ritchie worked on the Multics operating system.
[Contains English characters] While writing Multics, Thompson created the Bon programming language.
[Contains English characters] The two left the Multics project as it was becoming too complex, but they took the lessons they learned to Bell Labs, where, in 1969, Thompson and Ritchie were the principal creators of the UNIX operating system.
[Contains English characters] There, Thompson also wrote the B programming language, a precursor to Ritchies C.
[Contains English characters] Thompson had developed the CTSS version of the editor QED, which included regular expressions for searching text.
[Contains English characters] QED and Thompsons later editor ed contributed greatly to the eventual popularity of regular expressions, previously regarded mostly as a tool for logicians.
[Contains English characters] Regular expressions became pervasive in Unix text processing programs, and even more modern programming languages like Perl.
[Contains English characters] Almost all programs that work with regular expressions today use some variant of Thompsons notation for them.
[Contains English characters] Along with Joseph Condon, he created the hardware and software for Belle, a chess computer.
[Contains English characters] He also wrote programs for generating the complete enumeration of chess endings, for all 4, 5, and 6-piece endings, allowing chess-playing computer programs to make perfect moves once a position stored in them is reached.
[Contains English characters] Later, with the help of chess endgame expert John Roycroft, Thompson distributed his first results on CD-ROM.
[Contains English characters] Thompsons style of programming has influenced others, notably in the terseness of his expressions and a preference for clear statements.
[Contains English characters] In late 2000, Thompson retired from Bell Labs.
[Contains English characters] He worked at Entrisphere, Inc as a fellow until 2006, and now works at Google.

[Contains English characters] तमिळ दिनदर्शिका The Tamil calendar is used in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry in India, and by the Tamil population in Malaysia, Singapore and श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] It is used today for cultural, religious and agricultural events, with the Gregorian calendar having largely supplanted it for official use both within and outside India.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil calendar is based on the classical Hindu solar calendar also used in Assam, Bengal, केरळ, Manipur, Nepal, Orissa, Rajasthan and the Punjab.
[Contains English characters] There are several festivals based on the Tamil Hindu calendar.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil New Year follows the nirayanam vernal equinox and generally falls on April 13 or 14th of the Gregorian year.
[Contains English characters] April 13 or 14th marks the first day of the traditional Tamil calendar and this remains a public holiday in both Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] Tropical vernal equinox fall around 22 March, and adding 23 degrees of trepidation or oscillation to it, we get the Hindu sidereal or Nirayana Mesha Sankranti .
[Contains English characters] Hence, the Tamil calendar begins on the same date in April which is observed by most traditional calendars of the rest of India - Assam, Bengal, केरळ, Orissa, Manipur, Nepal, Punjab etc.
[Contains English characters] This also coincides with the traditional new year in Burma, Cambodia, Laos, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
[Contains English characters] The 60-year cycle is also very ancient and is observed by most traditional calendars of India and China, and is related to 5 revolutions of Jupiter according to popular belief, or to 60-year orbit of Nakshatras as mentioned in Surya Siddhanta.
[Contains English characters] The traditional Tamil year starts on April 14, 2010, Kaliyuga 5112. Vikrama and Shalivahana Saka eras are also used.
[Contains English characters] There are several references in early Tamil literature to the April new year.
[Contains English characters] Nakkirar, the author of the Nedunalvaadai writes in the 3rd century that the Sun travels from Mesha/Chitterai through 11 successive Raasis or signs of the zodiac.
[Contains English characters] Koodaloor Kizhaar in the 3rd century refers to Mesha Raasi/Chitterai as the commencement of the year in the Puranaanooru.
[Contains English characters] The 8th century Silappadikaaram mentions the 12 Raasis or zodiac signs starting with Mesha/Chitterai.
[Contains English characters] The Manimekalai alludes to the Hindu solar calendar as we know it today. . The days of the Tamil Calendar relate to the celestial bodies in the solar system: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn, in that order.
[Contains English characters] The week starts with Sunday.
[Contains English characters] This list compiles the days of the week in the Tamil calendar: For Tamils the each day begins at the sun set and that is why it is being said on the evening of Thursday it was told it is the meeting point of Thursday and Friday which is why loans are to be eschewed during this period onwards till Friday wanes off.
[Contains English characters] In this regard Parthimar Kalingar has done extensive research to prove the beginning of a Tamil day The number of days in a month varies between 29 and 32. The following list compiles the months of the Tamil Calendar.
[Contains English characters] Note: The Sanskrit months above would start one month ahead of Tamil months since the Tamil calendar is a solar calendar while the Sanskrit calendar is a lunisolar calendar The Tamil year, in keeping with the old Indic calendar, is divided into six seasons, each of which lasts two months: The 60-year cycle of the Tamil calendar is common to North and South Indian traditional calendars, with the same name and sequence of years.
[Contains English characters] Its earliest reference is to be found in Surya Siddhanta, which Varahamihirar believed to be the most accurate of the then current theories of astronomy.
[Contains English characters] However, in the Surya Siddhantic list, the first year was Vijaya and not Prabhava as currently used.
[Contains English characters] This 60-year cycle is also used in the Chinese calendar.
[Contains English characters] After the completion of sixty years, the calendar starts anew with the first year.
[Contains English characters] This corresponds to the Hindu century.
[Contains English characters] The Vakya or Tirukannitha Panchangam outlines this sequence.
[Contains English characters] The following list presents the current 60-year cycle of the Tamil calendar: The months of the Tamil Calendar have great significance and are deeply rooted in the faith of the Tamil Hindus.
[Contains English characters] Some months are considered very auspicious while a few are considered inauspicious as well.
[Contains English characters] Some of the celebrations for each month are listed below.

[Contains English characters] The most famous Hindu festival Deepavali is celebrated in this month.
[Contains English characters] The Fridays of this month - Aipassi velli - are dedicated to religious observance.
[Contains English characters] Each Monday of this month is dedicated to the worship of Lord Murugan.
[Contains English characters] Every Monday is called Somavaaram when 108 or 1008 sangabhishekam are offered to Lord Shiva and Lord Muruga.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil Calendar is so important to the life of Tamil-speaking people that most of the Festivals of Tamil Nadu are based on it.
[Contains English characters] Some of Festivals include Tamil New Year or Puthandu in mid-April, Thai Pongal, Deepavali, Panguni Uthiram, Thirukaarthigai, Aadiperukku, Navaratri etc.

This page covers advanced template techniques, in particular the use of variable template names and parameter names in templates.
[Contains English characters] Readers should be thoroughly familiar with the standard template techniques found in Help:Template.
[Contains English characters] Some techniques described below may be outdated or of limited use; for example, ParserFunctions may be more convenient than some of the branching techniques discussed.
[Contains English characters] सर्वसाधारणपणे,ही तंत्रे पुनर्कृति recursive पद्धतीच्या साच्यांवर प्रक्रिया करण्यावर अवलंबुन असतात.
[Contains English characters] जेंव्हा एखाद्या साच्यावर प्रक्रिया करण्यात येते,ती साच्याचा संकेतास string values भाषांतरीत करते.
[Contains English characters] दोन महिरपी कंसात text strings बद्ध केल्यावर साच्यांची नावे किंवा बदल नावे म्हणुनही त्यावर पुनर्प्रक्रिया केल्या जाउ शकते.
[Contains English characters] त्याने, string च्या किंमती बदलल्यामुळे, वेगवेगळे निकाल मिळतात.
[Contains English characters] In general, these techniques rely on the recursive processing of templates.
[Contains English characters] When a template is processed, it translates template code into string values.
[Contains English characters] These are often sent directly to the web browser for display, but they can be treated as code themselves.
[Contains English characters] By enclosing the text strings in double-curly-brackets, for instance, they can be reprocessed as template names or variable names, producing different results as the string values are changed.
[Contains English characters] In some cases, it may be useful for a template to call different templates depending on a variable or a passed parameter.
[Contains English characters] This allows a type of branching that can be simpler than Parser functions, though they are generally less versatile.
[Contains English characters] उदाहरण: The extra spaces in the above examples are needed: without them, the code is not processed as a template or a magic word, but just as a plain text string like so: NAMESPACE.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Hist5 Since there is no convenient way to test substring values, these techniques work best if the variable template has only a limited number of possible values.
[Contains English characters] For example, the variable CURRENTDAYNAME has only seven possible values, so all cases can be handled with seven templates, and the variable NAMESPACE currently has 18 possible values.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, CURRENTTIME has 1440 possible values, which would require the creation of 1440 template pages or redirects, which would be impractical.
[Contains English characters] Even with parser functions, all 1440 values would have to be listed and m:Template:minute .
[Contains English characters] In cases like that, it would be better to construct the template with multiple parameters that each only take a few values, rather than trying to account for all possibilities in a single parameter.
[Contains English characters] If a template depends on PAGENAME, then the many possible values of PAGENAME may not be a problem.
[Contains English characters] Only the pagenames of the pages that call the template apply, and these can be limited to a small, enumerable set.
[Contains English characters] Templates can be passed as parameters to other templates.
[Contains English characters] This can mean either that the template is evaluated and the result is passed as a parameter or that the template name is passed and evaluated as part of the other template.
[Contains English characters] A parameter name in a template can be a variable.
[Contains English characters] This is useful if you want the behavior of a template to change based on the information that is provided to it.
[Contains English characters] Choosing parameters contextually - t pnd|parameter name Template:t p contains capital is the capital of country, with two parameters - capital and country.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Timc can be used to select which parameter is used in a particular case.
[Contains English characters] Thus: This applies to integer parameters as well, since integer parameters can be specified using the #= notation.
[Contains English characters] Passing the integer value N to t pnd as its parameter will make it look for the Nth unnamed parameter.
[Contains English characters] The following branching methods are generally obsolete; Parser Functions give easier forms of control.
[Contains English characters] However, they may be useful in particular situations, and point out some unintuitive features of template behavior.
[Contains English characters] Variables names can also be generated as variables.

[Contains English characters] Thus, namespace|4 gives gallery, where Meta is the name of Namespace 4. साचा:H:f

[Contains English characters] कार्यकारी द्रवाचा दाब अतिक्रांतिक पातळीवर पोहोचल्याशिवाय, चक्राची तापमान कक्षा फारच कमी होते: turbine entry temperatures are typically 565°C and condenser temperatures are around 30°C.
[Contains English characters] This gives a theoretical Carnot efficiency of about 63% compared with an actual efficiency of 42% for a modern coal-fired power station.
[Contains English characters] This low turbine entry temperature is why the Rankine cycle is often used as a bottoming cycle in combined cycle gas turbine power stations.
[Contains English characters] The working fluid in a Rankine cycle follows a closed loop and is re-used constantly.
[Contains English characters] The water vapor with entrained droplets often seen billowing from power stations is generated by the cooling systems and represents the waste heat that could not be converted to useful work.
[Contains English characters] Note that cooling towers operate using the latent heat of vaporization of the cooling fluid.
[Contains English characters] The white billowing clouds that form in cooling tower operation are the result of water droplets which are entrained in the cooling tower airflow; they are not, as commonly thought, steam.
[Contains English characters] While many substances could be used in the Rankine cycle, water is usually the fluid of choice due to its favorable properties, such as nontoxic and unreactive chemistry, abundance, and low cost, as well as its thermodynamic properties.
[Contains English characters] One of the principal advantages the Rankine cycle holds over others is that during the compression stage relatively little work is required to drive the pump, the working fluid being in its liquid phase at this point.
[Contains English characters] By condensing the fluid to liquid, the work required by the pump consumes only 1% to 3% of the turbine power and contributes to a much higher efficiency for a real cycle.
[Contains English characters] The benefit of this is lost somewhat due to the lower heat addition temperature.
[Contains English characters] Gas turbines, for instance, have turbine entry temperatures approaching 1500°C.
[Contains English characters] Nonetheless, the efficiencies of actual large steam cycles and large modern gas turbines are fairly well matched.
[Contains English characters] There are four processes in the Rankine cycle, these states are identified by number in the diagram to the right.
[Contains English characters] In an ideal Rankine cycle the pump and turbine would be isentropic, i. e. , the pump and turbine would generate no entropy and hence maximize the net work output.
[Contains English characters] Processes 1-2 and 3-4 would be represented by vertical lines on the Ts diagram and more closely resemble that of the Carnot cycle.
[Contains English characters] The Rankine cycle shown here prevents the vapor ending up in the superheat region after the expansion in the turbine, which reduces the energy removed by the condensers.
[Contains English characters] Each of the first four equations is easily derived from the energy and mass balance for a control volume.
[Contains English characters] The fifth equation defines the thermodynamic efficiency of the cycle as the ratio of net power output to heat input.
[Contains English characters] As the work required by the pump is often around 1% of the turbine work output, equation 5 can be simplified.

[Contains English characters] In other words, these processes are non-reversible and entropy is increased during the two processes.
[Contains English characters] This somewhat increases the power required by the pump and decreases the power generated by the turbine.
[Contains English characters] In particular the efficiency of the steam turbine will be limited by water droplet formation.
[Contains English characters] As the water condenses, water droplets hit the turbine blades at high speed causing pitting and erosion, gradually decreasing the life of turbine blades and efficiency of the turbine.
[Contains English characters] The easiest way to overcome this problem is by superheating the steam.
[Contains English characters] On the Ts diagram above, state 3 is above a two phase region of steam and water so after expansion the steam will be very wet.
[Contains English characters] By superheating, state 3 will move to the right of the diagram and hence produce a dryer steam after expansion.
[Contains English characters] The overall thermodynamic efficiency can be increased by raising the average heat input temperature \displaystyle \left of that cycle.
[Contains English characters] Increasing the temperature of the steam into the superheat region is a simple way of doing this.
[Contains English characters] There are also variations of the basic Rankine cycle which are designed to raise the thermal efficiency of the cycle in this way; two of these are described below.
[Contains English characters] In this variation, two turbines work in series.
[Contains English characters] The first accepts vapor from the boiler at high pressure.
[Contains English characters] After the vapor has passed through the first turbine, it re-enters the boiler and is reheated before passing through a second, lower pressure turbine.
[Contains English characters] Among other advantages, this prevents the vapor from condensing during its expansion which can seriously damage the turbine blades, and improves the efficiency of the cycle, as more of the heat flow into the cycle occurs at higher temperature.
[Contains English characters] The regenerative Rankine cycle is so named because after emerging from the condenser the working fluid is heated by steam tapped from the hot portion of the cycle.
[Contains English characters] On the diagram shown, the fluid at 2 is mixed with the fluid at 4 to end up with the saturated liquid at 7. This is called direct contact heating.
[Contains English characters] The Regenerative Rankine cycle is commonly used in real power stations.
[Contains English characters] Another variation is where bleed steam from between turbine stages is sent to feedwater heaters to preheat the water on its way from the condenser to the boiler.
[Contains English characters] These heaters do not mix the input steam and condensate, function as an ordinary tubular heat exchanger, and are named closed feedwater heaters.
[Contains English characters] The regenerative features here effectively raise the nominal cycle heat input temperature, by reducing the addition of heat from the boiler/fuel source at the relatively low feedwater temperatures that would exist without regenerative feedwater heating.
[Contains English characters] This improves the efficiency of the cycle, as more of the heat flow into the cycle occurs at higher temperature.
[Contains English characters] The organic Rankine cycle uses an organic fluid such as n-pentane or toluene in place of water and steam.
[Contains English characters] This allows use of lower-temperature heat sources, such as solar ponds, which typically operate at around 70–90 °C.
[Contains English characters] The efficiency of the cycle is much lower as a result of the lower temperature range, but this can be worthwhile because of the lower cost involved in gathering heat at this lower temperature.
[Contains English characters] Alternatively, fluids can be used that have boiling points above water, and this may have thermodynamic benefits.
[Contains English characters] The Rankine cycle does not restrict the working fluid in its definition, so the inclusion of an organic cycle is simply a marketing concept that should not be regarded as a separate thermodynamic cycle.

[Contains English characters] Strikes make use of almost every part of the body such as the fists, elbows, feet, knees, etc.

[Contains English characters] Advanced students are taught the art of pressure point fighting called Varma Kalai.
[Contains English characters] Kaaladi, or footwork patterns, are a fundamental aspect of both kuttu varisai and silambam.
[Contains English characters] There are sixteen of them among which four are very important.
[Contains English characters] Traditionally, beginners practice only kaaladi for many months before learning any techniques but this is not often done today.
[Contains English characters] Training in kuttu varisai allows the practitioner to get a feel of silambam stick movements using their bare hands, that is, fighters have a preliminary training with bare hands before going to the stick.
[Contains English characters] Gradually, fighters study footwork to move precisely in conjunction with the stick movements.
[Contains English characters] The ultimate goal of the training is to defend against multiple armed opponents.

[Contains English characters] It teaches how to advance and retreat, to get in range of the opponent without lowering ones defence, aids in hitting and blocking, and it strengthens the body immensely enabling the person to receive non-lethal blows and still continue the battle.

[Contains English characters] चंद्रराशीत गुरू ज्या नदीच्या राशीगृही असेल तेथे हा मेळा होतो Pushkaram is a festival in India which occurs in any particular year with respect to one of twelve important rivers; the river for each years festival is based on which zodiacal sign Jupiter is in at that time.
[Contains English characters] The table to the right shows the association between rivers and signs.
[Contains English characters] The Pushkaram for each river come once every twelve years and lasts so long as the Jupiter remains in the corresponding Zodiac sign .
[Contains English characters] The first twelve days of Pushkaram are known as Adi Pushkaram, and the last twelve days are called Anthya Pushkaram.
[Contains English characters] It is believed that during the above period of twenty-four days, Pushkar the person, who is imbued with the power to make any river holy, will travel with Jupiter as Jupiter moves from one Zodiac house to another.
[Contains English characters] In Tamil Nadu, Pushkaram is celebrated in Tamraparni River when Jupiter is in Scorpio.
[Contains English characters] In the four places where River Tamraparni flows from south to north, Banathirtham, Papanasam, Thirupudaimaruthur and sinthupoondurai, the festival is celebrated in accordance with tradition.
[Contains English characters] The Tamraparni temple at Suthamalli is also a place of religious celebration during the Pushkaram year.

[Contains English characters] The proposal of marriage is an event where one person in a relationship asks for the others hand in marriage.
[Contains English characters] If accepted, it marks the initiation of engagement.
[Contains English characters] It often has a ritual quality, sometimes involving the presentation of an engagement ring and a formalized asking of a question such as Will you marry me? . In western culture, it is traditional for the man to propose to his girlfriend, as opposed to the other way around, while literally kneeling before her, and sometimes physically putting the ring on her finger, as opposed to merely giving it to her.
[Contains English characters] The average duration of preceding courtship varies considerably throughout the world.
[Contains English characters] In many Western cultures, the tradition has been for the man to propose to the woman.
[Contains English characters] In the United Kingdom and Ireland, the 29th of February in a Leap year is said to be the one day when a woman can propose to her partner.

[Contains English characters] भरतन साचा:Infobox actor Bharathan was a Malayalam film director, artist, sculptor, poster designer and art director.
[Contains English characters] He is widely regarded as one of the most influential filmmakers of Malayalam cinema, and also one of the most prolific.
[Contains English characters] At the time of his passing, at the age of 51, he had directed more than 50 movies in several languages.
[Contains English characters] He was born at Engakkadu near Wadakkancherry, in Thrissur district of Kerala, India.
[Contains English characters] After completing his diploma from the School of Fine Arts he entered the world of Cinema as an art director for Vincent, an accomplished director of the time and the movie was Ghandarva Kshetram.
[Contains English characters] He got the inspiration from his uncle, P. N. Menon — a veteran film director.
[Contains English characters] After working as an art director and assistant director for a few movies, he made his directorial debut in 1974 with Prayanam, based on Padmarajan’s script.
[Contains English characters] The movie received the national award for the best regional film in that year.
[Contains English characters] It also marked the rise of two early proponents of middle-stream Malayalam cinema.
[Contains English characters] Bharathans films were known for their realistic portrayal of rural life in Kerala.
[Contains English characters] Melodrama and escapism, often an integral part of mainstream cinema in India, were usually absent in his films.
[Contains English characters] He also managed to steer clear of the star-centric culture, prevalent in Indian cinema, throughout his career.
[Contains English characters] His later films did involve major movie stars but usually without compromising on plot or narrative.
[Contains English characters] Bharathan, along with Padmarajan and K. G. George were largely responsible for introducing a counter culture of meaningful mainstream cinema which often tread the middle path between art-house and commercial cinema.
[Contains English characters] This movement was often called the middle of the road cinema.
[Contains English characters] Bharathans films were known for their visually appealing shot compositions.
[Contains English characters] His background as a painter enabled him to create frames that were often credited for their visual beauty.
[Contains English characters] Natural props and nature itself often became important characters in his films .
[Contains English characters] Bharathan is one of the few Indian directors known to use an elaborate story-board system for filming.
[Contains English characters] He also often designed the posters for his films.
[Contains English characters] Several of his early films were known for their bold portrayal of sexual themes.
[Contains English characters] His films often defied social conventions and norms about man-woman relationships.
[Contains English characters] Rathinirvedam was the sexual-coming-of-age story of the relationship between a teenager and an older woman while Chaamaram dealt with the tumultuous affair between a student and his college lecturer.
[Contains English characters] In Kaatathe Killikoodu an elderly, married Professor falls for his student.
[Contains English characters] Kaathodu Kaathoram was about the social ostracism of a woman who has an adulterous relationship.
[Contains English characters] The latter half of Bharathans career saw a distinct change in film making style characterized by a wider canvas,more attention to detail with more distinct focus on narrative style .
[Contains English characters] Some critics argue that this quest for technical excellence was at the expense of the quality of thematic content.
[Contains English characters] Films like Vaishali and Amaram set a new benchmark for cinematographic excellence in Malayalam and Indian Cinema.
[Contains English characters] Thaazhvaaram was stylistically inspired by Classic Hollywood Westerns though the theme and backdrop were distinctly original.
[Contains English characters] His last few films did not receive much critical acclaim or commercial success.
[Contains English characters] The director showed a penchant for brilliantly portraying rustic life in rural Kerala.
[Contains English characters] Bharathan has directed over 50 films in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada.
[Contains English characters] Starting his career in 1975 with Prayanam, Bharathan rode to fame with his off-beat Thakara, a film about a dumb-witted central character who falls in love with the village beauty.
[Contains English characters] Some of his other memorable films include Rathinirvedam, Chamaram, Paalangal, Amaram, Vaishali and Alolam.
[Contains English characters] He displayed a rare talent in treating sex without falling into vulgarity which was to later became the trademark of the so called Bharathan touch.
[Contains English characters] His association with Padmarajan was the beginning of a golden era in malayalam cinema.
[Contains English characters] Few more films came out from the duos partnership before Padmarajan became an independent director himself.
[Contains English characters] Rathi Nirvedam and Thakara were the most noted among them with latter being considered one of his best.
[Contains English characters] Rathi Nirvedam was a sensitive treatment of teenage sexual angst.
[Contains English characters] In Thakara, he deals with life and longings of a mentally retarded youth and his association with the society.
[Contains English characters] In the early eighties he made several notable movies like Chaamaram, Marmaram, Paalangal, Oormakkai, Kaatathe Killikoodu, and many more.
[Contains English characters] They did well in theaters and set the trend for meaningful mainstream cinema.
[Contains English characters] Other noted directors also followed suit.
[Contains English characters] It was the romantic era of Malayalam cinema.
[Contains English characters] Not all of Bharathans films skirted with bold themes and controversy.
[Contains English characters] In Oru Minnaaminunginte Nurunguvettam, he tells the poignant story of a childless couple in their post retirement life.
[Contains English characters] The film deals with the isolation and loneliness that comes with old age.
[Contains English characters] The film was a departure from Bharathans usual style and proved to be a major commercial hit while garnering critical acclaim too.
[Contains English characters] His Vaisali is widely regarded as a modern day masterpiece in Malayalam cinema.
[Contains English characters] Scripted by the iconic Malayalam novelist M. T. Vasudevan Nair, it was an adaptation of a sub-story told in the epic Mahabharatha.
[Contains English characters] Another movie born from their association was Thazhvaram.
[Contains English characters] The subject was revenge, a theme quite uncharacteristic of Bharathan movies.
[Contains English characters] The style of the film was inspired by Classic Westerns with a brooding, reticent central character and expansive shots of barren landscape.
[Contains English characters] Even though he was not known to cater to the star-centric system, Bharathan was instrumental in bringing together the two screen icons of Tamil cinema Sivaji Ganesan and Kamal Hassan in the Tamil film Thevar Magan which won both critical acclaim and box office success.
[Contains English characters] Sivaji gave an uncharacteristically restrained yet brilliant performance in the film.
[Contains English characters] The movie was remade into many regional languages and bagged several national awards.
[Contains English characters] His more experimental films include Aaravam, more an arthouse than commercial venture, and Nidra, a film about the plight of a girl who is in love with a mentally deranged man.
[Contains English characters] His creativity was not confined to film direction.
[Contains English characters] He also wrote lyrics and tuned songs for his films.
[Contains English characters] Bharatan died at a private hospital in Madras on 29 July 1998 following prolonged illness.
[Contains English characters] He was suffering from liver cirrhosis.

[Contains English characters] Seed dispersal is likely to have several benefits for plant species.
[Contains English characters] First, seed survival is often higher away from the parent plant.
[Contains English characters] This higher survival may result from the actions of density-dependent seed and seedling predators and pathogens, which often target the high concentrations of seeds beneath adults.
[Contains English characters] Competition with adult plants may also be lower when seeds are transported away from their parent.
[Contains English characters] Seed dispersal also allows plants to reach specific habitats that are favorable for survival, a hypothesis known as directed dispersal.
[Contains English characters] For example, Ocotea endresiana is a tree species from Latin America which is dispersed by several species of birds, including the three-wattled bellbird.
[Contains English characters] Male bellbirds perch on dead trees in order to attract mates, and often defecate seeds beneath these perches where the seeds have a high chance of survival because of high light conditions and escape from fungal pathogens.
[Contains English characters] In the case of fleshy-fruited plants, seed-dispersal in animal guts often enhances the amount, the speed, and the asynchrony of germination, which can have important plant benefits.
