[Contains English characters] साचा:Copyeditसाचा:External links Language localisation can be defined as the second phase of a larger process of product translation and cultural adaptation to account for differences in distinct markets.
[Contains English characters] Thus, it is important not to reduce it to a mere translation activity because it involves a comprehensive study of the target culture in order to correctly adapt the product.
[Contains English characters] The localisation process is most generally related to cultural adaptation and translation of software, video games and websites, and less frequently to any written translation .
[Contains English characters] The process of localising can be done for regions or countries where people speak different languages, or where the same language is spoken.
[Contains English characters] Just recall the language differences in countries where Spanish is natively spoken, or where English is the official language .
[Contains English characters] As the LISA association explains, globalisation can best be thought of as a cycle rather than a single process.
[Contains English characters] To globalise is to plan in advance the way the product or the website should be designed and developed in order to avoid costs from going up and quality problems from emerging, to save time, and eventually to smooth the localising effort for each region/country.
[Contains English characters] Localisation is one phase, but an integral part, of the overall process called globalisation.
[Contains English characters] In this view, there are two primary technical processes that comprise globalisation, internationalisation and localisation, which make up a double-phase process.
[Contains English characters] See the right-hand diagram insipired in a chart found in the LISA association website.
[Contains English characters] The first phase, internationalisation, «encompasses the planning and preparation stages for a product in which it is built by design to support global markets.
[Contains English characters] This process means that all cultural assumptions are removed and any country or language-specific content is stored externally to the product so that it can be easily adapted».
[Contains English characters] If this is not done during this phase, they must be fixed during localisation, though, adding time and expense to the project.
[Contains English characters] It is important to acknowledge that in extreme cases, products that were not internationalised may not even be localisable.
[Contains English characters] The second phase, localisation, «refers to the actual adaptation of the product for a specific market».
[Contains English characters] The localisation phase involves, among other things, the four issues LISA association describes as linguistic, physical, business and cultural, and technical issues.
[Contains English characters] At the end of each phase, a testing and a quality assurance test are done to ensure that product works properly and to deliver it according to the clients quality expectations.
[Contains English characters] Localisation is often treated as a mere high-tech translation, but this view does not capture its importance, its complexity or what it encompasses.
[Contains English characters] Though it is sometimes somehow difficult to draw the limits between translation and localisation, in general localisation addresses significant, non-textual components of products or services.
[Contains English characters] In addition to strict translation, the localisation process might include adaptation of graphics, adoption of local currencies, use of proper forms for dates, addresses and phone numbers, and many other details, including rethinking the physical structure of a product.
[Contains English characters] All these changes aim to recognise local sensitivities and to enter the local market by merging into its needs and desires.
[Contains English characters] For example, localisation aims to offer country-specific websites of the same company or different editions of a book depending on the place it is published.
[Contains English characters] To explain this issue, lets analyse a given situation: suppose someone is working for a company that, until now, has operated exclusively in the United States.
[Contains English characters] However, your company is now opening a major office in China, and you need a website for this country, evidently, translated into Chinese.
[Contains English characters] Youll be offering pretty much the same products and services in both countries, with only some minor differences, but perhaps some of the elements that appeared in your original United States targeted website are offensive or upsetting.
[Contains English characters] Thus, that person might lose a potential market only because of small details of presentation.
[Contains English characters] Observe the cultural gap there is between most oriental cultures and European-occidental ones.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, this person might need to adapt the product to its new buyers; video games are the best example.
[Contains English characters] To illustrate this, read the following articles published in the October/November 2008 edition of the specialized magazine Multilingual: Practical skills for video game translators or Preserving the spell in games localization.
[Contains English characters] Now, suppose instead that this mans company has major offices in a dozen countries, and he needs a specifically-designed website in each of these countries.
[Contains English characters] Before he decides how to localise the website and the products offered in it any given country, a professional in the area might advise him to create an overall strategy: to globalise .
[Contains English characters] And he might want to design a framework to codify and support this global strategy.
[Contains English characters] The globalisation strategy and the globalisation framework will provide uniform guidance for your 12 separate localisation efforts and will earn a lot of time and money for him, as a businessman, and for the group of localisers and translators hired for the project.
[Contains English characters] Language tags are closely related to the localising process as they indicate the locale to which and from which the translation/adaptation is being done.
[Contains English characters] They are used in different contexts, for example, they might be informally used in a document published by the European Union or they might be introduced in the HTML tagging under the lang attribute.
[Contains English characters] In the latter, the language codes are generally defined by the IETFs BCP 47. BCP stands for «Best Current Practise», and is a persistent name for a series of RFCs whose numbers change as they are updated.
[Contains English characters] The latest one is RFC 4646, Tags for the Identification of Languages.
[Contains English characters] The election of one or other depends on the kind of project and the requirements the translator/localiser has.
[Contains English characters] Most frequently, there is a primary subtag that identifies the language and an optional subtag in capital letters that specifies the national variety .
[Contains English characters] The subtags are linked with a hyphen .
[Contains English characters] It is important to consult the ISO website for further inquires because there are more than one nomenclature possible for language codification.
[Contains English characters] For instance, language codes specified in ISO 639-2 use a three-letter nomenclature instead of a two-letter code, such as bul for Bulgarian or fij for Fijian.
[Contains English characters] However, be careful as these might not valid as language tags if the language also has two-letter code in ISO 639-1. Some examples of the two-letter codification are:

[Contains English characters] The proton–proton chain reaction is one of two nuclear fusion reactions, along with the CNO cycle, by which stars convert hydrogen to helium and which dominates in stars the size of the Sun or smaller.

[Contains English characters] In most legal systems, one becomes a legal adult on a particular birthday, and at different ages gains different rights and responsibilities – voting, certain drug use, eligibility for military conscription or voluntary enlistment, purchasing lottery tickets, vehicle driving licenses, etc.
[Contains English characters] Many cultures have one or more coming of age birthdays: The birthdays of historically significant people, like national heroes or founders, are often commemorated by an official holiday.
[Contains English characters] Some saints are remembered by a liturgical feast .
[Contains English characters] By analogy, the Latin term Dies natalis is applied to the anniversary of an institution .
[Contains English characters] A persons Golden or Grand Birthday, more commonly referred to as their Lucky Birthday, Champagne Birthday or Star Birthday, occurs when they turn the age of their birth day .
[Contains English characters] In some Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox countries such as फ्रांस, Poland, Russia, Bulgaria, Hungary, or Greece, it is common to have a name day/Saints day.
[Contains English characters] This is celebrated in much the same way as a birthday, but is held on the official day of a saint with the same Christian name as the birthday person; the difference being that one may look up a persons name day in a calendar, or easily remember common name days ; however in pious traditions, the two were often made to concur by giving a newborn the name of a saint celebrated on its birthday, or even the name of a feast, for example, Noel or Pascal .
[Contains English characters] Some notables, particularly monarchs, have an official birthday on a fixed day of the year, which may not necessarily match their actual birthday, but on which celebrations are held.
[Contains English characters] Examples are: While it is uncommon to have an official holiday for a republican head of states birthday, this can become a permanent posthumous honour, for example George Washingtons and Abraham Lincolns birthdays are celebrated together as Presidents Day.

[Contains English characters] com, birthdays are evenly distributed throughout the year, except for the months of October and September, which follow the holiday season by nine months.
[Contains English characters] The most frequent birthday is cited as October 5, with an average of 12,576 people born each year, while the least frequent birthday is cited as May 22 with an average of 10,259 persons born annually.
[Contains English characters] The birthday cake is traditionally highly decorated, and typically covered with lit candles when presented, the number of candles signifying the age of the celebrant.
[Contains English characters] The person whose birthday it is may make a silent wish and then blow out the candles.
[Contains English characters] After that, the person can open their presents.
[Contains English characters] It is also common for the person celebrating their birthday to cut the initial piece of the cake as a newlywed couple might with a wedding cake.
[Contains English characters] Each item was associated with a prediction.
[Contains English characters] For example, a person finding a gold coin in a birthday cake would supposedly become wealthy; a person discovering a thimble would never marry.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes special candles are substituted for the many individual candles in the shape of a numeral.
[Contains English characters] For example, on the first birthday, there may be one candle on the cake in the shape of the numeral one, and on the tenth birthday there may be two candles on the cake, one in the shape of the numeral one followed by the other in the shape of the number zero.
[Contains English characters] In addition to parties, it is common for people to receive gifts on their birthdays or surprise parties.
[Contains English characters] The popular gifts include toys, books, jewellery, clothes, flowers, technical devices, etc.
[Contains English characters] However, sometimes it is expected of the person celebrating their birthday to treat their party guests instead; this varies depending on the local culture and may involve party gifts or other gestures, for example inviting to the restaurant or bar, arranging party at home, or at work.
[Contains English characters] The origin of the birthday gift giving originates from the gift giving celebration of Christmas.
[Contains English characters] In most English-speaking countries it is traditional to sing the song Happy Birthday to You to the honored person celebrating a birthday.
[Contains English characters] Happy Birthday songs are common worldwide.
[Contains English characters] Similar songs exist in other languages such as Zhu ni sheng ri kuai le in Mandarin Chinese, Lang zal hij/zij leven in Dutch, Õnne soovime Sul in Estonian, Zum Geburtstag Viel Glück in German, Nα ζήσεις και χρόνια πολλά in Greek, Hayom Yom HUledet in Hebrew, Que los cumplas feliz or Feliz cumpleaños a ti in Spanish, Parabéns a você in Portuguese, Maligayang Bati in Filipino, Sto lat in Polish, Lá Breithe Shona Duit in Irish, multi ani traiasca in Romanian, Ja må du leva or Med en enkel tulipan in Swedish, Joyeux Anniversaire or Bonne Fête in French, Tanti Auguri a te in Italian and Iyi ki dogdun, Mutlu Yillar Sana in Turkish.
[Contains English characters] This song is a common greeting used on birthdays, along with greeting cards and verbal greetings with messages such as I wish you a Happy Birthday or Happy Birthday.
[Contains English characters] A persons birthday is usually recorded according to the time zone of the place of birth.
[Contains English characters] Thus people born in Samoa at 11:30 pm will record their birthdate as one day before Coordinated Universal Time and those born in the Line Islands will record their birthdate one day after UTC.
[Contains English characters] They will apparently be born two days apart, while some of the apparently older ones may be younger in hours.
[Contains English characters] Those who live in different time zones from their birth often exclusively celebrate their birthdays at the local time zone.
[Contains English characters] In addition, the intervention of Daylight Saving Time can result in a case where a baby born second being recorded as having been born up to an hour before their predecessor.
[Contains English characters] In Judaism, the perspective on birthday celebrations is disputed by various rabbis.
[Contains English characters] In the Hebrew Bible, the one single mention of a celebration being held in commemoration of someones day of birth is for the Egyptian Pharaoh, while Leviticus 18:1-3 states And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the people of Israel and say to them, I am the LORD your God.
[Contains English characters] You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived.
[Contains English characters] The bar mitzvah of 13-year-old Jewish boys, or bat mitzvah for 12-year-old Jewish girls, is perhaps the only Jewish celebration undertaken in what is often perceived to be in coalition with a birthday.
[Contains English characters] However, the essence of a bar/bat mitzvah celebration is entirely religious in origin and not secular, despite modern celebrations where the secular birthday element often overshadows the essence of it as a religious rite.
[Contains English characters] With or without the birthday celebration, the child nevertheless becomes a bar or bat mitzvah, and the celebration can be on that day or any date after it.
[Contains English characters] Since the foundation of Christianity historically lies in Judaism, if there is a stance against the celebration of birthdays, it often mirrors the Jewish religious arguments.
[Contains English characters] Few branches of Christianity, however, actually hold any official stance in regards to birthdays, be it in favour or against.
[Contains English characters] Orthodox Christianity prefers the celebration of name days only, though it is not because of any active theologically-based prohibition or discouragement.
[Contains English characters] Some Christian communities, especially in the Hispanosphere, celebrate both naming days and birthdays.
[Contains English characters] Jehovahs Witnesses and some Sacred Name groups, among others, do not celebrate birthdays at all.
[Contains English characters] They point to, for example, the birthday celebrations in the Bible for Pharaoh and for Herod, the latter being the occasion for the beheading of John the Baptist.
[Contains English characters] Also, the origins, magic, and superstitions surrounding the pagan celebration of birthdays are also a some other reasons for some Christian groups rejecting birthday celebrations.
[Contains English characters] In the branches of Christianity where there is active discouragement or prohibition against birthdays, by default, this also affects their stance in regards to Christmas.
[Contains English characters] After all, in its religiously presented form, Christmas is the commemoration of the birth of Jesus of Nazareth, that is, a birthday celebration for Jesus.
[Contains English characters] Hence, Jehovahs Witnesses do not espouse the celebration of Christmas either, although additional theological arguments are also cited.
[Contains English characters] Because of the very existence of Christmas as an integral celebration espoused by most branches of modern Christianity, it could be argued that this constitutes implicit acceptance of birthdays, contrary to this, it might put into question the legitimacy of Christmasaltogether.
[Contains English characters] A number of possible superstitious origins for customs associated with Birthday celebrations have been suggested.
[Contains English characters] One source states, that the tradition of birthday parties started in Europe a long time ago.
[Contains English characters] It was feared that evil spirits were particularly attracted to people on their birthdays.
[Contains English characters] To protect them from harm, friends and family would to come be with the birthday person and bring good thoughts and wishes.
[Contains English characters] Giving gifts brought even more good cheer to ward off the evil spirits.
[Contains English characters] This is how birthday parties began.
[Contains English characters] In ancient times, people prayed over the flames of an open fire.
[Contains English characters] They believed that the smoke carried their thoughts up to the gods.
[Contains English characters] Another reference comments, The various customs with which people today celebrate their birthdays have a long history.
[Contains English characters] Their origins lie in the realm of magic and religion.
[Contains English characters] The customs of offering congratulations, presenting gifts and celebrating - complete with lighted candles - in ancient times were meant to protect the birthday celebrant from the demons and to ensure his security for the coming year. . . . Down to the fourth century Christianity rejected the birthday celebration as a pagan custom.

[Contains English characters] Nuisance is a common law tort.
[Contains English characters] It means that which causes offence, annoyance, trouble or injury.
[Contains English characters] A nuisance can be either public or private.
[Contains English characters] A public nuisance was defined by English scholar Sir J. F. Stephen as, an act not warranted by law, or an omission to discharge a legal duty, which act or omission obstructs or causes inconvenience or damage to the public in the exercise of rights common to all His Majestys subjects.
[Contains English characters] Private nuisance is the interference with the right of specific people.
[Contains English characters] Nuisance is one of the oldest causes of action known to the common law, with cases framed in nuisance going back almost to the beginning of recorded case law.
[Contains English characters] Nuisance signifies that the right of quiet enjoyment is being disrupted to such a degree that a tort is being committed.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Tort lawUnder the common law, persons in possession of real property are entitled to the quiet enjoyment of their lands.
[Contains English characters] If a neighbour interferes with that quiet enjoyment, either by creating smells, sounds, pollution or any other hazard that extends past the boundaries of the property, the affected party may make a claim in nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Legally, the term nuisance is traditionally used in three ways: The law of nuisance was created to stop such bothersome activities or conduct when they unreasonably interfered either with the rights of other private landowners or with the rights of the general public A public nuisance is an unreasonable interference with the publics right to property.
[Contains English characters] It includes conduct that interferes with public health, safety, peace or convenience.
[Contains English characters] The unreasonableness may be evidenced by statute, or by the nature of the act, including how long, and how bad, the effects of the activity may be.
[Contains English characters] A private nuisance is simply a violation of ones use of quiet enjoyment of land.
[Contains English characters] It doesnt include trespass.
[Contains English characters] To be a nuisance, the level of interference must rise above the merely aesthetic.
[Contains English characters] For example: if your neighbour paints their house purple, it may offend you; however, it doesnt rise to the level of nuisance.
[Contains English characters] In most cases, normal uses of a property that can constitute quiet enjoyment cannot be restrained in nuisance either.
[Contains English characters] For example, the sound of a crying baby may be annoying, but it is an expected part of quiet enjoyment of property and does not constitute a nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Any affected property owner has standing to sue for a private nuisance.
[Contains English characters] If a nuisance is widespread enough, but yet has a public purpose, it is often treated at law as a public nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Owners of interests in real property have standing only to bring private nuisance suits.
[Contains English characters] In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, the law of nuisance became difficult to administer, as competing property uses often posed a nuisance to each other, and the cost of litigation to settle the issue grew prohibitive.
[Contains English characters] As such, most jurisdictions now have a system of land use planning that describes what activities are acceptable in a given location.
[Contains English characters] Zoning generally overrules nuisance.
[Contains English characters] For example: if a factory is operating in an industrial zone, neighbours in the neighbouring residential zone cant make a claim in nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Jurisdictions without zoning laws, essentially leave land use to be determined by the laws concerning nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Similarly, modern environmental laws are an adaptation of the doctrine of nuisance to modern complex societies, in that a persons use of his property may harmfully affect anothers property, or person, far from the nuisance activity, and from causes not easily integrated into historic understandings of nuisance law.
[Contains English characters] Under the common law, the only remedy for a nuisance was the payment of damages.
[Contains English characters] However, with the development of the courts of equity, the remedy of an injunction became available to prevent a defendant from repeating the activity that caused the nuisance, and specifying punishment for contempt if the defendant is in breach of such an injunction.
[Contains English characters] The law and economics movement has been involved in analyzing the most efficient choice of remedies given the circumstances of the nuisance.
[Contains English characters] In Boomer v.
[Contains English characters] Atlantic Cement Co.
[Contains English characters] a cement plant interfered with a number of neighbors, yet the cost of complying with a full injunction would have been far more than a fair value of the cost to the plaintiffs of continuation.
[Contains English characters] The New York court allowed the cement plant owner to purchase the injunction for a specified amount—the permanent damages.
[Contains English characters] In theory, the permanent damage amount should be the net present value of all future damages suffered by the plaintiff.
[Contains English characters] There are remedies such as money damages and equitable remedies.
[Contains English characters] An Inspector of Nuisance is, or was, the title of an office in several English-speaking jurisdictions.
[Contains English characters] In many jurisdictions this term is now archaic, the position and/or term having been replaced by others.
[Contains English characters] For example, in the UK, this office was generally associated with public health and sanitation.
[Contains English characters] Both the 1847 Nuisances Removal and Diseases Prevention Act and the Metropolis Management Act 1855 defined such an office.
[Contains English characters] Similar offices were established across the British Empire.
[Contains English characters] The nearest modern equivalent of this position in the UK is an Environmental health officer.
[Contains English characters] A modern example is found in Section 3767 of the Ohio Revised Code which defines such a position to investigate nuisances, where this term broadly covers establishments in which lewdness and alcohol are found.
[Contains English characters] The boundaries of the tort are potentially unclear, due to the public/private nuisance divide, and existence of the rule in Rylands v Fletcher.
[Contains English characters] Writers such as John Murphy of the University of Manchester have popularised the idea that Rylands forms a separate, though related, tort.
[Contains English characters] This is still an issue for debate, and is rejected by others Under English law, unlike in the USA, it is no defence that the claimant came to the nuisance: the 1879 case of Sturges v Bridgman is still good law, and a new owner can bring a claim in nuisance for the existing activities of a neighbour.
[Contains English characters] Many states have limited instances where a claim of nuisance may be brought.
[Contains English characters] Such limitation often became necessary as the sensibilities of urban dwellers were offended by smells of agricultural waste when they moved to rural locations.
[Contains English characters] For example: many states and provinces have right to farm provisions, which allow any agricultural use of land zoned or historically used for agriculture.
[Contains English characters] There are two classes of nuisance under the American law: a nuisance in fact, or nuisance per accidens, and a nuisance per se.
[Contains English characters] The classification determines whether the claim goes to the jury, or gets decided by the judge.
[Contains English characters] An alleged nuisance in fact is an issue of fact to be determined by the jury, who will decide whether the thing in question created a nuisance, by examining its location and surroundings, the manner of its conduct, and other circumstances.
[Contains English characters] A determination that something is a nuisance in fact also requires proof of the act and its consequences.
[Contains English characters] By contrast, a nuisance per se is an activity, or an act, structure, instrument, or occupation which is a nuisance at all times and under any circumstances, regardless of location or surroundings.
[Contains English characters] Liability for a nuisance per se is absolute, and injury to the public is presumed; if its existence is alleged and established by proof, it is also established as a matter of law.
[Contains English characters] Therefore, a judge would decide a nuisance per se, while a jury would decide a nuisance in fact.
[Contains English characters] Most nuisance claims allege a nuisance in fact, for the simple reason that not many actions or structures have been deemed to be nuisances per se.
[Contains English characters] In general, if an act, or use of property, is lawful, or authorized by competent authority, it cant be a nuisance per se.
[Contains English characters] Rather, the act in question must either be declared by public statute, or by case law, to be a nuisance per se.
[Contains English characters] There arent many state or federal statutes or case law declaring actions or structures to be a nuisance in and of themselves.
[Contains English characters] Nor are many activities or structures, in and of themselves, and under any and all circumstances, a nuisance; which is how courts determine whether or not an action or structure is a nuisance per se.
[Contains English characters] Over the last thousand years, public nuisance has been used by governmental authorities to stop conduct that was considered quasi-criminal because, although not strictly illegal, it was deemed unreasonable in view of its likelihood to injure someone in the general public.
[Contains English characters] Donald Gifford argues that civil liability has always been an “incidental aspect of public nuisance”.
[Contains English characters] Traditionally, actionable conduct involved the blocking of a public roadway, the dumping of sewage into a public river or the blasting of a stereo in a public park.
[Contains English characters] To stop this type of conduct, governments sought injunctions either enjoining the activity that caused the nuisance or requiring the responsible party to abate the nuisance.
[Contains English characters] In recent decades, however, governments blurred the lines between public and private nuisance causes of action.
[Contains English characters] William Prosser noted this in 1966 and warned courts and scholars against confusing and merging the substantive laws of the two torts.
[Contains English characters] In some states, his warning went unheeded and some courts and legislatures have created vague and ill-defined definitions to describe what constitutes a public nuisance.
[Contains English characters] For example, Florida’s Supreme Court has held that a public nuisance is any thing that causes “annoyance to the community or harm to public health.
[Contains English characters] ” Note: the term is also used less formally in the United States to describe the non-meritorious nature of frivolous litigation.
[Contains English characters] A lawsuit may be described as a nuisance suit, and a settlement a nuisance settlement, if the defendant pays money to the plaintiff to drop the case primarily to spare the cost of litigation, rather than because the suit would have a significant likelihood of winning.
[Contains English characters] A common nuisance is punishable as a misdemeanour at common law, where no special provision is made by statute.
[Contains English characters] In modern times, many of the old common law nuisances have been the subject of legislation.
[Contains English characters] Its no defence for a master or employer that a nuisance is caused by the acts of his servants, if such acts are within the scope of their employment, even though such acts are done without his knowledge, and contrary to his orders.
[Contains English characters] Nor is it a defence that the nuisance has been in existence for a great length of time, for no lapse of time will legitimate a public nuisance.
[Contains English characters] A private nuisance is an act, or omission, which causes inconvenience or damage to a private person, and is left to be redressed by action.
[Contains English characters] There must be some sensible diminution of these rights affecting the value or convenience of the property.
[Contains English characters] The real question in all the cases is the question of fact, whether the annoyance is such as materially to interfere with the ordinary comfort of human existence L. R. 3 Eq.
[Contains English characters] 409. A private nuisance, differing in this respect from a public nuisance, may be legalized by uninterrupted use for twenty years.
[Contains English characters] It used to be thought that, if a man knew there was a nuisance and went and lived near it, he couldnt recover, because, it was said, it is he that goes to the nuisance, and not the nuisance to him.
[Contains English characters] But this has long ceased to be law, as regards both the remedy by damages, and the remedy by injunction.
[Contains English characters] The remedy for a public nuisance is by information, indictment, summary procedure or abatement.
[Contains English characters] An information lies in cases of great public importance, such as the obstruction of a navigable river by piers.
[Contains English characters] In some matters, the law allows the party to take the remedy into his own hands, and to abate the nuisance.
[Contains English characters] Thus; if a gate be placed across a highway, any person lawfully using the highway may remove the obstruction, provided that no breach of the peace is caused thereby.
[Contains English characters] The remedy for a private nuisance is by injunction, action for damages or abatement.
[Contains English characters] An action lies in every case for a private nuisance; it also lies where the nuisance is public, provided that the plaintiff can prove that he has sustained some special injury.
[Contains English characters] In such a case, the civil is in addition to the criminal remedy.
[Contains English characters] In abating a private nuisance, care must be taken not to do more damage than is necessary for the removal of the nuisance.
[Contains English characters] In Scotland, theres no recognized distinction between public and private nuisances.
[Contains English characters] The law as to what constitutes a nuisance is substantially the same as in England.
[Contains English characters] A list of statutory nuisances will be found in the Public Health Act 1867, and amending acts.

[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda is a bear native to central-western and south western China.
[Contains English characters] It is easily recognized by its large, distinctive black patches around the eyes, over the ears, and across its round body.
[Contains English characters] Though it belongs to the order Carnivora, the Giant Pandas diet is 99% bamboo.
[Contains English characters] Other parts of its diet include honey, eggs, fish, yams, shrub leaves, oranges, and bananas when available.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda lives in a few mountain ranges in central China, mainly in Sichuan province, but also in the Shaanxi and Gansu provinces.
[Contains English characters] Due to farming, deforestation, and other development, the Giant Panda has been driven out of the lowland areas where it once lived.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda is a conservation reliant endangered species.
[Contains English characters] A 2007 report shows 239 Giant Pandas living in captivity inside China and another 27 outside the country.
[Contains English characters] Wild population estimates vary; one estimate shows that there are about 1,590 individuals living in the wild, while a 2006 study via DNA analysis estimated that this figure could be as high as 2,000 to 3,000. Some reports also show that the number of Giant Pandas in the wild is on the rise.
[Contains English characters] However, the IUCN does not believe there is enough certainty yet to reclassify the species from Endangered to Vulnerable.
[Contains English characters] While the dragon has historically served as Chinas national emblem, in recent decades the Giant Panda has also served as an emblem for the country.
[Contains English characters] Its image appears on a large number of modern Chinese commemorative silver, gold, and platinum coins.
[Contains English characters] Though the Giant Panda is often assumed to be docile, it has been known to attack humans, presumably out of irritation rather than predation.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has a black-and-white coat.
[Contains English characters] Adults measure around १.५ मीटर long and around ७५ सेंटीमीटर tall at the shoulder.
[Contains English characters] Males are 10–20% larger than females.
[Contains English characters] Males can weigh up to १५० किलोग्रॅम .
[Contains English characters] Females are generally smaller than males, and can occasionally weigh up to 125 kg .
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda lives in mountainous regions, such as Sichuan, Gansu and Shaanxi.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has a body shape typical of bears.
[Contains English characters] It has black fur on its ears, eye patches, muzzle, legs, arms and shoulders.
[Contains English characters] The rest of the animals coat is white.
[Contains English characters] Although scientists do not know why these unusual bears are black and white, some speculate that the bold coloring provides effective camouflage into its shade-dappled snowy and rocky surroundings.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Pandas thick, wooly coat keeps it warm in the cool forests of its habitat.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has large molar teeth and strong jaw muscles for crushing tough bamboo.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Pandas paw has a thumb and five fingers; the thumb is actually a modified sesamoid bone, which helps the Giant Panda to hold bamboo while eating.
[Contains English characters] Stephen Jay Gould used this example in his book of essays concerned with evolution and biology, The Pandas Thumb.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has the second longest tail in the bear family, with one that is १० to १५ सेंटीमीटर long.
[Contains English characters] The longest belongs to the Sloth Bear.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda can usually live to be 25–30 years old in captivity.
[Contains English characters] In the wild, the Giant Panda is a terrestrial animal and primarily spends its life roaming and feeding in the bamboo forests of the Qinling Mountains and in the hilly Sichuan Province.
[Contains English characters] Though generally alone, each adult has a defined territory and females are not tolerant of other females in their range.
[Contains English characters] Pandas communicate through vocalization and scent marking such as clawing trees or spraying urine.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda is able to climb and take shelter in hollow trees or rock crevices but does not establish permanent dens.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, pandas do not hibernate, which is similar to other subtropical mammals, and will instead move to elevations with warmer temperatures.
[Contains English characters] Pandas rely primarily on spatial memory rather than visual memory.
[Contains English characters] Social encounters occur primarily during the brief breeding season in which pandas in proximity to one another will gather.
[Contains English characters] After mating, the male leaves the female alone to raise the cub.
[Contains English characters] Despite its taxonomic classification as a carnivore, the Giant Panda has a diet that is primarily herbivorous, which consists almost exclusively of bamboo.
[Contains English characters] However, the Giant Panda still has the digestive system of a carnivore, as well as carnivore-specific genes, and thus derives little energy and little protein from consumption of bamboo.
[Contains English characters] Its ability to digest cellulose is ascribed to the microbes in its gut.
[Contains English characters] The average Giant Panda eats as much as 9 to 14 kg of bamboo shoots a day.
[Contains English characters] Because the Giant Panda consumes a diet low in nutrition, it is important for it to keep its digestive tract full.
[Contains English characters] The limited energy input imposed on it by its diet has affected the pandas behavior.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda tends to limit its social interactions and avoids steeply sloping terrain in order to limit its energy expenditures.
[Contains English characters] Two of the pandas most distinctive features, its large size and its round face, are adaptations to its bamboo diet.
[Contains English characters] Panda researcher Russell Ciochon observed that: “ like the vegetarian gorilla, the low body surface area to body volume is indicative of a lower metabolic rate.
[Contains English characters] This lower metabolic rate and a more sedentary lifestyle allow the giant panda to subsist on nutrient poor resources such as bamboo.
[Contains English characters] ” Similarly, the Giant Pandas round face is the result of powerful jaw muscles, which attach from the top of the head to the jaw.
[Contains English characters] Large molars crush and grind fibrous plant material.
[Contains English characters] Twenty-five species of bamboo are eaten by pandas in the wild, such as Fargesia dracocephala and Fargesia rufa.
[Contains English characters] Only a few bamboo species are widespread at the high altitudes pandas now inhabit.
[Contains English characters] Bamboo leaves contain the highest protein levels; stems have less.
[Contains English characters] Because of the synchronous flowering, death, and regeneration of all bamboo within a species, the Giant Panda must have at least two different species available in its range to avoid starvation.
[Contains English characters] While primarily herbivorous, the Giant Panda still retains decidedly ursine teeth, and will eat meat, fish, and eggs when available.
[Contains English characters] In captivity, zoos typically maintain the Giant Pandas bamboo diet, though some will provide specially formulated biscuits or other dietary supplements.
[Contains English characters] The giant panda genome was sequenced in 2009 using a next-generation sequencing technology.
[Contains English characters] Its genome contains 20 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.
[Contains English characters] For many decades the precise taxonomic classification of the Giant Panda was under debate because it shares characteristics of both bears and raccoons.
[Contains English characters] However, molecular studies suggest that the Giant Panda is a true bear and part of the Ursidae family, though it differentiated early in history from the main ursine stock.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Pandas closest ursine relative is the Spectacled Bear of South America.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has been referred to as a living fossil.
[Contains English characters] Despite the shared name, habitat type, and diet, as well as a unique enlarged bone called the pseudo thumb, the Giant Panda and Red Panda are only distantly related.
[Contains English characters] Molecular studies have placed the Red Panda in its own family Ailuridae, and not under Ursidae.
[Contains English characters] Two subspecies of Giant Panda have been recognized on the basis of distinct cranial measurements, color patterns, and population genetics .
[Contains English characters] In the past, pandas were thought to be rare and noble creatures – the mother of Emperor Wen of Han was buried with a panda skull in her vault.
[Contains English characters] The grandson of Emperor Taizong of Tang is said to have given Japan two pandas and a sheet of panda skin as a sign of goodwill.
[Contains English characters] Unlike many other animals in Ancient China, pandas were rarely thought to have medical uses.
[Contains English characters] The few known uses include the Sichuan tribal peoples use of panda urine to melt accidentally swallowed needles, and the use of panda pelts to control menses as described in the Qin Dynasty encyclopedia Erya.
[Contains English characters] The creature named mo mentioned in some ancient books has been interpreted as giant panda.
[Contains English characters] The dictionary Shuowen Jiezi says that the mo, from Shu, is bear-like, but yellow-and-black, although the older Erya describes mo simply as a white leopard.
[Contains English characters] The interpretation of the legendary fierce creature pixiu as referring to the giant panda are also common.
[Contains English characters] The comparative obscurity of the giant panda throughout most of Chinas history is illustrated by the fact that, despite there being a number of depictions of bears in Chinese art starting from its most ancient times, and the bamboo being one of the favorite subjects for Chinese painters, there are no known pre-20th-century artistic representations of giant pandas.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda was first made known to the West in 1869 by the French missionary, Armand David, who received a skin from a hunter on March 11, 1869. The first Westerner known to have seen a living Giant Panda is the German zoologist Hugo Weigold, who purchased a cub in 1916. Kermit and Theodore Roosevelt, Jr.
[Contains English characters] , became the first foreigners to shoot a panda, on an expedition funded by the Field Museum of Natural History in the 1920s.
[Contains English characters] In 1936, Ruth Harkness became the first Westerner to bring back a live Giant Panda, a cub named Su Lin who went to live at the Brookfield Zoo in Chicago.
[Contains English characters] In 1938 five Giant Pandas were sent to London; these activities were later halted because of wars and for the next half of the century, the West knew little of pandas.
[Contains English characters] Loans of Giant Pandas to American and Japanese zoos formed an important part of the diplomacy of the Peoples Republic of China in the 1970s, as it marked some of the first cultural exchanges between the Peoples Republic and the West.
[Contains English characters] This practice has been termed Panda Diplomacy.
[Contains English characters] By 1984, however, pandas were no longer used as agents of diplomacy.
[Contains English characters] Instead, China began to offer pandas to other nations only on 10-year loans.
[Contains English characters] The standard loan terms include a fee of up to US$1,000,000 per year and a provision that any cubs born during the loan are the property of the Peoples Republic of China.
[Contains English characters] Since 1998, due to a WWF lawsuit, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service only allows a U. S. zoo to import a panda if the zoo can ensure that China will channel more than half of its loan fee into conservation efforts for the Giant Panda and its habitat.
[Contains English characters] In May 2005, China offered a breeding pair to Taiwan.
[Contains English characters] The issue became embroiled in cross-Strait relations—both over the underlying symbolism, and over technical issues such as whether the transfer would be considered domestic or international, or whether any true conservation purpose would be served by the exchange.
[Contains English characters] Chinas offer was initially rejected by President Chen of Taiwan.
[Contains English characters] However when the presidency changed hands Chinas offer was accepted at the beginning of Ma Ying-jeous presidency in 2008, and the pandas themselves arrived in December of that year.
[Contains English characters] A contest to name the pandas was held in China, resulting in the politically charged names Tuan Tuan and Yuan Yuan .
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda is an endangered species, threatened by continued habitat loss and by a very low birthrate, both in the wild and in captivity.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda has been a target for poaching by locals since ancient times, and by foreigners since it was introduced to the West.
[Contains English characters] Starting in the 1930s, foreigners were unable to poach Giant Pandas in China because of the Second Sino-Japanese War and the Chinese Civil War, but pandas remained a source of soft furs for the locals.
[Contains English characters] The population boom in China after 1949 created stress on the pandas habitat, and the subsequent famines led to the increased hunting of wildlife, including pandas.
[Contains English characters] During the Cultural Revolution, all studies and conservation activities on the pandas were stopped.
[Contains English characters] After the Chinese economic reform, demand for panda skins from Hong Kong and Japan led to illegal poaching for the black market, acts generally ignored by the local officials at the time.
[Contains English characters] Though the Wolong National Nature Reserve was set up by the PRC government in 1958 to save the declining panda population, few advances in the conservation of pandas were made, due to inexperience and insufficient knowledge of ecology.
[Contains English characters] Many believed that the best way to save the pandas was to cage them.
[Contains English characters] As a result, pandas were caged at any sign of decline, and suffered from terrible conditions.
[Contains English characters] Because of pollution and destruction of their natural habitat, along with segregation due to caging, reproduction of wild pandas was severely limited.
[Contains English characters] In the 1990s, however, several laws helped the chances of survival for pandas.
[Contains English characters] With these renewed efforts and improved conservation methods, wild pandas have started to increase in numbers in some areas, even though they still are classified as a rare species.
[Contains English characters] In 2006, scientists reported that the number of pandas living in the wild may have been underestimated at about 1,000. Previous population surveys had used conventional methods to estimate the size of the wild panda population, but using a new method that analyzes DNA from panda droppings, scientists believe that the wild panda population may be as large as 3,000. Although the species is still endangered, it is thought that the conservation efforts are working.
[Contains English characters] As of 2006, there were 40 panda reserves in China, compared to just 13 reserves two decades ago.
[Contains English characters] The Giant Panda is among the worlds most adored and protected rare animals, and is one of the few in the world whose natural inhabitant status was able to gain a UNESCO World Heritage Site designation.
[Contains English characters] The Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries, located in the southwest Sichuan province and covering seven natural reserves, were inscribed onto the World Heritage List in 2006. Not all conservationists agree that the money spent on conserving pandas is money well spent.
[Contains English characters] Chris Packham has argued that breeding pandas in captivity is pointless because there is not enough habitat left to sustain them.
[Contains English characters] Packham argues that the money spent on pandas would be better spent elsewhere, and has said that he would eat the last panda if I could have all the money we have spent on panda conservation put back on the table for me to do more sensible things with, though he has apologized for upsetting people who like pandas.
[Contains English characters] He points out that The panda is possibly one of the grossest wastes of conservation money in the last half century.
[Contains English characters] Initially the primary method of breeding Giant Pandas in captivity was by artificial insemination, as they seemed to lose their interest in mating once they were captured.
[Contains English characters] This led some scientists to try extreme methods such as showing them videos of giant Pandas mating and giving the males Viagra.
[Contains English characters] Only recently have researchers started having success with captive breeding programs, and they have now determined that Giant Pandas have comparable breeding to some populations of the American Black Bear, a thriving bear family.
[Contains English characters] The current reproductive rate is considered one young every two years.
[Contains English characters] Giant Pandas reach sexual maturity between the ages of four and eight, and may be reproductive until age 20. The mating season is between March and May, when a female goes into her estrous cycle which lasts for two or three days and only occurs once a year.
[Contains English characters] When mating, the female is in a crouching, head-down position as the male mounts her from behind.
[Contains English characters] Copulation time is short, ranging from thirty seconds to five minutes, but the male may mount her repeatedly to ensure successful fertilization.
[Contains English characters] The gestation period ranges from 95 to 160 days.
[Contains English characters] Cubs weigh only 90 to 130 grams, which is about 1/900 of the mothers weight.
[Contains English characters] Usually, the female gives birth to one or two cubs.
[Contains English characters] Since cubs are born very small and helpless, they need the mothers undivided attention, so she is able to care for only one of her cubsसाचा:Dubious.
[Contains English characters] She usually abandons one of her cubs, and it dies soon after birth.
[Contains English characters] At this time, scientists do not know how the female chooses which cub to raise, and this is a topic of ongoing research.
[Contains English characters] The father has no part in helping raise the cub.
[Contains English characters] When the cub is first born, it is pink, fदुवाess, and blind.
[Contains English characters] A Giant Panda cub is also extremely small, and it is difficult for the mother to protect it because of the babys size.
[Contains English characters] It nurses from its mothers breast 6 to 14 times a day for up to 30 minutes at a time.
[Contains English characters] For three to four hours, the mother may leave the den to feed, which leaves the cub defenseless.
[Contains English characters] One to two weeks after birth, the cubs skin turns gray where its hair will eventually become black.
[Contains English characters] A slight pink color may appear on cubs fur, as a result of a chemical reaction between the fur and its mothers saliva.
[Contains English characters] A month after birth, the color pattern of the cubs fur is fully developed.
[Contains English characters] A cubs fur is very soft and coarsens with age.
[Contains English characters] The cub begins to crawl at 75 to 90 days; mothers play with their cubs by rolling and wrestling with them.
[Contains English characters] The cubs are able to eat small quantities of bamboo after six months, though mothers milk remains the primary food source for most of the first year.
[Contains English characters] Giant Panda cubs weigh 45 kg at one year, and live with their mothers until they are 18 months to two years old.
[Contains English characters] The interval between births in the wild is generally two years.
[Contains English characters] In July 2009, Chinese scientists confirmed the birth of the first cub to be successfully conceived through artificial insemination using frozen sperm.
[Contains English characters] The cub was born at 07:41 on 23 July that year in Sichuan as the third child of You You, an 11-year-old.
[Contains English characters] The technique for freezing the sperm in liquid nitrogen was first developed in 1980 and the first birth was hailed as a solution to the problem of lessening Giant Panda semen availability which had led to in-breeding.
[Contains English characters] It has been suggested that panda semen, which can be frozen for decades, could be shared between different zoos to save the species.
[Contains English characters] It is expected that zoos in destinations such as San Diego in the United States and Mexico City will now be able to provide their own semen to inseminate more Giant Pandas.
[Contains English characters] There is no conclusive source for the origin of the Anglicized name panda.
[Contains English characters] The closest candidate that has been accepted as the source originates in the Nepali word ponya, possibly referring to the adapted wrist bone.
[Contains English characters] The Western world originally applied this name to the Red Panda.
[Contains English characters] Until 1901, when it was erroneously stated that it was related to the Red Panda, the Giant Panda was known as mottled bear or particolored bear.
[Contains English characters] In most encyclopedic sources, the name panda or common panda originally referred to the lesser-known Red Panda, thus necessitated the inclusion of giant and lesser/red prefixes in front of the names.
[Contains English characters] Even now, Encyclopaedia Britannica still uses giant panda or panda bear for the bear and simply panda for the Ailuridae, despite the popular usage of the word panda today.
[Contains English characters] Since the earliest collection of Chinese writings, the Chinese language has given the bear 20 different names, such as 花熊 spotted bear and 竹熊 bamboo bear.
[Contains English characters] The most popular names in China today are 大熊貓, literally large bear cat, or just 熊貓, bear cat.
[Contains English characters] The name may have been inspired by the Giant Pandas eyes which have pupils that are cat-like vertical slits unlike other bear species with round pupils.
[Contains English characters] In Taiwan, the popular name for panda is the inverted 貓熊 cat bear, even though many encyclopedia and dictionaries in Taiwan still use bear cat as the correct name.
[Contains English characters] Some linguists argue that, in this construction, bear instead of cat is the base noun, making this name more grammatically and logically correct, which may have led to the popular choice despite official writings.
[Contains English characters] Pandas have been kept in zoos as early as the Western Han Dynasty in China, where the writer Sima Xiangru notes that the panda was the most treasured animal in the emperors garden of exotic animals in Xian.
[Contains English characters] Not until the 1950s were pandas again recorded to have been exhibited in Chinas zoos.
[Contains English characters] A 2006 New York Times article outlined the economics of keeping pandas, which costs five times more than that of the next most expensive animal, an elephant.
[Contains English characters] American zoos generally pay the Chinese government $1 million a year in fees, as part of a typical ten-year contract.
[Contains English characters] San Diegos contract with China was to expire in 2008 but got a five-year extension at about half of the previous yearly cost.
[Contains English characters] The last contract, with the Memphis Zoo in Memphis, Tennessee, ends in 2013.साचा:Seealso Many zoos and breeding centers in China house giant pandas.
[Contains English characters] These include: As of 2007, five major North American zoos have Giant Pandas: The first sequences of pandas in the wild were shot by Franz Camenzind for ABC in about 1982. They were bought by BBC Natural History Unit for their weekly magazine show Nature.
[Contains English characters] Recently, NHNZ has featured pandas in two documentaries.
[Contains English characters] Panda Nursery featured China’s Wolong National Nature Reserve in the mountains in Sichuan Province; forty Giant Pandas and a dedicated team of staff play a crucial role in ensuring the survival of the species.
[Contains English characters] As part of the Reserve’s panda breeding program, a revolutionary new method of rearing twin cubs called ‘swap-raising’ has been developed.
[Contains English characters] Each cub is raised by both its natural mother and one of the Reserve’s veterinarians, Wei Rongping, to increase the chances of both cubs surviving.
[Contains English characters] Growing Up: Giant Panda featured Chengdu Giant Panda Center in south-west China as one of the best in the world.
[Contains English characters] Yet with female pandas short fertility cycles and low birth rates, raising the captive panda population is an uphill battle.

[Contains English characters] तमिळ् ईळम्साचा:Article issuesसाचा:Article issues साचा:Contains Indic text साचा:Contains Indic textसाचा:Sri Lankan Tamil people Tamil Eelam is the name given by certain Tamil groups in Sri Lanka & the Sri Lankan Tamil diaspora to the state which they aspire to create in the north and east of श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Eelam has no official status or recognition by any other state or authority.
[Contains English characters] The name is derived from the ancient Tamil name for Sri Lanka, Eelam.
[Contains English characters] Great Britain gained control of the whole island of Sri Lanka, in 1815 and administratively unified the island with a legislative council in 1833 with three Europeans and one each for Sinhalese, Sri Lankan Tamils and Burghers.
[Contains English characters] British Governor William Manning, who arrived in Ceylon in 1919, created a reformed legislative council in 1921 and actively encouraged communal thinking in the legislative council.
[Contains English characters] As a result, the Tamils started to develop communal consciousness and began to think of themselves as needing to be represented by Tamil leadership.
[Contains English characters] It was this development that made way for the development of the Tamil political organization called the All Ceylon Tamil Congress headed by G. G. Ponnambalam. Sri Lanka achieved independence from the British in 1948 and in the same year the government of Sri Lanka, with the acceptance vote from G.
[Contains English characters] G. Ponnambalam, passed a new act called the Ceylon Citizenship Act which disenfranchised the Indian Tamil plantation workers Though Ponnambalam did not vote for all the bills pertaining to the Ceylon citizenship act, his silence in parliament made the Tamil public believe that he was not interested in Indian Tamil rights.
[Contains English characters] . In 1949 a new Tamil political party, named the Federal Party, was formed and was led by S.
[Contains English characters] J. V. Chelvanayakam who earlier broke away from All Ceylon Tamil Congress because of the latters decision to tie up with the UNP.
[Contains English characters] In 1956 the government enacted another act called the Official Language Act which made the Sinhala as the sole official language of Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] The Ceylon Citizen Act and the Sinhala Only Act were seen as discriminatory policies towards the minorities and led to increased ethnic and political tensions between the two communities.
[Contains English characters] The Federal Party opposed both the Ceylon Citizenship Act and the Sinhala Only Act and as a result became popular amongst the Tamil population .
[Contains English characters] As a result of their popularity the Federal party became the most dominant party in the Tamil districts after the 1956 elections.
[Contains English characters] The Federal Party became the most dominant Tamil political party in 1956 and lobbied for a unitary state which gave Tamil and Sinhalese equal rights, including recognition of two official languages and considerable autonomy for the Tamil areas.
[Contains English characters] It was against this backdrop that the Federal party decided to sign the Bandaranaike-Chelvanayakam Pact in July 1957. However, soon afterwards the agreement was abandoned by the Sinhala party.
[Contains English characters] In 1965, another pact, the Senanayake-Chelvanayakam pact was signed but also not implemented.
[Contains English characters] The failure of the Sinhalese dominated government to implement devolutionary agreements through the 1950s and 1960s, abrogation of power-sharing promises, worsening economic conditions, and lack of territorial autonomy caused further disillusionment and isolationamong northern Tamils.
[Contains English characters] In the 1970 election the United Front led by Sirimavo Bandaranaike came into power.
[Contains English characters] The new government adopted two new policies that were considered discriminatory by the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] First, the government introduced a discriminatory system regulating university admissions, specifically targeted at reducing the intake of overachieving Tamils and other minorities in the Sri Lankan educational system.
[Contains English characters] The scheme allotted up to 40% of the university placement to rural youth .
[Contains English characters] The government claimed that this was an affirmative action scheme to assist geographically disadvantaged students to gain tertiary education.
[Contains English characters] According to K. M. de Silva, a historian, the system of standardisation of marks required the Tamil students to achieve higher marks than the Sinhalese students to get into university.
[Contains English characters] A similar policy was adapted for employment in the public sector, leaving less than 10 percent of civil service jobs available to Tamil speakers.
[Contains English characters] The Federal Party opposed these policies and Chelvanayakam resigned his parliamentary seat on October 1972. The new constitution in 1972 further exacerbated long standing grievances and sense of discrimination for the Sri Lankan Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] This had emboldened younger Tamils to seek ways to form a Tamil homeland where the rights and freedoms of the Tamil people could be protected and nurtured.
[Contains English characters] In 1973, Tamil parties call for regional autonomy was replaced with the demand for a separate state called Tamil Eelam.
[Contains English characters] Two years later, in 1975, all Tamil political parties merged together and became known as the Tamil United Liberation Front .
[Contains English characters] On 1976, the first national convention of the Tamil United Liberation Front was held at Vaddukodai, where the party adopted a unanimous resolution called the Vaddukodai Resolution.
[Contains English characters] This resolution charged that the Sinhalese government, with the use of the constitution of 1972, had used its power to deprive the Tamil nation of its territory, language, citizenship, economic life, opportunities of employment and education thereby destroying all the attributes of nationhood of the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] The resolution further called for the Free, Sovereign, Secular Socialist State of TAMIL EELAM.
[Contains English characters] As a result of the Vaddukodai resolution, the Tamil United Liberation Front became the first Tamil political party to run its campaign on a separatist platform.
[Contains English characters] It swept the parliamentary elections in the Tamil-dominated districts of the North and East in 1977, winning 18 seats and became the largest opposition in Parliament.
[Contains English characters] The reason for the success of the TULF was seen as the result of growing Tamil agitation for self-determination.
[Contains English characters] During the time of the Vaddukodai declaration, there were several Tamil militant organizations who believed that armed struggle was the only way to protect the sovereignty of the Tamil areas.

[Contains English characters] DDCs were soon abandoned because the two sides were not able to agree to the number of District Ministers in the Tamil districts.
[Contains English characters] In 1983 the Sixth Amendment was passed and required Tamil members of parliament and Tamils in public office to take the oath of allegiance to the unitary state of Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] The Sixth Amendment forbade advocating a separate state even by peaceful means.
[Contains English characters] Consequently, the TULF was expelled from the parliament for refusing to take the oath.
[Contains English characters] At first, the concept of Tamil Eelam conceived by the Federal party was a state within a united Sri Lanka, but in time the concept developed into complete self-determination.
[Contains English characters] The concept of Tamil Eelam always implied the notion of freedom and self-government for the Tamil people The demand for a separate statehood of Tamil Eelam is believed to have grown as a result of job opportunities and university admissions being severely curtailed for Tamils because of discriminatory government quotas; and continuing decline of economic opportunities As a result the people began to believe that a separate state would win back their opportunities and the concept of Tamil Eelam was welcomed enthusiastically throughout Tamil areas In addition to the economical and social basis for separate state there is also a more fundamental basis for support for a separate statehood - safety In 1977, after the parliamentary election campaign by the TULF which was on a platform of separate state, a riot engulfed the island in which about 300 Tamil civilians were killed Likewise in 1983, another anti-Tamil riot engulfed the island as a result of an IED attack on group of Sri Lankan Soldiers by LTTE rebels.
[Contains English characters] The riot, known as Black July, killed between 1,000 and 3,000 The call for Tamil Eelam increased as a result of this violence against the Tamil minority perpetrated by the Sinhalese majority Furthermore, allegations of state terrorism and genocide committed by the Sri Lankan government have led to solidification of demand for a separate state for minority Tamils To add to the Tamil peoples separatist sentiments, acts of mass violence, rape, extrajudicial executions, whole scale round ups, forced detention, torture and other forms of inhuman treatment by members of Sinhalese dominated Sri Lankan security forces within the North and East provinces have further created communal tensions among the Tamil people The mistrust in the Sinhala dominated armed forces and the perceived discrimination faced by the Tamil population lead the Tamil people to believe that only Eelam could provide long term safety and came to believe that their very survival was possible only through formation of a separate Tamil state on the island The parts of northern and eastern Sri Lanka which were formerly under the control of the LTTE were run as a de facto state with its own government in these areas.

[Contains English characters] In 1824, Britain adopted a close approximation to the ale gallon known as the imperial gallon.
[Contains English characters] The imperial gallon was based on the volume of 10 lb of distilled water weighed in air with brass weights with the barometer standing at 30 in Hg at a temperature of 62 °F.
[Contains English characters] In 1963 this definition was refined as the space occupied by 10 lb of distilled water of density 0.998 859 g/ml weighed in air of density 0.001 217 g/ml against weights of density 8.136 g/ml.
[Contains English characters] This works out to 4.545 964 591 L, or 277.420 cu in.
[Contains English characters] The Weights and Measures Act of 1985 switched to a gallon of exactly 4.546 09 L .
[Contains English characters] In the 19th and 20th centuries Britain has used three different systems for mass and weight: The troy pound was made the primary unit of mass by the 1824 Act; however, its use was abolished in Britain on 6 January 1879, making the Avoirdupois pound the primary unit of mass with only the troy ounce and its decimal subdivisions retained.
[Contains English characters] The British ton, is 2240 pounds, which is very close to a metric tonne, whereas the ton generally used in the United States is the short ton of 2000 pounds .

[Contains English characters] A business proposal is a written offer from a seller to a prospective buyer.
[Contains English characters] Business proposals are often a key step in the complex sales process—i. e. , whenever a buyer considers more than price in a purchase.
[Contains English characters] There are three distinct categories of business proposals: formally solicited, informally solicited, and unsolicited.
[Contains English characters] Solicited proposals are written in response to published requirements, contained in a Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, or an Invitation for Bids .
[Contains English characters] RFPs provide detailed specifications of what the customers wants to buy and sometimes include directions for preparing the proposal, as well as evaluation criteria the customer will use to evaluate offers.
[Contains English characters] Customers issue RFPs when their needs cannot be met with generally available products or services.
[Contains English characters] Proposals in response to RFPs are seldom less than 10 pages and sometimes reach 1,000s of pages, without cost data.
[Contains English characters] Customers issue RFQs when they want to buy large amounts of a commodity and price is not the only issue—for example, when availability or delivering or service are considerations.
[Contains English characters] RFQs can be very detailed, so proposals written to RFQs can be lengthy but generally much shorter than an RFP-proposal.
[Contains English characters] RFQ proposals consist primarily of cost data, with small narratives addressing customer issues, such as quality control.
[Contains English characters] Customers issue IFBs when they are buying some service, such as construction.
[Contains English characters] The requirements are detailed, but the primary consideration is price.
[Contains English characters] For example, a customer provides architectural blueprints for contractors to bid on.
[Contains English characters] These proposals can be lengthy but most of the length comes from cost-estimating data and detailed schedules.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes before a customer issues an RFP or RFQ or IFB, the customer will issue a Request for Information .
[Contains English characters] The purpose of the RFI is to gain marketing intelligence about what products, services, and vendors are available.
[Contains English characters] RFIs are used to shape final RFPs, RFQs, and IFBs, so potential vendors take great care in responding to these requests, hoping to shape the eventual formal solicitation toward their products or services.
[Contains English characters] Informally solicited proposals are typically the result of conversations held between a vendor and a prospective customer.
[Contains English characters] The customer is interested enough in a product or service to ask for a proposal.
[Contains English characters] Typically, the customer does not ask for competing proposals from other vendors.
[Contains English characters] This type of proposal is known as a sole-source proposal.
[Contains English characters] There are no formal requirements to respond to, just the information gleaned from customer meetings.
[Contains English characters] These proposals are typically less than 25-pages, with many less than 5 pages.
[Contains English characters] Unsolicited proposals are marketing brochures.
[Contains English characters] They are always generic, with no direct connection between customer needs or specified requirements.
[Contains English characters] Vendors use them to introduce a product or service to a prospective customer.
[Contains English characters] They are often used as leave-behinds at the end of initial meetings with customers or give-aways at trade shows or other public meetings.
[Contains English characters] They are not designed to close a sale, just introduce the possibility of a sale.
[Contains English characters] A proposal puts the buyers requirements in a context that favors the sellers products and services, and educates the buyer about the capabilities of the seller in satisfying their needs.
[Contains English characters] A successful proposal results in a sale, where both parties get what they want, a win-win situation.
[Contains English characters] The professional organization devoted to the advancement of the art and science of proposal development is The Association of Proposal Management Professionals.
