[Contains English characters] The primary purpose of a web browser is to bring information resources to the user.
[Contains English characters] This process begins when the user inputs a Uniform Resource Identifier, for example http://en. wikipedia. org/, into the browser.
[Contains English characters] The prefix of the URI determines how the URI will be interpreted.
[Contains English characters] The most commonly used kind of URI starts with http: and identifies a resource to be retrieved over the Hypertext Transfer Protocol .
[Contains English characters] Many browsers also support a variety of other prefixes, such as https: for HTTPS, ftp: for the File Transfer Protocol, and file: for local files.
[Contains English characters] Prefixes that the web browser cannot directly handle are often handed off to another application entirely.
[Contains English characters] For example, mailto: URIs are usually passed to the users default e-mail application, and news: URIs are passed to the users default newsgroup reader.
[Contains English characters] In the case of http, https, file, and others, once the resource has been retrieved the web browser will display it.
[Contains English characters] HTML is passed to the browsers layout engine to be transformed from markup to an interactive document.
[Contains English characters] Aside from HTML, web browsers can generally display any kind of content that can be part of a web page.
[Contains English characters] Most browsers can display images, audio, video, and XML files, and often have plug-ins to support Flash applications and Java applets.
[Contains English characters] Upon encountering a file of an unsupported type or a file that is set up to be downloaded rather than displayed, the browser prompts the user to save the file to disk.
[Contains English characters] Information resources may contain hyperlinks to other information resources.
[Contains English characters] Each link contains the URI of a resource to go to.
[Contains English characters] When a link is clicked, the browser navigates to the resource indicated by the links target URI, and the process of bringing content to the user begins again.
[Contains English characters] Available web browsers range in features from minimal, text-based user interfaces with bare-bones support for HTML to rich user interfaces supporting a wide variety of file formats and protocols.
[Contains English characters] Browsers which include additional components to support e-mail, Usenet news, and Internet Relay Chat, are sometimes referred to as Internet suites rather than merely web browsers.
[Contains English characters] All major web browsers allow the user to open multiple information resources at the same time, either in different browser windows or in different tabs of the same window.
[Contains English characters] Major browsers also include pop-up blockers to prevent unwanted windows from popping up without the users consent.
[Contains English characters] Most web browsers can display a list of web pages that the user has bookmarked so that the user can quickly return to them.
[Contains English characters] Bookmarks are also called Favorites in Internet Explorer.
[Contains English characters] In addition, all major web browsers have some form of built-in web feed aggregator.
[Contains English characters] In Mozilla Firefox, web feeds are formatted as live bookmarks and behave like a folder of bookmarks corresponding to recent entries in the feed.
[Contains English characters] In Opera, a more traditional feed reader is included which stores and displays the contents of the feed.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, most browsers can be extended via plug-ins, downloadable components that provide additional features.
[Contains English characters] Most major web browsers have these user interface elements in common: Major browsers also possess incremental find features to search within a web page.
[Contains English characters] Most browsers support HTTP Secure and offer quick and easy ways to delete the web cache, cookies, and browsing history.

[Contains English characters] Early web browsers supported only a very simple version of HTML.

[Contains English characters] We ask for your help in updating any templates that dont look correct.
[Contains English characters] What kind of templates?
[Contains English characters] Specifically templates that notify readers and contributors about issues with the content of an article – the text and information in the article.

[Contains English characters] The Republic of India has hundreds of languages.
[Contains English characters] According to the Census of 2001, there are 1,635 rationalized mother tongues and 122 languages with more than 10,000 speakers.
[Contains English characters] During the British Raj, इंग्रजी was the official language.
[Contains English characters] When the Indian Independence Movement gained momentum in the early part of the 20th Century, efforts were undertaken to make Hindustani as a common language to unite various linguistic groups against the British Government.
[Contains English characters] As early as 1918, Mahatma Gandhi established the Dakshin Bharat हिंदी Prachar Sabha .
[Contains English characters] In 1925, the Indian National Congress switched to Hindustani from इंग्रजी for conducting its proceedings.
[Contains English characters] Both Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru were supporters of Hindustani and Congress wanted to propagate the learning of Hindustani in non-हिंदी speaking Provinces of India.
[Contains English characters] The idea of making Hindustani or हिंदी the common language, was not acceptable to Periyar E. V. Ramasamy, who viewed it as an attempt to make Tamils subordinate to North India.
[Contains English characters] The Indian National Congress won the 1937 elections in Madras Presidency. C. Rajagopalachari became the Chief Minister on 14 July 1937. He was a supporter of propagating हिंदी in South India.
[Contains English characters] Even before the elections, he had expressed support for हिंदी in a newspaper article : Government employment is limited.
[Contains English characters] All cannot get it.
[Contains English characters] Therefore one has to search for other jobs.
[Contains English characters] For that and for business, knowledge of हिंदी is necessary.
[Contains English characters] Only if we learn हिंदी, the south Indian can gain respect among the others.
[Contains English characters] On 11 August 1937, within a month of coming to power, he announced his intention to introduce हिंदी language teaching in secondary schools by issuing a policy statement.
[Contains English characters] This move followed lobbying by pro-हिंदी organisations like Hindustani Seva Dal and Hindustani Hitashi Sabha.
[Contains English characters] These organisations had earlier convinced many Congress led local governments to introduce compulsory हिंदी in schools in the early 1930s.
[Contains English characters] Periyar E. V. Ramasamy and the opposition Justicy Party led by A.
[Contains English characters] T. Panneerselvam immediately opposed the move.
[Contains English characters] An हिंदी-विरोधी conference was organised on 4 October 1937 to protest the announcement.
[Contains English characters] On 21 April 1938, Rajaji went ahead and passed a government order making the teaching of हिंदी compulsory in 125 Secondary schools in the Presidency.
[Contains English characters] Rajajis persistence was viewed by opponents as an attempt to destroy Tamil and promote हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] They started state wide protests against Rajaji and हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] The agitation was marked by protest marches, हिंदी-विरोधी conferences, observing a हिंदी-विरोधी day, fasts against government policies, black flag demonstrations and picketing of government offices and institutions.
[Contains English characters] It was active in Tamil speaking districts of the Presidency - Ramnad, Tinnevely, Salem, Tanjore and North Arcot.
[Contains English characters] The agitation lasted till the order was withdrawn in February 1940. Two persons -Thalamuthu and Natarajan - lost their lives.
[Contains English characters] Around 1,200 people including Periyar were imprisoned.
[Contains English characters] The हिंदी-विरोधी agitation was backed by Periyars Self-Respect Movement and the opposition Justice Party.
[Contains English characters] Periyar eventually became the President of the Justice Party during the course of the agitation.
[Contains English characters] The agitation was also supported by Tamil scholars like Maraimalai Adigal, Somasundara Bharathi, K.
[Contains English characters] Appadurai, Mudiyarasan and Ilakkuvanar.
[Contains English characters] In December 1937, Tamil Saivite scholars were among the first to announce their opposition to the हिंदी teaching in the Saiva Sidhandha Maha Samaja meeting at Velur.
[Contains English characters] Women also participated in the agitation in large numbers.
[Contains English characters] Moovalur Ramamirtham, Narayani, Va. Ba. Thamaraikani, Munnagar Azhagiyar, Dr.
[Contains English characters] Dharmambal, Malar Mugathammaiyar, Pattammal and Seethammal were some of the women who were arrested for participating in the agitation.
[Contains English characters] On 13 November 1938, the Tamil Nadu Womens Conference was convened to demonstrate womens support for the movement.
[Contains English characters] Despite the anti-Brahmin sentiments espoused by the backers of the agitation a, few Brahmins like Kanchi Rajagopalachari also participated in the movement.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil speaking Muslims in the Madras presidency supported the agitation . P. Kaliffulah, a Muslim League member representing Trichy in the Legislative Assembly, declared I may at once say that I am a Rowther myself; my mother tongue is Tamil and not Urdu.
[Contains English characters] I am not ashamed of it; I am proud of it. . We have not been told why हिंदी after all has been chosen as the common language of India.
[Contains English characters] Acknowledging the agitations popular support, Lord Erskine, the then Governor of Madras wrote to Viceroy Linlithgow in July 1938 that Compulsory हिंदी has been the cause of great trouble in this province and is certainly contrary to the wishes of the bulk of the population. . . On 1 May 1938, a young man named Stalin Jagadeesan went on a fast demanding the withdrawal of compulsory हिंदी teaching.
[Contains English characters] He became a symbol for the हिंदी-विरोधी agitators.
[Contains English characters] In an interview published in Periyars magazine Viduthalai he declared that his fast was to prove that Tamil thai still had loyal sons.
[Contains English characters] On 1 June, another man named Ponnusamy began a fast in front of Rajajis house.
[Contains English characters] Periyar did not approve of fasting as a form of protest.
[Contains English characters] But other leaders of the agitation like C. N. Annadurai used Jagadeesan as an example.
[Contains English characters] Annadurai declared in an हिंदी-विरोधी meeting that If Jagadeesan dies, I am ready to take his place, and die along with ten others.
[Contains English characters] As soon as Jagadeesan dies, you should also be prepared to die.
[Contains English characters] Jagadeesans fast was called off after ten weeks and it was reported that he had been eating regularly during the nights.
[Contains English characters] In August-September 1938, a protest march was jointly organised by Periyars Self-Respect movement and the Muslim league.
[Contains English characters] It was flagged of by Periyar and Khaliffullah.
[Contains English characters] The marchers who called themselves Tamilar Padai, started from Trichy on 1 August 1938. They were led by Kumarasamy Pillai and Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammal.
[Contains English characters] In the next 42 days, the marchers covered 234 villages and 60 towns.
[Contains English characters] They addressed 87 public meetings and received widespread coverage in the Press.
[Contains English characters] They reached Madras on 11 September 1938 and were arrested for picketing government offices.
[Contains English characters] The march succeeded in raising हिंदी-विरोधी and pro-Tamil support in smaller towns and villages they covered.
[Contains English characters] Two persons died during the agitation and were claimed as martyrs by the agitators.
[Contains English characters] Their deaths fueled the protests further.
[Contains English characters] Natarajan was arrested On 5 December 1938. He was admitted to the hospital on the 30 December and died on 15 January 1939. On 13 February 1939, Thalamuthu Nadar was arrested with others for picketing the Hindu Theological High School in Madras.
[Contains English characters] While imprisoned, he fell ill on 6 March and died on 11 March.
[Contains English characters] The government claimed that his death was due to Cellulitis and Amoebic dysentery and he was already in poor health when he died.
[Contains English characters] It dismissed their deaths and claimed they were illiterates.
[Contains English characters] When the issue was raised in the Assembly, Rajaji dismissed it casually.
[Contains English characters] The agitators were incensed by the government attitude and turned the dead men into martyrs.
[Contains English characters] Their funeral processions in Madras were attended by hundreds of mourners and witnessed fiery speeches denouncing the government.
[Contains English characters] Annadurai proclaimed that Natarajan’s name and deeds should be inscribed in gold in the history of the world.
[Contains English characters] The agitators praised their sacrifices and claimed that the dead men had refused early release in exchange for ending their activities.
[Contains English characters] In an interview given to the Sunday Observer on 27 January 1939, Natarajans father K.
[Contains English characters] Lakshmanan said when his son was hospitalized he refused to apologize to get an early release.
[Contains English characters] The हिंदी-विरोधी movement viewed the हिंदी legislation as an attempt by Brahmins to impose हिंदी and Sanskrit over Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Rajajis earlier attempt to translate an इंग्रजी Language Physics book into Tamil using Sanskrit words was viewed as proof of his preference of Sanskrit over Tamil.
[Contains English characters] The हिंदी-विरोधी movement portrayed the Brahmin dominated Tamil Nadu Congress party as a stooge of हिंदी Imperialists from the North.
[Contains English characters] The resistance of the Brahmin Tamil scholars for removing Sanskrit words from Tamil was viewed by some in the agitation as proof of Brahmin complicity in the attempt to destroy Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Rajaji was identified as an enemy of Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Dravidian movement newspapers carried cartoons depicting Rajaji hदुवाing a dagger at Tamil Thai and disrobing her.
[Contains English characters] Similar banners were displayed in the processions taken out by हिंदी-विरोधी agitators.
[Contains English characters] In an हिंदी-विरोधी meeting organised in August 1938, Pavalar Balasundaram accused the Brahmin community of killing Tamil Thai.
[Contains English characters] Rajajis dismissal of Natarasans death in the Assembly was denounced as Aryans laughing while Tamils shed tears for their hero.

[Contains English characters] While Rajaji and his supporters stuck to their position, Sathyamurti and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan were against it.
[Contains English characters] They wanted Rajaji to make हिंदी optional or to provide a conscience clause for allowing parents to withhold their children from हिंदी Classes.

[Contains English characters] 1,198 protesters were arrested and out of them 1,179 were convicted .
[Contains English characters] Periyar was sentenced to one year of rigorous imprisonment and Annadurai was jailed for four months.
[Contains English characters] On 7 June 1939, all those arrested for participating in the agitations were released without explanation.
[Contains English characters] Rajaji also organised pro-Hindustani meetings to counter the agitators.
[Contains English characters] On 29 October 1939, Rajajis Congress Government resigned protesting the involvement of India in the Second World War.
[Contains English characters] Madras provincial government was placed under Governors rule.
[Contains English characters] On 31 October, Periyar suspended the agitation and asked the Governor to withdraw the compulsory हिंदी order.
[Contains English characters] On 21 February 1940, Governor Erskine, issued a press communique withdrawing compulsory हिंदी teaching and making it optional.
[Contains English characters] During 1940-46, there were sporadic agitations against हिंदी by the Dravidar Kazhagam and Periyar.
[Contains English characters] Whenever the government introduced हिंदी as a compulsory language in schools, हिंदी-विरोधी protests happened and succeeded in stopping the move.
[Contains English characters] The largest हिंदी-विरोधी agitations in this period occurred in 1948-50. After India obtained independence in 1947, the Congress Government at the Centre urged all states to make हिंदी compulsory in schools.
[Contains English characters] The Congress Government of Madras Presidency under Omandur Ramasamy Reddiar complied and made हिंदी compulsory from the academic year 1948-49. It also introduced a minimum mark qualification in हिंदी for the promotion of students to higher standards .
[Contains English characters] Periyar once again launched a हिंदी-विरोधी agitation.
[Contains English characters] The 1948 agitation was supported by former Congress nationalists like M. P. Sivagnanam and Thiru.
[Contains English characters] Vi. Ka, who recanted their earlier pro-हिंदी policies.
[Contains English characters] On 17 July, the DK convened an all party हिंदी-विरोधी conference to oppose the compulsory हिंदी teaching.
[Contains English characters] As in the agitation of 1938-40, this agitation was also characterized by strikes, black flag demonstrations and हिंदी-विरोधी processions.
[Contains English characters] When Rajaji visited Madras on 23 August, the DK staged a black flag demonstration protesting against his visit.
[Contains English characters] On 27 August, Periyar and Annadurai were arrested.
[Contains English characters] The Government did not change its position on हिंदी and the agitation continued.
[Contains English characters] On 18 August Periyar and other DK leaders were arrested again.
[Contains English characters] A compromise was reached between the government and agitators.
[Contains English characters] The government stopped the legal action against the agitators and they in turn dropped the agitation on 26 December 1948. Eventually, the government made हिंदी teaching optional from the academic year 1950-51. Students who did not want to learn हिंदी were allowed to participate in other school activities during हिंदी classes.
[Contains English characters] The Indian Constituent Assembly was established on 9 December 1946, for drafting a Constitution when India became independent.
[Contains English characters] The Constituent Assembly witnessed fierce debates on the language issue.
[Contains English characters] The adoption of a National Language, the language in which the constitution was to be written in and the language in which the proceedings of the assembly were to be conducted were the main questions debated by the framers of the Constitution.
[Contains English characters] On one side were the members from the हिंदी speaking provinces like Algu Rai Sastri, R. V. Dhulekar, Balkrishna Sharma, Purushottam Das Tandon,, Babunath Gupta, Hari Vinayak Pataskar and Seth Govind Das .
[Contains English characters] They moved a large number of pro-हिंदी amendments and argued for adopting हिंदी as the sole National Language.
[Contains English characters] On 10 December 1946, Dhulekar declared People who do not know Hindustani have no right to stay in India.
[Contains English characters] People who are present in the House to fashion a constitution for India and do not know Hindustani are not worthy to be members of this assembly.
[Contains English characters] They had better leave.
[Contains English characters] The pro-हिंदी block was further divided into two camps: 1 The हिंदी faction comprising Tandon, Govind Das, Sampurnanand, Ravishankar Shukla and K. M. Munshi and 2the Hindustani faction represented by Jawaharlal Nehru and Abul Kalam Azad.
[Contains English characters] The adoption of हिंदी as the national language was opposed by members from South India like T. T. Krishnamachari, G.
[Contains English characters] Durgabai, T. A. Ramalingam Chettiar, N.
[Contains English characters] G. Ranga, N.
[Contains English characters] Gopalaswamy Ayyangar and S. V. Krishnamurthy Rao .
[Contains English characters] This हिंदी-विरोधी block favoured retaining इंग्रजी as official language.
[Contains English characters] Their views were reflected in the following pronouncement of Krishnamachari: We disliked the इंग्रजी language in the past.
[Contains English characters] I disliked it because I was forced to learn Shakespeare and Milton, for which I had no taste at all.
[Contains English characters] If we are going to be compelled to learn हिंदी, I would perhaps not be able to learn it because of my age, and perhaps I would not be willing to do it because of the amount of constraint you put on me.
[Contains English characters] This kind of intolerance makes us fear that the strong Centre which we need, a strong Centre which is necessary will also mean the enslavement of people who do not speak the language at the centre.
[Contains English characters] I would, Sir, convey a warning on behalf of people of the South for the reason that there are already elements in South India who want separation. . . , and my honourable friends in U.
[Contains English characters] P. do not help us in any way by flogging their idea of हिंदी Imperialism to the maximum extent possible.
[Contains English characters] So, it is up to my friends in Uttar Pradesh to have a whole India; it is up to them to have a हिंदी-India.
[Contains English characters] The choice is theirs.
[Contains English characters] After three years of debate, the assembly arrived at a compromise at the end of 1949. It was called the Munshi-Ayyangar compromise and it struck a balance between the demands of all groups.
[Contains English characters] Part XVII of the Indian Constitution was drafted according to this compromise.
[Contains English characters] It did not have any mention of a National Language.
[Contains English characters] Instead, it defined only the अधिकृत भाषा of the Union: हिंदी भाषा in देवनागरी script would be the official language of the Indian Union.
[Contains English characters] For fifteen years, इंग्रजी would also be used for all official purposes .
[Contains English characters] A language commission could be convened after five years to recommend ways to promote हिंदी as the sole official language and to phase out the use of इंग्रजी .
[Contains English characters] Official communication between states and between states and the Union would be in the official language of the union .
[Contains English characters] इंग्रजी would be used for all legal purposes - in court proceedings, bills, laws, rules and other regulations .
[Contains English characters] The Union was duty bound to promote the spread and usage of हिंदी .
[Contains English characters] India became independent on 15 August 1947 and the Constitution was adopted on 26 January 1950. The adoption of इंग्रजी as official language along with हिंदी was heavily criticized by pro-हिंदी politicians like Jana Sanghs founder Syama Prasad Mookerjee, who demanded that हिंदी should be made National language.
[Contains English characters] Soon after the Constitution was adopted on 26 January 1950, efforts were made to propagate हिंदी for official usage.
[Contains English characters] In 1952, the Ministry of Education launched a voluntary हिंदी teaching scheme.
[Contains English characters] On 27 May 1952, use of हिंदी was introduced in warrants for judicial appointments.
[Contains English characters] In 1955, in-house हिंदी training was started for all ministries and departments of the central government.
[Contains English characters] On 3 December 1955, the government started using हिंदी for specific purposes of the Union As provided for by Article 343, Nehru appointed the First Official Language Commission under the chairmanship of B. G. Kher on 7 June 1955. The commission delivered its report on 31 July 1956. It recommended a number of steps to eventually replace इंग्रजी with हिंदी .
[Contains English characters] The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language, chaired by Govind Ballabh Pant was constituted in September 1957 to review the Kher commission report.
[Contains English characters] After two years of deliberations, the Pant Committeee submitted its recommendations to the President on 8 February 1959. It recommended that हिंदी should be made the primary official language with इंग्रजी as the subsidiary one.
[Contains English characters] The Kher Commission and the Pant Committee recommendations were condemned and opposed by from non हिंदी politicians like Suniti Kumar Chatterji, Frank Anthony and P. Subbarayan. The Academy of Telugu opposed the switch from इंग्रजी to हिंदी in a convention held in 1956. Rajaji, once a staunch supporter of हिंदी, organised a All India Language Conference on 8 March 1958 to oppose the switch and declared हिंदी is as much foreign to non-हिंदी speaking people as इंग्रजी is to the protagonists of हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] As the opposition to हिंदी grew stronger, Nehru tried to reassure the concerns of non-हिंदी speakers.
[Contains English characters] Speaking in the parliamentary debate on the Pant committee report Nehru gave an assurance to them : For an indefinite period - I do not know how long - I should have, I would have इंग्रजी as an associate, additional language not because of facilities and all that but because I do not wish the people of Non-हिंदी areas to feel that certain doors of advance are closed to them because they are forced to correspond - the Government, I mean - in the हिंदी language.
[Contains English characters] They can correspond in इंग्रजी.
[Contains English characters] So I could have it as an alternate language as long as people require it and the decision for that - I would leave not to the हिंदी-knowing people, but to the non हिंदी-knowing people This assurance momentarily allayed the fears of the South Indians.
[Contains English characters] The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam which split from the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1949, inherited the हिंदी-विरोधी policies of its parent organisation.
[Contains English characters] DMKs founder Annadurai had earlier participated in the हिंदी-विरोधी agitations during 1938-40 and in the 1940s.
[Contains English characters] In July 1953, the DMK launched an agitation for changing the name of a town - Dalmiapuram - to Kallakudi.
[Contains English characters] They claimed that the towns name symbolised the exploitation of South India by the North.
[Contains English characters] On 15 July 1953, M.
[Contains English characters] Karunanidhi and other DMK members erased the हिंदी name in Dalmiapuram railway stations name board and lay down on the tracks.
[Contains English characters] In the altercation with the Police that followed the protests, two DMK members lost their lives and several others including Karunanidhi were arrested.
[Contains English characters] In the 1950s DMK continued its हिंदी-विरोधी policies along with the secessionist demand for Dravidistan.
[Contains English characters] On 28 January 1956, Annadurai along with Periyar and Rajaji signed a resolution passed by the Academy of Tamil Culture endorsing the continuation of इंग्रजी as the official language.
[Contains English characters] On 21 September 1957 the DMK convened a हिंदी-विरोधी Conference to protest against the imposition of हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] It observed 13 October 1957 as हिंदी-विरोधी Day.
[Contains English characters] On 31 July 1960, another open air हिंदी-विरोधी conference was held at Kodambakkam, Madras.
[Contains English characters] In November 1963, DMK dropped its secessionist demand in the wake of the Sino-Indian War and the passage of the anti-secessionist 16th Amendment to the Indian Constitution.
[Contains English characters] But the हिंदी-विरोधी stance remained and hardened with the passage of अधिकृत भाषा Act of 1963. The DMKs view on हिंदीs qualifications for official language status were reflected in Annadurais response to the numerical superiority of हिंदी argument: If we had to accept the principle of numerical superiority while selecting our national bird, the choice would have fallen not on the peacock but on the common crow.
[Contains English characters] As the deadline stipulated in Part XVII of the Constitution for switching to हिंदी as primary official language approached, the Central Government stepped up its efforts to spread हिंदीs official usage.
[Contains English characters] In 1960, compulsory training for हिंदी typing and stenography was started.
[Contains English characters] The same year, Indias president Rajendra Prasad acted on the Pant Committees recommendations and issued orders for preparation of हिंदी glossaries, translating procedural literature and legal codes to हिंदी, imparting हिंदी education to government employees and other efforts for propagating हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] To give legal status to Nehrus assurance of 1959, the अधिकृत भाषा Act was passed in 1963. In Nehrus own words : This is a Bill, in continuation of what has happened in the past, to remove a restriction which had been placed by the Constitution on the use of इंग्रजी after a certain date i. e. 1965. It is just to remove that restriction that this is placed.
[Contains English characters] The bill was introduced in Parliament on 21 January 1963. Opposition to the Bill came from DMK members who objected to the usage of the word may instead of shall in section 3 of the bill .
[Contains English characters] DMK s argument was that the term may could be interpreted as may not by future administrations.
[Contains English characters] They feared that minority opinion will not be considered and non हिंदी speakers views would be ignored.
[Contains English characters] On 22 April, Nehru assured the parliamentarians that, for that particular case may had the same meaning as shall.
[Contains English characters] The DMK then demanded, if that was the case why shall was not used instead of may.
[Contains English characters] Leading the opposition to the bill was Annadurai .
[Contains English characters] He pleaded for the indefinite continuation of the status quo.
[Contains English characters] He argued for the continuation of इंग्रजी as official Language as it distributes advantages or disadvantages evenly.
[Contains English characters] The Bill was passed on 27 April without any change in the wording.
[Contains English characters] As he had warned earlier, Annadurai launched state wide protests against हिंदी.
[Contains English characters] In November 1963, Annadurai was arrested along with 500 DMK members for burning part XVII of the Constitution at an हिंदी-विरोधी Conference.
[Contains English characters] Nehru died in May 1964 and Lal Bahadur Shastri became Prime Minister of India.
[Contains English characters] Shastri and his senior cabinet members Morarji Desai and Gulzari Lal Nanda were strong supporters of हिंदी being the sole official language.
[Contains English characters] This increased the apprehension that Nehrus assurances of 1959 and 1963 will not be kept despite Shastris assurances to the contrary.
[Contains English characters] Concerns over the preference of हिंदी in central government Jobs, civil service examinations and the fear that इंग्रजी will be replaced with हिंदी as medium of instruction brought students into the हिंदी-विरोधी Agitation camp in large numbers.
[Contains English characters] On 7 March 1964, the chief minister of Madras State, M.
[Contains English characters] Bhaktavatsalam at a session of the Madras Legislative Assembly recommended the introduction of Three-language formula in the state.
[Contains English characters] Apprehension over the Three-language formula increased student support for the हिंदी-विरोधी cause As January 26, 1965 approached, the Anti हिंदी agitation in Tamil Nadu grew in numbers and urgency.

[Contains English characters] A volley of sandals from the students returned the insult.
[Contains English characters] The provoked Congress volunteers, who ran back into the Party’s office, returned with knives and attacked students, wounding seven.

[Contains English characters] Efforts to amend the अधिकृत भाषा Act according to Shastris assurances given in February 1965 faced stiff resistance from the pro-हिंदी lobby.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Infobox Institute The National Institute of Virology, Pune is Indias Premier Virology Research institute, part of Indian Council of Medical Research .
[Contains English characters] It was previously known as Virus Research Center and was founded in collaboration with the Rockefeller Foundation.
[Contains English characters] Today it has been is now designated as WHO H5 reference Laboratory for SE Asia region The Virus Research Center, Pune came into existence in 1952 under the joint auspices of the ICMR and the Rockefeller Foundation, as a part of the global programme of investigations on the arthropod-borne group of viruses.
[Contains English characters] In view of its expanded scope and activities, the VRC was redesignated as the National Institute of Virology in 1978. The NIV is identified today as the WHO Collaborating Center for arboviruses reference and hemorrhagic fever reference and research.
[Contains English characters] NIV is also the National Monitoring Center for Influenza, Japanese encephalitis, Rota, Measles and Hepatitis.
[Contains English characters] The National Institute of Virology is one of the major Institutes of the Indian Council of Medical Research .
[Contains English characters] It was established at Pune, Maharashtra State in 1952 as Virus Research Centre under the auspices of the ICMR and the Rockefeller Foundation, USA.
[Contains English characters] It was an outcome of the global programme of the RF for investigating the Arthropod Borne viruses.
[Contains English characters] Since the studies on arboviruses and their arthropod vectors involve most of the basic principles and techniques of general virology, entomology and zoology, these viruses were also considered to be an ideal group, to begin with, for intensive training and research in virology in our country.
[Contains English characters] The RF withdrew its support in 1967 and since then the Institute is entirely funded by the ICMR The Institute was designated as one of the collaborating laboratories of the World Health Organization in 1967 and it started functioning as the regional centre of the WHO for South-East Asia for arbovirus studies from 1969. Since 1974, it has been functioning as a WHO collaborating centre for arbovirus reference and research.
[Contains English characters] In 1995 it has been redesignated as the WHO Collaborating Centre for Arbovirus and Haemorrhagic Fever Reference and Research and Rapid Diagnosis of Viral Diseases.
[Contains English characters] NIV is also the National Centre for Hepatitis and Influenza.
[Contains English characters] The field unit of NIV at Bangalore is one of the centers under National Polio Surveillance Program conducting surveillance of acute flaccid paralysis cases from Kamataka as a part of Global Polio Eradication Prograrnme of the WHO South-East Asia region since 1997. Institute also conduct M. Sc. & PhD course under aegis of University of Pune.
[Contains English characters] The research activities of the center were made more meaningful and self reliant by organizing new areas of research, such as Cell repository, Electron microscopy, Rickettsioses, Hepatitis, Influenza and related viruses, Clinical virology, Biochemistry, Virus registry, and Biostatistics.
[Contains English characters] The research activities of the Institute are coordinated by a Scientific Advisory Committee consisting of eminent scientists.
[Contains English characters] By the 70s the Institute had developed deep scientific roots, nurtured through the sustained efforts of many dedicated workers.
[Contains English characters] With the expertise in virological training and research and emphasis on self-reliance, the centre was well prepared to undertake full responsibility as a National Institute.
[Contains English characters] On the recommendation of the SAC, the VRC acquired its status of national importance and was renamed as National Institute of Virology in 1978. Subsequently studies on Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, Rotavirus gastroenteritis, acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis, Rabies, Herpes sirnplex, Buffalo pox, Measles, and Poliomyelitis were also initiated A Microbial Containment Complex having P-3 biosafety levels for handling microorganisms of highly infectious nature is being established at Pashan, 11 km off the main laboratory at Pune.
[Contains English characters] This laboratory will provide National Containment facility for safe handling of highly hazardous pathogens.

[Contains English characters] इलामो द्राविडीयन भाषाकुटुंब The Elamo-Dravidian languages are a hypothesised language family which includes the living Dravidian languages of India, in addition to the extinct Elamite language of ancient Elam, in what is now southwestern Iran.
[Contains English characters] Linguist David McAlpin has been a chief proponent of the Elamo-Dravidian Hypothesis.
[Contains English characters] The Elamo-Dravidian hypothesis claims that the extinct Harappan language may be part of the same family.
[Contains English characters] McAlpin identified several similarities between Elamite and Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] According to McAlpin, 20% of Dravidian and Elamite vocabulary are cognates; a further 12% are probable cognates.
[Contains English characters] Elamite and Dravidian possess similar second-person pronouns and parallel case endings.
[Contains English characters] They have identical derivatives, abstract nouns, and the same verb stem+tense marker+personal ending structure.
[Contains English characters] Both have two positive tenses, a past and a non-past.
[Contains English characters] However modern linguists point out the probability of commonalities being found even between two disparate languages.
[Contains English characters] This understanding has led to specific criticisms of the Elamo-Dravidian Hypothesis.
[Contains English characters] Georgiy Starostin criticized McAlpins proposed morphological correspondences between Elamite and Dravidian as no closer than correspondences with other nearby language families.
[Contains English characters] Proto-Nostratic was already hypothesized to be an ancestor of Dravidian, and Václav Blažek had proposed that Elamite was related to Afroasiatic, so Starostin performed a lexicostatistical comparison using the Swadesh list between Elamite, Proto-Afroasiatic, Proto-Nostratic, and Proto-Sino-Caucasian.
[Contains English characters] He concluded that Elamite is related to Afroasiatic and Nostratic but not a member of either, with Sino-Caucasian being more distant from those three.
[Contains English characters] In addition, the Dravidian Brahui language of Baluchistan, which McAlpin supposed to be the link between Elamite and the Central Indian Dravidian languages , has been suggested by J. H. Elfenbein to be a late, c.
[Contains English characters] 1000 year old immigrant from Central India.
[Contains English characters] As such, it cannot reflect a remnant of a Dravidian language speaking Indus population.
[Contains English characters] Apart from the linguistic similarities, the Elamo-Dravidian Hypothesis rests on the claim that agriculture spread from the Near East to the Indus Valley region via Elam.
[Contains English characters] This would suggest that agriculturalists brought a new language as well as farming from Elam.
[Contains English characters] Supporting ethno-botanical data include the Near Eastern origin and name of wheat .
[Contains English characters] Later evidence of extensive trade between Elam and the Indus Valley Civilization suggests ongoing links between the two regions.
[Contains English characters] The disjunct distribution of living Dravidian languages, concentrated mostly in southern India but with isolated pockets in South Eastern Iran, Southern Afghanistan and Pakistan and in northeast India, suggests to some a wider past distribution of the Dravidian languages.
[Contains English characters] The Indo-European languages of modern India and Pakistan were later arrivals in the Indo-Gangetic plain, leaving isolated islands of the older Dravidian languages in the surrounding mountains.
[Contains English characters] These northern Dravidian languages however arrived in their present locations only around 1000 CE .
[Contains English characters] A variety of Dravidian loan words in Vedic Sanskrit suggests that the two languages existed for a time in proximity.
[Contains English characters] Retroflex consonants, which exist in Vedic Sanskrit and Dravidian but do not exist in Iranian or European languages could suggest a Dravidian substratum or adstratum in Vedic Sanskrit, which however could derive from other northwestern languages as well.
[Contains English characters] Proponents of the hypothesis claims similarities between the early हडप्पा लिपी, which has not been deciphered, and early Elamite script that, however, is hardly even recognized as such so far.
[Contains English characters] Some who claim to have deciphered the Harappan script, including Asko Parpola and Walter A.
[Contains English characters] Fairservis Jr.
[Contains English characters] , suggest that the Harappans spoke a Dravidian language, while others, for instance S. R. Rao, suggest that the Harappan script represents an Indo-European language, similar to Sanskrit.

[Contains English characters] Following the demise of Chola rule in the 13th century, the Thanjavur country came under the rule of the Pandyas who ruled for about a century .
[Contains English characters] Following the invasion of Malik Kafur, the Tanjore country fell into disorder.
[Contains English characters] The rule of the Delhi Sultanate lasted for half a century before Pandya chieftains reasserted their independence.
[Contains English characters] Soon afterwards, however, they were conquered by the Vijayanagar Empire.
[Contains English characters] The supremacy of Vijayanagar was challenged by the Nayaks of Madurai who eventually conquered Thanjavur in 1646. The rule of the Thanjavur Nayaks lasted until 1673 when Chokkanatha Nayak the ruler of Madurai invaded Thanjavur and killed the ruler Vijayaraghava.
[Contains English characters] Chokkanatha placed his brother Alagiri on the throne of Thanjavur, but within a year the latter threw off his allegiance, and Chokkanatha was forced to recognise the independence of Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] A son of Vijaya Raghava induced the Bijapur Sultan to help him get back the Thanjavur throne.
[Contains English characters] In 1675, the Sultan of Bijapur sent a force commanded by the Maratha general Venkoji to recapture the kingdom from the new invader.
[Contains English characters] Venkaji defeated Alagiri with ease, and occupied Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] He did not, however, place his protege on the throne as instructed by the Bijapur Sultan, but seized the kingdom and made himself king.
[Contains English characters] Thus began the rule of the Marathas over Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] साचा:TNhistory Venkoji, a half-brother of the great Maratha king Shivaji was the first Raja of Thanjavur from the Bhonsle dynasty.
[Contains English characters] It is believed that he took over the administration of Thanjavur in April 1674 and ruler till 1684. During his reign, his brother Shivaji invaded Gingee and Thanjavur in 1676-1677 and made his brother Santaji the ruler of all lands to the north of the Coleroon.
[Contains English characters] During the last years of his reign, Venkoji also allied with Chokkanatha of Madurai to repulse an invasion from Mysore.
[Contains English characters] Shahuji I was the eldest son of Venkoji and he ascended the throne at the age of twelve.
[Contains English characters] During his reign, the Mughals occupied the Coromandel coast and Tiruchirapalli and forced Shahuji I to pay tribute.
[Contains English characters] Shahuji was a patron of literature.
[Contains English characters] During his reign, there were frequent skirmishes and battles with the Raja of Madurai and Ramnad for control of the border lands.
[Contains English characters] Serfoji I was a younger son of Venkoji and he ruled from 1712 to 1728. His rule was marked by regular warfare and disputes with the Madurai Nayak.
[Contains English characters] Tukkoji, a younger brother of Serfoji I ruled Thanjavur from 1728 to 1736. His reign witnessed the invasion of Chanda Sahib and he is credited with having repulsed a Muhammedan invasion of Madurai.
[Contains English characters] A period of anarchy followed the death of Tukkoji and came to an end when Pratapsingh succeeded to the throne in 1739. He ruled up to 1763. He allied with Muhammad Ali, the Nawab of the Carnatic and aided the British against the French in the Carnatic Wars and the Seven Years War.
[Contains English characters] He was the last king to be addressed to be the Directors of the British East India Company as His Majesty.
[Contains English characters] In 1762, a tripartite treaty was signed between Thanjavur, Carnatic and the British by which he became a vassal of the Nawab of the Carnatic.
[Contains English characters] Thuljaji was a very weak ruler and the last independent ruler of Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] In 1773, Thanjavur was annexed by the Nawab of the Carnatic who ruled till 1786. The throne was restored to him by the Directors of the British East India Company.
[Contains English characters] But his restoration came at a heavy price as it deprived him of his independence.
[Contains English characters] Thuljaji was succeeded by his teenage son Serfoji in 1787. Soon afterwards, he was deposed by his uncle and regent Amarsingh who seized the throne for himself.
[Contains English characters] With the help of the British, Serfoji II recovered the throne in 1798. A subsequent treaty forced him to hand over the reins of the kingdom to the British East India Company.
[Contains English characters] Serfoji II was however left in control of the Fort and the surrounding areas.
[Contains English characters] He reigned till 1832. His reign is noted for the literary, scientific and technological accomplishments of the Tanjore country.
[Contains English characters] Shivaji was the last Maratha ruler of Thanjavur and reigned from 1832 to 1855. He was a weak and feeble prince with barely any authority.
[Contains English characters] As he died childless in 1855, Thanjavur was annexed by the British as per the provisions of the Doctrine of Lapse.
[Contains English characters] The Thanjavur Maratha Rajas favored Sanskrit and Telugu to such an extent that classical Tamil began to decline.
[Contains English characters] Most of the plays were in Sanskrit.
[Contains English characters] Venkoji, the first ruler of the Bhonsle dynasty composed a Dvipada Ramayana in Telugu.
[Contains English characters] His son Shahuji was a great patron of learning and of literature.
[Contains English characters] Most of the Thanjavur Maratha literature is from his period.
[Contains English characters] Most of them were versions of the Ramayana or plays and short stories of a historical nature.
[Contains English characters] Sanskrit and Telugu were the languages used in most of these plays while there were some Tamil koothu as well.
[Contains English characters] Advaita Kirtana is one of the prominent works from this period.
[Contains English characters] Later Thanjavur rulers like Serfoji II and Shivaji immersed themselves in learning and literary pursuits when they were dispossessed of their empire.
[Contains English characters] Serfoji built the Saraswathi Mahal Library within the precints of the palace to house his enormous book and manuscript collection.
[Contains English characters] Apart from Indian languages, Serfoji II was proficient in English, French, Dutch, Greek and Latin as well.
[Contains English characters] The king was assisted in the administration of his country by a council of ministers.
[Contains English characters] The supreme head of this council of ministers was a Mantri or Dalavoy.
[Contains English characters] The Dalavoy was also the Commander-in-chief of the Army.
[Contains English characters] Next in importance at the court was a Pradhani or Dewan also called Dabir Pandit.
[Contains English characters] The country was divided into subahs, seemais and maganams in the decreasing order of size and importance.
[Contains English characters] The five subahs of the country were पट्टुकोट्टै, मायावरम, कुंभकोणम, मन्नारगुडी and तिरूवडी.
[Contains English characters] The ruler collected his taxes from the people through his mirasdars or puttackdars.
[Contains English characters] They were collected right from the village level onwards and were based on the agricultural produce of the village.
[Contains English characters] Rice was one of the primary crops in the region and the land used for cultivation was owned by big landlords.
[Contains English characters] It was Anatharama Sashtry who proposed collecting taxes to improve conditions for the poor.
[Contains English characters] No foreign trade was carried out.
[Contains English characters] The only foreign trade in the country was carried out by European traders who paid a particular amount of money as rent to the Raja.
[Contains English characters] The currency system used was that of a chakram or pon .
[Contains English characters] Other systems of coinage used were that of pagoda, a big panam and a small panam.

[Contains English characters] साचा:WiktionaryparIn computer science, a cache सय is a collection of data duplicating original values stored elsewhere or computed earlier, where the original data is expensive to fetch or to compute, compared to the cost of reading the cache.
[Contains English characters] In other words, a cache is a temporary storage area where frequently accessed data can be stored for rapid access.
[Contains English characters] Once the data is stored in the cache, it can be used in the future by accessing the cached copy rather than re-fetching or recomputing the original data.
[Contains English characters] A cache has proven to be extremely effective in many areas of computing because access patterns in typical computer applications have locality of reference.
[Contains English characters] There are several kinds of locality, but this article primarily deals with data that are accessed close together in time .
[Contains English characters] The data might or might not be located physically close to each other .
[Contains English characters] Use of the word cache in the computer context originated in 1967 during preparation of an article for publication in the IBM Systems Journal.
[Contains English characters] The paper concerned an exciting memory improvement in Model 85, a latecomer in the IBM System/360 product line.
[Contains English characters] The Journal editor, Lyle R.
[Contains English characters] Johnson, pleaded for a more descriptive term than high-speed buffer.
[Contains English characters] When none was forthcoming, he suggested the noun cache, meaning a safekeeping or storage place .
[Contains English characters] The paper was published in early 1968, the authors were honoured by आय. बी. एम. , their work was widely welcomed and subsequently improved upon, and cache soon became standard usage in computer literature.
[Contains English characters] A cache is a block of memory for temporary storage of data likely to be used again.
[Contains English characters] CPUs and hard drives frequently use a cache, as do web browsers and web servers.
[Contains English characters] A cache is made up of a pool of entries.
[Contains English characters] Each entry has a datum which is a copy of the datum in some backing store.
[Contains English characters] Each entry also has a tag, which specifies the identity of the datum in the backing store of which the entry is a copy.
[Contains English characters] When the cache client wishes to access a datum presumably in the backing store, it first checks the cache.
[Contains English characters] If an entry can be found with a tag matching that of the desired datum, the datum in the entry is used instead.
[Contains English characters] This situation is known as a cache hit.
[Contains English characters] So, for example, a web browser program might check its local cache on disk to see if it has a local copy of the contents of a web page at a particular URL.
[Contains English characters] In this example, the URL is the tag, and the contents of the web page is the datum.
[Contains English characters] The percentage of accesses that result in cache hits is known as the hit rate or hit ratio of the cache.
[Contains English characters] The alternative situation, when the cache is consulted and found not to contain a datum with the desired tag, is known as a cache miss.
[Contains English characters] The previously uncached datum fetched from the backing store during miss handling is usually copied into the cache, ready for the next access.
[Contains English characters] During a cache miss, the CPU usually ejects some other entry in order to make room for the previously uncached datum.
[Contains English characters] The heuristic used to select the entry to eject is known as the replacement policy.
[Contains English characters] One popular replacement policy, least recently used, replaces the least recently used entry .
[Contains English characters] More efficient caches compute use frequency against the size of the stored contents, as well as the latencies and throughputs for both the cache and the backing store.
[Contains English characters] While this works well for larger amounts of data, long latencies and slow throughputs, such as experienced with a hard drive and the Internet, it is not efficient for use with a CPU cache.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Fact When a datum is written to the cache, it must at some point be written to the backing store as well.
[Contains English characters] The timing of this write is controlled by what is known as the write policy.
[Contains English characters] In a write-through cache, every write to the cache causes a synchronous write to the backing store.
[Contains English characters] Alternatively, in a write-back cache, writes are not immediately mirrored to the store.
[Contains English characters] Instead, the cache tracks which of its locations have been written over .
[Contains English characters] The data in these locations is written back to the backing store when those data are evicted from the cache, an effect referred to as a lazy write.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, a read miss in a write-back cache will often require two memory accesses to service: one to retrieve the needed datum, and one to write replaced data from the cache to the store.
[Contains English characters] Data write-back may be triggered by other policies as well.
[Contains English characters] The client may make many changes to a datum in the cache, and then explicitly notify the cache to write back the datum.
[Contains English characters] No-write allocation is a cache policy where only processor reads are cached, thus avoiding the need for write-back or write-through when the old value of the datum was absent from the cache prior to the write.
[Contains English characters] The data in the backing store may be changed by entities other than the cache, in which case the copy in the cache may become out-of-date or stale.
[Contains English characters] Alternatively, when the client updates the data in the cache, copies of that data in other caches will become stale.
[Contains English characters] Communication protocols between the cache managers which keep the data consistent are known as coherency protocols.
[Contains English characters] Small memories on or close to the CPU can be made faster than the much larger main memory.
[Contains English characters] Most CPUs since the 1980s have used one or more caches, and modern high-end embedded, desktop and server microprocessors may have as many as half a dozen, each specialized for a specific function.
[Contains English characters] While CPU caches are generally managed entirely by hardware, other caches are managed by a variety of software.
[Contains English characters] The page cache in main memory, which is an example of disk cache, is usually managed by the operating system kernel.
[Contains English characters] While the hard drives hardware disk buffer is sometimes misleadingly referred to as disk cache, its main functions are write sequencing and read prefetching.
[Contains English characters] Repeated cache hits are relatively rare, due to the small size of the buffer in comparison to HDDs capacity.
[Contains English characters] In turn, fast local hard disk can be used to cache information held on even slower data storage devices, such as remote servers or local tape drives or optical jukeboxes.
[Contains English characters] Such a scheme is the main concept of hierarchical storage management.
[Contains English characters] Web caches are employed by web browsers and web proxy servers to store previous responses from web servers, such as web pages.
[Contains English characters] Web caches reduce the amount of information that needs to be transmitted across the network, as information previously stored in the cache can often be re-used.
[Contains English characters] This reduces bandwidth and processing requirements of the web server, and helps to improve responsiveness for users of the web.
[Contains English characters] Modern web browsers employ a built-in web cache, but some internet service providers or organizations also use a caching proxy server, which is a web cache that is shared between all users of that network.
[Contains English characters] Another form of cache is P2P caching, where the files most sought for by peer-to-peer applications are stored in an ISP cache to accelerate P2P transfers.
[Contains English characters] The BIND DNS daemon caches a mapping of domain names to IP addresses, as does a resolver library.
[Contains English characters] Write-through operation is common when operating over unreliable networks, because of the enormous complexity of the coherency protocol required between multiple write-back caches when communication is unreliable.
[Contains English characters] For instance, web page caches and client-side network file system caches are typically read-only or write-through specifically to keep the network protocol simple and reliable.
[Contains English characters] Search engines also frequently make web pages they have indexed available from their cache.
[Contains English characters] For example, Google provides a Cached link next to each search result.
[Contains English characters] This is useful when web pages are temporarily inaccessible from a web server.
[Contains English characters] Another type of caching is storing computed results that will likely be needed again, or memoization.
[Contains English characters] An example of this type of caching is ccache, a program that caches the output of the compilation to speed up the second-time compilation.
[Contains English characters] Database caching can substantially improve the throughput of database applications, for example in the processing of indexes, data dictionaries, and frequently used subsets of data.
[Contains English characters] The terms are not mutually exclusive and the functions are frequently combined; however, there is a difference in intent.
[Contains English characters] A buffer is a temporary memory location, that is traditionally used because CPU instructions cannot directly address data stored in peripheral devices.
[Contains English characters] Thus, addressable memory is used as intermediate stage.
[Contains English characters] Additionally such a buffer may be feasible when a large block of data is assembled or disassembled, or when data may be delivered in a different order than that in which it is produced.
[Contains English characters] Also a whole buffer of data is usually transferred sequentially, so buffering itself sometimes increases transfer performance.
[Contains English characters] These benefits are present even if the buffered data are written to the buffer once and read from the buffer once.
[Contains English characters] A cache also increases transfer performance.
[Contains English characters] A part of the increase similarly comes from the possibility that multiple small transfers will combine into one large block.
[Contains English characters] But the main performance gain occurs because there is a good chance that the same datum will be read from cache multiple times, or that written data will soon be read.
[Contains English characters] A caches sole purpose is to reduce accesses to the underlying slower storage.
[Contains English characters] Cache is also usually an abstraction layer that is designed to be invisible from the perspective of neighbouring layers.

[Contains English characters] These elevators are designed for much greater capacity than other elevators, up to 200,000 pounds of aircraft and equipment.
[Contains English characters] Smaller elevators lift munitions to the flight deck from magazines deep inside the ship.
[Contains English characters] On some passenger double-deck aircraft such as the Boeing 747, Lockheed L-1011 or other widebody aircraft, lifts transport flight attendants and food and beverage trolleys from lower deck galleys to upper passenger carrying decks.
[Contains English characters] The residential elevator is often permitted to be of lower cost and complexity than full commercial elevators.
[Contains English characters] They may have unique design characteristics suited for home furnishings, such as hinged wooden shaft-access doors rather than the typical metal sliding doors of commercial elevators.
[Contains English characters] Construction may be less robust than in commercial designs with shorter maintenance periods, but safety systems such as locks on shaft access doors, fall arrestors, and emergency phones must still be present in the event of malfunction.
[Contains English characters] The limited-use, limited-application elevator is a special purpose passenger elevator used infrequently, and which is exempt from many commercial regulations and accommodations.
[Contains English characters] For example, a LU/LA potentially may not necessarily be handicapped accessible, and there might only be room for a single standing passenger.
[Contains English characters] A special type of elevator is the paternoster, a constantly moving chain of boxes.
[Contains English characters] A similar concept, the humanlift, moves only a small platform, which the rider mounts while using a handhold and was once seen in multi-story industrial plants.
[Contains English characters] A different kind of elevator is used to transport material.
[Contains English characters] It generally consists of an inclined plane on which a conveyor belt runs.
[Contains English characters] The conveyor often includes partitions to prevent the material from sliding backwards.
[Contains English characters] These elevators are often used in industrial and agricultural applications.
[Contains English characters] When such mechanisms are used to elevate grain for storage in large vertical silos, the entire structure is called a grain elevator.
[Contains English characters] There have occasionally been lift belts for humans; these typically have steps about every seven feet along the length of the belt, which moves vertically, so that the passenger can stand on one step and hold on to the one above.
[Contains English characters] These belts are sometimes used, for example, to carry the employees of parking garages, but are considered too dangerous for public use.
[Contains English characters] There are at least four means of moving an elevator: Geared traction machines are driven by AC or DC electric motors.
[Contains English characters] Geared machines use worm gears to control mechanical movement of elevator cars by rolling steel hoist ropes over a drive sheave which is attached to a gearbox driven by a high speed motor.
[Contains English characters] These machines are generally the best option for basement or overhead traction use for speeds up to 500 ft/min .
[Contains English characters] Gearless traction machines are low speed, high torque electric motors powered either by AC or DC.
[Contains English characters] In this case, the drive sheave is directly attached to the end of the motor.
[Contains English characters] Gearless traction elevators can reach speeds of up to 2,000 ft/min, or even higher.
[Contains English characters] A brake is mounted between the motor and drive sheave to hold the elevator stationary at a floor.
[Contains English characters] This brake is usually an external drum type and is actuated by spring force and held open electrically; a power failure will cause the brake to engage and prevent the elevator from falling .
[Contains English characters] In each case, cables are attached to a hitch plate on top of the cab or may be underslung below a cab, and then looped over the drive sheave to a counterweight attached to the opposite end of the cables which reduces the amount of power needed to move the cab.
[Contains English characters] The counterweight is located in the hoist-way and rides a separate rail system; as the car goes up, the counterweight goes down, and vice versa.
[Contains English characters] This action is powered by the traction machine which is directed by the controller, typically a relay logic or computerized device that directs starting, acceleration, deceleration and stopping of the elevator cab.
[Contains English characters] The weight of the counterweight is typically equal to the weight of the elevator cab plus 40-50% of the capacity of the elevator.
[Contains English characters] The grooves in the drive sheave are specially designed to prevent the cables from slipping.
[Contains English characters] Traction is provided to the ropes by the grip of the grooves in the sheave, thereby the name.
[Contains English characters] As the ropes age and the traction grooves wear, some traction is lost and the ropes must be replaced and the sheave repaired or replaced.
[Contains English characters] Elevators with more than 100 of travel have a system called compensation.
[Contains English characters] This is a separate set of cables or a chain attached to the bottom of the counterweight and the bottom of the elevator cab.
[Contains English characters] This makes it easier to control the elevator, as it compensates for the differing weight of cable between the hoist and the cab.
[Contains English characters] If the elevator cab is at the top of the hoist-way, there is a short length of hoist cable above the car and a long length of compensating cable below the car and vice versa for the counterweight.
[Contains English characters] If the compensation system uses cables, there will be an additional sheave in the pit below the elevator, to guide the cables.
[Contains English characters] If the compensation system uses chains, the chain is guided by a bar mounted between the counterweight rails.
[Contains English characters] A climbing elevator is a self-ascending elevator with its own propulsion.
[Contains English characters] The propulsion can be done by an electric or a combustion engine.
[Contains English characters] Climbing elevators are used in guyed masts or towers, in order to make easy access to parts of these constructions, such as flight safety lamps for maintenance.
[Contains English characters] An example would be the Moonlight towers in Austin, Texas, where the elevator holds only one person and equipment for maintenance.
[Contains English characters] Elevator air conditioning is fast becoming a popular concept around the world.
[Contains English characters] The primary reason for installing an elevator air conditioner is the comfort that it provides while travelling in the elevator.
[Contains English characters] It stabilizes the condition of the air inside the lift car.
[Contains English characters] Some elevator air conditioners can be used in countries with cold climates if a thermostat is used to reverse the refrigeration cycle to warm the lift car.
[Contains English characters] One of the many benefits of installing an elevator air conditioner is the clean air that it provides.
[Contains English characters] Air is sucked from the elevator’s hoist way straight into the car using a motorised fan.
[Contains English characters] The air sucked into the hoist way may be filled with dust mites, germs and bacteria.
[Contains English characters] With an elevator air conditioner, air provided is much cleaner because the cold air is the same air that comes from the car itself.
[Contains English characters] Not only that, the cold air that is produced from the air conditioner also goes through a layer of filter.
[Contains English characters] This filtration removes particles that are harmful to the human body.
[Contains English characters] A poorly maintained air-conditioning system may promote the growth and spread of microorganisms, but as long as the air conditioner is kept clean these health hazards can be avoided.
[Contains English characters] Elevator lobby air conditioning constantly leaks into the elevator shaft due to elevator movements and elevator shaft ventilation requirements, resulting in wasted energy.
[Contains English characters] By using elevator air conditioners, less energy is used because the air conditioner is able to cool the inside of the elevator more effectively.
[Contains English characters] Heat generated from the cooling process is rejected into the hoistway.
[Contains English characters] The elevator cab is not air-tight, and some of this heat will reenter the car and reduce the overall cooling effect, which may be less than ideal.
[Contains English characters] Air conditioning poses a problem to elevators because of the condensation that occurs.
[Contains English characters] The condensed water produced has to be disposed of; otherwise, it would create flooding in the elevator car and hoistway.
[Contains English characters] There are at least four ways to remove condensed water from the air conditioner.
[Contains English characters] However, each solution has its pros and cons.
[Contains English characters] Atomizing, also known as misting the condensed water, is another way to dispose of the condensed water.
[Contains English characters] Spraying ultra fine water droplets on to the hot coils of the air conditioner would ensure the condensed water evaporates quickly.
[Contains English characters] Though this is one of the best methods to dispose of the condensed water, it is also one of the costliest because the nozzle that atomizes the water easily gets choked.
[Contains English characters] The majority of the cost goes to maintaining the entire atomizing system.
[Contains English characters] Disposing of condensed water works by firstly collecting the condensed water and then heating it to above boiling point.
[Contains English characters] The condensed water would eventually be evaporated thereby disposing it.
[Contains English characters] Consumers are reluctant to employ this system because of the high rate of energy used just to dispose of this water.
[Contains English characters] The cascading method works by flowing the condensed water directly onto the hot coils of the air conditioner.
[Contains English characters] This would eventually evaporate the condensed water.
[Contains English characters] The downside of this technology is that the coils have to be at extremely high temperature for the condensed water to be evaporated.
[Contains English characters] There is a chance that the water might not evaporate entirely and that would cause water to overflow on to the exterior of the car.
[Contains English characters] Drainage system works by creating a sump to collect the condensed water and using a pump to dispose it off through using a drainage system.
[Contains English characters] It is an efficient method, but it comes at a heavy price because the cost of building the sump, and maintaining the pump to make sure it operates, is very expensive.
[Contains English characters] Moreover, the pipes used for drainage would look ugly on the exterior.
[Contains English characters] This system also cannot be implemented on a built project.

[Contains English characters] If the particular elevator is currently serving traffic in a certain direction, it will only answer hall calls in the same direction unless there are no more calls beyond that floor.
[Contains English characters] In a group of two or more elevators, the call buttons may be linked to a central dispatch computer, such that they illuminate and cancel together.
[Contains English characters] This is done to ensure that only one car is called at one time.
