[Contains English characters] Some skyscraper buildings feature a destination operating panel where a passenger would register their floor calls before entering the car.
[Contains English characters] The system would let them know which car to wait for, instead of everyone boarding the next car.
[Contains English characters] In this way, travel time is reduced as the elevator makes fewer stops for individual passengers, and the computer distributes adjacent stops to different cars in the bank.
[Contains English characters] It can also improve accessibility, as a mobility-impaired passenger can move to his or her designated car in advance.
[Contains English characters] Inside the elevator there is no call button to push, or the buttons are there but they cannot be pushed – they only indicate stopping floors.
[Contains English characters] The system was first pioneered by Schindler Elevator as the Miconic 10. Manufacturers of such systems claim that average traveling time can be reduced by up to 30%.
[Contains English characters] There are some problems with the system, though, and it is subject to gaming.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, one person enters the destination for a large group of people going to the same floor.
[Contains English characters] The dispatching algorithm is usually unable to completely cater for the variation, and late comers may find the elevator they are assigned to is already full.
[Contains English characters] Also, occasionally, one person may press the floor multiple times.
[Contains English characters] This is common with up/down buttons when people believe this to be an effective way to hurry elevators.
[Contains English characters] However, this will make the computer think multiple people are waiting and will allocate empty cars to serve this one person.
[Contains English characters] The same destination scheduling concept can also be applied to public transit such as in group rapid transit.
[Contains English characters] Anti-Crime Protection will force each car to stop at a pre-defined landing and open its doors.
[Contains English characters] This allows a security guard or a receptionist at the landing to visually inspect the passengers.
[Contains English characters] The car stops at this landing as it passes to serve further demand.
[Contains English characters] During Up Peak mode, elevator cars in a group are recalled to the lobby to provide expeditious service to passengers arriving at the building, most typically in the morning as people arrive for work or at the conclusion of a lunch-time period.
[Contains English characters] Elevators are dispatched one-by-one when they reach a pre-determined passenger load, or when they have had their doors opened for a certain period of time.
[Contains English characters] The next elevator to be dispatched usually has its hall lantern or a this car leaving next sign illuminated to encourage passengers to make maximum use of the available elevator system capacity.
[Contains English characters] The commencement of Up Peak may be triggered by a time clock, by the departure of a certain number of fully loaded cars leaving the lobby within a given time period, or by a switch manually operated by a building attendant.
[Contains English characters] During Down Peak mode, elevator cars in a group are sent away from the lobby towards the highest floor served, after which they commence running down the floors in response to hall calls placed by passengers wishing to leave the building.
[Contains English characters] This allows the elevator system to provide maximum passenger handling capacity for people leaving the building.
[Contains English characters] The commencement of Down Peak may be triggered by a time clock, by the arrival of a certain number of fully loaded cars at the lobby within a given time period, or by a switch manually operated by a building attendant.
[Contains English characters] In areas with large populations of observant Jews or in facilities catering to Jews, one may find a Sabbath elevator.
[Contains English characters] In this mode, an elevator will stop automatically at every floor, allowing people to step on and off without having to press any buttons.
[Contains English characters] This prevents violation of the Sabbath prohibition against operating electrical devices when Sabbath is in effect for those who observe this ritual.
[Contains English characters] However, Sabbath mode has the side effect of wasting considerable amounts of energy, needlessly running the elevator car sequentially up and down every floor of a building, repeatedly servicing floors where it is not needed.
[Contains English characters] For a tall building with many floors, the car must move on a frequent enough basis so as to not cause undue delay for potential users that will not touch the controls as it opens the doors on every floor up the building.
[Contains English characters] Independent service is a special service mode found on most elevators.
[Contains English characters] It is activated by a key switch either inside the elevator itself or on a centralized control panel in the lobby.
[Contains English characters] When an elevator is placed on independent service, it will no longer respond to hall calls. . The elevator will remain parked on a floor with its doors open until a floor is selected and the door close button is held until the elevator starts to travel.
[Contains English characters] Independent service is useful when transporting large goods or moving groups of people between certain floors.
[Contains English characters] Inspection service is designed to provide access to the hoistway and car top for inspection and maintenance purposes by qualified elevator mechanics.
[Contains English characters] It is first activated by a key switch on the car operating panel usually labelled Inspection, Car Top, Access Enable or HWENAB.
[Contains English characters] When this switch is activated the elevator will come to a stop if moving, car calls will be cancelled, and hall calls will be assigned to other elevator cars in the group .
[Contains English characters] The elevator can now only be moved by the corresponding Access key switches, usually located at the top-most and bottom-most landings.
[Contains English characters] The access key switches will bypass the door lock circuit for the floor it is located on and allow the car to move at reduced inspection speed with the hoistway door open.
[Contains English characters] This speed can range from anywhere up to 60% of normal operating speed on most controllers, and is usually defined by local safety codes.
[Contains English characters] Elevators have a car top inspection station that allows the car to be operated by a mechanic in order to move it through the hoistway.
[Contains English characters] Generally, there are three buttons - UP, RUN, and DOWN.
[Contains English characters] Both the RUN and a direction button must be held to move the car in that direction, and the elevator will stop moving as soon as the buttons are released.
[Contains English characters] The inspection panel also has standard power outlets for work lamps and powered tools.
[Contains English characters] Depending on the location of the elevator, fire service code will vary state to state and country to country.
[Contains English characters] Fire service is usually split up into two modes: Phase One and Phase Two.
[Contains English characters] These are separate modes that the elevator can go into.
[Contains English characters] Phase one mode is activated by a corresponding smoke sensor or heat sensor in the building.
[Contains English characters] Once an alarm has been activated, the elevator will automatically go into phase one.
[Contains English characters] The elevator will wait an amount of time, then proceed to go into nudging mode to tell everyone the elevator is leaving the floor.
[Contains English characters] Once the elevator has left the floor, depending on where the alarm was set off, the elevator will go to the Fire Recall Floor.
[Contains English characters] However, if the alarm was activated on the fire recall floor the elevator will have an alternate floor to recall to.
[Contains English characters] When the elevator is recalled, it proceeds to the recall floor and stops with its doors open.
[Contains English characters] The elevator will no longer respond to calls or move in any direction.
[Contains English characters] Located on the fire recall floor is a fire service key switch.
[Contains English characters] The fire service key switch has the ability to turn fire service off, turn fire service on or to bypass fire service.
[Contains English characters] The only way to return the elevator to normal service is to switch it to bypass after the alarms have reset.
[Contains English characters] Phase two mode can only be activated by a key switch located inside the elevator on the centralized control panel.
[Contains English characters] This mode was created for firefighters so that they may rescue people from a burning building.
[Contains English characters] The phase two key switch located on the COP has three positions: off, on, and hold.
[Contains English characters] By turning phase two on, the firefighter enables the car to move.
[Contains English characters] However, like independent service mode, the car will not respond to a car call unless the firefighter manually pushes and holds the door close button.
[Contains English characters] Once the elevator gets to the desired floor it will not open its doors unless the firefighter holds the door open button.
[Contains English characters] This is in case the floor is burning and the firefighter can feel the heat and knows not to open the door.
[Contains English characters] The firefighter must hold door open until the door is completely opened.
[Contains English characters] If for any reason the firefighter wishes to leave the elevator, they will use the hold position on the key switch to make sure the elevator remains at that floor.
[Contains English characters] If the firefighter wishes to return to the recall floor, they simply turn the key off and close the doors.
[Contains English characters] Commonly found in hospitals, Code Blue service allows an elevator to be summoned to any floor for use in an emergency situation.
[Contains English characters] Each floor will have a Code Blue recall key switch, and when activated, the elevator system will immediately select the elevator car that can respond the fastest, regardless of direction of travel and passenger load.
[Contains English characters] Passengers inside the elevator will be notified with an alarm and indicator light to exit the elevator when the doors open.
[Contains English characters] Once the elevator arrives at the floor, it will park with its doors open and the car buttons will be disabled to prevent a passenger from taking control of the elevator.
[Contains English characters] Medical personnel must then activate the Code Blue key switch inside the car, select their floor and close the doors with the door close button.
[Contains English characters] The elevator will then travel non-stop to the selected floor, and will remain in Code Blue service until switched off in the car.
[Contains English characters] Some hospital elevators will feature a hold position on the Code Blue key switch which allows the elevator to remain at a floor locked out of service until Code Blue is deactivated.
[Contains English characters] Many elevator installations now feature emergency power systems which allow elevator use in blackout situations and prevent people from becoming trapped in elevators.
[Contains English characters] When power is lost in a traction elevator system, all elevators will initially come to a halt.
[Contains English characters] One by one, each car in the group will return to the lobby floor, open its doors and shut down.
[Contains English characters] People in the remaining elevators may see an indicator light or hear a voice announcement informing them that the elevator will return to the lobby shortly.
[Contains English characters] Once all cars have successfully returned, the system will then automatically select one or more cars to be used for normal operations and these cars will return to service.
[Contains English characters] The car selected to run under emergency power can be manually overridden by a key or strip switch in the lobby.
[Contains English characters] In order to help prevent entrapment, when the system detects that it is running low on power, it will bring the running cars to the lobby or nearest floor, open the doors and shut down.
[Contains English characters] In hydraulic elevator systems, emergency power will lower the elevators to the lowest landing and open the doors to allow passengers to exit.
[Contains English characters] The doors then close after an adjustable time period and the car remains unusable until reset, usually by cycling the elevator main power switch.
[Contains English characters] Typically, due to the high current draw when starting the pump motor, hydraulic elevators arent run using standard emergency power systems.
[Contains English characters] Buildings like hospitals and nursing homes usually size their emergency generators to accommodate this draw.
[Contains English characters] However, the increasing use of current limiting motor starters, commonly known as Soft-Start contactors, avoid much of this problem and the current draw of the pump motor is less of a limiting concern.
[Contains English characters] Elevators may feature talking devices as an accessibility aid for the blind.
[Contains English characters] In addition to floor arrival notifications, the computer announces the direction of travel, and notifies the passengers before the doors are to close.
[Contains English characters] In addition to the call buttons, elevators usually have floor indicators and direction lanterns.
[Contains English characters] The former are almost universal in cab interiors with more than two stops and may be found outside the elevators as well on one or more of the floors.
[Contains English characters] Floor indicators can consist of a dial with a rotating needle, but the most common types are those with successively illuminated floor indications or LCDs.
[Contains English characters] Likewise, a change of floors or an arrival at a floor is indicated by a sound, depending on the elevator.
[Contains English characters] Direction lanterns are also found both inside and outside elevator cars, but they should always be visible from outside because their primary purpose is to help people decide whether or not to get on the elevator.
[Contains English characters] If somebody waiting for the elevator wants to go up, but a car comes first that indicates that it is going down, then the person may decide not to get on the elevator.
[Contains English characters] If the person waits, then one will still stop going up.
[Contains English characters] Direction indicators are sometimes etched with arrows or shaped like arrows and/or use the convention that one that lights up red means down and green means up.
[Contains English characters] Since the color convention is often undermined or overrided by systems that do not invoke it, it is usually used only in conjunction with other differentiating factors.
[Contains English characters] An example of a place whose elevators use only the color convention to differentiate between directions is the Museum of Contemporary Art in Chicago, where a single circle can be made to light up green for up and red for down.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes directions must be inferred by the position of the indicators relative to one another.
[Contains English characters] In addition to lanterns, most elevators have a chime to indicate if the elevator is going up or down either before or after the doors open, usually in conjunction with the lanterns lighting up.
[Contains English characters] Universally, one chime is for up, two is for down, and none indicates an elevator that is free.
[Contains English characters] Observatory service elevators often convey other facts of interest, including elevator speed, stopwatch, and current position, as with the case for Taipei 101s service elevators.
[Contains English characters] The mechanical and electrical design of elevators is dictated according to various standards, which may be international, national, state, regional or city based.
[Contains English characters] Whereas once many standards were prescriptive, specifying exact criteria which must be complied with, there has recently been a shift towards more performance-based standards where the onus falls on the designer to ensure that the elevator meets or exceeds the standard.
[Contains English characters] Some of the national elevator standards include: Because an elevator is part of a building, it must also comply with standards relating to earthquake resilience, fire standards, electrical wiring rules and so forth.
[Contains English characters] The American National Elevator Standards Group sets an elevator weight standard to be 2200 lbs.
[Contains English characters] Additional requirements relating to access by disabled persons, may be mandated by laws or regulations such as the Americans with Disabilities Act.
[Contains English characters] In most US and Canadian jurisdictions, passenger elevators are required to conform to the American Society of Mechanical Engineers Standard A17.1, Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators.
[Contains English characters] In Canada the document is the CAN/CSA B44 Safety Standard, which was harmonized with the US version in the 2000 edition.
[Contains English characters] In addition, passenger elevators may be required to conform to the requirements of A17.3 for existing elevators where referenced by the local jurisdiction.
[Contains English characters] Passenger elevators are tested using the ASME A17.2 Standard.
[Contains English characters] The frequency of these tests is mandated by the local jurisdiction, which may be a town, city, state or provincial standard.
[Contains English characters] Passenger elevators must also conform to many ancillary building codes including the Local or State building code, National Fire Protection Association standards for Electrical, Fire Sprinklers and Fire Alarms, Plumbing codes, and HVAC codes.
[Contains English characters] Also, passenger elevators are required to conform to the Americans with Disabilities Act and other State and Federal civil rights legislation regarding accessibility.
[Contains English characters] Residential elevators are required to conform to ASME A17.1. Platform and Wheelchair lifts are required to comply with ASME A18.1 in most US jurisdictions.
[Contains English characters] Most elevators have a location in which the permit for the building owner to operate the elevator is displayed.
[Contains English characters] While some jurisdictions require the permit to be displayed in the elevator cab, other jurisdictions allow for the operating permit to be kept on file elsewhere – such as the maintenance office – and to be made available for inspection on demand.
[Contains English characters] In such cases instead of the permit being displayed in the elevator cab, often a notice is posted in its place informing riders of where the actual permits are kept.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Unreferenced नेम्मारा वेला किंवा नेम्मारा-वल्लंगी वेला हा केरळ राज्याच्या पलक्कड जिल्ह्यातील नेम्मारा गावातील वार्षिक उत्सव आहे.
[Contains English characters] The Vela is a festival celebrated in the villages of the Palakkad and Thrissur districts in summer, after the harvest.
[Contains English characters] The prominent crop in this area is rice.
[Contains English characters] After the harvest, the fields are empty and dry, and this is the time for the Vela.
[Contains English characters] The Nemmara Vela is celebrated on a grand scale, equalling the famous Trissur Pooram.
[Contains English characters] The festival is believed to be the birthday of the presiding deity of the village temple or the memory of a major event like the killing of a demon by the goddess.
[Contains English characters] The Vela falls on the 20th day of Meenam, the month in the Malayalam era .
[Contains English characters] Two competing groups, Nemmara and Vallangi, have their own temples plus a common temple, the Nellikkulangara, where the two groups can mingle.
[Contains English characters] The festivities start ten days earlier than the actual day of Vela, with the hoisting of a flag, in the respective temples.
[Contains English characters] Natives are not supposed to leave the village once the flags have been raised.
[Contains English characters] The Nemmara group starts its Vela from the Mandam or Vela Mandam and the Vallangi from the Siva temple.
[Contains English characters] There are 11 to 15 elephants for each of the two groups.
[Contains English characters] These elephants are decorated and to the accompaniment of percussion instruments, are paraded through the main thoroughfares of the town.
[Contains English characters] In the evening, these groups reach the Nellikulangara temple.
[Contains English characters] There is an area of empty fields here, enough to accommodate a large crowd.
[Contains English characters] The festival attracts a lot of people not only from nearby, but also from the neighbouring districts of Trissur, Malappuram and from Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The Vela is also an occasion for family reunions.
[Contains English characters] People of the villages settled elsewhere, make it a point to attend the festival.
[Contains English characters] People celebrate this event as a whole without any discrimination of caste/religion.
[Contains English characters] Some foreign tourists are also usually seen.
[Contains English characters] Many TV channels broadcast the festival live.
[Contains English characters] Another attraction of the festival is the Aana Pandal which is an arch-like structure, where the caparisoned elephants remain for some time.
[Contains English characters] The Pandal, fully decorated with coloured electric lamps, give out different light patterns when switched on.
[Contains English characters] Both groups keep the design of the illuminations a secret.
[Contains English characters] The switching on of the Pandal on the previous day of the festival is a grand occasion for the local people.
[Contains English characters] The finale of the festival is the fireworks display.
[Contains English characters] It is a magnificent show, with both sides vying to get the upper hand.
[Contains English characters] New techniques are tried every year to bring out the best performance.
[Contains English characters] The quality and quantity of the fireworks are discussed by the people for many days after the event.
[Contains English characters] The selection of the elephants is another prestigious issue for the organisers.
[Contains English characters] They compete to get the best elephants in Kerala, paying exorbitant sums.
[Contains English characters] Both sides, are very competitive.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, they try to get the same elephant, resulting in unrealistic bidding.
[Contains English characters] If the Nemmara have 21 elephants, the Vallengi will try to match that or have more and vice versa.
[Contains English characters] Various folk arts like Kummatti, Karivela and Andivela and so on, mark the next few days.
[Contains English characters] The Pothundy Dam is 6 km from Nemmara and is a stopping point for visitors to the Nelliyampathy hills.
[Contains English characters] Nearest Airport: Kochi or CoimbatoreNearest railway station: Palakkad or Trichur or Kollengode.
[Contains English characters] From Kochi Airport: travel to Trichur - 30 km, take a taxi to Nemmara or by bus from Trichur bus stand to Nemmara - 48 km.
[Contains English characters] From Coimbatore Airport : By Taxi or bus to Palakkad - 60 km.
[Contains English characters] From Palakkad: By taxi or bus to Nemmara, 28 km.

[Contains English characters] As a continuation of Silappatikaram, this epic describes how Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, followers of Jainism, takes up social service as the primary aim of her life and how she sacrifices her entire life for the same cause.
[Contains English characters] Manimekalai is set in both Tamil Nadu and in Nainatheevu, Jaffna Peninsula in modern श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] The story runs as follows.
[Contains English characters] Manimekalai is on the verge of marrying a prince, when she is abducted and taken to an island Manipallava Theevu by her fairy God Mother known as Manimegala Theivam.
[Contains English characters] There she comes across Arughar and she acquires the enchanted aaputhiran kai amutha surabhi - a cornucopia bowl.
[Contains English characters] She uses this bowl to feed Kayasandigai, a cursed Yaksha who is suffering from Yaanai - Thee disease - an eating disorder caused due to excessive desire to eat.
[Contains English characters] After this, Manimekalai is brought back to Tamil Nadu, where she uses her bowl to feed the needy.
[Contains English characters] Manimekalai - The daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, who was born with bravery and virtues.
[Contains English characters] Udhayakumaran - The Chola King, who was madly in love with Manimekalai.

[Contains English characters] Sudhamadhi - Manimekalais most faithful and trustworthy friend.

[Contains English characters] In computing, internationalization and localization are means of adapting computer software to different languages and regional differences.
[Contains English characters] Internationalization is the process of designing a software application so that it can be adapted to various languages and regions without engineering changes.
[Contains English characters] Localization is the process of adapting internationalized software for a specific region or language by adding locale-specific components and translating text.
[Contains English characters] Due to their length, the terms are frequently abbreviated to the numeronyms i18n and L10n respectively.
[Contains English characters] The capital L in L10n helps to distinguish it from the lowercase i in i18n.
[Contains English characters] Some companies, like Microsoft, आय. बी. एम. and Sun Microsystems, use the term globalization for the combination of internationalization and localization.
[Contains English characters] Globalization can also be abbreviated to g11n.
[Contains English characters] This term is also known as NLS .
[Contains English characters] Focal points of internationalization and localization efforts include: The distinction between internationalization and localization is subtle but important.
[Contains English characters] Internationalization is the adaptation of products for potential use virtually everywhere, while localization is the addition of special features for use in a specific locale.
[Contains English characters] Internationalization is done once per product, while localization is done once for each combination of product and locale.
[Contains English characters] The processes are complementary, and must be combined to lead to the objective of a system that works globally.
[Contains English characters] Subjects unique to localization include: In order to Internationalize a product, it is important to look at a variety of markets that your product will foreseeably enter.
[Contains English characters] Details such as field length for addresses, ability to make the zip code field optional to address countries that do not have zip codes, plus the introduction of new registration flows that adhere to local laws are just some of the examples that make internationalization a complex project.
[Contains English characters] The current prevailing practice is for applications to place text in resource strings which are loaded during program execution as needed.
[Contains English characters] These strings, stored in resource files, are relatively easy to translate.
[Contains English characters] Programs are often built to reference resource libraries depending on the selected locale data.
[Contains English characters] One software library that aids this is gettext.
[Contains English characters] Thus to get an application to support multiple languages one would design the application to select the relevant language resource file at runtime.
[Contains English characters] Resource files are translated to the required languages.
[Contains English characters] This method tends to be application-specific and at best, vendor-specific.
[Contains English characters] The code required to manage date entry verification and many other locale-sensitive data types also must support differing locale requirements.
[Contains English characters] Modern development systems and operating systems include sophisticated libraries for international support of these types.
[Contains English characters] While translating existing text to other languages may seem easy, it is more difficult to maintain the parallel versions of texts throughout the life of the product.
[Contains English characters] For instance, if a message displayed to the user is modified, all of the translated versions must be changed.
[Contains English characters] This in turn results in somewhat longer development cycle.
[Contains English characters] Many localization issues require more profound changes in the software than text translation.
[Contains English characters] For example, OpenOffice.
[Contains English characters] Org achieves this with compilation switches.
[Contains English characters] To some degree, the development team needs someone who understands foreign languages and cultures and has a technical background.
[Contains English characters] In large societies with one dominant language/culture, it may be difficult to find such a person.
[Contains English characters] In a commercial setting, the benefit from localization is access to more markets.
[Contains English characters] Some argue that the commercial case to localize products into multiple languages is very obvious, and that all is needed is a budgetary commitment from the producer to finance the considerable costs.
[Contains English characters] It costs more to produce products for international markets, but in an increasingly global economy, supporting only one language/market is scarcely an option.
[Contains English characters] Still, proprietary software localization is impacted by economic viability and usually lacks the ability for end users and volunteers to self-localize, as is often the case in open-source environments.
[Contains English characters] Since open source software can generally be freely modified and redistributed, it is more amenable to internationalization.
[Contains English characters] The KDE project, for example, has been translated into over 100 languages.

[Contains English characters] Master of Commerce is a postgraduate Masters Degree focusing on commerce, management and economics related subjects.
[Contains English characters] Like the undergraduate Bachelor of Commerce, the degree is offered in Commonwealth nations.
[Contains English characters] The Master of Commerce typically requires one year of full-time study.
[Contains English characters] The curriculum is usually concentrated on one subject area — such as accounting, economics, finance or marketing — and emphasises underlying theory.
[Contains English characters] Relatedly, programs usually include a thesis component, or may even be exclusively research based.
[Contains English characters] Given this structure, the MComm differs from other business and management degrees.
[Contains English characters] Its concentration on one area distinguishes it from generalist degrees, such as the मास्टर ऑफ बिझिनेस ऍडमिनीस्ट्रेशन; some universities offer the MComm in general management, although this is more similar to the Master of Management than to the MBA.
[Contains English characters] As compared to specialised Professional degrees - such as the Master of Science in Finance or Master of Accounting - the MComm places more emphasis on theory, although sometimes less on practice; generally, though, there is a close correspondence between these degrees and the related MComm; see also Master of Science in Management.
[Contains English characters] Admission is usually on the basis of an existing Bachelors degree, generally the Bachelor of Commerce.
[Contains English characters] Depending on the degree focus, a related undergraduate major and / or a fairly strong quantitative background may also be a prerequisite.
[Contains English characters] Some programs admit students from non-business backgrounds such as liberal arts, engineering, or the sciences - these programs usually require that students complete a bridging course.
[Contains English characters] Based on specialisation, graduates are typically employed in fields related to their degree focus, such as financial services, marketing and project management; graduates also often work in general management and business consulting .
[Contains English characters] The Master of Commerce includes a research component and thus provides access to a doctorate; progressing from the Master of Commerce, a student can pursue a Doctor of Commerce, Doctor of Business Administration, or a Doctor of Philosophy degree program.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Cleanup Affection is a disposition or state of mind or body that is often associated with a feeling or type of love.
[Contains English characters] It has given rise to a number of branches of philosophy and psychology concerning: emotion ; disease; influence; state of being ; and state of mind .
[Contains English characters] Affection is popularly used to denote a feeling or type of love, amounting to more than goodwill or friendship.
[Contains English characters] Writers on ethics generally use the word to refer to distinct states of feeling, both lasting and spasmodic.
[Contains English characters] Some contrast it with passion as being free from the distinctively sensual element.
[Contains English characters] More specifically the word has been restricted to emotional states, the object of which is a person.
[Contains English characters] In the former sense, it is the Greek pathos and as such it appears in the writings of French philosopher René Descartes, Dutch philosopher Baruch Spinoza, and most of the writings of early British ethicists.
[Contains English characters] However, on various grounds, it is generally and usefully distinguished from passion.
[Contains English characters] In this narrower sense the word has played a great part in ethical systems, which have spoken of the social or parental affections as in some sense a part of moral obligation.
[Contains English characters] For a consideration of these and similar problems, which depend ultimately on the degree in which the affections are regarded as voluntary, see H.
[Contains English characters] Sidgwick, Methods of Ethics pp.
[Contains English characters] 345–349. Numerous behaviors are used by people to express affection.
[Contains English characters] Some theories suggest that affectionate behavior evolved from parental nurturing behavior due to its associations with hormonal rewards with research verifying that expressions of affection, although commonly evaluated positively, can be considered negative if they pose implied threats to ones well being.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, affectionate behavior in positively valenced relationships may be associated with numerous health benefits.
[Contains English characters] Other, more loving type gestures of affectionate behavior include obvious signs of liking a person.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Unreferenced sectionIn psychology the terms affection and affective are of great importance.
[Contains English characters] As all intellectual phenomena have by experimentalists been reduced to sensation, so all emotion has been and is regarded as reducible to simple mental affection, the element of which all emotional manifestations are ultimately composed.
[Contains English characters] The nature of this element is a problem that has been provisionally, but not conclusively, solved by many psychologists; the method is necessarily experimental, and all experiments on feeling are peculiarly difficult.
[Contains English characters] The solutions proposed are two.
[Contains English characters] In the first, all affection phenomena are primarily divisible into those that are pleasurable and those that are the reverse.
[Contains English characters] The main objections to this are that it does not explain the infinite variety of phenomena, and that it disregards the distinction that most philosophers admit between higher and lower pleasures.
[Contains English characters] The second solution is that every sensation has its specific affective quality, though by reason of the poverty of language many of these have no name. W. Wundt, Outlines of Psychology, maintains that we may group under three main affective directions, each with its negative, all the infinite varieties in question; these are pleasure, or rather pleasantness, and displeasure, tension and relaxation, excitement and depression.
[Contains English characters] These two views are antithetic and no solution has been discovered.
[Contains English characters] American psychologist Henry Murray developed a theory of personality that was organized in terms of motives, presses, and needs.
[Contains English characters] According to Murray, these psychogenic needs function mostly on the unconscious level, but play a major role in our personality.
[Contains English characters] Murray classified five affection needs: Two methods of experiment on affection have been tried: Mention should also be made of a third method that has hardly yet been tried, namely, that of endeavouring to isolate one of the three directions by the method of suggestion or even hypnotic trance observations.

[Contains English characters] ORCID identifiers consist of a reserved block of ISNI identifiers for scholarly researchers and administered by a separate organisation.
[Contains English characters] Individual researchers can create and claim their own ORCID identifier.
[Contains English characters] The two organisations coordinate their efforts.
[Contains English characters] ISNI is governed by an International Agency, commonly known as the ISNI-IA.
[Contains English characters] This UK registered, not-for-profit company has been founded by a consortium of organisations consisting of the Confédération Internationale des Sociétés d´Auteurs et Compositeurs, the Conference of European National Librarians, the International Federation of Reproduction Rights Organisations, the International Performers Database Association, the Online Computer Library Center and ProQuest.
[Contains English characters] It is managed by directors nominated from these organisations and, in the case of CENL, by representatives of the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the British Library.
[Contains English characters] ISNI-IA uses an assignment system comprising a user interface, data-schema, disambiguation algorithms, and database that meets the requirements of the ISO standard, while also using existing technology where possible.
[Contains English characters] The system is based primarily on the Virtual International Authority File service, which has been developed by OCLC for use in the aggregation of library catalogues.
[Contains English characters] Access to the assignment system and database, and to the numbers that are generated as the output of the process, are controlled by independent bodies known as registration agencies.
[Contains English characters] These registration agencies deal directly with customers, ensuring that data is provided in appropriate formats and recompensing the ISNI-IA for the cost of maintaining the assignment system.
[Contains English characters] Registration agencies are appointed by ISNI-IA but will be managed and funded independently.
[Contains English characters] As of 2017-08-05 ISNI holds public records of over 9.41 million identities, including 8.757 million individuals and 654,074 organisations.

[Contains English characters] The initial crust that formed when the Earths surface first solidified totally disappeared from a combination of this fast Hadean plate tectonics and the intense impacts of the Late Heavy Bombardment.
[Contains English characters] It is however assumed that this crust must have been basaltic in composition like todays oceanic crust, because little crustal differentiation had yet taken place.
[Contains English characters] The first larger pieces of continental crust, which is a product of differentiation of lighter elements during partial melting in the lower crust, appeared at the start of the Archaean, about 4.0 Ga.
[Contains English characters] What is left of these first small continents are called cratons.
[Contains English characters] These pieces of Archaean crust form the cores around which todays continents grew.
[Contains English characters] The oldest rocks on Earth are found in the North American craton of Canada.
[Contains English characters] They are tonalites and about 4.0 Ga.
[Contains English characters] They show traces of metamorphism by high temperature, but also sedimentary grains that have been rounded by erosion during transport by water, showing rivers and seas existed at the time.
[Contains English characters] Cratons consist mostly of two alternating types of terranes.
[Contains English characters] The first are so called greenstone belts, consisting of low grade metamorphosed sedimentary rocks.
[Contains English characters] These greenstones are similar to the sediments today found in oceanic trenches, above subduction zones.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, greenstones are sometimes seen as evidence for subduction during the Archaean.
[Contains English characters] The second type are complexes of felsic magmatic rocks.
[Contains English characters] These rocks are mostly tonalite, trondhjemite or granodiorite, types of rock similar in composition to granite .
[Contains English characters] TTG-complexes are seen as the relicts of the first continental crust, formed by partial melting in basalt.
[Contains English characters] The alternation between greenstone belts and TTG-complexes is interpreted as a tectonic situation in which small proto-continents were separated by a thorough network of subduction zones.
[Contains English characters] The details of the origin of life are unknown, but the broad principles have been established.
[Contains English characters] There are two schools of thought about the origin of life.
[Contains English characters] One suggests that organic components arrived on Earth from space, while the other argues that they originated on Earth.
[Contains English characters] Nevertheless, both schools propose similar mechanisms by which life initially arose.
[Contains English characters] Perhaps it arose around 4 Ga.
[Contains English characters] In the energetic chemistry of early Earth, a molecule gained the ability to make copies of itself–a replicator.
[Contains English characters] The replication was not always accurate: some copies were slightly different from their parent.
[Contains English characters] If the change destroyed the copying ability of the molecule, the molecule did not produce any copies, and the line “died out”.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, a few rare changes might make the molecule replicate faster or better: those “strains” would become more numerous and “successful”.
[Contains English characters] This created evolution.
[Contains English characters] As choice raw materials became depleted, strains which could exploit different materials, or perhaps halt the progress of other strains and steal their resources, became more numerous.
[Contains English characters] The nature of the first replicator is unknown because its function was long since superseded by life’s current replicator, DNA.
[Contains English characters] Several models have been proposed explaining how a replicator might have developed.
[Contains English characters] Different replicators have been posited, including organic chemicals such as modern proteins, nucleic acids, phospholipids, crystals, or even quantum systems.
[Contains English characters] There is currently no way to determine whether any of these models closely fits the origin of life on Earth.
[Contains English characters] One of the older theories, and one which has been worked out in some detail, will serve as an example of how this might occur.
[Contains English characters] The high energy from volcanoes, lightning, and ultraviolet radiation could help drive chemical reactions producing more complex molecules from simple compounds such as methane and ammonia.
[Contains English characters] :38 Among these were many of the relatively simple organic compounds that are the building blocks of life.
[Contains English characters] As the amount of this “organic soup” increased, different molecules reacted with one another.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes more complex molecules would result—perhaps clay provided a framework to collect and concentrate organic material.
[Contains English characters] :39 The presence of certain molecules could speed up a chemical reaction.
[Contains English characters] All this continued for a very long time, with reactions occurring more or less at random, until by chance it produced a replicator molecule.
[Contains English characters] In any case, at some point, the function of the replicator was superseded by DNA; all known life use DNA as their replicator, in an almost identical manner .
[Contains English characters] Modern life has its replicating material packaged inside a cellular membrane.
[Contains English characters] It is easier to understand the origin of the cell membrane than the origin of the replicator, because a cell membrane is made of phospholipid molecules which often form a bilayer spontaneously when placed in water.
[Contains English characters] Under certain conditions, many such spheres can be formed .
[Contains English characters] :40 The prevailing theory is that the membrane formed after the replicator, which perhaps by then was RNA, along with its replicating apparatus and maybe other biomolecules.
[Contains English characters] Initial protocells may have simply burst when they grew too large; the scattered contents may then have recolonized other “bubbles”.
[Contains English characters] Proteins that stabilized the membrane, or that later assisted in an orderly division, would have promoted the proliferation of those cell lines.
[Contains English characters] RNA is a likely candidate for an early replicator, because it can both store genetic information and catalyze reactions.
[Contains English characters] At some point DNA took over the genetic storage role from RNA, and proteins known as enzymes took over the catalysis role, leaving RNA to transfer information and modulate the process.
[Contains English characters] There is increasing belief that these early cells evolved in association with underwater volcanic vents known as black smokers:42 or even hot, deep rocks.
[Contains English characters] It is believed that of this multiplicity of protocells, only one survived.
[Contains English characters] Current evidence suggests that the last universal common ancestor lived during the early Archean eon, perhaps roughly 3.5 Ga or earlier.
[Contains English characters] This “LUCA” cell is the ancestor of all life on Earth today.
[Contains English characters] It was probably a prokaryote, possessing a cell membrane and probably ribosomes, but lacking a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria or chloroplasts.
[Contains English characters] Like all modern cells, it used DNA as its genetic code, RNA for information transfer and protein synthesis, and enzymes to catalyze reactions.
[Contains English characters] Some scientists believe that instead of a single organism being the last universal common ancestor, there were populations of organisms exchanging genes in lateral gene transfer.
[Contains English characters] The Proterozoic is the eon of Earths history that lasted from 2.500 billion to 542 million years ago.
[Contains English characters] In this time span, the cratons grew into continents with modern sizes.
[Contains English characters] For the first time it is clear that plate tectonics took place in a more or less modern sense.
[Contains English characters] Another important development was the change to an oxygen rich atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] Life developed from prokaryotes into eukaryotes and multicellular forms.
[Contains English characters] The Proterozoic saw a couple of very severe ice ages called snowball Earths.
[Contains English characters] After the end of the last Snowball Earth about 600 million years ago, the evolution of life on Earth accelerated.
[Contains English characters] About 580 million years ago, the Ediacara biota formed the prelude for the Cambrian Explosion.
[Contains English characters] It is likely that the initial cells were all heterotrophs, using surrounding organic molecules as raw material and an energy source.
[Contains English characters] As the food supply diminished, a new strategy evolved in some cells.
[Contains English characters] Instead of relying on the diminishing amounts of free-existing organic molecules, these cells adopted sunlight as an energy source.
[Contains English characters] Estimates vary, but by about 3 Ga, something similar to modern photosynthesis had probably developed.
[Contains English characters] This made the sun’s energy available not only to autotrophs but also to the heterotrophs that consumed them.
[Contains English characters] Photosynthesis used the plentiful carbon dioxide and water as raw materials and, with the energy of sunlight, produced energy-rich organic molecules .
[Contains English characters] Moreover, oxygen was produced as a waste product of photosynthesis.
[Contains English characters] At first it became bound up with limestone, iron, and other minerals.
[Contains English characters] There is substantial proof of this in iron-oxide rich layers in geological strata that correspond with this time period.
[Contains English characters] The reaction of the minerals with oxygen would have turned the oceans green.
[Contains English characters] When most of the exposed readily-reacting minerals were oxidized, oxygen finally began to accumulate in the atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] Though each cell only produced a minute amount of oxygen, the combined metabolism of many cells over a vast period of time transformed Earth’s atmosphere to its current state.
[Contains English characters] :50-51 Among the oldest examples of oxygen-producing lifeforms are fossil stromatolites.
[Contains English characters] This was Earth’s third atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] Some of the oxygen was stimulated by incoming ultraviolet radiation to form ozone, which collected in a layer near the upper part of the atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] The ozone layer absorbed, and still absorbs, a significant amount of the ultraviolet radiation that once had passed through the atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] It allowed cells to colonize the surface of the ocean and ultimately the land: without the ozone layer, ultraviolet radiation bombarding the surface would have caused unsustainable levels of mutation in exposed cells.
[Contains English characters] Photosynthesis had another, major, and world-changing impact.
[Contains English characters] Oxygen was toxic; probably much life on Earth died out as its levels rose in what is known as the oxygen catastrophe.
[Contains English characters] Resistant forms survived and thrived, and some developed the ability to use oxygen to enhance their metabolism and derive more energy from the same food.
[Contains English characters] An oxygen-rich atmosphere had two important advantages for life.
[Contains English characters] Organisms not using oxygen for their metabolism, such as anaerobe bacteria, base their metabolism on fermentation.
[Contains English characters] The abundance of oxygen makes respiration possible, a much more effective energy source for life.
[Contains English characters] The second advantage of an oxygen-rich atmosphere is that oxygen forms ozone in the higher atmosphere, causing the origin of the Earths ozone layer.
[Contains English characters] The ozone layer protects the Earths surface from ultraviolet radiation, which is harmful for life.
[Contains English characters] Without the ozone layer, the development of more complex life later on would probably have been impossible.
[Contains English characters] The natural evolution of the Sun made it gradually more luminous during the Archaean and Proterozoic eons.
[Contains English characters] The Suns luminosity increases 6% every billion years.
[Contains English characters] As a result, the Earth began to receive more heat from the Sun in the Proterozoic eon.
[Contains English characters] However, the Earth did not get warmer.
[Contains English characters] Instead, the geological record seems to suggest it cooled dramatically during the early Proterozoic.
[Contains English characters] Glacial deposits found on all cratons show that about 2.3 Ga, the Earth underwent its first big ice age .
[Contains English characters] Some scientists suggest this and following Proterozoic ice ages were so severe that the planet was totally frozen over from the poles to the equator, a hypothesis called Snowball Earth.
[Contains English characters] Not all geologists agree with this scenario and older, Archaean ice ages have been postulated, but the ice age 2.3 Ga is the first such event for which the evidence is universally accepted.
[Contains English characters] The ice age around 2.3 Ga could have been directly caused by the increased oxygen concentration in the atmosphere, which caused the decrease of methane in the atmosphere.
[Contains English characters] Methane is a strong greenhouse gas, but with oxygen it reacts to form CO2, a less effective greenhouse gas.
[Contains English characters] When free oxygen became available in the atmosphere, the concentration of methane could have decreased dramatically, enough to counter the effect of the increasing heat flow from the Sun.
[Contains English characters] Modern taxonomy classifies life into three domains.
[Contains English characters] The time of the origin of these domains is speculative.
[Contains English characters] The Bacteria domain probably first split off from the other forms of life, but this supposition is controversial.
[Contains English characters] Soon after this, by 2 Ga, the Neomura split into the Archaea and the Eukarya.
[Contains English characters] Eukaryotic cells are larger and more complex than prokaryotic cells, and the origin of that complexity is only now coming to light.
[Contains English characters] Around this time, the first proto-mitochondrion was formed.
[Contains English characters] A bacterial cell related to today’s Rickettsia entered a larger prokaryotic cell.
[Contains English characters] Perhaps the large cell attempted to ingest the smaller one but failed .
[Contains English characters] Or, perhaps the smaller cell tried to parasitize the larger one.
[Contains English characters] In any case, the smaller cell survived inside the larger cell.
[Contains English characters] Using oxygen, it was able to metabolize the larger cell’s waste products and derive more energy.
[Contains English characters] Some of this surplus energy was returned to the host.
[Contains English characters] The smaller cell replicated inside the larger one.
[Contains English characters] Soon, a stable symbiosis developed between the large cell and the smaller cells inside it.
[Contains English characters] Over time, the host cell acquired some of the genes of the smaller cells, and the two kinds became dependent on each other: the larger cell could not survive without the energy produced by the smaller ones, and these in turn could not survive without the raw materials provided by the larger cell.
[Contains English characters] The whole cell is now considered a single organism, and the smaller cells are classified as organelles called mitochondria.
[Contains English characters] A similar event occurred with photosynthetic cyanobacteria entering larger heterotrophic cells and becoming chloroplasts.
[Contains English characters] :60-61 Probably as a result of these changes, a line of cells capable of photosynthesis split off from the other eukaryotes more than 1 billion years ago.
[Contains English characters] There were probably several such inclusion events, as the figure at right suggests.
[Contains English characters] Besides the well-established endosymbiotic theory of the cellular origin of mitochondria and chloroplasts, it has been suggested that cells gave rise to peroxisomes, spirochetes gave rise to cilia and flagella, and that perhaps a DNA virus gave rise to the cell nucleus,, though none of these theories are generally accepted.
[Contains English characters] Archaeans, bacteria, and eukaryotes continued to diversify and to become more sophisticated and better adapted to their environments.
[Contains English characters] Each domain repeatedly split into multiple lineages, although little is known about the history of the archaea and bacteria.
[Contains English characters] Around 1.1 Ga, the supercontinent Rodinia was assembling.
[Contains English characters] The plant, animal, and fungi lines had all split, though they still existed as solitary cells.
[Contains English characters] Some of these lived in colonies, and gradually some division of labor began to take place; for instance, cells on the periphery might have started to assume different roles from those in the interior.
[Contains English characters] Although the division between a colony with specialized cells and a multicellular organism is not always clear, around 1 billion years ago the first multicellular plants emerged, probably green algae.
[Contains English characters] Possibly by around 900 million years ago true multicellularity had also evolved in animals.
[Contains English characters] At first it probably somewhat resembled that of today’s sponges, where all cells were totipotent and a disrupted organism could reassemble itself.
[Contains English characters] As the division of labor became more complete in all lines of multicellular organisms, cells became more specialized and more dependent on each other; isolated cells would die.
[Contains English characters] When the theory of plate tectonics was developed around 1960, geologists began to reconstruct the movements and positions of the continents in the past.
[Contains English characters] This appeared relatively easy until about 250 million years back, when all continents were united in what is called the supercontinent Pangaea.
[Contains English characters] Before that time, reconstructions cannot rely on apparent similarities in coastlines or ages of oceanic crust, but instead solely rely on geologic observations and, more importantly, on paleomagnetic data.
[Contains English characters] Throughout the history of the Earth, there have been times when the continental mass came together to form a supercontinent, followed by the break-up of the supercontinent and new continents moving apart again.
[Contains English characters] This repetition of tectonic events is called a Wilson cycle.
[Contains English characters] The further back in time, the scarcer and harder to interpret the data get.
[Contains English characters] It is at least clear that, about 1000 to 830 million years ago, most continental mass was united in the supercontinent Rodinia.
[Contains English characters] It is very probable Rodinia was not the first supercontinent and a number of early Proterozoic supercontinents have been proposed.
[Contains English characters] This means plate tectonic processes similar to todays must have been active during the Proterozoic.
[Contains English characters] After the break-up of Rodinia about 800 million years ago, it is possible the continents joined again around 550 million years ago.
[Contains English characters] The hypothetical supercontinent is sometimes referred to as Pannotia or Vendia.
[Contains English characters] The evidence for it is a phase of continental collision known as the Pan-African orogeny, which joined the continental masses of current-day Africa, South-America, Antarctica and Australia.
[Contains English characters] It is very likely however, that the assemblage of continental masses was not complete, since a continent called Laurentia had already started breaking off around 610 million years ago.
[Contains English characters] It is at least certain that by the end of the Proterozoic eon, most of the continental mass lay united in a position around the south pole.
[Contains English characters] Proterozoic शेवटी समुद्र पृष्ठभाग शकते पूर्णपणे जप्त केली आहेत की त्यांना गंभीर किमान दोन बर्फाचा Earths पाहिले.
[Contains English characters] या Cryogenian सुमारे 710 आणि 640 दशलक्ष वर्षांपूर्वी झाले.
[Contains English characters] या गंभीर glaciations लवकर Proterozoic बर्फाचा पृथ्वी पेक्षा स्पष्ट करण्यासाठी कमी सोपे आहेत.
[Contains English characters] सर्वात paleoclimatologists थंड भाग supercontinent Rodinia निर्मिती काहीतरी होते वाटते.
[Contains English characters] Rodinia विषुववृत्त सुमारे केंद्रीत होते कारण, दर weathering कार्बन डायऑक्साइड वातावरण काढून घेण्यात आले वाढ झाली.
[Contains English characters] बर्फाचा Earths दरम्यान समान मार्ग नाही, मध्ये युरोपिअन बहुतांश पृष्ठभाग glaciations शेवटी अग्रगण्य, पुन्हा weathering रासायनिक रक्कम कमी जे ध्रुवप्रदेशाकडील कायम गाठलेली जमीन मध्ये होते.
[Contains English characters] एक पर्यायी गृहीते ते पुरेसे कार्बन डायऑक्साइड परिणामी हरितगृह परिणाम आणि जागतिक तापमान असण्याचा ज्वालामुखीचा outgassing सुटका आहे.
[Contains English characters] Whereas the Ediacaran life forms appear yet primitive and not easy to put in any modern group, at the end of the Cambrian most modern phyla were already present.
[Contains English characters] Because of the development of hard body parts such as shells, skeletons or exoskeletons in animals like molluscs, echinoderms, crinoids and arthropods made the preservation and fossilisation of such life forms easier than those of their Proterozoic ancestors.
[Contains English characters] For this reason, much more is known about life in and after the Cambrian than about that of older periods.
[Contains English characters] The boundary between the Cambrian and Ordovician is characterized by a large mass-extinction, in which some of the new groups disappeared altogether.
[Contains English characters] Some of these Cambrian groups appear complex but totally different compared to modern life, examples are Anomalocaris and Haikouichthys.
[Contains English characters] During the Cambrian, the first vertebrate animals, among them the first fishes, had appeared.
[Contains English characters] A creature that could have been the ancestor of the fishes or was probably closely related to it, was Pikaia.
[Contains English characters] It had a primitive notochord, a structure that could have developed into a vertebral column later.
[Contains English characters] The first fishes with jaws appeared during the Ordovician.
[Contains English characters] The colonisation of new niches resulted in gigantic body sizes.
[Contains English characters] In this way, fishes with increasing sizes evolved in the course of the early Paleozoic, such as the gigantic placoderm Dunkleosteus, which could become 7 meters long.
[Contains English characters] At the end of the Proterozoic, the supercontinent Pannotia had broken apart in the smaller continents Laurentia, Baltica, Siberia and Gondwana.
[Contains English characters] During periods when continents move apart, more oceanic crust is formed by volcanic activity.
[Contains English characters] Because young volcanic crust is relatively hot and less dense than old oceanic crust, the ocean floors will rise during such periods.
[Contains English characters] This causes the sea level to rise.
[Contains English characters] Therefore, in the first half of the Paleozoic, large areas of the continents were below sea level.
[Contains English characters] Early Paleozoic climates were generally warmer than today, but the end of the Ordovician saw a short ice age, in which glaciers covered the south pole, where the huge continent Gondwana was situated.
[Contains English characters] Traces of glaciation from this period are only found on former Gondwana.
[Contains English characters] During the Late Ordovician ice age, a number of mass extinctions took place, in which many brachiopods, trilobites, Bryozoa and corals disappeared.
[Contains English characters] These marine species could probably not cope with the decreasing temperature of the sea water.
[Contains English characters] After the extinctions new species evolved, more diverse and better adapted.
[Contains English characters] They would fill the niches left by the extinct species.
[Contains English characters] The continents Laurentia and Baltica collided between 450 and 400 million years ago, during the Caledonian Orogeny, to form Laurussia.
[Contains English characters] Traces of the mountain belt which resulted from this collision can be found in Scandinavia, Scotland and the northern Appalachians.
[Contains English characters] In the Devonian period Gondwana and Siberia began to move towards Laurussia.
[Contains English characters] The collision of Siberia with Laurussia caused the Uralian Orogeny, the collision of Gondwana with Laurussia is called the Variscan or Hercynian Orogeny in Europe or the Alleghenian Orogeny in North America.
[Contains English characters] The latter phase took place during the Carboniferous period and resulted in the formation of the last supercontinent, Pangaea.
[Contains English characters] Oxygen accumulation from photosynthesis resulted in the formation of an ozone layer that absorbed much of Sun’s ultraviolet radiation, meaning unicellular organisms that reached land were less likely to die, and prokaryotes began to multiply and become better adapted to survival out of the water.
[Contains English characters] Prokaryotes had probably colonized the land as early as 2.6 Ga even before the origin of the eukaryotes.
[Contains English characters] For a long time, the land remained barren of multicellular organisms.
[Contains English characters] The supercontinent Pannotia formed around 600 Ma and then broke apart a short 50 million years later.
[Contains English characters] Fish, the earliest vertebrates, evolved in the oceans around 530 Ma.
[Contains English characters] A major extinction event occurred near the end of the Cambrian period, which ended 488 Ma.
[Contains English characters] Several hundred million years ago, plants and fungi started growing at the edges of the water, and then out of it.
[Contains English characters] The oldest fossils of land fungi and plants date to 480–460 Ma, though molecular evidence suggests the fungi may have colonized the land as early as 1000 Ma and the plants 700 Ma.
[Contains English characters] Initially remaining close to the water’s edge, mutations and variations resulted in further colonization of this new environment.
[Contains English characters] The timing of the first animals to leave the oceans is not precisely known: the oldest clear evidence is of arthropods on land around 450 Ma, perhaps thriving and becoming better adapted due to the vast food source provided by the terrestrial plants.
[Contains English characters] There is also some unconfirmed evidence that arthropods may have appeared on land as early as 530 Ma.
[Contains English characters] At the end of the Ordovician period, 440 Ma, additional extinction events occurred, perhaps due to a concurrent ice age.
[Contains English characters] Around 380 to 375 Ma, the first tetrapods evolved from fish.
[Contains English characters] It is thought that perhaps fins evolved to become limbs which allowed the first tetrapods to lift their heads out of the water to breathe air.
[Contains English characters] This would let them survive in oxygen-poor water or pursue small prey in shallow water.
[Contains English characters] They may have later ventured on land for brief periods.
[Contains English characters] Eventually, some of them became so well adapted to terrestrial life that they spent their adult lives on land, although they hatched in the water and returned to lay their eggs.
[Contains English characters] This was the origin of the amphibians.
[Contains English characters] About 365 Ma, another period of extinction occurred, perhaps as a result of global cooling.
[Contains English characters] Plants evolved seeds, which dramatically accelerated their spread on land, around this time .
[Contains English characters] Some 20 million years later, the amniotic egg evolved, which could be laid on land, giving a survival advantage to tetrapod embryos.
[Contains English characters] This resulted in the divergence of amniotes from amphibians.
[Contains English characters] Another 30 million years saw the divergence of the synapsids from the sauropsids .
[Contains English characters] Other groups of organisms continued to evolve and lines diverged—in fish, insects, bacteria, and so on—but less is known of the details.
[Contains English characters] 300 million years ago, the most recent hypothesized supercontinent formed, called Pangaea.
[Contains English characters] The most severe extinction event to date took place 250 Ma, at the boundary of the Permian and Triassic periods; 95% of life on Earth died out, possibly due to the Siberian Traps volcanic event.
[Contains English characters] The discovery of the Wilkes Land crater in Antarctica may suggest a connection with the Permian-Triassic extinction, but the age of that crater is not known.
[Contains English characters] But life persevered, and around 230 Ma, dinosaurs split off from their reptilian ancestors.
[Contains English characters] An extinction event between the Triassic and Jurassic periods 200 Ma spared many of the dinosaurs, and they soon became dominant among the vertebrates.
[Contains English characters] Though some of the mammalian lines began to separate during this period, existing mammals were probably all small animals resembling shrews.
[Contains English characters] By 180 Ma, Pangaea broke up into Laurasia and Gondwana.
[Contains English characters] The boundary between avian and non-avian dinosaurs is not clear, but Archaeopteryx, traditionally considered one of the first birds, lived around 150 Ma.
[Contains English characters] The earliest evidence for the angiosperms evolving flowers is during the Cretaceous period, some 20 million years later .
[Contains English characters] Competition with birds drove many pterosaurs to extinction and the dinosaurs were probably already in decline when, 65 Ma, a १०-किलोमीटर meteorite probably struck Earth just off the Yucatán Peninsula where the Chicxulub crater is today.
[Contains English characters] This ejected vast quantities of particulate matter and vapor into the air that occluded sunlight, inhibiting photosynthesis.
[Contains English characters] Most large animals, including the non-avian dinosaurs, became extinct, marking the end of the Cretaceous period and Mesozoic era.
[Contains English characters] Thereafter, in the Paleocene epoch, mammals rapidly diversified, grew larger, and became the dominant vertebrates.
[Contains English characters] Perhaps a couple of million years later, the last common ancestor of primates lived.
[Contains English characters] By the late Eocene epoch, 34 Ma, some terrestrial mammals had returned to the oceans to become animals such as Basilosaurus which later gave rise to dolphins and baleen whales.
[Contains English characters] A small African ape living around six million years ago was the last animal whose descendants would include both modern humans and their closest relatives, the bonobos, and chimpanzees.
[Contains English characters] Only two branches of its family tree have surviving descendants.
[Contains English characters] Very soon after the split, for reasons that are still debated, apes in one branch developed the ability to walk upright.
[Contains English characters] Brain size increased rapidly, and by 2 Ma, the very first animals classified in the genus Homo had appeared.
[Contains English characters] Of course, the line between different species or even genera is rather arbitrary as organisms continuously change over generations.
[Contains English characters] Around the same time, the other branch split into the ancestors of the common chimpanzee and the ancestors of the bonobo as evolution continued simultaneously in all life forms.
[Contains English characters] The ability to control fire probably began in Homo erectus, probably at least 790,000 years ago but perhaps as early as 1.5 Ma.
[Contains English characters] In addition it has sometimes suggested that the use and discovery of controlled fire may even predate Homo erectus.
[Contains English characters] Fire was possibly used by the early Lower Paleolithic hominid Homo habilis and/or by robust australopithecines such as Paranthropus.
[Contains English characters] It is more difficult to establish the origin of language; it is unclear whether Homo erectus could speak or if that capability had not begun until Homo sapiens.
[Contains English characters] As brain size increased, babies were born sooner, before their heads grew too large to pass through the pelvis.
[Contains English characters] As a result, they exhibited more plasticity, and thus possessed an increased capacity to learn and required a longer period of dependence.
[Contains English characters] Social skills became more complex, language became more advanced, and tools became more elaborate.
[Contains English characters] This contributed to further cooperation and brain development.
[Contains English characters] Anatomically modern humans — Homo sapiens — are believed to have originated somewhere around 200,000 years ago or earlier in Africa; the oldest fossils date back to around 160,000 years ago.
[Contains English characters] The first humans to show evidence of spirituality are the Neanderthals ; they buried their dead, often apparently with food or tools.
[Contains English characters] However, evidence of more sophisticated beliefs, such as the early Cro-Magnon cave paintings did not appear until some 32,000 years ago.
[Contains English characters] Cro-Magnons also left behind stone figurines such as Venus of Willendorf, probably also signifying religious belief.

[Contains English characters] Some dictionaries list the words of more than one language and/or give translations in more than one language.
[Contains English characters] The dictionary is a list of words with their definitions, a list of characters with their glyphs, or a list of words with corresponding words in other languages.
[Contains English characters] In a few languages, words can appear in many different forms, but only the lemma form appears as the main word or headword in most dictionaries.
[Contains English characters] Many dictionaries also provide pronunciation information; grammatical information; word derivations, histories, or etymologies; illustrations; usage guidance; and examples in phrases or sentences.

[Contains English characters] Most dictionaries are produced by lexicographers.
[Contains English characters] The art and craft of writing dictionaries is called lexicography.
[Contains English characters] The Erya, from the early 3rd century BC, was the first Chinese language dictionary.
[Contains English characters] The book organized Chinese characters by semantic groups.
[Contains English characters] The intention of this dictionary was to explain the true meaning and interpretation of words in the context of older ancient texts.
[Contains English characters] One of the earliest dictionaries known, and which is still extant today in an abridged form, was written in Latin during the reign of the emperor Augustus.
[Contains English characters] It is known by the शीर्षक De Significatu Verborum and was originally compiled by Verrius Flaccus.
[Contains English characters] It was twice abridged in succeeding centuries, first by Sextus Pompeius Festus, and then by Paul the Deacon.
[Contains English characters] Verrius Flaccus dictionary was an abridged list of difficult or antiquated words, whose usage was illustrated by quotations from early Roman authors.
[Contains English characters] The word dictionary comes from neoclassical Latin, dictio, meaning simply word.
[Contains English characters] The first true English dictionary was Robert Cawdreys Table Alphabeticall of 1604, although it only included 3,000 words and the definitions it contained were little more than synonyms.
[Contains English characters] The first one to be at all comprehensive was Thomas Blounts dictionary Glossographia of 1656. Though many believe that Samuel Johnsons famous and more complete dictionary of 1755 was the first dictionary it was predated by Blount, as well as Kersey and Bailey.
[Contains English characters] In 1806, Noah Websters dictionary was published by the G&C Merriam Company of Springfield, Massachusetts which still publishes Merriam-Webster dictionaries, but the term Websters is considered generic and can be used by any dictionary.

[Contains English characters] Today, dictionaries of most languages with alphabetic and syllabic writing systems list words in lexicographic order, usually alphabetical or some analogous phonetic system.
[Contains English characters] In many languages, words are grouped together according to their true or normal origin, and these roots are arranged alphabetically.
[Contains English characters] If English dictionaries were arranged like this, the words import, export, support, report, porter, port, important and transportation would all be listed under port.
[Contains English characters] This method has the advantage that all words of a common origin are listed together, but the disadvantage is that one has to know how to recognise all prefixes of a word before one can look it up.
