[Contains English characters] A dictionary that attempts to cover as many words from a particular speech community as possible is called a maximizing dictionary, whereas a dictionary that attempts to cover only a limited selection of words from a speech community is called a minimizing dictionary .
[Contains English characters] There are many different types of dictionaries, including bilingual, multilingual, historical, biographical, and geographical dictionaries.
[Contains English characters] In bilingual dictionaries, each entry has translations of words in another language.
[Contains English characters] For example, in a Japanese-English dictionary, the entry tsuki has a corresponding English word, moon.
[Contains English characters] In dictionaries between English and a language using a non-Roman script, entry words in the non-English language may be either printed and sorted in the native order, or romanized and sorted in Roman alphabetical order.
[Contains English characters] Specialised dictionaries focus on linguistic and factual matters relating to specific subject fields.
[Contains English characters] A specialised dictionary may have a relatively broad coverage, e. g. a picture dictionary, in that it covers several subject fields such as science and technology, or their coverage may be more narrow, in that they cover one particular subject field such as law or even a specific sub-field such as contract law .
[Contains English characters] Specialised dictionaries may be maximizing dictionaries, i. e. they attempt to achieve comprehensive coverage of the terms in the subject field concerned, or they may be minimizing dictionaries, i.
[Contains English characters] e. they attempt to cover only a limited number of the specialised vocabulary concerned.
[Contains English characters] Generally, multi-field dictionaries tend to be minimizing, whereas single-field and sub-field dictionaries tend to be maximizing.

[Contains English characters] These characters are not arbitrary; they are composed of simpler characters, one of which is called the radical, which indicates its category.
[Contains English characters] The ordering of the characters in the dictionary is by radical, in order of the number of strokes in the radical.
[Contains English characters] Characters using that radical are then ordered by the number of strokes added to the radical.
[Contains English characters] To fit more strokes in a character, radicals can come in simplified variants, which have to be learned; for example, the character for dog is altered when it is used as the radical of the character for cat.

[Contains English characters] Noah Webster, intent on forging a distinct identity for the American language, altered spellings and accentuated differences in meaning and pronunciation of some words.
[Contains English characters] This is why American English now uses the spelling color while the rest of the English-speaking world prefers colour.
[Contains English characters] Large 20th-century dictionaries such as the ऑक्सफर्ड इंग्लिश डिक्शनरी and Websters Third are descriptive, and attempt to describe the actual use of words.
[Contains English characters] While descriptivists argue that prescriptivism is an unnatural attempt to dictate usage or curtail change, prescriptivists argue that to indiscriminately document improper or inferior usages sanctions those usages by default and causes language to deteriorate.
[Contains English characters] Although the debate can become very heated, only a small number of controversial words are usually affected.
[Contains English characters] But the softening of usage notations, from the previous edition, for two words, aint and regardless, out of over 450,000 in Websters Third in 1961, was enough to provoke outrage among many with prescriptivist leanings, who branded the dictionary as permissive.
[Contains English characters] The prescriptive/descriptive issue has been given so much consideration in modern times that most dictionaries of English apply the descriptive method to definitions, while additionally informing readers of attitudes which may influence their choices on words often considered vulgar, offensive, erroneous, or easily confused.
[Contains English characters] Merriam-Webster is subtle, only adding italicized notations such as, sometimes offensive or nonstand American Heritage goes further, discussing issues separately in numerous usage notes.
[Contains English characters] Encarta provides similar notes, but is more prescriptive, offering warnings and admonitions against the use of certain words considered by many to be offensive or illiterate, such as, an offensive term for. . . or a taboo term meaning.
[Contains English characters] . . Because of the broad use of dictionaries, and their acceptance by many as language authorities, their treatment of the language does affect usage to some degree, even the most descriptive dictionaries providing conservative continuity.
[Contains English characters] In the long run, however, usage primarily determines the meanings of words in English, and the language is being changed and created every day.

[Contains English characters] Since words and their meanings develop over time, dictionary entries are organized to reflect these changes.
[Contains English characters] Dictionaries may either list meanings in the historical order in which they appeared, or may list meanings in order of popularity and most common use.
[Contains English characters] Dictionaries also differ in the degree to which they are encyclopedic, providing considerable background information, illustrations, and the like, or linguistic, concentrating on etymology, nuances of meaning, and quotations demonstrating usage.
[Contains English characters] Any dictionary has been designed to fulfil one or more functions.
[Contains English characters] The dictionary functions chosen by the maker of the dictionary provide the basis for all lexicographic decisions, from the selection of entry words, over the choice of information types, to the choice of place for the information .
[Contains English characters] There are two main types of function.
[Contains English characters] The communication-oriented functions comprise text reception, text production, text revision, and translation.
[Contains English characters] The knowledge-oriented functions deal with situations where the dictionary is used for acquiring specific knowledge about a particular matter, and for acquiring general knowledge about something.
[Contains English characters] The optimal dictionary is one that contains information directly relevant for the needs of the users relating to one or more of these functions.
[Contains English characters] It is important that the information is presented in a way that keeps the lexicographic information costs at a minimum.

[Contains English characters] Language attrition is the loss of a first or second language or a portion of that language by individuals.
[Contains English characters] Speakers who routinely use more than one language may not use either of their languages in ways which are exactly like that of a monolingual speaker.
[Contains English characters] In sequential bilingualism, for example, there is often evidence of interference from the first language in the second language system.
[Contains English characters] Describing these interference phenomena and accounting for them on the basis of theoretical models of linguistic knowledge has long been a focus of interest of Applied Linguistics.
[Contains English characters] More recently, research has started to investigate linguistic traffic which goes the other way: L2 interferences and contact phenomena evident in the L1. Such phenomena are probably experienced to some extent by all bilinguals.
[Contains English characters] They are, however, most evident among speakers for whom a language other than the L1 has started to play an important, if not dominant, role in everyday life .
[Contains English characters] This is the case for migrants who move to a country where a language is spoken which, for them, is a second or foreign language.
[Contains English characters] We refer to the phenomena of L1 change and L2 interference which can be observed in such situations as language attrition.
[Contains English characters] Only in the past few decades has the study of language attrition become a sub-field of linguistics beginning with a 1980 conference at the University of Pennsylvania titled Loss of Language Skills .
[Contains English characters] The aim of this conference was to discuss areas of second language attrition and to ideate on possible areas of future research in L2 loss.
[Contains English characters] The conference revealed that attrition is a wide topic covering different types of language loss and that there are many possible reasons for the loss.
[Contains English characters] A related phenomenon is the loss of language due to contact with other, more dominant languages, possibly leading to language death.
[Contains English characters] The field gained new momentum with two conferences held in Amsterdam in 2002 and 2005, as well as a series of graduate workshops and panels at international conferences such as the International Symposium on Bilngualism, the annual conferences of the European Second Language Association and the AILA W0rld Congress .
[Contains English characters] The outcome of some of these meetings have been published in edited volumes and special issues of journals, such as the Journal of Neurolinguistics, the International Journal of Bilingualism and Bilingualism: Language and Cognition .
[Contains English characters] The term First Language Attrition refers to the gradual decline in native language proficiency among migrants.
[Contains English characters] As a speaker uses his/her L2 frequently and becomes proficient in it, some aspects of the L1 can become subject to L2 influence or deteriorate.
[Contains English characters] L1 attrition is a process which is governed by two factors: the presence and development of the L2 system on the one hand, and the diminished exposure to and use of the L1 on the other ; that is, it is a process typically witnessed among migrants who use the later-learned environmental language in daily life.
[Contains English characters] The current consensus is that attrition manifests itself first and most noticeably in lexical access and the mental lexicon while grammatical and phonological representations appear more stable among speakers for whom emigration took place after puberty .
[Contains English characters] Attrition research has often wrestled with the problem of how to establish the border between the ‘normal’ influence of the L2 on the L1, which all bilinguals probably experience to some degree, and the process of L1 attrition, which is confined to migrants.
[Contains English characters] It has recently been suggested that this distinction is not only impossible to draw, but also unhelpful, as “bilinguals may not have one ‘normal’ language and one ‘deviant’ one ” .
[Contains English characters] Rather, while L1 attrition may be the most clearly pronounced end of the entire spectrum of multicompetence, and therefore a more satisfying object of investigation than the L1 system of a beginning L2 learner, attrition is undoubtedly part of this continuum, and not a discrete and unique state of development.
[Contains English characters] Like second language acquisition, FLA is mediated by a number of external factors, such as exposure and use, attitude and motivation or aptitude .
[Contains English characters] However, the overall impact of these factors is far less strongly pronounced than what has been found in SLA.
[Contains English characters] L1 attriters, like L2 learners, may use language differently from native speakers.
[Contains English characters] In particular, they can have variability on certain rules which native speakers apply deterministically .
[Contains English characters] In the context of attrition, however, there is strong evidence that this optionality is not indicative of any underlying representational deficits: the same individuals do not appear to encounter recurring problems with the same kinds of grammatical phenomena in different speech situations or on different tasks .
[Contains English characters] This suggests that problems of L1 attriters are due to momentary conflicts between the two linguistic systems and not indicative of a structural change to underlying linguistic knowledge .
[Contains English characters] This assumption is in line with a range of investigations of L1 attrition which argue that this process may affect interface phenomena but will not touch the narrow syntax .
[Contains English characters] It has often been pointed out that L1 attrition usually first manifests itself in the lexicon .
[Contains English characters] It is possible for lexical representations in the L1 to be influenced by the semantic potential of corresponding items in the L2. Instances of such interlanguage effects are reported by e. g. Pavlenko, who concludes that for her L1 Russian speakers, a number of Russian terms appear to have gained a different meaning by semantic extension from their L2, English.
[Contains English characters] Secondly, it has been noted that among attriters, lexical access can become impaired, resulting in poorer performance on picture naming tasks and reduced lexical diversity in free speech .
[Contains English characters] Generative approaches to L1 attrition often focus on the possibility that the developing linguistic system may show evidence of irrevocable structural changes to the actual grammar of a native language.
[Contains English characters] This was highlighted early on in the history of attrition research: “It is crucial to know whether a given example of language loss can be attributed to a change in how the relevant language is represented in the mind of the user or to a change in the way stable knowledge is being used.
[Contains English characters] In a similar vein, Seliger and Vago define the object of investigation as “the disintegration or attrition of the structure of a first language in contact situations with a second language ” .
[Contains English characters] However, most research appears to indicate that attrition does not affect uninterpretable features, but that variability may be observed in features that are interpretable at the interface levels .
[Contains English characters] There therefore seems to be little evidence for an actual restructuring of the language system: the narrow syntax remains unaffected, and the observed variability may be ascribed to the cognitive demands of bilingual processing.
[Contains English characters] Lambert and Moore attempted to define numerous hypotheses regarding the nature of language loss, crossed with various aspects of language.
[Contains English characters] They envisioned a test to be given to American State Department employees that would include four linguistic categories and three skill areas .
[Contains English characters] A translation component would feature on a sub-section of each skill area tested.
[Contains English characters] The test was to include linguistic features which are most difficult, according to teachers, for students to master.
[Contains English characters] Such a test may confound testing what was not acquired with what was lost.
[Contains English characters] Lambert, in personal communication with Köpke and Schmid, described the results as not substantial enough to help much in the development of the new field of language skill attrition.
[Contains English characters] The use of translation tests to study language loss is inappropriate for a number of reasons: it is questionable what such tests measure; too much variation; the difference between attriters and bilinguals is complex; activating two languages at once may cause interference.
[Contains English characters] Yoshitomi attempted to define a model of language attrition that was related to neurological and psychological aspects of language learning and unlearning.
[Contains English characters] She discussed four possible hypotheses and five key aspects related to acquisition and attrition.
[Contains English characters] The hypotheses are: According to Yoshitomi, the five key aspects related to attrition are: neuroplasticity, consolidation, permastore/savings, decreased accessibility, and receptive vs.
[Contains English characters] productive abilities.
[Contains English characters] The regression hypothesis, first formulated by Roman Jakobson in 1941, goes back to the beginnings of psychology and psychoanalysis.
[Contains English characters] Generally speaking, it states that that which was learned first will be retained last, both in normal processes of forgetting and in pathological conditions such as aphasia or dementia.
[Contains English characters] As a template for language forgetting, the regression hypothesis has long seemed an attractive paradigm.
[Contains English characters] However, as Keijzer points out, regression is not in itself a theoretical or explanatory framework.
[Contains English characters] Both order of acquisition and order of attrition need to be put into the larger context of linguistic theory in order to gain explanatory adequacy.
[Contains English characters] Keijzer conducts a study on the L1 attrition of Dutch in anglophone Canada.
[Contains English characters] Her study compares language acquisition in children with non-pathological language attrition found in emigrant populations and contrasts it with language use in non-attrited, mature speakers.
[Contains English characters] In particular, it examines the parallels and divergences between advanced stages of L1 Dutch acquisition and the L1 attrition of Dutch émigrés in Anglophone Canada, as opposed to control subjects.
[Contains English characters] She finds some evidence that later-learned rules, for example with respect to diminutive and plural formation, do indeed erode before the earlier learned information.
[Contains English characters] However, there is also considerable interaction between the first and second language, so a straightforward regression pattern cannot be observed.
[Contains English characters] Citing the studies on the regression hypothesis that have been done, Yukawa says that the results have been contradictory.
[Contains English characters] It is possible that attrition is a case-by-case situation depending on a number of variables .
[Contains English characters] The threshold hypothesis states that there may be a level of proficiency that once attained, enables the attriting language to remain stable.
[Contains English characters] While attriters are reliably outperformed by native speakers on a range of tasks measuring overall proficiency there is an astonishingly small range of variability and low incidence of non-targetlike use in data even from speakers who claim not to have used their L1 for many decades, provided they emigrated after puberty: the most strongly attrited speakers still tend to compare favourably to very advanced L2 learners .
[Contains English characters] If, on the other hand, environmental exposure to the L1 ceases before puberty, the L1 system can deteriorate radically.
[Contains English characters] There are few principled and systematic investigations of FLA specifically investigating the impact of AoA.
[Contains English characters] However, converging evidence suggests an age effect on FLA which is much stronger and more clearly delineated than the effects which have been found in SLA research.
[Contains English characters] Two studies which consider pre- and postpuberty migrants find that AoA is one of the most important predictors of ultimate proficiency, while a number of studies which investigate the impact of age among postpuberty migrants fail to find any effect whatsoever .
[Contains English characters] A range of studies conducted by Montrul on Spanish heritage speakers in the US as well as Spanish-English bilinguals with varying levels of AoA also suggests that the L1 system of early bilinguals may be similar to that of L2 speakers, while later learners pattern with monolinguals in their L1 .
[Contains English characters] These findings therefore indicate strongly that early and late exposure to an L2 environment have a different impact on possible fossilization and/or deterioration of the linguistic system.
[Contains English characters] A recent investigation, focussing specifically on the age effect in L1 attrition, lends further substantiation to the assumption of a qualitative change around puberty: Bylund investigates the L1 of 31 Spanish speakers who emigrated to स्वीडन between the ages of 1 and 19 years and concludes that there is a small gradual decline in attrition susceptibility during the maturation period followed by a major decline at its end .
[Contains English characters] The strongest indication that an L1 can be extremely vulnerable to attrition if exposure ceases before puberty, on the other hand, comes from a study of Korean adoptees in France reported by Pallier .
[Contains English characters] This investigation could find no trace of L1 knowledge in speakers on a range of speech identification and recognition tasks, nor did an fMRI study reveal any differences in brain activation when exposing these speakers to Korean as opposed to unknown languages .
[Contains English characters] In all respects, the Korean adoptees presented in exactly the same way as the French controls.
[Contains English characters] All available evidence on the age effect for L1 attrition therefore indicates that the development of susceptibility displays a curved, not a linear, function.
[Contains English characters] This suggests that in native language learning there is indeed a Critical Period effect, and that full development of native language capacities necessitates exposure to L1 input for the entire duration of this CP.
[Contains English characters] In Hansen & Reetz-Kurashige, Hansen cites her own research on L2-Hindi and Urdu attrition in young children.
[Contains English characters] As young pre-school children in India and Pakistan, the subjects of her study were often judged to be native speakers of Hindi or Urdu; their mother was far less proficient.
[Contains English characters] On return visits to their home country, the United States, both children appeared to lose all their L2 while the mother noticed no decline in her own L2 abilities.
[Contains English characters] Twenty years later, those same young children as adults comprehend not a word from recordings of their own animated conversations in Hindi-Urdu; the mother still understands much of them Yamamoto found a link between age and bilinguality.
[Contains English characters] In fact, a number of factors are at play in bilingual families.
[Contains English characters] In her study, bicultural families that maintained only one language, the minority language, in the household, were able to raise bilingual, bicultural children without fail.
[Contains English characters] Families that adopted the one parent - one language policy were able to raise bilingual children at first but when the children joined the dominant language school system, there was a 50% chance that children would lose their minority language abilities.
[Contains English characters] In families that had more than one child, the older child was most likely to retain two languages, if it was at all possible.
[Contains English characters] Younger siblings in families with more than two other brothers and sisters had little chance of maintaining or ever becoming bilingual.
[Contains English characters] One of the basic predictions of psycholinguistic research with respect to L1 attrition is that language loss can be attributed to language disuse .
[Contains English characters] According to this prediction, attrition will be most radical among those individuals who rarely or never speak their L1 in daily life, while those speakers who use the L1 regularly, for example within their family or with friends, will to some degree be protected against its deterioration.
[Contains English characters] This assumption is based on the simple fact that rehearsal of information can maintain accessibility.
[Contains English characters] The amount of use which a potential attriter makes of her L1 strikes most researchers intuitively as one of the most important factors in determining the attritional process .
[Contains English characters] Obler believes that less-frequently used items are more difficult to retrieve.
[Contains English characters] The speed of retrieving a correct form or the actual production of an incorrect form is not indicative of loss but may be retrieval failure instead.
[Contains English characters] In other words, what appears to be lost is in fact difficult to retrieve.
[Contains English characters] There is, however, little direct evidence that the degree to which a language system will attrite is dependent on the amount to which the language is being used in everyday life.
[Contains English characters] Two early studies report that those subjects who used their L1 on an extremely infrequent basis showed more attrition over time .
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, there is also some evidence for a negative correlation, suggesting that the attriters who used their L1 on a daily basis actually performed worse on some tasks .
[Contains English characters] However, more recent, larger-scale studies of attrition which attempt to systematically elicit information on language use in a large range of settings have failed to discover any strong links between frequency of L1 use and degree of L1 attrition Paradis predicts that Motivation/affect may play an important role by influencing the activation threshold.
[Contains English characters] Thus attrition may be accelerated by a negative emotional attitude toward L1, which will raise the L1 activation threshold.
[Contains English characters] It may be retarded by a positive emotional attitude toward L1, which will lower its activation threshold.
[Contains English characters] However, the link between motivation and attrition has been difficult to establish.
[Contains English characters] Schmid & Dusseldorp fail to find any predictors for individual performance among a large number of measures of motivation, identity, and acculturation.
[Contains English characters] Given Paradis prediction, this finding is surprising, and may be linked to methodological difficulties of measurement: by definition, studies of language attrition are conducted a long time after migration has taken place .
[Contains English characters] The operative factor for the degree of attrition, however, is probably the attitude towards both L1 and L2 at the beginning of this period, when massive and intensive L2 learning is taking place, affecting the overall system of multicompetence.
[Contains English characters] However, attitudes are not stable and constant across a persons life, and what is measured at the moment that the degree of individual attrition is assessed may bear very little relation to the original feelings of the speaker.
[Contains English characters] It is difficult to see how this methodological problem can be overcome, as it is impossible for the attrition researcher to go back in time, and impractical to measure attitudes at one point in time and attrition effects at a second point, decades later.
[Contains English characters] The only study which has made an attempt in the direction of assessing identity at the time of migration is Schmid, who investigated attrition in historical context.
[Contains English characters] Her analysis of oral history interviews with German Jews points strongly towards an important correlation of attitude and identity at the moment of migration and eventual L1 attrition.
[Contains English characters] The reasons for this pattern of L1 attrition probably lie in a situation where the persecuted minority had the same L1 as the dominant majority, and the L1 thus became associated with elements of identity of that dominant group.
[Contains English characters] In such situations, a symbolic link between the language and the persecuting regime can lead to a rejection of that language.
[Contains English characters] Discovering such a link and its impact on the language attrition process is extremely complicated for most groups of migrants, since measurements are usually applied a long time after migration took place.
[Contains English characters] However, the findings presented here suggest that it is the attitude at the moment of migration, not what is assessed several decades later, that impacts most strongly on the attritional process.
[Contains English characters] Gardner, Lalonde, & Moorcroft investigated the nature of L2-French skills attriting by L1-English grade 12 students during the summer vacation, and the role played by attitudes and motivation in promoting language achievement and language maintenance.
[Contains English characters] Students who finished the L2 class highly proficient are more likely to retain what they knew.
[Contains English characters] Yet, interestingly, high achievers in the classroom situation are no more likely to make efforts to use the L2 outside the classroom unless they have positive attitudes and high levels of motivation.
[Contains English characters] The authors write: an underlying determinant of both acquisition and use is motivation”.
[Contains English characters] In fact, the nature of language acquisition is still so complex and so much is still unknown, not all students will have the same experiences during the incubation period.
[Contains English characters] It is possible that some students will appear to attrite in some areas and others will appear to attrite in other areas.
[Contains English characters] Some students will appear to maintain the level that they had previously achieved.
[Contains English characters] And still, other students will appear to improve.
[Contains English characters] Murtagh investigated retention and attrition of L2-Irish in Ireland with second level school students .
[Contains English characters] At Time 1, she found that most participants were motivated instrumentally, yet the immersion students were most likely to be motivated integratively and they had the most positive attitudes towards learning Irish.
[Contains English characters] Immersion school students were also more likely to have opportunities to use Irish outside the classroom/school environment.
[Contains English characters] Self-reports correlated with ability.
[Contains English characters] She concludes that the educational setting and the use of the language outside the classroom were the best predictors for L2-Irish acquisition.
[Contains English characters] Eighteen months later, Murtagh finds that the majority of groups 1 and 2 believe their Irish ability has attrited, the immersion group less so.
[Contains English characters] The results from the tests, however, do not show any overall attrition .
[Contains English characters] Time as a factor did not exert any overall significant change on the samples proficiency in Irish .
[Contains English characters] Fujita, in a study evaluating attrition among bilingual Japanese children, says that a number of factors are seen as necessary to maintain the two languages in the returnee child.
[Contains English characters] Those factors include: age on arrival in the L2 environment, length of residence in the L2 environment, and proficiency levels of the L1. Furthermore, she found that L2 attrition was closely related to another factor: age of the child on returning to the L1 environment.
[Contains English characters] Children returning around or before 9 were more likely to attrite than those returning later.
[Contains English characters] Upon returning from overseas, pressure from society, their family, their peers and themselves force returnee children to switch channels back to the L1 and they quickly make effort to attain the level of native-like L1 proficiency of their peers.
[Contains English characters] At the same time, lack of L2 support in the schools in particular and in society in general results in an overall L2 loss .
[Contains English characters] The loss of a native language is often experienced as something profoundly moving, disturbing or shocking, both by those who experience it and by those who witness it in others: “To lose your own language was like forgetting your mother, and as sad, in a way”, because it is “like losing part of one’s soul” is how Alexander McCall Smith puts it .
[Contains English characters] This intuitive appeal of the topic of language attrition can be seen as both a blessing and a curse.
[Contains English characters] Researchers who investigate level-ordered morphology or articulatory phonetics will probably rarely find that their friends and family, or even colleagues who work in different areas, show great interest in or enthusiasm for their work.
[Contains English characters] Those of us who study language attrition find ourselves with a much more receptive audience.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, we also find an audience with many preconceived ideas about attrition – a much rarer problem for the level-ordered morphologist or articulatory phonetician.
[Contains English characters] Worse, we may find such notions in ourselves.
[Contains English characters] Preconceived ideas are unscientific.
[Contains English characters] They are also often wrong.
[Contains English characters] In order to achieve a better understanding of the process of language attrition, scientific investigations first have to identify those areas of the L1 system which are most likely to be affected by influence from the L2. Initially, in the absence of experimental data and evidence of L1 attrition itself, a profitable approach is to look to neighbouring areas of linguistic investigation, such as language contact, creolisation, L2 acquisition, or aphasia.
[Contains English characters] In the early years of L1 attrition research, the 1980s, many researchers made valuable contributions of this nature, often augmented by small-scale experiments and/or case studies .
[Contains English characters] A number of strong predictions with intriguing theoretical implications were made during this period of L1 attrition research .
[Contains English characters] There are a number of factors which will impact in different ways on the process of L1 attrition.
[Contains English characters] Frequent use of a particular language may help to maintain the native language system intact, and so may a positive attitude towards the language or the speech community.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, none of these factors may be enough in themselves, and not all exposure to the language may be helpful.
[Contains English characters] A small, loose-knit L1 social network may even have a detrimental effect and accelerate language change.
[Contains English characters] Most importantly, however, the opportunity to use a language and the willingness to do so are factors which interact in complex ways to determine the process of language attrition.
[Contains English characters] As yet, our understanding of this interaction is quite limited.

[Contains English characters] The word semantics itself denotes a range of ideas, from the popular to the highly technical.
[Contains English characters] It is often used in ordinary language to denote a problem of understanding that comes down to word selection or connotation.
[Contains English characters] This problem of understanding has been the subject of many formal inquiries, over a long period of time.
[Contains English characters] The word is derived from the Greek word σημαντικός, significant, from σημαίνω, to signify, to indicate and that from σήμα, sign, mark, token.
[Contains English characters] In linguistics, it is the study of interpretation of signs or symbols as used by agents or communities within particular circumstances and contexts.
[Contains English characters] Within this view, sounds, facial expressions, body language, proxemics have semantic content, and each has several branches of study.
[Contains English characters] In written language, such things as paragraph structure and punctuation have semantic content; in other forms of language, there is other semantic content.

[Contains English characters] It may be particularly difficult to choose a single authorized heading for individuals whose various names have controversial political or social connotations, when the choice of authorized heading may be seen as endorsement of the associated political or social ideology.
[Contains English characters] An alternative to using authorized headings is the idea of access control, where various forms of a name are related without the endorsement of one particular form.
[Contains English characters] Before the advent of digital online public access catalogs and the Internet, creating and maintaining a librarys authority files were generally carried out by individual cataloging departments within each library.
[Contains English characters] Naturally, then, there was considerable difference in the authority files of the different libraries.
[Contains English characters] For the early part of library history, it was generally accepted that, as long as a librarys catalog was internally consistent, the differences between catalogs in different libraries did not matter greatly.
[Contains English characters] As libraries became more attuned to the needs of researchers and began interacting more with other libraries, the value of standard cataloging practices came to be recognized.
[Contains English characters] With the advent of automated database technologies, catalogers began to establish cooperative consortia, such as OCLC and RLIN in the United States, in which cataloging departments from libraries all over the world contributed their records to, and took their records from, a shared database.
[Contains English characters] This development prompted the need for national standards for authority work.
[Contains English characters] In the United States, the primary organization for maintaining cataloging standards with respect to authority work operates under the aegis of the Library of Congress, and is known as the Name Authority Cooperative Program, or NACO Authority.
[Contains English characters] There are various standards using different acronyms.

[Contains English characters] As with most academic disciplines, there are a very large number of archaeological sub-disciplines characterised by a specific method or type of material, geographical or chronological focus, other thematic concern, or a specific archaeological culture or civilisation .
[Contains English characters] Historical archaeology is the study of cultures with some form of writing.
[Contains English characters] In इंग्लंड, archaeologists have uncovered the long-lost layouts of medieval villages abandoned after the crises of the 14th century and the equally lost layouts of 17th century parterre gardens swept away by a change in fashion.
[Contains English characters] In downtown New York City archaeologists have exhumed the 18th century remains of the African burial ground.
[Contains English characters] Ethnoarchaeology is the archaeological study of living people.
[Contains English characters] The approach gained notoriety during the emphasis on middle range theory that was a feature of the processual movement of the 1960s.
[Contains English characters] Early ethnoarchaeological research focused on hunting and gathering or foraging societies.
[Contains English characters] Ethnoarchaeology continues to be a vibrant component of post-processual and other current archaeological approaches.
[Contains English characters] Ethnoarchaeology is the use of ethnography to increase and improve analogs, which are then used as analogies to interpret the archaeological record.
[Contains English characters] In short, ethnoarchaeology is the application of ethnography to archaeology.
[Contains English characters] Experimental archaeology represents the application of the experimental method to develop more highly controlled observations of processes that create and impact the archaeological record.
[Contains English characters] In the context of the logical positivism of processualism with its goals of improving the scientific rigor of archaeological epistemologies the experimental method gained importance.
[Contains English characters] Experimental techniques remain a crucial component to improving the inferential frameworks for interpreting the archaeological record.
[Contains English characters] Archaeometry is a field of study that aims to systematize archaeological measurement.
[Contains English characters] It emphasizes the application of analytical techniques from physics, chemistry, and engineering.
[Contains English characters] It is a lively field of research that frequently focuses on the definition of the chemical composition of archaeological remains for source analysis.
[Contains English characters] A relatively nascent subfield is that of archaeological materials, designed to enhance understanding of prehistoric and non-industrial culture through scientific analysis of the structure and properties of materials associated with human activity.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Original research While archaeology can be done as a pure science, it can also be an applied science, namely the study of archaeological sites that are threatened by development.
[Contains English characters] In such cases, archaeology is a subsidiary activity within Cultural resources management, also called heritage management in the United Kingdom.
[Contains English characters] Today, CRM accounts for most of the archaeological research done in the United States and much of that in western Europe as well.
[Contains English characters] In the US, CRM archaeology has been a growing concern since the passage of the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, and most taxpayers, scholars, and politicians believe that CRM has helped preserve much of that nations history and prehistory that would have otherwise been lost in the expansion of cities, dams, and highways.
[Contains English characters] Along with other statutes, the NHPA mandates that projects on federal land or involving federal funds or permits consider the effects of the project on each archaeological site.
[Contains English characters] The application of CRM in the United Kingdom is not limited to government-funded projects.
[Contains English characters] Since 1990 PPG 16 has required planners to consider archaeology as a material consideration in determining applications for new development.
[Contains English characters] As a result, numerous archaeological organisations undertake mitigation work in advance of construction work in archaeologically sensitive areas, at the developers expense.
[Contains English characters] In England, ultimate responsibility of care for the historic environment rests with the Department for Culture, Media and Sport in association with English Heritage.
[Contains English characters] In Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, the same responsibilities lie with Historic Scotland, Cadw and the Northern Ireland Environment Agency respectively.
[Contains English characters] Among the goals of CRM are the identification, preservation, and maintenance of cultural sites on public and private lands, and the removal of culturally valuable materials from areas where they would otherwise be destroyed by human activity, such as proposed construction.
[Contains English characters] This study involves at least a cursory examination to determine whether or not any significant archaeological sites are present in the area affected by the proposed construction.
[Contains English characters] If these do exist, time and money must be allotted for their excavation.
[Contains English characters] If initial survey and/or test excavation indicates the presence of an extraordinarily valuable site, the construction may be prohibited entirely.
[Contains English characters] CRM is a thriving entity, especially in the United States and Europe where archaeologists from private companies and all levels of government engage in the practice of their discipline.
[Contains English characters] Cultural resources management has, however, been criticized.
[Contains English characters] CRM is conducted by private companies that bid for projects by submitting proposals outlining the work to be done and an expected budget.
[Contains English characters] It is not unheard-of for the agency responsible for the construction to simply choose the proposal that asks for the least funding.
[Contains English characters] CRM archaeologists face considerable time pressure, often being forced to complete their work in a fraction of the time that might be allotted for a purely scholarly endeavour.
[Contains English characters] Compounding the time pressure is the vetting process of site reports which are required to be submitted by CRM firms to the appropriate State Historic Preservation Office .
[Contains English characters] From the SHPOs perspective there is to be no difference between a report submitted by a CRM firm operating under a deadline, and a multi-year academic project.
[Contains English characters] The end result is that for a Cultural Resource Management archaeologist to be successful, they must be able to produce academic quality documents at a corporate world pace.
[Contains English characters] The annual ratio of open academic archaeology positions to the annual number of archaeology MA/MSc and PhD students is grossly disproportionate.
[Contains English characters] This dearth of academic positions causes a predictable excess of well educated individuals who join the ranks of the following years crop of non-academically employed archaeologists.
[Contains English characters] Cultural Resource Management, once considered an intellectual backwater for individuals with strong backs and weak minds has reaped the benefit of this massive pool of well educated professionals.
[Contains English characters] This results in CRM offices increasingly staffed by advance degreed individuals with a track record of producing scholarly articles but who have the notches on their trowels to show they have been in the trenches as a shovelbum.
[Contains English characters] Early archaeology was largely an attempt to uncover spectacular artifacts and features, or to explore vast and mysterious abandoned cities.
[Contains English characters] Such pursuits continue to fascinate the public.
[Contains English characters] Books, films, and video games, such as The City of Brass, King Solomons Mines, Indiana Jones, Tomb Raider, The Mummy and Relic Hunter all testify to the publics interest in the discovery aspect of archaeology.
[Contains English characters] Much thorough and productive research has indeed been conducted in dramatic locales such as Copán and the Valley of the Kings, but the bulk of activities and finds of modern archaeology are not so sensational.
[Contains English characters] Archaeological adventure stories tend to ignore the painstaking work involved in carrying out modern survey, excavation, and data processing.
[Contains English characters] Some archaeologists refer to such portrayals as pseudoarchaeology.
[Contains English characters] Archaeology has been portrayed in the mainstream media in sensational ways.
[Contains English characters] This has its advantages and disadvantages.
[Contains English characters] Many practitioners point to the childhood excitement of Indiana Jones films and Tomb Raider video games as the inspiration for them to enter the field.
[Contains English characters] Archaeologists are also very much reliant on public support, the question of exactly who they are doing their work for is often discussed.
[Contains English characters] Motivated by a desire to halt looting, curb pseudoarchaeology, and to help preserve archaeological sites through education and fostering public appreciation for the importance of archaeological heritage, archaeologists are mounting public-outreach campaigns.
[Contains English characters] They seek to stop looting by combatting people who illegally take artifacts from protected sites, and by alerting people who live near archaeological sites of the threat of looting.
[Contains English characters] Common methods of public outreach include press releases, and the encouragement of school field trips to sites under excavation by professional archaeologists.
[Contains English characters] Public appreciation of the significance of archaeology and archaeological sites often leads to improved protection from encroaching development or other threats.
[Contains English characters] One audience for archaeologists work is the public.
[Contains English characters] They increasingly realize that their work can benefit non-academic and non-archaeological audiences, and that they have a responsibility to educate and inform the public about archaeology.
[Contains English characters] Local heritage awareness is aimed at increasing civic and individual pride through projects such as community excavation projects, and better public presentations of archaeological sites and knowledge.
[Contains English characters] The U. S. Dept. of Agriculture, Forest Service operates a volunteer archaeology and historic preservation program called the Passport in Time .
[Contains English characters] Volunteers work with professional USFS archaeologists and historians on national forests throughout the U. S. Volunteers are involved in all aspects of professional archaeology under expert supervision.
[Contains English characters] In the UK, popular archaeology programs such as Time Team and Meet the Ancestors have resulted in a huge upsurge in public interest.
[Contains English characters] Where possible, archaeologists now make more provisions for public involvement and outreach in larger projects than they once did, and many local archaeological organizations operate within the Community archaeology framework to expand public involvement in smaller-scale, more local projects.
[Contains English characters] Archaeological excavation, however, is best undertaken by well-trained staff that can work quickly and accurately.
[Contains English characters] Often this requires observing the necessary health and safety and indemnity insurance issues involved in working on a modern building site with tight deadlines.
[Contains English characters] Certain charities and local government bodies sometimes offer places on research projects either as part of academic work or as a defined community project.
[Contains English characters] There is also a flourishing industry selling places on commercial training excavations and archaeological holiday tours.
[Contains English characters] Archaeologists prize local knowledge and often liaise with local historical and archaeological societies, which is one reason why Community archaeology projects are starting to become more common.
[Contains English characters] Often archaeologists are assisted by the public in the locating of archaeological sites, which professional archaeologists have neither the funding, nor the time to do.
[Contains English characters] Pseudoarchaeology is an umbrella term for all activities that claim to be archaeological but in fact violate commonly accepted and scientific archaeological practices.
[Contains English characters] It includes much fictional archaeological work, as well as some actual activity.
[Contains English characters] Many non-fiction authors have ignored the scientific methods of processual archaeology, or the specific critiques of it contained in post-processualism.
[Contains English characters] An example of this type is the writing of Erich von Däniken.
[Contains English characters] His 1968 book, Chariots of the Gods?
[Contains English characters] , together with many subsequent lesser-known works, expounds a theory of ancient contacts between human civilisation on Earth and more technologically advanced extraterrestrial civilisations.
[Contains English characters] This theory, known as palaeocontact theory, or Ancient astronaut theory, is not exclusively Dänikens, nor did the idea originate with him.
[Contains English characters] Works of this nature are usually marked by the renunciation of well-established theories on the basis of limited evidence and the interpretation of evidence with a preconceived theory in mind.
[Contains English characters] Looting of archaeological sites is an ancient problem.
[Contains English characters] For instance, many of the tombs of the Egyptian pharaohs were looted during antiquity.
[Contains English characters] Archaeology stimulates interest in ancient objects, and people in search of artifacts or treasure cause damage to archaeological sites.
[Contains English characters] The commercial and academic demand for artifacts unfortunately contributes directly to the illicit antiquities trade.
[Contains English characters] Smuggling of antiquities abroad to private collectors has caused great cultural and economic damage in many countries whose governments lack the resources and or the will to deter it.
[Contains English characters] Looters damage and destroy archaeological sites, denying future generations information about their ethnic and cultural heritage.
[Contains English characters] Indigenous peoples especially lose access to and control over their cultural resources, ultimately denying them the opportunity to know their past.
[Contains English characters] Popular consciousness often associates looting with poor Third World countries, but this is a false assumption.
[Contains English characters] A lack of financial resources and political will are chronic worldwide problems inhibiting more effective protection of archaeological sites.
[Contains English characters] Many Native American Indians today, such as Vine Deloria, Jr.
[Contains English characters] , consider any removal of cultural artifacts from a Native American Indian site to be theft, and much of professional archaeology as academic looting.
[Contains English characters] In 1937 W. F. Hodge the Director of the Southwest Museum in Los Angeles CA, released a statement that the museum would no longer purchase or accept collections from looted contexts.
[Contains English characters] The first conviction of the transport of artifacts illegally removed from private property under the Archaeological Resources Protection Act was in 1992 in the State of Indiana.
[Contains English characters] In the United States, examples such as the case of Kennewick Man have illustrated the tensions between Native Americans and archaeologists which can be summarized as a conflict between a need to remain respectful towards burials sacred sites and the academic benefit from studying them.
[Contains English characters] For years, American archaeologists dug on Indian burial grounds and other places considered sacred, removing artifacts and human remains to storage facilities for further study.
[Contains English characters] In some cases human remains were not even thoroughly studied but instead archived rather than reburied.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, Western archaeologists views of the past often differ from those of tribal peoples.
[Contains English characters] The West views time as linear; for many natives, it is cyclic.
[Contains English characters] From a Western perspective, the past is long-gone; from a native perspective, disturbing the past can have dire consequences in the present.
[Contains English characters] As a consequence of this, American Indians attempted to prevent archaeological excavation of sites inhabited by their ancestors, while American archaeologists believed that the advancement of scientific knowledge was a valid reason to continue their studies.
[Contains English characters] This contradictory situation was addressed by the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act, which sought to reach a compromise by limiting the right of research institutions to possess human remains.
[Contains English characters] Due in part to the spirit of postprocessualism, some archaeologists have begun to actively enlist the assistance of indigenous peoples likely to be descended from those under study.
[Contains English characters] Archaeologists have also been obliged to re-examine what constitutes an archaeological site in view of what native peoples believe to constitute sacred space.
[Contains English characters] To many native peoples, natural features such as lakes, mountains or even individual trees have cultural significance.
[Contains English characters] Australian archaeologists especially have explored this issue and attempted to survey these sites in order to give them some protection from being developed.
[Contains English characters] Such work requires close links and trust between archaeologists and the people they are trying to help and at the same time study.
[Contains English characters] While this cooperation presents a new set of challenges and hurdles to fieldwork, it has benefits for all parties involved.
[Contains English characters] Tribal elders cooperating with archaeologists can prevent the excavation of areas of sites that they consider sacred, while the archaeologists gain the elders aid in interpreting their finds.
[Contains English characters] There have also been active efforts to recruit aboriginal peoples directly into the archaeological profession.
[Contains English characters] A new trend in the heated controversy between First Nations groups and scientists is the repatriation of native artifacts to the original descendants.
[Contains English characters] An example of this occurred June 21, 2005, when community members and elders from a number of the 10 Algonquian nations in the Ottawa area convened on the Kitigan Zibi reservation near Maniwaki, Quebec, to inter ancestral human remains and burial goods — some dating back 6,000 years.
[Contains English characters] It was not determined, however, if the remains were directly related to the Algonquin people who now inhabit the region.
[Contains English characters] The remains may be of Iroquoian ancestry, since Iroquoian people inhabited the area before the Algonquin.
[Contains English characters] Alternatively, the oldest of these remains might have no relation at all to the Algonquin or Iroquois, and belong to an earlier culture who previously inhabited the area.
[Contains English characters] The remains and artifacts, including jewelry, tools and weapons, were originally excavated from various sites in the Ottawa Valley, including Morrison and the Allumette Islands.
[Contains English characters] They had been part of the Canadian Museum of Civilization’s research collection for decades, some since the late 1800s.
[Contains English characters] Elders from various Algonquin communities conferred on an appropriate reburial, eventually deciding on traditional redcedar and birchbark boxes lined with redcedar chips, muskrat and beaver pelts.
[Contains English characters] Now, an inconspicuous rock mound marks the reburial site where close to 90 boxes of various sizes are buried, no further scientific study is possible.
[Contains English characters] Although negotiations were at times tense between the Kitigan Zibi community and museum, they were able to reach agreement.
[Contains English characters] Kennewick Man is another repatriation candidate that has been the source of heated debate.

[Contains English characters] Lizards are a widespread group of squamate reptiles, with approximately 6,000 species, ranging across all continents except Antarctica, as well as most oceanic island chains.
[Contains English characters] The group, traditionally recognized as the suborder Lacertilia, is defined as all extant members of the Lepidosauria that are neither sphenodonts nor snakes – they form an evolutionary grade.
[Contains English characters] While the snakes are recognized as falling phylogenetically within the Toxicofera clade from which they evolved, the sphenodonts are the sister group to the squamates, the larger monophyletic group, which includes both the lizards and the snakes.
[Contains English characters] Lizards typically have feet and external ears, while snakes lack both of these characteristics.
[Contains English characters] However, because they are defined negatively as excluding snakes, lizards have no unique distinguishing characteristic as a group.
[Contains English characters] Lizards and snakes share a movable quadrate bone, distinguishing them from the sphenodonts, which have more primitive and solid diapsid skulls.
[Contains English characters] Many lizards can detach their tails to escape from predators, an act called autotomy.
[Contains English characters] Vision, including color vision, is particularly well developed in most lizards, and most communicate with body language or bright colors on their bodies, as well as with pheromones.
[Contains English characters] Lizards are the most speciose among extant reptiles, comprising about 60% of all living species.
[Contains English characters] The adult length of species within the suborder ranges from a few centimeters for chameleons such as Brookesia micra and geckos such as Sphaerodactylus ariasae to nearly 3 m in the case of the largest living varanid lizard, the Komodo dragon.
[Contains English characters] Some extinct varanids reached great size.
[Contains English characters] The extinct aquatic mosasaurs reached 17 m, and the giant monitor Megalania is estimated to have reached perhaps 7 m .
[Contains English characters] The name Sauria was coined by James Macartney ; it was the Latinisation of the French name Sauriens, coined by Alexandre Brongniart for an order of reptiles in the classification proposed by the author, containing lizards and crocodilians, later discovered not to be each others closest relatives.
[Contains English characters] Later authors used the term Sauria in a more restricted sense, i. e. as a synonym of Lacertilia, a suborder of Squamata that includes all lizards but excludes snakes.
[Contains English characters] This classification is rarely used today because Sauria so-defined is a paraphyletic group.
[Contains English characters] It was defined as a clade by Jacques Gauthier, Arnold G.
[Contains English characters] Kluge and Timothy Rowe as the group containing the most recent common ancestor of archosaurs and lepidosaurs and all its descendants.
[Contains English characters] A different definition was formulated by Michael deBraga and Olivier Rieppel who defined Sauria as the clade containing the most recent common ancestor of Choristodera, Archosauromorpha and Lepidosauromorpha and all their descendants.
[Contains English characters] However, neither of these uses have not gained wide acceptance among researchers specializing in lizards.
